at the base's last run, 83.2-89.1 ms here).

## ADR-8818: W-11 D1 crater edits: one pass per owner tile, each roof's plane built once per edit, an edited state's own ground height ranges, promotion by coarse cell and row reads for the renderer
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 121 § 11 budgets a D1 edit at 0.2 ms for a 6 m crater "including the index rebuild of its ground
tiles". W-31 (ADR-8662, D6) measured `GeomState::apply_ground_edit` at 0.36-0.38 ms on the Android test device and
0.48 ms on the Steam Deck for a 6 m radius (1154 vertices at Switchbacks' 0.3125 m pitch). The walk read every
footprint vertex by its own lookups: `d²` three times from six `vertex_mm` divisions, the ring-pin list searched
twice and the hanging list once, `count_in_tile`'s tile search (about eight integer divisions), a column-cell search
plus one decoded `f32` triangle and plane (three edges) per roof whose box holds the vertex for the ceiling stop, and
a searched, sorted insert into the tile's block. And there was no index rebuild: as built (ADR-8313) an edited state's
segments stopped skipping ground by the height pyramid, which is where W-31's sight-line speed-up lives. Measured on
this lane with 30 craters along the Switchbacks tube: one mixed tick of § 11 cost 3.93 ms on the Pixel (0.93 fresh)
and 6.54 ms on the Deck (1.63 fresh), `line_of_sight` 25 µs a call against 2.5. Two more costs sat beside the edit:
on a `Nested` map the first crater in a coarse ground tile took 3.6 ms on the Deck (the promotion's fills were read
one by one and each compared with every earlier fill), and `height_rects`, which a host calls after each edit to
forward the changed heights, took as long as the edit (75 µs on the Deck for a 6 m crater's rectangle).
Decision:
1. **One pass per owner tile** (`edit::TileWalk`). The disc keeps one squared offset per candidate column and row
   (`Disc`, two `[i64; 128]`), so `d²` is one add and the columns inside the radius on a row are one run. The profile
   walks the footprint one owner tile at a time, row by row: a tile stored at full pitch gives its counts as a row
   slice (`TileCounts`; a vertex on a tile's first column or row, which also lies in a neighbor's range, keeps
   `count_in_tile`'s search, as does every vertex of a tile stored coarser); the ring pins and hanging overrides
   inside the footprint's vertex range and the tile's own override block are read by cursor; the tile's new block is
   built in one merge and swapped in. The integer profile, `m_to_mm`, the clamp, the hash terms and the write rule (an
   override equal to the cooked hanging override is not stored) are the same expressions.
2. **The ceiling stop builds a roof's plane once per edit** (`query::RoofStops`). A column-grid cell is looked up once
   per run of columns; its roofs whose box reaches the footprint's box are listed once with their planes; a roof whose
   z range misses the row is dropped once per row. Each drop is `xz_outside`'s own comparison on the same `f32`
   bounds (a box wholly beyond the footprint's first or last column or row is outside at every vertex of it), so the
   same roofs reach `Plane::crossing` with the same cell list in the same order.
3. **An edited state keeps its own ground height ranges** (`edit::EditedRanges`): the height pyramid's
   `[lowest, highest]` per node, copied on a state's first edit and widened, with its ancestors, by every height an
   edit writes into each ground tile the vertex touches. `GroundLattice::edited_range` hands them to `ground_node`,
   and `segment_inner` uses the pyramid whenever the state has them. The ranges only grow (an undone crater leaves
   them wide): they are a bound, so they can prevent a skip and never hide a hit. They are not part of the state's
   value: `GroundEdits`' `==` compares overrides and promoted tiles, the hash and the snapshot do not carry them,
   `decode` rebuilds them from the overrides, and a clone shares them until the next edit (about 44 KB on
   Switchbacks, the size of the cooked pyramid, beside the 34.0 MB geometry).
4. **Promotion reads a coarse cell once** (`GeomState::promotion_buckets`, `CoarseCell`). The fills of a promoted tile
   are `height_in_tile` of the coarse surface at each fine vertex. The coarse cell's four corners are now read once
   per run of vertices inside it and the lattice cell of a vertex once per tile column and row (`locate` is per
   axis); the diagonal's edge function, `plane_height` and `m_to_mm` are the same calls. Only a border vertex can
   already hold a fill from another tile of the same edit, so only those are checked against a sorted list. The fills
   are grouped by the tile that stores them and merged into its block once.
5. **`height_rects` reads rows** (`GeomState::row_heights`): one owner tile's run of a row at a time, with the same
   count rows and cursors as the edit walk. A row past the lattice keeps the one-vertex form.
6. **The per-vertex forms stay as the reference** (`GeomState::apply_ground_edit_reference` with `profile_writes` and
   `promotion_fills`, `cfg(any(test, feature = "stats"))`, the pattern of `segment_without_pyramid`).
   `tests/ground_edit_walks.rs` holds the two walks equal after every edit of seeded books (state, state hash,
   generation, snapshot bytes, dirty rectangle or error, work counters; a disc's rectangle also against a test of
   every vertex of the map; `height_rects` of the dirty rectangle against `vertex_height_mm` of each vertex): 572,367
   vertex writes on a roofed gallery (roof edges on lattice lines, a roof sloping through the ground), 1,413,962 on
   two `Nested` maps (promotion of one tile and of four at a corner, hanging overrides, coarse tiles, a last tile
   two cells wide) and 602,434 on the cooked Switchbacks map (tube roofs, mouth rings, ground-tile borders, the map's
   corners). `edited_state_segments_equal_the_full_walk` holds `segment` equal to `segment_without_pyramid` on edited
   states (1892 rays by two masks on Switchbacks after 36 edits, 305 ground hits under the cooked ground and 455 over
   it; again after a snapshot round trip and an undo; and on a `Nested` map with promoted tiles).
   `height_rects_equal_the_vertex_reads` covers whole edited maps in pieces of 128 and rectangles past the lattice.
7. **Both readings of "6 m crater" are measured** (ADR-8662 D6, the owner's ruling): the bench prints
   `ground_edit_crater_3m` (a 6 m diameter, 288 vertices) beside the budget row `ground_edit_crater_6m` (a 6 m radius,
   1154 vertices), plus `ground_edit_crater_6m_on_edited_state`, `query_bench_mixed_calls_on_edited_state` (the mixed
   tick after 30 craters), `ground_edit_height_rects_6m`, and on a small `Nested` map
   `ground_edit_crater_6m_nested_first_touch` and `ground_edit_crater_6m_nested_promoted`, without budget rows.
8. `#[inline]` on `GroundEdits::{is_empty, get, is_promoted}`: every ground read of every query calls them across a
   module.
Consequences: Measured (`docs/evidence/w11-crater-edits/`; p50, before → after at df274bc3d):
`ground_edit_crater_6m` Pixel 9 Pro 0.359-0.381 → 0.060-0.065 ms, Steam Deck 0.479-0.482 → 0.083-0.084 ms (bar 0.2);
`ground_edit_crater_3m` Pixel 0.087-0.088 → 0.019 ms, Deck 0.123 → 0.023 ms; a 6 m crater on a state that shares 30
craters' blocks: Pixel 0.40-0.43 → 0.056-0.061 ms, Deck 0.57 → 0.082-0.086 ms. The mixed tick on the cratered state:
Pixel 3.93 → 0.99-1.02 ms, Deck 6.54 → 1.77 ms. The first crater in a coarse tile of a `Nested` map (one 64-cell
tile promoted, 4165 fills): Deck 3.60-3.66 → 0.241 ms, the build server 3.39 → 0.20-0.23 ms, Pixel 0.168-0.171 ms (no
before); it is still over 0.2 ms on the Deck, and four tiles at a corner cost about four times that.
`height_rects` of a 6 m crater's rectangle: Deck 0.074-0.075 → 0.012 ms, the build server 0.068 → 0.011 ms, Pixel 0.010 ms.
The test machine was loaded all lane (load 27-36 on 32 threads): 0.21-0.34 → 0.047-0.072 ms for the 6 m crater there is
not an idle-core number. Heap requests per 6 m crater: at most 19 (the per-vertex walk: at least 22;
`a_crater_asks_the_heap_a_bounded_number_of_times`, bar 20). No answer changes: `QUERY_BITS_VERSION`, the state hash,
the snapshot layout and the two-peer drive's run hash (`74e9d8f805407ffe`, the base's) are the same. No API change in
a default or `stage_b` build; under `stats` there are two more methods (`apply_ground_edit_reference`,
`keeps_ground_ranges`). This lane changed two statements in lane 001's `segment_inner`/`ground_node`
(`query_segment.rs`), added `RoofStops` beside `highest_roof_at_or_below` in `query.rs`, and one accessor in
`ground.rs`; `highest_roof_at_or_below`, `cooked_override_at` and `is_ring_vertex` are now `cfg(any(test, feature =
"stats"))` (the reference walk's). Spec 121 § 6 and § 11, `docs/perf/budgets.ron` (the row's note) and the book's
ground-edit section say so.
The mixed tick on a fresh state is unchanged within what code placement alone moves it: across this lane's builds
it read 0.87-0.96 ms on the Pixel and 1.61-1.72 ms on the Deck with no source change in the calls that moved
(`push_disc` + `clamp_under_ceiling` 1.72 or 2.85 µs a call on the Pixel, 2.58 or 3.07 on the Deck; `segment` 7.0 or
8.0 µs on the Deck; one build with `query_segment.rs` byte-identical to the base read 1.72 ms on the Deck). The final
build reads 0.93-0.94 ms (Pixel) and 1.65 ms (Deck); the base 0.93-0.96 and 1.63-1.64. Lane 001 inherits that: a
faster `push_disc` code shape exists for the same source (`gather_walls` and its sort inlined into `push_disc`; an
experiment build with `#[inline(always)]` on them, not in this branch, read 3.08 → 2.62 µs a call on the Deck), and a
device A/B needs interleaved runs of builds that differ only in the change under test. Left for others: `support` on an edited state costs about 10 % more than on a
fresh one (`GroundEdits::get`'s two searches per vertex; lane 003's column).

## ADR-8899: nav cell v3: conservative navmesh rasterisation (v0.7 format batch 2)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7558 kept `regia_nav::heightfield::rasterize_triangle` centre-sampled in v0.5.x: a cell took a
triangle only where the cell centre lay inside the triangle's XZ projection, so a wall top, a plank or a steep face
thinner than `cell_size` (0.25 m by default) could fall between two centres and vanish, and agents walked through the
wall or missed the plank depending on the grid offset. ADR-7724 row (d) planned the fix with a `nav-cell` 2 → 3
bump; the owner held it out of v0.6.0 (it re-cooks DO27's navigation) and approved it for v0.7 with format batch 2
(2026-11-19).
Decision: (1) A triangle reaches every cell whose square its XZ projection overlaps with a positive area (2D
separating-axis test: the square's two axes and the triangle's three edge normals; the square is shrunk by
`1e-4 * cell_size` so a triangle that only touches a cell edge, such as a floor edge on a grid line, does not reach
the neighbour). A cell whose centre the triangle covers records the plane height at the centre exactly as before; a
cell it only overlaps records the height range of the triangle clipped to the cell square (Sutherland-Hodgman). (2)
In the per-column merge, a merged span's top is the highest centre-sampled top unless an overlap-only top is more
than `cell_height` above it (or there is no centre sample), so a coplanar neighbour triangle that overlaps a
diagonal cell cannot raise a walkable slope by its gradient across the cell, while a thin wall top or a steep face
that stands a voxel above the sampled surface takes the cell. The rule is a function of the set of spans, so the
result stays independent of the triangle order. A span whose top came from overlap only is `partial`: for an agent
with a radius, erosion treats a partial cell as a boundary (the top layer clears it before eroding, the layered span
graph seeds it at distance 0), so the partly covered cells at a floor edge never widen the surface an agent with a
body stands on (`tq_gaps::a_floor_narrower_than_the_agent_has_no_walkable_surface` failed without this: a 0.6 m
strip with an off-grid edge gained its partial third cell and kept a one-cell strip for a 0.35 m agent); a radius-0
agent may stand on partial cells, so a thin plank carries it. (3) `NAV_CELL_FORMAT_VERSION` 2 → 3, `nav_cell_migration_sources`
`[1, 2]`. The byte layout (`NAV_CELL_LAYOUT`) does not change, so its hash stays and only the version moves. A v1 or
v2 cell keeps loading as the centre-sampled cell it is (the plan row: a cooked cache, no `upgrade-project` row, no
rewrite) and the loader logs a warning naming the re-cook; `regia cook` re-cooks streamed levels on every run, and
the version in the header makes every cooked blob differ, so a cook rewrites them. Vertical triangles still record
nothing in the span pass (the layered build's `WallExtents` covers them, ADR-8076). (4) The editor's reflect
`@Range` hints of `NavAgentParams` now offer only agents the builder accepts: `height` 0.01..=24 (was 0..=24) and
`max_slope` 0..=1.57 (was 0..=1.6, past pi/2). They are reflect attributes, not hashed by any format.
Consequences: a flat floor whose edges lie on grid lines and every cell a centre sample filled on a walkable slope
keep their top heights bit for bit, and for an agent with a radius the eroded surface of such geometry is unchanged
(unit tests against a copy of the old rasteriser); floor edges off the grid gain partial cells only for radius-0
agents; thin geometry blocks agents, and a thin plank carries a radius-0 agent. Navigation determinism pins that hash built meshes
move where such geometry exists (the lead re-pins; old and new values in the lane report). DO27 must re-cook its
streamed levels' navigation (`regia cook`) when it adopts v0.7; until then its v2 cells load, and a seam between a
v2 cell and a runtime region rebuild can disagree. Specs updated: 12 § 4a (row appended); `docs/formats/nav-cell.md`;
book/agents/navigation.md. Supersedes ADR-7558's decision for v0.7 and later.

## ADR-8809: Lockstep host migration (spec 120 § 10.5, N301)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 10.5 (row S4, owner question Q1, moved into scope by the owner 11-16) asks that a lockstep match
continues when its host quits. It re-derives the owner's DO27 live re-host design: a 600-frame cache on every seat,
a deterministic best-connected election, the winner on the agreed port or the next of 16, resume at the highest next
tick, the next ranked after 3 s, and the readout `HostLost` / `Electing` / `Resuming { in_ticks }`. It adds an
authenticated election: each seat's Noise static key and a per-match migration secret go out at join, and only seats
of the match can win or join. The lockstep core is sans-IO, and its host and seats are separate types.
Decision: A new `regia_net::lockstep::migration` module with `HostMigration`, one per seat, also sans-IO. It reads the
roster and matrix through the seat, takes the time and the migration messages, and hands out actions (`Listen`,
`StopListening`, `Connect { addrs, key }` with the key to pin, `Send`) and events.
1. Frame cache: `LockstepSeat` keeps the bodies of its last `frame_log_ticks` (600) frames with the delta base
   before them. This costs one extra decode per frame as it leaves the cache.
2. Roster and matrix: `LockstepHost::share_roster` sends them as two new lockstep stream payload kinds (0x14, 0x15),
   sealed like every lockstep payload. They are not frame fields and there is no transport framing change, so
   `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` stays (a seat built before this change refuses the new kinds as `lockstep_malformed`;
   share a roster only with seats of this version). The roster is shared again when a seat id gets a new player or
   membership changes, and drops seats that left. The matrix (`note_transport_rtt`, `note_pair_rtt`) goes out every
   3 s and on any membership or silence change. It names the seats the host found silent.
3. Election: `rank_survivors` sorts by (silent, sum of round trips to the other survivors, seat id). A pair round trip
   the game measured beats the estimate through the old host. Matrices of different versions converge on the newer
   one, which claims and election answers carry. A follower passes a winner that has not answered after
   `next_candidate_after_ms` (3 s), or after `hello_wait_ms` + 3 s once it said hello.
4. Re-host messages (claim, election answer, hello frames in parts of at most 256 frames and 8 KiB, hello, resume)
   carry the match id, the epoch and the sender's seat, under a keyed BLAKE3 MAC whose key is derived from the
   migration secret. The winner's side is also covered by the pinned Noise key. The seats' side relies on the MAC
   alone, because the transport handshake has no client static key: a seat of the match can claim another seat's
   id. Recorded as a known issue.
5. Resume: the winner resumes at the highest tick it holds contiguously (its own cache plus the hello frames). Every
   survivor sends frames from the winner's next tick, so this is the highest next tick. `LockstepHost::resumed`
   builds a relay host from the cache and the winner seat's stamp schedule: frame clock due `resume_lead_ms` (1 s)
   later, `tick_base` so the clock needs no history, every chain member a seat, hello seats acknowledged at their
   next tick. The others get frames through the existing redundancy and stream paths, which batch a catch-up
   longer than one payload. The winner's own seat stays a seat on an in-process link, so its inputs keep the same
   delay as everyone's. `LockstepSeat::rehost` resets only what belonged to the old connection.
6. Resume tokens are keyed BLAKE3 of (seat, generation) under the migration secret once a roster is shared. Any host
   of the match accepts them, so the old host comes back as a player through `resume` + `catch_up`.
7. Silence: lockstep payloads plus `LockstepSeat::note_host_heard`, so the transport's keepalives count; spec 120
   § 10.5 says "Interrupted". A winner that got no hello by `hello_wait_ms` does not resume alone (no split match
   when one seat alone lost the host).
Consequences: Host-visible additions only (new types and methods, `LockstepStatus::migration`; see the release
fragment). DO27's ten scenarios are cargo tests on seeded virtual time (`lockstep/migration_tests.rs`). Not built:
the replication-game successor journal (N302/N303); NAT traversal toward the winner (the roster carries the address
the host saw; § 10.7 is another lane); a seat that claims after the winner resumed gets `migration_unexpected` and
must come back through its resume token; a match whose only other survivor is dead does not continue alone. Specs
updated: spec 120 § 10.5 "Built" note; book `agents/net-lockstep.md` (Host migration, error codes),
`user-guide/networking.md`.

## ADR-8819: Hover hulls in the predicted schedule (`regia_framework::net_hover`, spec 73 § 9.2)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_framework::det_hover` (ADR-8550) steps hover hulls in `FixedUpdate` on one authority; its report left
open how a client predicts its own hull. Characters re-run per entity (spec 73 § 9); vehicles cannot, because their
chassis lives in the rapier world (§ 9.1, ADR-3080). A hover hull's step is `det_hover::tick_hull`: a pure function of
(hull tuning, `HoverBody`, input, floor sampler, world, hop speed, `dt`) that only calls `regia_detsim` lockstep
arithmetic and touches nothing else, so it can re-run per entity like a character.
Decision:
(1) Where it runs. `NetHoverPlugin` (or `install_net_hover::<I>` for a game's own command type) adds one predicted system,
`net_hover_step::<I>`, to `regia_net`'s predicted schedule (`NetSet::Predict`). It runs on the server for every
`NetHover` hull it simulates and on the owning client for its `NetRole::Predicted` copy, once per tick and again on every
re-run. Per hull, in `(NetId, entity)` order: resolve the hull tuning, write `DetHoverInput` from the owner's command
(a hull with no owner reads its own `DetHoverInput`, which the server's game writes), `tick_hull`, then the
presentation (`DetHoverLean`, `Transform`) exactly as `present_det_hover_hulls` writes it. Hulls never interact in the
step, so the order only fixes the stats. `DetHoverPlugin`'s own step and present systems skip hulls marked
`DetHoverSteppedExternally` (required by `NetHover`), so a hull is stepped once per tick, and a proxy's interpolated
`Transform` is never overwritten from its late state. `dt` is `DetHoverConfig::dt` (the offline hull's setting, so a
networked hull steps the same bits as an offline one); a `dt` more than 1e-4 s off the net tick step logs
`net.hover_dt_mismatch` once. The floor is `DetHoverFloor`: static world geometry both sides must hold (spec 73 § 6.1).
(2) Tuning. `NetHover { local_player, hull }` is replicated; `hull` is `hull_key(&DetHoverHull)`, FNV-1a 64 over the
273 lockstep handshake bytes (ADR-8632) plus the footprint's `f32` bits (integer work only, the same on every target).
Each side lists its hulls in the `NetHoverHulls` resource. A copy whose own `DetHoverHull` has another key takes the
listed hull with the replicated key; a key nobody listed leaves the hull unstepped and counts `unknown_hull` (shown
by `net.hovers` as `fault: "hover_hull_unknown"`), never stepping with a guessed tuning.
(3) Input. Default command `HoverNetInput { throttle, strafe, steer, hop, jump }`: each axis 8 bits (`i8`, -127..=127,
zero exact, `i8::MIN` refused on decode with `hover_input_range`), `hop` and `jump` one bit each; 3 bytes + 2 bits full,
2 bits + 1 change bit when only the buttons repeat. Both sides step `HoverNetInput::quantized()`, so the client predicts
with what the server receives. `on_missing` keeps the axes and clears `hop` and `jump` (presses, not holds);
`merge_late` ORs the presses and takes the newer axes. Games with richer input implement `HoverCommand` on their
own `NetInput` type (`hover_input(&self) -> DetHoverInput`).
(4) Predicted components: `DetHoverState` and `Transform`. `DetHoverState` travels at full `f32` precision (a rollback
must restart from the server's exact bits for the re-run to match it), with a per-field change mask in the delta
(a hull at rest sends one bit per field). `Transform` is predicted for the rollback set and the visual offset (§ 6.4
reads poses from it); it is derived from the state, so the one `EntityTolerance` (`hover_tolerance`) decides on
`DetHoverState` alone: position and hover height (`altitude`) within 0.01 m; yaw, roll, pitch, cushion pitch, ground
pitch and roll, slope within 0.01 rad (wrapped); velocity (all three axes and `vertical_vel`) within 0.05 m/s; yaw,
roll and cushion pitch rates and `ground_climb` within 0.05 per second; `hop_cooldown` within 1/240 s; `coast_drop_left`
within 0.05 m/s; `prev_terrain` both unset or within 0.01 m; `airborne`, `jump_active`, `level_off`, `yaw_modern`,
`thrusting` exact. The state has no integer counters; the timers and the coast drop are its charge state. Same-build
peers step the same bits, so the tolerances only absorb cross-platform drift (spec 73 § 11).
(5) `NetResimulating(true)` / § 8. `tick_hull` has no side effects, so nothing in the step is suppressed. The effects are
the hop and jump launches: `net_hover_step` appends `NetHoverEffect { entity, tick, kind }` to the `NetHoverEffects`
resource only when the tick runs for the first time on this client (`PredictionState::first_time`) or on the server,
and the `hops`/`jumps` counters of `NetHoverStats` count those runs only; `resim_steps` counts re-runs. A game plays
launch sounds from `NetHoverEffects`, never from the re-run.
(6) Agent surface: `net.hovers` (read, `{}`): every networked hull with entity, NetId, role, hull key, whether the
key is known, position, rendered position, velocity, yaw, altitude, airborne, the client's correction stats, and the
counters. Error: `F0002` with `data.reason` `net_not_running` (the `net.vehicles` reason). Guide page
`book/agents/net-hover.md`, topic `net-hover`.
(7) Outside moves. On the server only, a hull whose `Transform` translation differs from the one the step left (a
private `NetHoverMemo`) was moved by game code (knockback) or `net.force_correction`: the next step takes that
translation into `DetHoverState::pos` and counts `adopted_moves`. The rotation is always the step's. A client never
adopts: its `Transform` is derived, and a rollback writes the server's (quantized) one.
Consequences: Spec 73 gains § 9.2 "Hover hulls". `det_hover` gains the public marker `DetHoverSteppedExternally`
(additive; its step and present queries filter it out). New public items in `regia_framework::net_hover` (feature
`net`). No format, no new dependency, no `regia_detsim` change (DO27's pins do not move). No vehicle soak profile exists
in `regia_net_soak`, so no hover case was added there. A hull's tuning cannot change in flight (the key is read per tick,
but both sides must list the new hull first).

## ADR-8569: Mouth bands drawn in every terrain pass with the terrain's own pipelines (W-15 item 3; spec 26 § 2a.4 steps 5-6; completes ADR-8470's "Deferred")
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed (lane do27-mesh-layers-seam-gpu-b; builds on ADR-8291 and ADR-8470)
Context: ADR-8470 cut a filled mouth on the lattice but left the band (zipper strip, skirt, throat) undrawn, so the
cut showed nothing in it. The terrain's shared pipelines exist per shader source, colour format, depth format and hole
cut, with colour variants for the ground look, the virtual texture, the local-light loop and the cloud map, all
warmed by `warm_shared` and counted by the warm tests. A band pipeline would need every one of those variants (or an
uncounted extra), and the render-core rule forbids touching the frame graph or its dispatch.
Decision:
1. **No band pipeline.** The band is drawn by the pass's own plain (no hole cut) terrain pipeline, the one
   `draw_shared` already binds for that pass (`TerrainGpu::bind_shared`, split out of `draw_shared`), with one
   non-indexed draw whose `vertex_index` starts at `BAND_VERTEX_BASE` (2^24). `terrain.wgsl`'s `displaced`, which
   every terrain vertex entry point (colour, depth, velocity, receiver, cascade, and their hole variants) calls, reads
   such a vertex from the band words instead of the node grid. The band therefore draws in every colour variant, the
   depth prepass, velocity, the decal receiver and every sun cascade, with no new pipeline, bind group layout or
   warm entry: the warm and pipeline-count pins do not move. The grass and impostor shaders never call `displaced`.
2. **Band words.** The band rides in the hole storage buffer after the windows (no new binding: group 2 stays at three
   vertex-stage storage buffers). Header words 1-3, unused until now, hold the band's word offset, its corner count and
   its vertex count; then the corners (indices, each triangle in both windings because the colour pipelines cull back
   faces), then five vertex sets of `xyz` f32: set 0 for the camera passes, set `1 + i` for cascade `i`. The buffer is
   now `STORAGE | COPY_DST`; a changed band topology rebuilds it (`holes_generation` bumps, so camera views rebind);
   per-frame placement writes only the changed sets through the shared upload belt.
3. **Placement per pass (spec 26 § 2a.4 step 5).** `MouthBands::from_layers` flattens the open mouths: a ring vertex
   and the skirt bottom under it (the zipper's trailing skirt vertices with the same lattice XZ) follow the attach,
   every other vertex is fixed at its cook position (authored loop, throat). Each prepare for the host camera,
   `TerrainSharedDraw::place_bands` places set 0 on the camera's selection and eye and set `1 + i` on cascade `i`'s
   anchored selection and morph eye, with `attach_ring_on` (the `attach_ring` mirror on the draw's own map, config and
   root level). A set is placed and uploaded only when its key (selection or cascade key, morph eye bits, heights
   generation, band generation) changed; a held camera places nothing. The cascade shadow key mixes in the set's key,
   so a band that opens, closes or re-places redraws that cascade. The region redraw of a cascade draws the band too.
4. **Material.** The band takes the terrain's ground material and shading (the vertex is its own heightfield point:
   no relief, no morph, pyramid level 0). Spec 26 § 2a.4 step 6 names the layer's material; `TerrainMeshLayers` carries
   none in this presentation (ADR-8291), so the ground look is the honest default for a lip of ground. A layer material
   on the band is a follow-up that needs a material slot in the band words and is not done here.
5. **Wiring and agent surface.** `TerrainHoles::request_bands` (the sync system `sync_mesh_layer_lattice` requests
   bands with the cut, so an opened mouth shows both on the same prepare), `TerrainSharedDraw::set_mouth_bands`,
   `TerrainGpu::{set_mouth_bands, mouth_bands, write_band_positions, draw_mouth_bands}`. `DrawnPass` gains `band` (the
   vertices as that pass drew them; `TerrainDrawPasses::set_band`, `clear_bands`), and `terrain.seam_report` gains
   `band_vertices`.
6. **Not drawn:** in a texture view (a probe capture) and in the precipitation occlusion tile, like grass and
   impostors. The velocity pass uses the static-world motion of the terrain (the band's own LOD re-placement between
   frames is not in its motion vectors, as the terrain's morph is not).
Tests: `tests/mesh_layer_band.rs`. `no_void_pixel_along_the_mouth`: hilly ground, a lattice-cut 12 x 20 m mouth, an
authored tube 0.8 m inside the ring and an unlit magenta plane under everything; four views from 14 to 120 m (several
levels and morphs at the ring); with the band, no magenta pixel anywhere and none within 3 px of the projected ring;
the control without the band must show the void along the ring. `band_casts_with_the_cascade_selection`: a throat shelf
(band) shadows the tube floor under a side sun (ratio to the lit floor < 0.6; the no-band control stays lit > 0.85),
and the camera's and every drawn cascade's `DrawnPass::band` equals `MouthBands::place` on that pass's own published
selection and morph eye, bit for bit; on a 230 m view whose camera then moves 6 m inside the cascade anchor, the
cascades' bands (morph 0.534 at the ring) sit up to 2.1 cm off the camera's (morph 0.346) on lavapipe, so the
cascade really draws its own placement.
Consequences: the hole words grow by the band (a 150-vertex ring with its skirt and strip is a few thousand words; 64
mouths stay well under a megabyte). Ring placement costs ring vertices x active passes per changed pass, under the
`terrain_place_bands` span. A host drawing the terrain from `terrain.wgsl` itself sees `displaced` branch on
`BAND_VERTEX_BASE`. Spec 26 § 2a.4 step 6 gains an as-built note. No file format changes.

## ADR-8824: The mouth band in every terrain pass: texture views, the precipitation tile, and a per-pass band draw count (v07-meshlayers-seam-gpu-passes; follows ADR-8569)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8569 drew the mouth band (zipper strip, skirt, throat) in the main camera's colour, depth, velocity and
decal receiver passes and in each sun cascade, but not in texture views or in the precipitation occlusion tile. A
texture view (a probe capture, mirror, screen or stereo eye; `SharedPassDraw::set_view`) drew the cut ground with no
band, so it saw the void through the mouth's ring. The precipitation tile had no band either, so rain fell through
the strip between the ring and the authored loop. The v0.7 brief asks for the band in every pass that draws terrain,
each pass proved by a test or a counter.
Decision:
- **Band cameras.** The hole words carry `BAND_CAMERAS` (2) × `BAND_PASSES` (5) position sets. Camera 0 is the
  host's main camera, camera 1 the texture view being drawn. `TerrainGpu::band_camera` is part of the per-camera
  state that `set_view` swaps (`ViewGpu`), so `write_band_positions` and `draw_mouth_bands` address the active
  camera's sets without a new parameter. Every camera's prepare places its own bands (`place_bands` no longer skips a
  texture view), on its own selection and its own cascades. Texture views take turns on camera 1. The draw keeps the
  owner of camera 1's placement and its keys, so a view whose prepare follows another view's places again. Each
  view's band writes are copied in its own `render_into` submission, before its passes, so a view never draws another
  view's placement. The shader is unchanged. Its set index already comes from the vertex index, and only its comment
  changes.
- **Precipitation tile.** `draw_precip_occlusion` draws the band with the camera's set 0, because the tile draws the
  camera's nodes. `SharedPassDraw::content_key`, which keys the tile and screen reuse, now mixes the holes
  generation. A hole or band change therefore redraws the tile. A draw that never set holes keeps its key, because
  the generation is 0.
- **Counters.** `TerrainDrawStats::band_draws` and `view_band_draws` return `BandDrawCounts` for each camera. The
  counts cover the colour, depth, velocity and receiver passes, the four cascades' full draws and page redraws, and
  the precipitation tile. A count goes up only when `draw_mouth_bands` drew. `TerrainDrawPasses::band_draws` reads
  them (`draw_passes_handle` links the draw's counters), and `terrain.seam_report` returns them as `band_draws`.
- **Not raster passes.** The ray-traced sun (ADR-2310) and the GI trace read the heightfield and the hole coverage
  words, not the drawn triangles, so the band does not cast or bounce there. This is a known issue, not a pass.
- **The band's material.** The band keeps the ground material: `TerrainMeshLayers` has no layer material, and
  giving the terrain pipelines a per-layer material is not a small change. This stays a known issue.
Consequences: the hole words double the band position sets (one more camera, a few thousand words for a 150-vertex
ring). A texture view now places bands: ring vertices × its active passes on each changed key, under the
`terrain_place_bands` span. `TerrainGpu::draw_mouth_bands` returns `bool`. `BandDrawCounts` and `BAND_CAMERAS` are new public items.
`terrain.seam_report` gains a key. No format, pipeline or warm-list change. Tests:
`no_void_pixel_along_the_mouth_in_a_texture_view`, `the_band_covers_the_precipitation_tile` and
`every_terrain_pass_draws_the_band` (regia_terrain `mesh_layer_band`), plus `seam_report_reads_the_drawn_pass`
(regia_agent, `band_draws`).

## ADR-8825: A tunnels-armed showcase scene for the D8 frame bars (v07-tunnels-showcase-scene)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Two D8 bars of the tunnels plan (sprint-tunnels-perf-low-tiers: "interior frame <= outdoors on the Deck
preset" and "ULTRA_LOW 720p30 on the N150 with tunnels armed") had no Regia scene to measure on. `do27_bench` needs
DO27 content. The only Regia frame tests of tunnels were the synthetic `tunnel_scene` test and a bore plate with no
terrain. No runtime host armed a cooked map's tunnels: the level path loads `TerrainMeshLayers` with no mouths, so
`lattice_hole_cut` is `None` outside tests, and the only headless agent host with terrain, scatter and render-out
(`showcase`) knew nothing of mesh layers. A sample cannot link `regia_asset_pipeline`, which holds the chunk LOD
cook (layer table: Pipeline sits above Sample).
Decision: Tunnels become an optional showcase feature, switched on by `tunnels/tunnels.ron` in a scene directory
(`showcase::tunnels`; a scene without the file is unchanged):
1. At load (CPU), the scene heightfield becomes the cook's ground lattice (one count a sample, from the file's
   `ground_offset_m` and `ground_step_m`). The heightfield must be square and on the counts
   (`tunnels_ground_mismatch`). `regia_world_geom::cook::cook` cooks the named mesh-layers document, the same cook
   `regia cook` runs for a level (`tunnels_cook_failed` carries its code).
2. Each cooked mouth is an open named hole (`HoleShape::lattice_rings`) and a `LayerMouth` with its rings. The
   terrain draw gets the holes and `TerrainMeshLayers::lattice_hole_cut` (ADR-8470): the drawn cut is the sim's.
   Scatter placement gets the holes.
3. The presentation section's triangles draw as one flat-shaded mesh per passage. A point light goes every
   `spacing_m` along covered tube and gallery centrelines. The cooked `VisCells` become the renderer's resource, so
   the portal cull applies to terrain and scatter.
4. `tunnels.state` and `tunnels.view` (capability `showcase_tunnels`) report what was armed and play a view of the
   scene's `perf_views.json` by name, or by `pair` and `side`.
`samples/showcase/tunnels_scene/` is generated (`showcase::tunnels_example`) from the Switchbacks passages
fixture on a flat 4096² canyon floor at -256 m. The document fills every mouth, with the ramp-facet waiver the
cook asks for (ADR-8359/8436). The views are `tube_<pair>` (inside the longest sealed run of each half of the
tube) and `outdoor_<pair>` (the same path and look direction on the plain right above), plus `mouth_drive`. The
measurement is `tests/tunnels_frames.rs`: `tunnels.view`, then a `render.out_start` job, with `play.hitch_report`
during it and the renderer's per-frame GPU pass timings read in-process. `render_ms` is wall time and is reported
only as such. Lavapipe asserts no time; a device run writes the report the D8 bars read
(`interior_over_outdoor`).
Consequences: Regia has a tunnels-armed frame scene that needs no DO27 content and no golden. The tubes draw the
presentation mesh as entities, not the chunk stream: the chunk LODs need the pipeline's chunk cook. The tube meshes
carry no `VisCell` tag, so from outdoors they are frustum-culled only. The plain is flat. The showcase sample gains
`regia_world_geom` (already in its graph through `regia_terrain`), three load codes (`ErrorCode` grows from 22 to
25), three `ShowcaseStats` fields and a `Features::tunnels` field. The shared test harness `JobSpec` gains
`place_camera` and `during`, and `Outcome` gains `during`. No engine crate, format or shader changes. Book:
`agents/showcase-tunnels.md`; `agents/showcase.md` lists the feature and codes.
Packaging: the showcase has no `Regia.toml`, so there is no `regia package` row to add. The scene directory is
packaged the way showcase scenes are: generated, byte-compared by a test, and listed in
`docs/asset-licences.toml` (Regia-made, `LicenseRef-Regia-Engine`). The cook runs at load, so the scene ships no
cooked file.

## ADR-8692: The pacer's burst floor is four packets: the `rpc_p95_with_bulk` up leg measured (amends spec 120 § 4.2 item 7, ADR-8658)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8658 left `rpc_p95_with_bulk` on congested+bulk failing 5 of seeds 1-24 (1 2 12 21 24) and put the
remaining cause on the up leg. Measured here (seeds 1 and 24, every round-trip sample, controller round and down
datagram printed by scratch overlays):
(a) The client's round trips before the transfer sit at 64 (minimum), 80, 96 and 112 ms. During the transfer 15 of
2,950 samples on seed 1 read 48 ms, every one with ack delay 0, and each lines up with a 42-byte acknowledgment-only
packet on that client's down link (ack-only packets on the four down links: 15 before the transfer, 50 during it,
because since ADR-8658 a bulk fragment waits for its whole packet's tokens and the due acknowledgment leaves alone).
On the 256 kbit/s down link a packet's serialization runs from 1.3 ms (42 B) to 37.5 ms (1,200 B), so an
acknowledgment riding alone comes back up to 36 ms sooner than one riding a snapshot or bulk packet.
(b) The 10 s minimum falls 64 -> 48 ms; the rounds' smallest samples stay at 80 ms; the threshold detector's reading
(round minimum - minimum) goes 16 -> 32 ms (p95 32 -> 48), over the 25 ms threshold, on an idle 1 Mbit/s uplink. It is
the return path's packet size, not a queue on the up leg. Client delay cuts go 19 -> 73 per ~1,000 rounds and the
target p50 28.4 -> 17.3 kB/s (850 of 1,187 rounds app-limited: each cut takes 0.85x a small delivery rate).
(c) A 4 KiB command (4 packets) then leaves 2 packets at once (the bucket's floor) and trickles out the rest at 1.25x
the target: on seed 24 its last fragment waited 272 ms at the client's pacer (tokens 189 B when first seen, target
16.7 kB/s, reading 64 ms). Leg split, seed 1: up leg p95 96 ms before the transfer, 212 ms during it; down leg p95
56 -> 80 ms.
Decision: `cc::PACING_BURST_PACKETS` goes from 2 to 4: the pacer's and the budget's buckets (and the essential
class's) hold at least four packets, so a 4 KiB reliable message an idle sender queues leaves in one poll. RFC 9002
§ 7.7 allows bursts up to the initial window (64 packets here); four is the smallest floor that passes all 24 seeds.
Nothing else moves: the target, the detectors and the wire format are unchanged, and a backlogged sender never
accumulates a full bucket, so bulk and saturating senders pace as before. The default wire's pin
(`pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical`) moves, because packets on that wire leave in
different groups: in one binary with the floor switched back to two packets (bucket depths and the essential class's
first burst) the run gives ADR-8624's hash `0x1da5_8fd9_fb37_db95` and 1,384 + 1,282 datagrams; at four,
`0x86bf_0110_1268_3c45` and 1,388 + 1,282. The pin is retaken with that proof in its doc comment.
Rejected, with numbers (one binary, scratch switches; seeds 1-104 for the bar, ADR-8534's rows):
- An app-limited round's delay overuse holds instead of cutting (the reading in (b) is a queue that sender did not
  build): bar 10 of 104 over, but listen-uplink/64 1-40 goes from 5 to 10 seeds with a second over the uplink (worst
  100.8 -> 101.9 %). Many app-limited peers do build one real queue on a shared uplink, so it is wrong. With the burst
  floor as well: 2 of 104, listen 7 over (worst 102.9 %): rejected.
- The whole reported ack delay comes off the round's smallest sample (not clamped to `MAX_ACK_DELAY_MS`): 7 of 24
  over (worse).
- The floor at four for the pacer and the budget only, the essential class's bucket left at two packets (to keep
  the wire pin): the same bar (0 of 24, 2 of 104) and the same rows, but the pin moves all the same (the pacer's floor
  binds on the clean wire too), so the split buys nothing and is not taken.
- A confirmed minimum for the delay readings (the 5th percentile of the latest 10 s of round minima, never under the
  connection's minimum) on top of the floor: seed 1's client delay cuts during the transfer 73 -> 16, queue reading
  p50 32 -> 16 ms, target p50 17.0 -> 23.5 kB/s, so it does remove most of the misreading in (a)-(b); but the bar
  moves within noise (1 of 104 at the 5th percentile, 3 at the minimum's second sample and at the 10th percentile, vs
  2), and it changes every delay reading on every path. Left to the controller's owner with these numbers.
- Burst floors of 3, 5, 6, 8 packets: bar 11 / 1 / 0 / 0 of 104 over; listen-uplink 10 / 4 / 7 / 7 seeds over (worst
  100.7 / 100.8 / 100.7 / 102.6 %). At 4: 2 of 104, listen 4 over (worst 101.0 %). The listen row moves 4-10 seeds
  between neighbouring variants with no trend, so it reads as noise around the base's 5.
Consequences: `rpc_p95_with_bulk` on congested+bulk, seeds 1-24: 5 -> 0 over 1.5x (mean ratio 1.278 -> 0.997; mean
control p95 210.7 -> 164.0 ms, transfer p95 260.0 -> 158.7 ms: commands get faster outside the transfer too); seeds
1-104: 26 -> 2 (42, 77; both faster in absolute terms than at the base, e.g. seed 42 control 288 -> 144 ms and
transfer 272 -> 240 ms; the ratio fails because the control improved more). ADR-8534's rows: seeded links 1-400 0 fail
(unchanged); congested 1-400 0 seconds over (worst 100.0 %); listen-uplink/64 1-40 4 over (base 5), worst 101.0 %
(base 100.8 %); bufferbloat+bulk 1-100 0 over (66.7 %); lossy-fat-pipe 1-100 seed 69 `random_loss_kept` as before.
Two unit tests pinned the old floor and now read the constant (`the_pacer_spreads_packets_at_one_and_a_quarter_times_the_target`,
`a_capped_connection_sends_no_first_burst_over_its_share`); their bounds are the same formulas. Spec 120 § 4.2 item 7
note added. `PACING_BURST_PACKETS` is a public constant: its value changes, its type does not.
Known issues: the delay misreading in (a)-(b) remains: on a slow return path a client's RTT-based delay detector reads
the size of the packets carrying its acknowledgments as a queue, and cuts an app-limited target. The burst floor makes
a command independent of that target; the 2 seeds of 104 still over are the same mechanism with a command that meets
an emptied bucket. The fix of the measurement is a one-way delay for the threshold detector (receive timestamps,
ADR-8423, are negotiated but off by default and feed only the trendline), which moves the wire.

## ADR-8858: Wire 6, part 1: the resumption ticket and the client's resume flight; ADR-8733 (3) amended for replay protection and key confirmation
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed (amends ADR-8733 (3))
Context: ADR-8733 (3) is the v0.7 design of the one-round-trip ticket resume (wire 6). Its review (lane
v06-net-soak-followups-review, finding C) found four gaps before any code existed. (a) Paragraph (iii) admits the peer
when `ResumeInit` opens, while paragraph (iv) says admission follows key confirmation (ADR-8535): a replayed
`ResumeInit` still opens under the PSK, so an implementer who follows (iii) lets a replay take a peer over, spend a
goodbye hold or move an address (review finding A again, on the new flight). (b) The strike register's "the newest
ephemeral replaces the older" is arrival order: an older captured flight that arrives later replaces the real client's
pending row, and both then wait out the row. (c) A byte-identical replay from the ticket's block skips the cookie and
is charged `ee` and `handshakes_per_ip_per_s` each time. (d) The ticket is stateless and still opens after a
successful resume; the only spend was the strike register, which had no eviction rule, so "single use" needs state that
outlives the register row: a peer epoch inside the ticket. The lead's brief (11-20) has this lane write the amendment
before it changes the wire, then build part 1 of 3: the ticket, the client flight and the wire step. The server's
admission and its replay register are lane v07-wire6-resume-server's.
Decision: **A. The amended clause.** ADR-8733 (3) stands except where A1-A8 say otherwise.
A1 **Nothing is admitted on `ResumeInit`** (replaces "(iii) ... it admits ... and answers `ResumeReply`"). A
`ResumeInit` that passes every check makes one *pending resume*: the finished `Noise_NNpsk0` responder state (the link
keys), the stored `ResumeReply` bytes and a fresh session token. It installs no peer, takes over no connection, moves no
address, spends no goodbye hold, retires no ticket and emits no event. The server admits (dormant or live takeover, or
ADR-8733 (1)'s held slot, by the rules of spec 120 § 10.3) only when the first sealed record under the pending link's
keys arrives: only the holder of that flight's ephemeral private key can seal it (key confirmation, ADR-8535). An
admission that fails then (full, per-address cap, banned) is answered with a sealed `Disconnect` on the pending link,
and nothing else changes. A pending resume lives `PENDING_TTL_MS`, like a half-open key exchange.
A2 **The peer epoch makes a ticket single use without per-ticket state** (replaces "(iv) ... the ticket is spent
when ..."). Every peer (live or dormant) carries two counters: `confirmed`, the epoch of the newest accept its client
proved it holds, and `minted`, the epoch of the newest ticket the server sealed for it. A resumption ticket carries the
epoch it was minted at; every accept (the join's, each `ResumeReply`'s) mints `minted + 1`. A ticket is good while
`confirmed <= epoch <= minted`. The client's first sealed record on a connection confirms that connection's accept:
`confirmed` becomes its epoch, and every older ticket is dead from every address for good (`resume_epoch`), with no row
to evict. Until then the older ticket and the newer one both name the peer, which is ADR-8535's rule (a ticket is spent
when the client proves it holds the newer one) and ADR-8623's chain, at a cost of eight bytes per peer. A goodbye's
ticket names no peer: it is good while its address hold exists (ADR-8733 (1)), and the hold is spent at the key
confirmation of A1, never earlier.
A3 **The register orders flights by the client's own count, never by arrival** (replaces "the newest ephemeral replaces
the older"). The first payload field of Noise message 1 is a 32-bit flight number, authenticated by the PSK; a client
raises it for every flight it makes with one credential. Per ticket id the register keeps the highest flight number it
has seen and at most two pending resumes. A flight above the highest takes a free row, or replaces the row with the
lower flight number (the client abandoned that flight when it made the next). A flight at or below the highest that
matches no pending row is a replay of an older flight: dropped with no answer, no `ee`, no charge. So an older flight
that arrives late never replaces a newer one, and a replayer, who cannot raise the number without the PSK, never moves
the real client's row.
A4 **A byte-identical replay costs nothing twice.** A `ResumeInit` whose Noise message equals a pending row's, byte for
byte, gets that row's stored `ResumeReply` again (a lost reply), drawn from the pre-proof answer budget like a
`Challenge`: no AEAD beyond the ticket's, no `ee`, no charge to `handshakes_per_ip_per_s` or `max_handshakes_per_s`. Once
the row has lapsed the flight is at or below the highest number (A3) and is dropped. `ee` and the two handshake budgets
are charged once per distinct flight, and only a holder of the PSK makes a distinct flight.
A5 **The register's bound and its only two exits.** At most `max_peers` x 8 ticket rows (unchanged). A row leaves when
its resume is confirmed (A2 has made the ticket dead by then) or when its ticket expires; never to make room. When the
register is full a new ticket's flight is refused to the full handshake (`resume_busy`): the bound fails closed to the
three-round-trip path, never to a replayable state.
A6 **Three packet kinds, not two.** `ResumeInit` = 11, `ResumeReply` = 12, `ResumeRetry` = 13. ADR-8733 (3) answered
both "this ticket is dead" and "prove your address" with a `Challenge`, which the client cannot tell apart, so a dead
ticket would cost a fourth round trip. Now: a refused resume (any `resume_*` code but `resume_other_block`) is answered
with a plain `Challenge` for the same client nonce, and the client carries on with the full handshake from it, in the
same three round trips as a fresh join (`ResumeInit` carries everything a `ConnectRequest` does, the version stamp
included). A source outside the ticket's block is answered `ResumeRetry` (the nonce and a cookie, 29 bytes) and the
client resends the same `ResumeInit` with the cookie: two round trips. The cookie is not in the Noise prologue, so the
resend is the same Noise message and the same flight. A `ResumeInit` whose PSK does not open message 1 still gets no
answer.
A7 **The PSK's source, and where the `Accept` rides.** `snow` exposes the handshake hash and the two transport keys
of a finished handshake, not the chaining key. The PSK is `blake3::derive_key("regia resume psk", handshake hash ||
initiator-to-responder key || responder-to-initiator key)`: the same secret inputs (the split keys are the chaining
key's only outputs), one-way, so the PSK reveals no transport key. A resumed link derives its next PSK the same way, from
its own `ee`, so a PSK that leaked does not give the next one. That makes "message 2 whose payload is the `Accept`"
(ADR-8733 (3)(iii)) circular: the `Accept`'s new ticket seals the next PSK, which depends on the hash of message 2,
which covers its payload. So message 2 (`e, ee`) carries the session token only, as `KeyReply`'s message does, and the
`Accept` follows it in the same datagram as an ordinary sealed `Accept` record under the new link's keys. One datagram,
one round trip, and the PSK is still never sent.
A8 **The client's fallbacks** (new; ADR-8733 (3) named none). A wire 5 server drops kind 11 as foreign, and a path may
drop a 1,200-byte datagram that passes a 256-byte one. After three `ResumeInit` sends without any answer the client
also sends its `ConnectRequest` with every resend, so an old server answers the documented `protocol_mismatch` deny
with its version stamp (spec 120 § 12.2) instead of nothing. After a `Challenge` the client stops resending
`ResumeInit` but keeps the flight until the full handshake has its own keys: a `ResumeReply` that still opens wins.
**B. Built in this lane (wire 6, part 1 of 3).** `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` 5 -> 6: the one wire step of v0.7 (owner
11-19); later v0.7 lanes add to wire 6 before the 11-28 freeze.
B1 `regia_net::crypto::resume`: the resumption ticket, 142 bytes: version, key id, a 16-byte nonce, and the AEAD
(`ChaChaPoly`, through `snow`'s cipher) of 105 bytes of claims {peer id, epoch, PSK, address block, issue and expiry
times on the server's clock, protocol id, a hash of the build id, password-verified, the 16-byte resume ticket's id}.
Each ticket is sealed under its own key, `blake3` keyed with the ticket key over the version, the key id and the nonce,
so a changed header reaches another key and fails the tag, and no nonce is ever reused under one key. `TicketKeys` is
stateless: key id = `now_ms / resume_grace_ms` + 1, the key a keyed hash of the server secret and the id; the current id
and the one before it open (a ticket lives one grace, so a key outlives every ticket it sealed), an older id is
`resume_key_retired`, a newer one `resume_key_unknown`. Refusals, each with its own lowercase code (`ResumeRefusal`):
`resume_malformed`, `resume_key_retired`, `resume_key_unknown`, `resume_ticket_auth` (another server's key, or a
changed byte), `resume_expired`, `resume_protocol`, `resume_epoch`, `resume_other_block`, `resume_psk`, `resume_no_peer`,
`resume_busy`, `resume_unavailable`. `ResumeEpochs` is A2's pair of counters.
B2 `Accept` carries `resumption: Option<[u8; 142]>` after the resume ticket (a flag byte, then the ticket). The server
mints one in every sealed accept when `resume_grace_ms` is above 0; a plain link has no PSK and gets none. The peer's
epochs travel with it through dormancy and takeover, and its first authenticated packet confirms its accept's epoch.
B3 The client flight: `ResumeFlight` (`Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s`; prologue = a `blake3` derive-key hash of
the protocol id, the client nonce, the suite version and the ticket), `ResumeInit` padded to 1,200 bytes
(`RESUME_INIT_BYTES`; a shorter one is refused undecoded), payload `ResumeHello` {flight, name, role, build, join data}:
no input, no reliable message, no password proof (no 0-RTT data). `ResumeReply` = the client nonce, message 2
(`e, ee`, payload: the session token) and the sealed `Accept` record (A7). `ClientConfig::resumption` (a `ResumeCredential`: ticket, PSK and a
flight counter shared by every clone; never serialized) starts a connect with the flight; `NetClient::resumption`
returns the credential of the last accept. The client follows A6 and A8 and is `Connected` when `ResumeReply` opens;
its next flush sends a sealed record (the key confirmation of A1).
B4 The server side of this lane is the codec (`ResumeInit::decode`, `ResumeReply`, `ResumeRetry`, `open_ticket`,
`ResumeResponder`) and a stub: `NetServer` decodes a `ResumeInit`, answers a protocol mismatch with the stamped deny,
and refuses every other one with `resume_unavailable` (a `Challenge`, A6), counted in
`EndpointTotals::resume_fallbacks`. A client with a credential therefore joins a part 1 server in the same three round
trips as before, through the 16-byte resume ticket in its join token. Lane v07-wire6-resume-server replaces the stub
with A1-A5. The shared port (`server_host::shared_port`) routes a `ResumeInit` by its protocol id, the stateless rule
of the `ConnectRequest` it stands in for (a resume from a new address has no route, and the session half would deny the
link's flight), and a `ResumeReply` claims the address and the token of the sealed accept it carries.
Rejected: a random 64-bit AEAD nonce under the ticket key (a birthday bound per key; the per-ticket key has none); a
counter nonce (it tells every client how many tickets the server has sealed); `resume` as a flag byte on `Challenge`
(every stored `Challenge` fixture and corpus entry would change shape for one bit; a new 29-byte kind changes none);
the caller counting flights (a caller that clones its config for every attempt would repeat a number; the credential's
shared counter cannot); admitting on `ResumeInit` and rolling back if no confirmation comes (the rollback is the bug
class of finding A).
Consequences: wire 6 refuses wire 5 at the handshake (`protocol_mismatch`, the version stamp and probe name the older
side, spec 120 § 12.2); there is no cross-wire path (§ 12.1). Host-visible API (release fragment
v0.1.28-v07-wire6-resume-ticket, Upgrade): `Accept::resumption` and `ClientConfig::resumption` (struct literals),
`PacketKind::{ResumeInit, ResumeReply, ResumeRetry}` (exhaustive matches), `EndpointTotals::{resume_inits,
resume_fallbacks}`. The owed tests of ADR-8733 (3) stay owed to the server lane, with the review's three asserts now
derivable from A1, A3 and A4: a replayed `ResumeInit` from the same and from another block installs no peer, spends no
hold and leaves the previous ticket good until the confirming sealed record; a second flight with a higher number does
not disturb the pending row of the first, and a lower one never replaces it; a byte-identical replay charges neither
`ee` nor `handshakes_per_ip_per_s` again. Still owed after part 1: `NetLink`, the reconnect timeline and the soak's
scripted rejoin present the credential (they keep the 16-byte ticket until the server admits); the asym-bufferbloat
rows stay red until then. Specs updated: spec 120 §§ 10.3, 11.4, 11.5, 12.1 (Built notes); book/agents/net-link.md,
net-trust.md, net-crypto.md, fuzzing.md; book/user-guide/networking.md; provenance rows for the ticket and the flight.

## ADR-8843: Grass, scatter impostors and water cull through the outdoor portals, for every window view (v07-interior-cull-portals)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8413 (W-22) culled the terrain nodes and the runtime scatter through the narrowed
frusta an eye inside a cell sees the outdoors by, for the frame's first window view only. v0.6.0
KI-RN-008 left grass, scatter impostors and water drawing behind the tube walls, and a second
split-screen player inside a tube culled nothing. v0.7 (DO27's switch bar, plan § 2.2 item E)
needs all of it.
Decision:
1. Per view. `cull_unreachable_cells` walks the outdoor frusta for every window view whose walk
   starts inside a cell and hits no cap, into `ExtractedFrame::outdoor_portal_views`
   (`OutdoorPortalViews`, lists kept between frames so a steady frame allocates nothing). The
   window paths (`render_windows`, `render_views_offscreen`) hand each view its own list
   (`ExtractedFrame::outdoor_portals_for`) before `render_into`. `ExtractedFrame::outdoor_portals`
   becomes the union: restricted only when every window view has a restricted list, with the first
   window view's eye. The scatter (one draw list for every view) emits through the union, as do
   hosts that draw one view through `sync_view_tables` / `render_extracted_into`.
2. Grass: after a selection, a patch whose blade box (ground rect and heights, widened by the
   class's blade headroom up and sideways) no frustum admits within `OUTDOOR_NODE_MARGIN_M` loses
   its camera blades. A shadow patch stays with the new flag `PATCH_NO_CAMERA` (4), which
   `grass_cull.wgsl` reads to skip the camera regions; other patches leave the list. The list's
   frusta hash joins the selection key, so a held camera keeps the culled list.
3. Impostors: each uploaded tile keeps a box holding every card it can draw (both the centre and
   pivot spheres at the cull's 1.1 × radius, plus `CLIFF_RELIEF_MAX_M` + 1 m in height for the
   seat). On a restricted frame the draw uploads one bit per instance slot (only when the mask
   changes) and `impostor_cull.wgsl` (new binding 5, `counts.z` flag) skips the unset slots.
4. Water: `TranslucentLayer::set_outdoor_portals` (default no-op) carries the list to the water
   layer, `FrameRenderer::set_outdoor_portals` forwards it to every translucent layer. The water
   keeps each mesh body's index range and vertex box and draws only the admitted ranges, and on the
   ring grid leaves out the chunks no frustum admits (`visible_ranges_through_into`, with or
   without the opt-in frustum cull). The underwater fog is not culled.
5. Counters: `OutdoorCullCounts` gains `grass_patches_{drawn,culled}` and
   `impostors_{kept,culled}`; `WaterFrameStats` gains `portal_restricted`, `bodies_drawn`,
   `portal_culled_bodies`, `portal_culled_ring_chunks`; `render.stats` `interior` gains `views`,
   the terrain fields and `water`. The brief named `VisCellStats`; that resource is written before
   the draws run, so the per-class counts live with the draws that produce them (the same place
   W-22's terrain counts live).
Consequences: An eye outdoors, a capped walk, no cells and `cull: false` draw exactly as before:
every new path is gated on a restricted list made for the view's eye. The impostor cull layout
gains a binding (no pipeline cache key outside the crate). New struct fields break struct literals
(release fragment, Upgrade). Updated: `book/agents/viscells.md`, spec 25 § 7.7, `book/COVERAGE.md`,
`docs/provenance.md`. The source lane's follow-up "merge coplanar quads per cell pair" stays open
(the walk cap still falls back to unrestricted).

## ADR-8855: Lockstep KI batch 3: an outvoted observer takes the majority's state; the lockstep server soaks on the real endpoints; a default-run 40-seat wander-fire row
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 notes list seven lockstep and desync known issues for v0.7 (plan v0.7-to-v1.0 § 2.2 item A, batch 3). DO27 needs lockstep most, correctness first. KI-NT-036: the dedicated server's observer (`LockstepServer`, ADR-8558), once the quorum outvotes it, left the quorum for the match (`observer.diverged`), so a later desync between two seats was a 1-1 split with no majority and no blame. KI-NT-040: the server's 40-seat soak (ADR-8656 (3)) modelled the stream lane instead of running `NetServer`/`NetClient`. KI-TD-010: the 40-seat, 600 s wander-fire lockstep test is `#[ignore]`, so no default run had 40 wander-fire seats. KI-TD-009: `cargo xtask det-scan` reported `Instant::now` and `std::thread::Builder` in the scanned lockstep module. KI-NT-038: under rollback (ADR-8361) the host holds a due frame for a live seat's input up to twice the window, so a seat whose round trip exceeds the delay plus the window (and its clock lead) made every other seat wait at its window's edge on nearly every frame. KI-NT-037 and KI-NT-039 are late-stamp, redundancy and probe issues (decided below).
Decision: (1) KI-NT-036. `LockstepObserver` gains two defaulted methods, `loads_state() -> bool` (asked once at spawn; default `false`) and `load_state(tick, &[u8]) -> bool` (default loads nothing). For an observer that loads, a `HostEvent::ResyncHost` naming a majority seat no longer takes it out of the quorum: the server records the pending transfer (`LockstepServer::observer_transfer()`); the quorum ignores the observer's votes meanwhile (its existing transfer state). The game hands the majority seat's bytes (what that seat sends for `SeatEvent::ProvideState`) to `LockstepServer::load_observer_state(tick, bytes)`. The observer thread gets one ordered message after the frames already handed to it: the state, plus the frames after `tick` the host holds (`frames_since(tick + 1)`, every frame built so far); it loads, steps them and reports its hash at `tick`, which the server passes to `LockstepHost::revote`; the quorum takes the observer back when that hash is the reference (`Quorum::recovered`). A refused load (bad bytes), a simulation that cannot load, or `HostFault` keep the v0.6 behavior: out of the quorum for the match (`diverged`). Refusals: `lockstep_observer_no_transfer` (no transfer pending for that tick), `lockstep_observer_state_too_old` (the frames after the tick are gone; the quorum orders the transfer again at its deadline). `LockstepSeatLink::observer_state(tick)` (defaulted, `None`) lets a `LockstepHostGame` deliver the bytes from its transport. Status: `ObserverStatus::resyncs`, `transfer_tick` (also in `health_json` and the console line). The soak kit's `LockSim` loads its JSON catch-up bytes. No wire change: the transfer is the game's, as for seats. (2) KI-NT-040. New `regia_net_soak/tests/lockstep_server_endpoints.rs`: the same `LockstepServer` behind a real `NetServer` and 40 real `NetClient`s on the impaired network (handshake, encryption, congestion control, reliable channel, path validation, NAT rebinding), 40 s each on `bad-wifi`, `mobile-4g`, `lockstep-mix` and `hostile` links with an off-path attacker (garbage from its own address and with seat 0's address forged). Checks: every seat connects and stays connected; in order, one hash at the common tick, no verdict, observer voting; frames on the clock from the start; nothing refused either way; no seat marked lagging; seat provenance; a seat whose game goes quiet with its connection up is removed by `TimeoutPolicy`, never early; the attacker moves nothing. The modelled-stream file stays: its hostile seat hands the server another seat's plaintext payloads, which the authenticated transport never lets through, so it is the only place the lockstep layer's own seat provenance is exercised. (3) KI-TD-010. `lockstep_mix_40_seats_desync_zero_1_min` runs by default: the same profile, seed, 40 seats, wander-fire mix and checks as the ten-minute run, over 3,600 ticks (65 s of virtual clock, the same 5 s start slack); the ten-minute run stays the ignored evidence run and the gate row is unchanged. (4) KI-NT-038. Under rollback the host computes each seat's median arrival margin against the frame clock over the feedback window (`InputArrivals::margin_p50_at`, the same samples its `LinkFeedback` reports; integers, no side effects) before it decides a hold. With at least 30 arrivals (half a second) and a median more than the window late, the seat is `hold_released`: the host builds due frames without holding them for it, and its inputs that come after their frame are merged late as any late input is. It is held for again once its median margin is two ticks inside the window. A seat that is late only now and then (jitter, a loss run) keeps the full GGPO hold of ADR-8361; only a seat whose median input the hold could not bring in is released, so it alone pays for its link. `SeatLockstepStatus::hold_released` (serde default) shows it in `net.lockstep`. `LockstepConfig::release_slow_seat_hold` (default `true`, serde default) turns it off for a game that wants every seat to wait for the slowest (a 1v1 game may); `the_host_holds_a_frame_for_a_live_seats_input_up_to_twice_the_window` sets it `false` and keeps testing the pure two-window hold of ADR-8361 with every assertion as it was (with the release on, its 200 ms seat is released after about a second and 84 instead of over 100 frames wait in its 3 s run: that count was the KI-NT-038 behavior). Strict mode is unchanged (its hold is `late_grace_ms`, at most a tick). (5) KI-TD-009 was fixed on the v0.6 line by ADR-8656 (the server moved to `crates/regia_net/src/lockstep_server.rs`, outside the scanned directory); this lane reran `cargo xtask det-scan` (report table) and changed nothing in the scanned module for it.
Consequences: host-visible API (release fragment, Upgrade): `ObserverStatus` gains `resyncs` and `transfer_tick` (struct literals break; it derives `Default`); `LockstepServerError` gains `ObserverNoTransfer` and `ObserverStateTooOld` (exhaustive matches break); `LockstepObserver` and `LockstepSeatLink` gain defaulted methods (no implementer breaks); new `LockstepServer::load_observer_state` and `observer_transfer`; `/health` and `server.lockstep_status` observer objects gain `resyncs` and `transfer_tick`; `LockstepConfig` gains `release_slow_seat_hold` (every in-tree literal uses `..`; a literal without it breaks); `SeatLockstepStatus` gains `hold_released` (struct literals break; `net.lockstep` seat rows, the agent schema string and `docs/api-snapshots/agent-protocol.txt` gain it). Under rollback a released seat's inputs land later than it sampled them (merged late), so its own confirmed state rolls back more often; the other seats stop waiting for it. An observer under transfer still steps live frames (its hashes are ignored until it recovers); the host's per-tick hash ring for the probe keeps the observer's diverged hashes between the transfer tick and the load (diagnosis only). Specs: spec 120 § 7.1 Built note; book `agents/net-lockstep-server.md`.
Decided, not built: KI-NT-037: interleaved redundancy repairs some loss runs a tick later than `Adaptive` by design (ADR-8209 traded that tick for upload, and the 40-seat upload bar depends on it); a client that delays every packet cannot be told from a slow uplink by timing alone, and under `Shared` it can raise the frame delay up to `max_delay_ticks` (the bound); `desync_zero` gating waits for the owner's net-soak gate row switch (`GATE_ROW_ENABLED`), which this lane must not move. KI-NT-038 follow-up, not built: a per-seat lead under rollback (the released seat stamps further ahead, as `DelayPolicy::PerSeat` does in strict mode) would let its inputs land on time at the cost of its own input delay; it needs the `RollbackRunner` to predict its own input at the stamped tick. KI-NT-039: naming the subsystem only when two agreeing references' rows agree needs a second reference in the probe and a "disputed" outcome in `DesyncReport`, which `*.desync.ron` v1 carries: a format-batch-2 item (bump, migrator, corpus) for the 11-28 freeze, not built here.
Alternatives rejected: replaying the observer from the state on the server thread (it would block the host's tick; the seats must never wait for the observer); sending the replay frames through the frame channel again (frames after the load message would be stepped twice); counting the load as a frame in `frames_stepped` (the status row means live frames); turning the transfer on for every observer (a game that cannot deliver bytes would see the transfer reordered until `HostFault`, which asks the session to migrate); for KI-NT-038, capping every seat's hold at one window (a transiently late seat would lose the GGPO wait ADR-8361 chose) and releasing on the 5th-percentile margin (one loss run would release an on-time seat).

## ADR-8841: Deterministic and presentation movement: which movement model runs on a lockstep sim
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Nothing in the specs or the book told a game which movement model belongs on a lockstep simulation and
which is presentation-only. Spec 15 § 5 offered rapier's `enhanced-determinism` flag "for lockstep games" without
evidence; spec 25 § 4 said physics "never affects the sim" for DO27's shell only; the lockstep hover page did not
mention the rapier hover craft (ADR-2301) or when to pick which. The movement-physics build-out audit (§ 2 boundary
table, gap 4.5 row 5) recommended the table below; movement-physics-12 (ADR-8511, lane
`buildout-mp-rapier-crossarch-evidence`, head 7d1095f10, not yet on the v0.7 line) measured the rigid-body row: with
`physics-cross-platform-determinism` (rapier `enhanced-determinism`), five rapier scenarios (`rapier_stack_50`,
`rapier_ramp_slide`, `rapier_chain_joints`, `rapier_kcc_course`, `rapier_ray_car`; 1200 steps at 60 Hz, a per-step hash
of every body's pose, velocity and sleep bits) hash equal on x86_64-linux, aarch64-macos and x86_64-windows (MSVC);
without the feature every scenario differs between x86-64 and aarch64 from step 0-22 (rotation bits first); the
feature changes the bits on one machine too; aarch64-android and the Steam Deck were not measured (devices
unreachable), and multibody joints, CCD, the `parallel` solver, other shapes and other joint kinds have no scenario.
Decision: (1) **The boundary.** Each movement model has a lockstep form, a rapier form, or both:

| model | lockstep side (cross-arch bits) | rapier side (same build, same arch) | on the v0.7 line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hover hull, arcade | **yes**: `regia_detsim::hover` (ADR-8079, ADR-8164), limits and worlds (ADR-8349), its host kit `hover::host` (ADR-8508), hull files (ADR-8512); goldens `hover_libm_1000`, `hover_mixed`, `hover_fleet_terrain`, `hover_bad_input` | `regia_physics::hover` ray-thruster craft (ADR-2301) for physical hover in server-authoritative or single-player games | built (both) |
| Walking character (steps, slopes, jump windows, crouch, suit or jet flight) | **yes**: the collision side is `regia_world_geom::mover::{move_disc, move_capsule}` (W-30, ADR-8323); the walker intent step is **planned** (movement-physics-09, lane `buildout-mp-det-walker`) | rapier character controller (`regia_physics::character`) with the framework state machine (`regia_framework::character`), predicted by `regia_framework::net_character` | mover built; det walker planned; rapier built |
| Wheeled and tracked ground vehicles | **yes, kinematic models only**: `regia_detsim::ground_vehicle::{tracked, wheeled}` (ADR-8551); golden `ground_vehicle_mix` | tire, drivetrain and suspension vehicles (`regia_physics::vehicle`) stay rapier-only | built (both) |
| Projectiles (gravity, drag, wind, swept hits, bounce, fuse) and aim | **yes**: `regia_detsim::projectile` and `regia_detsim::aim` (ADR-8509); golden `projectile_mix` | cosmetic shells, casings, tracers and debris arcs | built |
| Body against body contact (discs in height bands, mass ratio, ram events) | **yes**: `regia_detsim::contact` over `regia_detsim::broadphase` (ADR-8563); golden `contact_pile` | rapier contacts | built (both) |
| Rigid bodies: stacking, joints, ragdolls, cloth, destruction | **no: not promised** (decision 4) | yes: debris, ragdolls, cloth, destruction and props; presentation-only inside a lockstep game (`regia_framework::sim_bridge::presentation`, ADR-8356) | rapier built; lockstep promise: owner ruling |
| World gravity, air density, vacuum, low gravity | **yes**: `site_physics::WorldPhysics` (also `hover::WorldPhysics`; its 10 bytes go in the settings handshake), `site_physics`, `lowg`; golden `lowg_ballistic_mixed` | gravity from `LevelSettings` (spec 15 § 1) | built (both) |

Reasons: (a) a lockstep match needs the same bits on x86-64, aarch64 (Android, Apple) and the Deck in one match
(ADR-8012 A-4); the lockstep side is det-scanned and pinned by goldens per target, rapier is an external crate outside
det-scan's reach and its cross-arch result is a feature flag measured on three targets. (b) Kinematic models are what
lockstep games of most genres use for units: a few numbers per unit, hundreds to thousands per tick, easy to pin.
(c) The pure lockstep steps are also the best client-prediction models for server-authoritative games (a rollback
replays a pure function), so they are not lockstep-only.
(2) **The read rule.** A lockstep game's simulation reads only the steps and queries of the lockstep closure
(`docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`: `regia_detsim`, `regia_world_geom`, `regia_nav::det`, `regia_rules`,
`regia_net::lockstep`) and its own det-scanned code. Rapier output never feeds back: the simulation reads no rapier
pose, velocity, contact, query hit or event, no `Transform` that physics writes, and no ECS adapter state.
Presentation physics is driven from the simulation's snapshot and events, one way (spec 25 § 4 Destruction row,
generalized to any game on an authoritative sim); two clients may show different debris, and that is not a desync.
ECS adapters such as `regia_framework::det_hover` are not on the closure: a lockstep simulation calls `regia_detsim`
directly.
(3) **Server-authoritative games** may use either side. The server's simulation is the truth; rapier movement is
deterministic per build and architecture, which is what replays and prediction need on one machine.
(4) **Rigid bodies in lockstep games (owner question D-12, movement Q3).** Default, until the owner rules by
2026-12-01: **documented as not promised.** Regia does not promise rapier rigid bodies on a lockstep simulation;
rapier is presentation-only in a lockstep game. ADR-8511's measured subset (cuboid and capsule colliders, revolute
impulse joints, `move_character`, the ray-cast vehicle with the damper tire and the simple drivetrain, the feature on
every peer) is published as evidence, not as a promise: a game that puts it on its simulation does so outside Regia's
support, carries the feature setting in its content handshake, and runs its own leg on every target it ships. If the
owner rules "promised", the rigid-body row becomes "yes, the measured subset, feature on every peer", the gate runs
the feature goldens (`cargo test -p regia_physics --features physics-cross-platform-determinism --test
crossarch_golden`), the aarch64-android and Deck legs become required, and this ADR and the movement-models page
change with it.
(5) **Spec 15 § 5's flag description is corrected**: the feature makes a measured subset of rapier bit-identical
across the targets measured; it is not a lockstep promise.
(6) **Planned, not available:** the lockstep walker step (movement-physics-09), hover client prediction in the
netcode (net-sota 1306), a feel-parity test between the rapier and lockstep hover (not briefed), lockstep aircraft
beyond suit flight, and gravity vectors and volumes (not briefed).
Consequences: Games pick a model per genre from one table; agents get the rule (the simulation reads only the
closure). Nothing in the engine changes: no code, format, API or golden. Specs: 15 § 5 (the flag bullet corrected,
one paragraph), 25 § 4 (Destruction row generalized). Book: new user-guide page "Movement models"
(`book/user-guide/movement-models.md`, SUMMARY row); a pointer section at the end of "Deterministic simulation"; the
physics page's Determinism paragraph and the vehicles page's Determinism section; "Which hover?" in the lockstep hover
agent page and "Which vehicle?" in the vehicles agent page. When ADR-8511's lane merges, its physics-page section
"Lockstep and rigid bodies" must say "measured, not promised" under decision 4 until the owner rules. DO27 switch
note: none (DO27 keeps rapier presentation-only).

## ADR-8834: Pack provenance records migrate into `.meta` provenance extensions; `.meta` stays v2
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: plan row C-24 (absorb plan § 3, v0.7 "ready for the game to switch"). The owner's game keeps provenance in one
TOML record per content pack (`provenance/<pack>.toml`: `schema` 3, `pack_id`, `status`, `[[files]]` rows with path,
sha256, byte_len, origin, tool, generator, seed, created_utc, reviewer, foreign_game_file, third_party_mod_file; voice
rows add line_id, variant, text, voice, tts, take_approved_utc). Regia keeps provenance in the `.meta` provenance block
(`regia_asset::meta::Provenance`), checked by `config/provenance.ron` (ADR-2428). The game's reader
(`ir-content/src/provenance.rs`, regia-absorb-4 c9513623f) deserialized rows into a fixed struct and dropped every
