other field, so a straight port would lose the voice fields. ADR-8113, reserved for the first (blocked, never built)
run of this row, is void; this ADR replaces it.
Decision: new module `regia_asset::provenance_import` (runtime crate, next to `asset_ids`, so the agent method can live
in `regia_agent`), CLI `regia assets provenance-import RECORD... [--project DIR] [--under DIR] [--dry-run] [--json]`,
agent method `assets.provenance_import { records, under?, dry_run? }` (assets permission). The `.meta` shape does not
change: the block's existing `extensions` map (string to string) takes what the block has no field for, so `.meta`
stays v2 and this is not a format batch 2 row (no version step, corpus, fuzz target or `upgrade-project` row). Rules:
(1) built-in fields: origin; generator (`none` = no generator); created_utc; reviewer `owner` = owner, empty or
`pending` = pending, any other name = a named reviewer; tool = `hand` for the label `hand`, `generator` when a
generator is named, else `import`; a row field named `client`, `session` or `model` fills that built-in field.
(2) Extensions the import sets: `sha256` (lowercase), `byte_len`, `source_tool` (the label verbatim),
`foreign_game_file`, `third_party_mod_file`, `pack_id`, `pack_status`, `seed_signed`. (3) Signed seeds: the record
holds an i64, the block a u64. A seed of 0 or more is the block's `seed`; a negative seed leaves `seed` empty and is
kept exactly as `seed_signed` (no wrapping cast: a re-run must see the recorded value). (4) Unknown fields are kept:
every other row field becomes an extension under its own name (strings as they are; numbers, booleans, dates and
arrays as TOML writes them); every other pack-level field `x` becomes `pack_x` on each row. A field is refused
(`provenance_import_invalid`) only when it cannot be kept: its name is not an extension key (the policy's rule:
lowercase ascii, digits, `_`, 1-64 bytes), it would overwrite a key from (2) or the `pack_` prefix, or its value is a
table. (5) Duplicates: rows are grouped by destination path folded to ASCII lowercase (a case-insensitive disk holds
one file); every group of two or more is reported in `duplicates` (`path`, `records`, `identical`); identical rows
migrate once, differing ones are a `duplicate_differs` conflict. (6) Checks: the source must exist (else
`missing_source`, skipped) and match the recorded length and SHA-256 (else `byte_len_mismatch`/`hash_mismatch`); the
`.meta` must exist (else `missing_meta`, skipped: the import never mints an id or guesses an importer; import or cook
first, or `assets.ids_import`) and read (else `meta_unreadable`). (7) A `.meta` whose block equals the migrated one
is kept untouched; an empty block (absent or default) is replaced; any other block is `provenance_differs`. (8) All
or nothing: any conflict answers `provenance_import_conflict` with `data.conflicts`/`data.duplicates` and writes
nothing; writes are tmp + rename, and a `.meta` that changed since it was read is left (`meta_changed`). A second run
writes nothing and leaves the bytes (idempotent). Record `schema` 1 to 3 is read; a higher one is refused. Paths are
`/`-separated, relative, no `..`, `\`, `:` or `.meta` names; `--under` names the packs' content root inside `assets/`.
The game's allowed-tool list and owner-only reviewer rule are game policy: they are not copied; a project expresses
them in `config/provenance.ron` over `source_tool`/`reviewer`.
Consequences: a project switching from pack records runs one command and its policy, validator and cook see the
provenance; nothing is lost, so the game's own doctor can be retired after the switch. The SHA-256 is the repository's
own FIPS 180-4 code (copied from `regia_pt::sha256` into `regia_asset`, as `regia_net_soak` did). Codes:
`provenance_import_conflict`, `provenance_import_invalid`, `provenance_import_unreadable`,
`provenance_import_write_failed`. New: `regia_asset::provenance_import`, `AssetsCommand::ProvenanceImport`, agent
method `assets.provenance_import`, guide topic `provenance-import`, book page `agents/provenance-import.md`. Tests:
`regia_asset` `tests/provenance_import.rs` (`voice_row_survives_migration`,
`unknown_fields_are_kept_and_unkeepable_ones_refused`, `duplicate_row_is_reported`, `migration_is_idempotent`,
`signed_seeds_are_kept_exactly`, `conflicts_write_nothing`, ...), `regia_cli`
`assets_provenance_import::tests`, `regia_agent` `provenance_import::tests`. Specs: none changed (spec 12 § 1a already
names project extension fields).

## ADR-8900: Format batch 2 rows (v0.7): `.logic.ron` 1 → 2 (typed entity and world variables) and `.uianim.ron` 1 → 2 (frame events)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Renumbered from ADR-8832 by integ-v07a (it collided with the earlier ADR-8832, "The glyph atlas
pins the pages a UI frame draws from").
ADR-10132 renumbered it to ADR-20132 on its own branch; integ-v07-freeze folded that onto this number (ADR-10265).
Context: Two parity items waited on frozen-format steps. (1) P-177 / audit row L9 (w12-logic-debugger): the Logic Graph
panel could type and default graph locals but not entity or world variables, because `.logic.ron` v1 has no place
to declare them (entity keys live in the entity's `Blackboard`, world boards are names only). (2) w13-ui-seq-tracks
(46816e0f2) built the UI animation dope sheet but deferred frame events: `.uianim.ron` v1 has no event field and
ADR-8105 (the v0.6.0 UI format rows) has no `uianim` row. Both formats shipped v1 in v0.6.0 (`format-hashes.ron` at
02381fd90); ADR-7724 allows one version step per format per release, and format batch 2 (owner approved 11-19, freeze
Sat 11-28; `queue/staged/v07/FORMAT-BATCH-2.md`) lists both as one step to v2. No other lane has bumped either format
on the v0.7 line.
Decision: (1) **`.logic.ron` 1 → 2.** `LogicGraphDef` gains `entity_vars: [EntityVarDef { name, default }]` and
`world_vars: [WorldVarDef { board, name, default }]`, both `serde(default)` and not written when empty. A variable's
type is its default's `Literal` kind. Runtime: when a graph starts (and after a restart) each declared default is
written into the entity's `Blackboard` (added when missing) or the world board unless the key is already there, before
the `BlackboardChanged` baseline, so a seed fires no rule. Compile: names non-empty without `/`, unique (entity) or
unique per board (world), a world variable's board must be in `world:` (`unknown_scope`), finite float defaults, at
most `MAX_LOCALS` (64) each; a built-in `logic::SetBlackboard` with a literal key naming a declared variable must keep
its type (`set` of another literal kind, `increment` of a non-number, `append` to a non-string: `bad_value`). A v1
definition (file or code) is a valid v2 body: `from_ron` accepts 1 and 2 and stores 2; `logic_migration_sources()` is
`[1]`. Editor: the Variables list declares, retypes, re-defaults, renames (declaration and every reference) and removes
entity variables (scope `entity`) and world variables (scope `world`, name `<board>/<key>`; a name without `/` is the
board; declaring a variable of an undeclared board declares the board; a board rename moves its variables), one undo
step each, through the existing `editor.logic_variable_set` / `_remove` (no new method; `bad_scope` no longer refuses an
entity `Set`). New ops `LogicOp::SetEntityVar` and `LogicOp::SetWorldVar` (`editor.logic_edit` JSON `set_entity_var`,
`set_world_var`). (2) **`.uianim.ron` 1 → 2.** `UiAnimDef` gains `events: [AnimEvent { time, name, payload }]`
(`serde(default)`, not written when empty): at most 256, `time` finite in `0..=duration()`, name 1 to 256 bytes, payload
up to 256 bytes, no control characters (`AnimError::Event(index)`). `UiAnimDef::compile_events(reverse, speed)` places
each event once per pass on the playback timeline (backward passes at `duration - time`, in reverse order; times
divided by the speed), sorted; `UiAnimDef::to_tween` hands them to `UiTween::with_events`. `advance_tweens` keeps a
cursor into the sorted events and, after it moves `elapsed`, sends `UiAnimEventFired { entity, name, payload, at }` for
every event with `at <= elapsed` past the cursor (every remaining event when the tween ends): each event fires exactly
once per crossing, also when one step jumps over several (a long frame, reduced motion jumping to the end), in timeline
order and before `UiTweenFinished`; a replaced or removed tween fires no more. `record_anim_events` keeps the last 64
in `UiAnimEventLog`. Agent: `ui.play_anim` `play` uses the events, `sample` lists those a playback from 0 has crossed by
`time`, `list` counts them, new action `events { clear? }` reads the log. Editor: an event track under the dope sheet
(flags on the sheet's last row; Add event at the playhead, a row per event, time / name / payload fields, Remove
event), `AnimOp::SetEvent` / `RemoveEvent`, `editor.ui_anim_edit` ops `set_event { index?, time, event, payload? }`
and `remove_event { index }`, error `ui_anim_unknown_event`. This supplies the `uianim` row ADR-8105 lacked; it is a
v0.7 row, not a v0.6.0 one. (3) **The batch procedure for both rows** (ADR-7724 one-step rule, sprint-w11-fmt-bump-plan):
number-only migrators (`regia upgrade-project` rows `migrate_logic` and `migrate_uianim` replace `unmigrated`: the loader
checks the file, then `rewrite_ron_version` moves only the number; a uianim file without `format_version` is re-saved
at v2); corpus `logic/v2.ron` and `uianim/v2.ron` with `FROZEN.txt` lines (every v1 fixture byte-identical); fuzz
targets `logic-vars` (fixture `fuzz_targets/fixtures/logic-vars.example.ron`, the corpus copy) and `uianim-events`
(reads the corpus file); `docs/formats/logic-ron.md` and `uianim-ron.md` version sections; the spec 12 § 4a v0.7 rows;
`cargo xtask check-formats --update` for these two rows only. Older builds refuse the new files with their existing
errors: v0.6 `.logic.ron` "logic graph format_version 2 is not supported (this build reads version 1)"
(`unsupported_version`), v0.6 `.uianim.ron` "format_version 2 is newer than the supported 1".
Consequences: Projects re-cook nothing: both are source formats; a v1 file keeps loading and is rewritten only by
`regia upgrade-project --write` or an editor save. A v2 file does not load in v0.6 builds. Host code: `UiAnimDef`,
`LogicGraphDef` and `LogicGraphDoc` gain fields (struct literals break), `AnimError::Event`, `AnimOp::{SetEvent,
RemoveEvent}` and `LogicOp::{SetEntityVar, SetWorldVar}` are new variants (exhaustive matches break), `advance_tweens`
writes a new message (a world that runs it by hand needs `Messages<UiAnimEventFired>`), and `UiTween` gains `events`.
Specs updated: 12 § 4a (v0.7 rows), docs/formats/logic-ron.md, docs/formats/uianim-ron.md.

## ADR-8847: v0.6 editor smoke residue: play sessions between smoke steps, hidden mesh parts after an undo, three order-dependent editor tests
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Plan E-08 carried three v0.6.0 editor-smoke findings. (1) On the headless card runs 78 of 83 FAILs were
"the screenshot is one flat color" after `menu:Play/Players/2..4 players`: the harness stopped play only before its
keyboard pass, so the 4-player split-screen session ran through every later menu and command step, and a headless
`seeing.screenshot` during play looks through the possessed game cameras of the sample's empty level (black).
(2) `menu:Create/Shape/Cuboid` and `menu:Create/Player start` failed as a pair: "undo of 1 entry did not restore the
level", 51b7e0d6b5a3d192 → 476bcd01709251e0 and back; the leftover was a nameless entity with only a
`GlobalTransform` at the camera target and the two visibility components. (3) Three `regia_editor --lib` tests
failed in the full run and passed alone: `nav_preview::the_gather_runs_on_the_bake_worker_not_the_editor_thread`
(0 gathers counted where 1 ran) and the two `panic_trace` backtrace tests (no backtrace captured).
Decision: (1) A smoke step that is not a play control starts in edit mode: when `editor.play_state` is not
`stopped`, the harness calls `editor.stop`, waits three frames and requires `stopped` (the step's reason says it
did; a session that does not stop fails the step). Play controls keep the session (Play menu items, `play.*`
actions and commands, the `editor.play`/`pause`/`resume`/`step`/`stop`/`simulate`, `editor.play_*` and
`editor.pie_*` routes), so Pause after Play is still exercised. A play control's own flat screenshot still fails;
its reason names the play view. On an undo mismatch the step also lists every component of each entity the undo
left behind (`scene.get_entity`, unreflected ones included). (2) Cause: the edit world draws a `Primitive` or a
`MeshSource` through hidden part entities (`MeshRenderer`, `MeshPart`, `EditorHidden`, `GlobalTransform`), and the
parts of a despawned owner were swept only by the next `resolve_mesh_sources`, which runs when a viewport
renders. The headless editor renders only for a capture, so an undone Create left its part, which
`scene.serialize` lists; each later shape's capture swept the old part and left its own, and Player start (no
primitive) swept the last one, so its own undo "changed" the level the other way. `ResolvedMesh` and
`ResolvedPrimitive` now have `on_despawn` hooks that despawn the owner's parts (after the despawn in progress;
a part that is gone or belongs to another owner is skipped). (3) Each test owns its state. The nav test counted
gathers with a probe `tracing` subscriber, but callsite interest is process-wide: when the probe is the only live
dispatcher, tracing-core's single-dispatcher path lets another test thread's first hit of `nav_preview_gather`
compute its interest from that thread's default (no subscriber) and cache "never". It now reads a test-only
per-thread gather count; the span stays for profiling. `std` has no atomic way to wrap the panic hook: two
chaining installs (`take_hook` then `set_hook`) at once can lose one, with every hook it chained. The editor's
installers (the capture hook, the crash reporter's two, the PIE recorder test that runs next to `panic_trace`) now
go through `panic_trace::chain_hook` / `with_hook_lock`, which hold one lock across the pair; `install_hook` does
nothing on a panicking thread (where `std` refuses the change); the `panic_trace` tests hold that lock while they
panic, because between another installer's take and set the default hook runs alone.
Consequences: The harness no longer reports the split-screen session's view as 78 later failures, and a session
that will not stop is a finding of its own. A headless Create undo leaves the edit world as it was, without a
render. New public items: `panic_trace::{PanicHook, chain_hook, with_hook_lock}`; editor code that installs a panic
hook should use `chain_hook`. No format, agent method, permission class, CLI or dependency change. Open: whether
a headless capture during split-screen play should show the possessed game cameras (the play controls'
own shots of an empty level stay flat and fail) is for the headless-editor owner.

## ADR-8895: integ-v07a (v0.7 roll-up 1): how the W-11 edited-ground walks, the lattice pins and the guide test were combined
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Roll-up 1 of the v0.7 line merges the rules line (integ-rules-v07b), the tunnels critical path
(tunnels-perf-low-tiers with native-acceptance-suite, tunnels-stage-b-correctness, the four W-11 speed lanes,
w11-fmt-nav-cell-v3), the net critical path (net-migration-lockstep, net-hover-prediction, v07-wire6-resume-ticket,
v07-net-ki-lockstep), the P0 tunnels lanes (v07-meshlayers-seam-gpu-passes, v07-tunnels-showcase-scene) and the
DONE staged lanes. Three conflicts needed a decision, not a side:
(1) `WorldGeom::ground_node` (regia_world_geom `query_segment.rs`). w11-native-query-speed (ADR-8815) passes the
state's D1 edits down the height-pyramid walk and trusts a node's cooked range, and the plain-tile cell path, only
at a level-0 tile that no edit touches (not promoted, no override owned by it or its east, north and north-east
neighbors). w11-crater-edits (ADR-8818) keeps edited ranges per pyramid node on the state
(`GroundEdits::edited_range`) and walked the pyramid only when the state keeps them (`pyramid_bounds`).
(2) `tests/lattice_ground.rs`. tunnels-stage-b-correctness re-pinned the cooked Switchbacks/Cinder content hashes
because the cooked value moved (ADR-8898, the skylight climbs cut from the meshed layout); w11-index-build split the
pin into the version 1 layout hashes (`PINNED_V1_HASHES`, the value) and the v2 layout hashes (`PINNED_HASHES`, the
format's new hash definition) with the v0.6.0 value.
(3) The game-modes guide. The rules line's playlist-rotation section put a `.playlist.ron` example in a ```ron
block, and editor-authoring's guide test parses every ```ron block with `format_version` as a rule set.
Decision: (1) Both: an untouched level-0 tile keeps the cooked range and the plain-cell path (ADR-8815); every other
node of an edited state is bounded by the state's own edited range when it keeps them (ADR-8818), at every level;
without ranges the node is walked unbounded, as ADR-8815 does. The ADR-8662 under-range return and the
`GROUND_SKIP_MARGIN_M` slab cut apply to whichever range bounds the node. The walk is no longer gated on
`pyramid_bounds` (the bound is per node). Both lanes' bit-equivalence tests (the fast walk against
`segment_in_full_order` on edited states) are the proof. (2) `PINNED_V1_HASHES` takes stage-b's re-pin (the cooked
value moved); `PINNED_HASHES` (v2 layout) is re-pinned to the combined cook's measured value, both changes being
intended. (3) The rule-set test skips a block with the playlist's required `entries` list (the six rule-set ids it
checks are unchanged), and regia_net `formats::tests::the_playlist_in_the_game_modes_guide_loads` parses every such
block with `PlaylistFile::from_ron`.
Also on this line: four lane ADRs collided with older ADRs of the same number and were renumbered from
`queue/adr-counter` with every reference the lanes added (ADR-8730 playlist rotation -> ADR-8897, ADR-8810 Stage B
correctness -> ADR-8898, ADR-8811 nav cell v3 -> ADR-8899, ADR-8832 format batch 2 logic/uianim -> ADR-8900), and
`docs/decisions.md` was rebuilt with one copy of each ADR the merges had appended several times.
Consequences: an edited state's segment and sight-line walk skips more of the pyramid than either lane alone; the
`mixed_calls` bench's edited-state rows measure the combination. No format, API or agent-surface change of its own.
Updated: spec 121 and `docs/perf-log.md` keep both lanes' measurement rounds.

## ADR-8902: Wire 6, part 2: the server admits a one-round-trip resume at key confirmation; the pending-resume register
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8858 amended ADR-8733 (3) and built the ticket, the client flight and a server stub that refused every
`ResumeInit` to the full handshake. This lane (v07-wire6-resume-server, part 2 of 3) replaces the stub with A1-A5. Four
things the amendment left to the implementation had to be decided, and one line of the lane's brief reads differently
from the amendment. (a) A goodbye's return is a new `PeerId` (ADR-8733 (1)), but the `Accept` inside `ResumeReply` names
the peer id, and A1 forbids installing a peer before the confirmation. (b) What names a ticket in the register. (c) Which
address the confirming record may come from. (d) `admit` mints the accept's tickets and sends the accept; a resume's
accept is with the client before `admit` runs. (e) The brief asks that "a third pending resume is refused"; A3 says a
flight above the highest replaces the row with the lower flight number.
Decision: **1. Order of the checks on `ResumeInit`** (`NetServer::on_resume_init`), cheapest first, nothing admitted:
decode (1,200 bytes or refused unread); the protocol id (`resume_protocol`: the stamped `protocol_mismatch` deny); the
server can resume at all (not closing, `resume_grace_ms` above 0, an identity, the suite version: `resume_unavailable`);
the ticket opens (one AEAD: `resume_key_retired`, `resume_key_unknown`, `resume_ticket_auth`, `resume_expired`,
`resume_malformed`); the address: inside the ticket's block, or the cookie of a `ResumeRetry` verifies, else `ResumeRetry`
(`resume_other_block`, 29 bytes, from the pre-proof answer budget; the cookie that comes back proves and refunds that
answer as a `KeyInit`'s does, ADR-8764); the ban list (`resume_unavailable`: the full handshake says `banned` after its
cookie); **a byte-identical copy of a pending flight gets the stored `ResumeReply`** from the pre-proof answer budget and
nothing else (A4: no AEAD beyond the ticket's, no `ee`, no handshake charge; `resume_replays`); message 1 opens under the
ticket's PSK (one AEAD; a failure is `resume_psk` and gets no answer); the hello agrees with the ticket and the server
(protocol id and build hash `resume_protocol`, a password the ticket does not vouch for `resume_unavailable`, join data
that does not decode or validate `resume_malformed`: the full handshake's deny carries the reason); the ticket still
names something (below); the flight's number against the register (A3: at or below the highest and matching no row is
`resume_stale_flight`, no answer; a new ticket with the register full is `resume_busy`); the handshake budgets, charged
once per distinct flight (`handshakes_per_ip_per_s` through both per-address limiters a full handshake passes, and
`max_handshakes_per_s`; over either is `resume_busy`); and only then the curve work, `ResumeResponder::reply` (the `ee`).
**2. Who a ticket names.** The peer whose 16-byte ticket chain holds the ticket's `resume_id` (`ticket_owner`: newest or
unconfirmed, ADR-8535/8623) when that peer is the ticket's `peer` and the ticket's epoch is inside the peer's window (A2,
else `resume_epoch`); otherwise the goodbye hold of `resume_id` when the flight comes from the hold's own block
(ADR-8733 (1); from another block it is no return, as ADR-8883 rules for the full handshake); otherwise `resume_epoch`
when the ticket's peer exists and its epoch is outside the window (the precise code for a spent ticket), else
`resume_no_peer`. **3. The peer id of a goodbye's return** is issued when the flight is answered
(`Session::issue_id`: the next id of the counter, with no peer added and no slot taken) and the peer joins under it at
the confirmation (`Session::add_peer_as`). An id issued and never confirmed is skipped until the counter comes round,
like the id of a peer that left; only a holder of the PSK can cause one, each costs a charged handshake, and
`add_peer_as` refuses an id that is live by then. This keeps A1 (no peer, no slot, no event before the confirmation)
with an accept that already names its peer. Rejected: giving the return its old id (ADR-8733 (1) makes it a new peer in
the full handshake; two paths must not disagree); a second accept after the confirmation (a second round trip).
**4. Minting is not admission.** Answering a flight mints the next 16-byte ticket and the resumption ticket of the peer's
next epoch (A2: `minted` goes up by one per answered flight; `confirmed` and every ticket the client holds are
untouched) and seals the accept under the new link (A7). They are stored in the pending row and installed by `admit`
when the resume is confirmed; `admit` gained a third path (`JoinPath::Resume`) that brings its own link, tickets and
epoch, skips the per-address join charge and the password proof (both settled when the flight was answered), sends no
second accept, and refuses with a sealed `Disconnect` on the pending link, three copies like any goodbye (`full` is
`server_full`, `banned` is `banned`, closing is `server_shutdown`, anything else `protocol_error`). **A pending resume is
admitted as what it was answered for or not at all:** the same peer with the ticket's epoch still inside the window
(another resume confirmed since makes it `resume_epoch`), or the held slot from its own block (`resume_no_peer` once
spent); it never becomes a fresh join. Every other rule of the join is the one path every join takes: the live-peer
check, the per-address cap with the resumed peer or the held slot excluded, capacity, the store-ticket hook, the
takeover, the events (`PeerResumed`, or `PeerJoined` for a goodbye's return) and the counters (`resumes`,
`resume_takeovers`, `held_slot_returns`). The hold is spent inside that admission, which is the key confirmation: this
is ADR-8883's rule (spent only after confirm) by construction on this path, and it composes with ADR-8883's claim on
the full handshake's path (the claim is taken and spent by the same record here).
**5. The confirmation** (`NetServer::on_resume_confirm`): a sealed record whose session token is a pending resume's and
which opens under that link. A record that fails its tag changes nothing. It must come from the address the flight
proved (same canonical IP; the port may differ, as for a pending handshake's join) or from inside the ticket's own
block; any other source is counted in `rebinds_refused` and ignored, because an authentic record copied to another
address proves nothing about that address (RFC 9000 § 9.3). A `Payload` record admits and is then delivered as the peer's
first packet (which confirms the accept's epoch and the ticket chain as on every connection); a `Disconnect` drops the
pending resume (the client left before it was a peer); any other kind is counted malformed and drops it.
**6. The register** (`regia_net::resume_register`, crate-private). Keyed by the ticket's key id and nonce (bytes 1..21:
chosen by this server, unique per sealed ticket, covered by the ticket's key derivation and tag), so two tickets of one
peer have two rows. Per row: the highest flight number seen, the ticket's expiry, at most two pending resumes. At most
`max_peers` x 8 rows (at least 8). A row leaves when a resume of its ticket is confirmed (with its other pending
flight) or when its ticket expires; a pending resume lapses after `PENDING_TTL_MS` and its row stays, so a lapsed
flight played again is stale. A session-token index finds the pending resume of a confirming record in one probe.
**7. "A third pending resume is refused" is A3's replacement**, not a `resume_busy` for the newest flight. With two
pending, a flight above the highest takes the place of the lower one; the one refused is that lower flight: its stored
reply is gone, its bytes get no answer (`resume_stale_flight`), and its client, even if it heard its reply, is not
admitted (its record finds no pending link). Refusing the newest instead would send an honest client whose two earlier
replies were lost to the three-round-trip path for the rest of `PENDING_TTL_MS`, on exactly the paths this resume
exists for, and it would not bound anything the replacement does not: only the PSK's holder raises the number.
**8. Status.** `EndpointTotals::{resumed_one_rtt, resume_replays, resume_lapsed}`; `NetStatus::resume_refusals`, a map
from the lowercase refusal code to its count (absent from the JSON while empty), which also counts a resume refused at
its confirmation; `NetServer::{resume_refusals, pending_resumes}`; `ResumeRefusal::StaleFlight`
(`resume_stale_flight`), the thirteenth code, and `ResumeRefusal::index`. The client counts `resumed_one_rtt` too.
`resume_fallbacks` keeps its meaning (flights answered with a `Challenge` or a deny); a `ResumeRetry` and an unanswered
flight are not fallbacks.
Consequences: a client that presents its credential to a server that keeps tickets is connected after one round trip
(two from another block) as the same peer, or as the held slot's new peer, and nothing a replayer can send before the
client's own confirmation changes the server's peers, addresses, holds or tickets. Measured on the impaired in-process
network over `asym-bufferbloat` (four seeds, virtual time, `regia_net_soak` test `resume_one_rtt`): the resume connects
inside the 3,000 ms reconnect grace after one flight and one pass of the path's 1 s queue (the client sends the flight
again while its answer waits in the queue, and each copy gets the stored reply: A4 at work on an honest client); the
same rejoin without the credential takes three round trips and misses it (3,140 ms at the gate seed). Host-visible API (release fragment v0.1.28-v07-wire6-resume-server, Upgrade): three `EndpointTotals` fields
and one `NetStatus` field (struct literals), `ResumeRefusal::StaleFlight` (exhaustive matches; `ResumeRefusal::ALL` is
13 long), `Session::issue_id`. No wire change beyond wire 6 as ADR-8858 made it: no packet shape moved. Behavior: a
server with `resume_grace_ms` above 0 now answers `ResumeInit` with `ResumeReply`; part 1's `resume_unavailable` for
every flight is gone, and the part 1 test that pinned it now pins a refusal that still exists (`resume_expired`).
Still owed (part 3): `NetLink`, the reconnect timeline, `NetSession` and the soak's scripted rejoin present the
credential, and the soak's `asym-bufferbloat` server keeps tickets; until then the two `reconnect_within_grace` rows of
the gate plan stay red although the engine path they need exists. **Measured, not shipped:** this lane ran that soak
change as an experiment (the scripted rejoin presents the credential; the profile's server keeps tickets for 60 s, as
the `cgnat` profile's does) over `asym-bufferbloat` at 8 and 32 clients on six seeds. All 12 rows' scripted rejoins were
one-round-trip resumes of the held slot, connected 1,040 ms after the link was up (1,280 ms in three rows), inside the
3,000 ms grace. But 3 of the 12 rows then lost one client to `reassembly_stalled` (a reliable fragment from the server
that did not arrive inside the stall ceiling of spec 120 § 5.2), and in two of those rows it was a client that never
left or resumed; the gate seed's 8-client row was one of the three, so that row would trade one red bar for another.
That failure is not on the resume path. It has to be understood (the profile's drop-tail queue against the reliable
stream's retransmission and stall clocks, once joins and leaves come closer together) before the soak's scenario
changes, so the change is left to part 3 with the patch and the per-seed log in the lane's report. Not merged here: lane v061-net-fixes-c (ADR-8883,
the hold claim on the full handshake's path) was unbuilt work in progress when this lane ran; its tests
`a_lost_accept_retry_of_a_held_slot_ticket_is_the_same_peer` and `a_forged_ticket_does_not_spend_or_skip_the_hold` run
on plain loopback links, which carry no resumption ticket, so this lane's path does not reach them. Specs updated: spec
120 §§ 10.3, 11.4, 11.5 (Built notes); book/agents/net-link.md, net-trust.md; book/user-guide/networking.md; a
provenance row for the register and the admission.

## ADR-10051: The client's version ring holds an `rtt-extreme` round trip and lets go below the named baseline (wire 6)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: KI-NT-009, ADR-8419's known issue. On the state channel (spec 72 § 4) a client keeps the last versions of each
entity so the server can send a delta against the one the client acknowledged, and the server falls back to a full record
when that baseline is `STATE_VERSION_RING` versions behind. The ring was 64. For an entity that changes every tick the
acknowledged baseline is one round trip of versions behind, so above a 64-tick round trip (1.07 s at 60 Hz, 500 ms at
128 Hz) every baseline expired as its acknowledgment arrived and every record went as a full state. Spec 120 § 15.1's
`high-rtt` profile (650 ms) is 83 ticks at 128 Hz; `rtt-extreme` (1,500 ms one way, 20 % loss) is 180 ticks at 60 Hz and
384 at 128 Hz. Full records are several times a delta, so the peer the engine promises never to drop for ping was the one
whose budget went on repeating state it already had (at the 4,096 B/s minimum rate it starved). The constant is part of
the protocol (the server reads it as what the client still holds), so it moves only with the wire version; v0.7 opens
wire 6 (ADR-8858).
Decision: (1) `STATE_VERSION_RING` = 512 inside wire 6. Sizing: the worst profile round trip at the fastest tick the
engine's tests run is 384 versions (`rtt-extreme` at 128 Hz); a 20 % loss delays an acknowledgment by a tick per lost
frame (five in a row is 0.03 %), jitter and the hop ticks add a few more. 512 leaves 128 versions above that and holds a
round trip of 4 s at 128 Hz, 8.5 s at 60 Hz and 17 s at 30 Hz. The server's expiry test is unchanged
(`number - base_number >= STATE_VERSION_RING`), and so is every byte on the wire: `base_ago` already had the varint form
for distances over 32. (2) A fixed 512 would cost every client eight times the memory for entities that change every
tick, whatever its round trip, so the client no longer stores by count alone. The server's baseline for an entity only
moves forward (`apply_state_ack` replaces it only with a newer version), so once a frame names baseline `b`, every frame
sent after it names `b` or newer, and versions older than `b` are needed only by frames sent earlier and still on their
way. The client remembers `(frame tick, b)` and, when a frame of that entity at least `STATE_BASE_REORDER_TICKS` (8)
newer arrives, lets go of everything older than `b` (`EntityRing::note_named`). A ring therefore holds one round trip of
versions plus those of 8 to 16 ticks, and the count cap of 512 only bounds a client whose acknowledgments do not arrive. (3) A frame
reordered by more than the margin can name a version let go since. Its record is dropped and the frame is taken back
from the acknowledgment (`StateAcks::forget`), so it reads as lost: acknowledged, its versions could become the server's
baseline although this client could not decode them. No resync is asked (the copy has newer state). Every late frame
(older than the newest that carried the entity) naming a version the client does not hold takes this path
(counted by `ClientStateChannel::retired_baselines`), whether the version went below the floor or with a resync that cleared the
ring; a missing baseline in the newest frame is still a real loss of state and asks for the full state as before
(`baseline_missing`). (4) Surfaces: `ClientStateChannel::{stored_bytes, longest_ring}`,
`ClientStateChannel::retired_baselines`; `net.state_channel` on a client gains `version_ring`, `longest_ring`,
`version_bytes_stored` and `records_retired_baseline`.
Rejected: a fixed 512 without (2) (memory, below); a ring sized from the measured round trip and told to the server
(a wire field and a second place for the two ends to disagree; the named baseline already tells the client what the
server can still use); time-based expiry on the client (the server counts versions, not ticks); a margin of 0 (the
`high-rtt` profile's 20 ms jitter swaps neighboring frames at 60 Hz, and each swap would take a frame back); asking for
a resync when a late frame names a version let go (a path change that delivers a second of old frames late would ask for
the full state of every moving entity, three times in five seconds reads as a resync loop).
Memory per client: a stored version is 192 bytes plus its component list (16 bytes and 24 per component); the
component values are shared with the version it was decoded against unless they changed
(`ClientStateChannel::stored_bytes`). An entity that changes every tick stores one round trip of the versions sent to it plus those of 8 to 16
ticks and a few for late acknowledgments. Measured on the timed harness (60 Hz, the default send every second tick, 24
entities that change every tick; `regia_net_soak` tests/state_ring.rs): 9 to 10 versions per entity on a 12 ms path,
24 to 30 on `high-rtt` (470 and 670 ms), 87 to 90 on the `rtt-extreme` peer (3,000 ms), where the base stored 64 on
every path. For 500 such entities with three components each (280 bytes a version) that is 1.4 MB, 4.2 MB and 12.6 MB,
against 9.0 MB flat with the old 64 and 71.7 MB flat for a fixed 512. Sending every tick doubles the three figures. An entity that
does not change stores one version, as before.
Consequences: wire 6 only (a wire 5 peer is refused at the handshake, ADR-8858; there is no cross-wire path). No frame
layout changed, so recordings replay: a recorder connection acknowledges every frame, its baselines are one version
back. Host-visible API (release fragment v0.1.28-v07-net-state-ring-reorder): `STATE_VERSION_RING` changes value; `STATE_BASE_REORDER_TICKS`,
`StateAcks::forget` and `ClientStateChannel::{stored_bytes, longest_ring, retired_baselines}` are new (additive; no
struct or enum changed shape). Behavior: a round trip of up to 512
versions keeps deltas; a frame more than 8 ticks late that names a version let go counts as lost (its other records are
applied but sent again). Known limits: above 512 versions of round trip the baselines still expire (full records, as
before above 64); the margin is in ticks, so at 30 Hz it is 267 ms and at 128 Hz 62 ms. R1 (spec 120 § 8.1, the
standalone `SnapshotEncoder`) was found already built by N108 (ADR-7983); this lane's audit of it is in the lane report.
Specs updated: spec 120 § 8.1 (Built note); book/agents/net-state-channel.md, book/user-guide/networking.md; one
provenance row.

## ADR-8859: A foreground message's burst is the message's; an overuse cut reads the latest second; the stall deadline stat carries its bound (amends spec 120 § 4.2 items 2 and 7, ADR-8692, ADR-8658)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: lane v07-net-rpc-p95-up-leg, on the v0.6.0 tag with v06-net-soak-followups, net-rpc-p95-up-leg (ADR-8692),
v06-net-review-fixes and v06-security-gaps-fixes merged. ADR-8692 left `rpc_p95_with_bulk` on congested+bulk over the
bar on 2 of seeds 1-104 (42, 77). Over seeds 1-1000 the merged base is over on 34 (3.4 %): 42 and 77 are the two that
fall inside 1-104, not two special seeds. The bar compares the second-largest of about 39 command round trips with
1.5x the second-largest of about 34, so it fails whenever two commands of the transfer window are slow. Measured (seeds
42, 77 and 640; every fragment's wait at the sender, every controller round and both legs of every command printed by
scratch overlays):
(a) The up leg: the pacing bucket's burst is what the bucket has left. Seed 42's two slow commands (400 and 240 ms)
met a bucket holding 536 and 1,032 of its 4,800 bytes at targets of 20.6 and 15.1 kB/s; their last fragments waited
304 and 128 ms at the client's own pacer on an idle 1 Mbit/s uplink. The client's inputs had drained the bucket: the
soak's client re-bundles its unacknowledged inputs into every tick's packet and 3 % of them carry a 0.5-1 KiB tail,
so the essential class sends 4-5 kB within 100 ms about twice a second, and it spends the same buckets as reliable
data whenever they are ready. ADR-8692's four-packet floor lets a 4 KiB command leave whole only from a full bucket.
It happens before the transfer too (seed 77: 363 bytes left at 36.9 kB/s, a 208 ms command); during the transfer the
targets are lower (b), so the waits are longer.
(b) A cut read one round. An overuse cut set the target to 0.85x the delivery rate of the round that saw it. A round
is one round trip (about 100 ms here) and holds one to four packets, so its rate is quantized by whole packets. Seed
640, the server's connection to client 3, t = 33.97 s: rounds delivering 15-22 kB/s, then a round whose
acknowledgments named one 525-byte packet (5.25 kB/s) while the queue reading stood over the threshold for the second
round. The target went from 17,002 to 4,462 B/s on a link carrying 16 kB/s; growth of 8 %/s needs 16 s to undo that,
and meanwhile each 6-byte command reply waited 134-166 ms for the pacer to leave its debt (down leg p95 116 ms in the
transfer window, 64 ms before it). A client's cuts are the same rule on thinner rounds (ADR-8692 (b): "each cut takes
0.85x a small delivery rate"). With clients never cutting on delay the bar is over on 1 of 1,000 seeds: 640, the
server's cut.
(c) ADR-8692's delay misreading (the size of the packets carrying acknowledgments read as a queue) still makes the
cuts more frequent during the transfer (client overuse rounds 25 -> 50 and 24 -> 67 on seeds 42 and 77). It is why
the two windows differ; (a) and (b) are why either of them is slow.
(d) `LinkStats::reassembly_stall_deadline_ms` reported `max(4 x RTO, 2 s)` x the loss stretch without ADR-8658's
bound (before the first round-trip sample the RTO is never below the wait of the oldest unanswered ack-eliciting
packet): `stats()` has no clock. A link the check let live to 4 s reported a 2 s deadline with 2 s counted against it
(KI-NT-034 of v0.6.0).
Decision:
1. A foreground reliable message's burst is the message's. When the pacer lets a packet carry the first fragment of
   a message on a foreground stream, the rest of that message leaves in the same poll, up to
   `cc::PACING_BURST_PACKETS` packets from its start, even when the buckets are spent. Each such packet is charged to
   the pacer and the budget (they go into debt, so the rate over time is the target's) and to an excess allowance:
   the tokens the budget bucket could not hold while the sender used less than its target, at most
   `PACING_BURST_PACKETS` packets of them (the excess bucket of RFC 2697's single-rate meter, which fills only from
   the committed bucket's overflow). A sender that fills its target earns none, so its pacing is unchanged; a
   connection under a shared uplink's share earns none either (the aggregate hands a peer's unused share to the
   other peers, ADR-8534). A message's first fragment always waits for the pacer, fragments leave in id order, and a
   message longer than the allowance paces the rest as before. `Pacer::refill_overflow` is `Pacer::refill` returning
   the tokens that did not fit.
2. An overuse cut's base is the larger of the round's delivery rate and the delivery rate of the latest
   `DELIVERY_WINDOW_MS` (1 s), still never above the target: `target = 0.85 x min(max(round, window), target)`. GCC
   cuts to 0.85x the incoming rate of a 0.5-1 s window; a queue that stood through the window delivered the
   bottleneck's rate over it, which is also what `measure_bottleneck` reads at the same cut. A real fall of the path's
   rate still cuts at once and again each round trip as the window slides. On a server that splits a shared uplink
   among its peers (a listen server, or a fixed `uplink_bytes_per_second`; the server marks every peer through
   `Connection::set_shared_uplink` and `RateController::set_shared_uplink`, whether or not a share is in force) the
   round alone still sets the cut: see the last rejected variant.
3. The connection keeps the clock of its latest stall check and `stats()` reports the deadline as that check enforced
   it. Nothing sent changes; `Connection::reassembly_stall_ms()` keeps its meaning (the deadline without the bound).
Rejected, with numbers (one diag binary, one switch per rule; the bar over seeds 1-1000):
- A burst floor of 6 or 8 packets: 3 and 1 over. It passes by deepening every class's burst, the input bundles that
  drain the bucket included.
- The message burst without the excess allowance (the buckets' debt alone): 1 over alone, 0 with rule 2, but on
  listen-uplink/64 seeds 1-40 the seeds with a second over the uplink go 4 -> 10 (12 with rule 2) and congested 1-400
  goes 0 -> 1: a saturating sender's bursts land on a link that is already full. With the excess allowance
  listen-uplink 1-40 is 4 -> 4.
- Rule 2 alone: 15 over. Rule 1 alone: 1 over (seed 640).
- Rule 2 on a server that splits a shared uplink as well: the debug suite's
  `rate_control::listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh` (seed 3) fails with "server up: 2 of 12
  seconds over 20000000 bit/s (first at 8 s, worst 20008712 bit/s)"; over listen-uplink/64 seeds 1-200 the seeds with
  a second over the uplink go 26 -> 30 (worst second 110.0 -> 100.9 %, `no_wedged_client` failures 11 -> 4). The
  aggregate hands out the whole uplink (`max_min_shares` of the fixed rate), and the peers' deep cuts were part of what
  kept the sum under it. Keeping the old rule only while a share is in force was not enough: on congested/8 with a
  listen server (no share in force most of the time) the seeds with a second over a client's downlink went 6 -> 20 of
  40, while the clients' mean download rose 57 % at the gate seed (67 -> 105 kbit/s) and staleness p99 improved a
  little (mean 24.6 -> 23.6 ticks). Those seconds were not traced; the likely reading is that a server which no longer
  starves the link reaches the blind spot of Known issues as often as a dedicated server does (25-46 of 100 seeds at
  that shape). The windowed base belongs on listen servers too, but only once the aggregate holds headroom of its own
  and the minimum round trip is re-measured; that is the listen rows' own work.
Consequences (the build server diag binary of the committed code; "base" is the same binary with both rules switched off, which
reproduces the merged base's 2 of 104):
- `rpc_p95_with_bulk`, congested+bulk/4, seeds 1-1000: 34 -> 0 over 1.5x. Mean control p95 158.8 -> 139.0 ms, mean
  transfer p95 158.5 -> 141.2 ms. Seeds 42, 77, 640: 240/144, 256/144, 224/144 ms -> 128/128, 128/128, 144/144.
- congested/4 seeds 1-2000, seeds with a second over the 256 kbit/s downlink: 5 -> 6 (1011, 1211, 1433, 1831, 1858 in
  both; 218 new at 103.1 %; 1831's worst second 101.2 -> 102.5 %). See Known issues: it is not burst traffic on that
  link.
- listen-uplink/64 seeds 1-200, seeds with a second over the host's uplink: 26 -> 24 (the server's side is
  unchanged; the clients' own controllers follow the new rules), worst second 110.0 -> 107.4 %, `no_wedged_client`
  failures 11 -> 11, `staleness_p99` failures 5 -> 5. Seed 3 (the suite's): 97.5 % in both, no second over.
  congested/8 on a listen server, seeds 1-40: a second over a client's downlink on 6 -> 6 seeds.
- congested/8 and congested+bulk/8 on a dedicated server (the gate plan's shape, 60 s), seeds 1-100, seeds with a
  second over a downlink: 33 -> 25 and 43 -> 46 (`rate_vs_bottleneck` does not gate; see Known issues).
- `rpc_p95_with_bulk` at 8 clients, seeds 1-500: 6 -> 0 over.
- Thirteen more profiles at 8 clients, 60 s, seeds 1-40 each (asym-bufferbloat, bufferbloat, bad-wifi, good-wifi,
  mobile-4g, transatlantic, mixed, rtt-step, wifi-to-cell, flappy, high-rtt, downstream-loss, mtu-1280): the same
  failing-bar counts, ends and staleness means before and after on every one.
- bufferbloat+bulk/4 seeds 1-400: 0 -> 0 seconds over (worst 66.7 %). lossy-fat-pipe/4 seeds 1-400: `random_loss_kept`
  fails 4 -> 4 (minimum budget 39 of 140 in both).
- The default wire's pin (`pmtud::probing_off_by_default_leaves_the_clean_wire_byte_identical`) does not move.
- Tests: `connection::uplink_cap_tests::{a_four_kib_command_behind_an_input_burst_leaves_in_one_poll,
  a_long_message_takes_the_burst_floor_once, a_sender_that_fills_its_target_earns_no_message_burst,
  a_shared_uplink_share_earns_no_message_burst}`, `cc::tests::{one_thin_round_does_not_set_an_overuse_cut,
  under_a_shared_uplink_the_round_still_sets_the_cut}`, `connection::tests::stats_report_the_stall_deadline_with_the_unanswered_packet_bound`,
  soak `bars::rpc_p95_with_bulk_passes_on_the_residual_seeds`. Spec 120 § 4.2 items 2 and 7 carry "Built" notes.
- API, additions only: `Pacer::refill_overflow`, `RateController::set_shared_uplink`, `Connection::set_shared_uplink`
  (`cargo xtask api-snapshot` names no changed item of this lane). No wire, format or agent-method change; `LinkStats::reassembly_stall_deadline_ms` keeps its name and type.
Known issues:
- congested, a second up to 3 % over the downlink on 5-6 of 2,000 seeds at 4 clients and 20 s, and on a quarter to
  half of the seeds at 8 clients and 60 s (base and here). Traced on one seed (218, 4 clients): the server's 10 s
  minimum round trip to that client was first measured under the queue its join burst left standing (100 ms where
  the path's is 66), so its delay detector reads no queue and the target grows 8 %/s past the link until one sample
  finds the real minimum. Without rule 1 that seed finds it at 6.57 s and cuts at 8.67 and 9.07 s; with rule 1 the
  timing of the client's packets differs, no sample finds it before 11 s, and second 10 offers 103.1 %. The
  controller has no step that drains its own queue to re-measure the minimum (BBR's PROBE_RTT is the public design
  for it). The other seeds were not traced; whether they share this cause is open.
- ADR-8692's delay misreading (c) remains; its cuts now cost 15 % of the latest second's rate, and commands no longer
  wait on the target. The measurement fix is a one-way delay, which changes the wire (a candidate for wire 6).
- On a server that splits a shared uplink the thin-round cut remains (see the last rejected variant).
- The soak's clients run `LinkConfig::default()`, whose rate floor is the server's 32 KiB/s, not
  `RateConfig::client()`'s 16 KiB/s. Not changed here.

## ADR-10081: Scale at 128 clients: the loss detector scans only open packets; per-poll scratch leaves the heap (spec 120 § 1.1, § 15.2)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8454 recorded the 128-client run of the scale soak missing its `tick_p99` tier (30,608 µs against 16,666 µs,
measured on the build server at a 1-minute load of 170-205) and the server tick growing faster than the client count; it named
`Session::peer_by_addr` and the token scan of `on_rebind`, which ADR-8299 has since made maps. Re-measured on the v0.6.0
tag plus the v0.6.1 net lanes, one run at a time pinned to one the test machine core (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 1-minute load 14-25 from
other lanes' builds): tick p99 0.48-0.77 / 1.0-1.8 / 3.0-5.2 ms at 40 / 64 / 128 clients, so the 128 tier is met on a
quiet core by a factor of three and the 30 ms was the loaded host. The growth was still superlinear (tick p50 371 µs at
40, 2,514 µs at 128, for 3.2 times the clients). A profile with timing scopes (not committed; the build server and the test machine
core) of the 128-client run showed where: `Connection::detect_losses` walked every tracked sent-packet record on every
poll and on every acknowledgment that named a new packet. Records stay tracked long after their verdict, for late
acknowledgments (`LATE_ACK_WINDOW`, up to `SENT_WINDOW` = 1,024 records, about 130 KiB a peer), so on any path that
ever lost a packet each call touched about a thousand records: 28 % of the flush and 37 % of the receive on the
the test machine core, 46-48 % and 58 % on the build server, where 128 peers' windows (16 MiB) fall out of a loaded core's cache.
That is the faster-than-linear part. Encryption came next (seal 35 % of the flush, open 22 % of the receive on the
the test machine core), then packet building. The server also allocated 41.8 times per client per tick.
Decision:
1. **The loss detector starts where verdicts end.** `Connection::loss_scan_from` is the packet number below which
   every tracked packet is acknowledged or declared lost. Neither verdict is taken back for this scan (a late
   acknowledgment turns lost into acknowledged; nothing turns either into "open"), so `detect_losses` starts there and
   examines only packets whose fate is open. The verdicts are the same ones the full walk gave: it skipped exactly
   those records. `connection::WorkCounters::loss_scan_records` (crate-private) counts the records examined.
2. **Per-poll scratch leaves the heap.** `poll_transmit` kept three per-stream vectors per poll and one per packet
   (`cap_held`, `planned_end`, `new_seen`, `packet_starts`): they are arrays of `MAX_STREAMS` on the stack. The packet
   body buffer is one buffer the connection keeps (`body_scratch`) instead of one allocation per packet and one more
   per poll; the acknowledgment frame's writer allocates only when a frame is written; `send_order` returns at once
   when nothing reliable is queued.
3. **`NetServer::send` encodes into a kept buffer** (`encode_scratch`, dropped past 64 KiB) and copies the message once
   at its exact size, instead of a writer that grows from empty (about ten reallocations for a 1 KiB state message,
   per peer per tick). `WireWriter::{reusing, reserve, clear}` are crate-private.
4. **Not done here, with the numbers for a ruling.** After this ADR encryption is the largest single cost of the
   server at 128 clients (seal about 1.85 µs per 1.2 KiB datagram and open about 1.5 µs per client datagram on the
   the test machine core, through `snow`'s ChaCha20-Poly1305). Cutting it means sealing peers on worker threads or another
   cipher implementation (a dependency decision); neither is needed for a tier: the 128 tier has eight times its
   margin on one core. The relevance sweep is not on this path (the soak's sample game sends its own snapshots; the
   ECS replication path has its own scale test, ADR-8031).
5. **The shared uplink reads its queue trend before the witness gate** (found by the scale plan, not a cost change).
   `listen-uplink/16` on a listen server passes at the v0.6.0 tag and fails with the witness gate of ADR-8733 (2)
   (v06-net-soak-followups; bisected, and confirmed by removing the gate): 108 `protocol_error` ends in 180 s, and
   over ten seeds 0/10 runs pass (9/10 at the tag); `good-wifi/16` on a listen server falls from 10/10 to 2/10.
   Per-peer queueing delay reads about one tick apart (24 to 34 ms in the soak), right at the 25 ms threshold, so
   the number of peers over it crosses the gate from round to round. Each silenced round put a zero into the queue
   floor's window; the return to the unchanged reading then satisfied `floor > prev_floor_ms`, was taken for a queue
   building at the host, and held the aggregate at `BOTTLENECK_HEADROOM` of what the peers delivered again, with
   growth capped by that estimate: 3 % down per flap, 870 kB/s to 60 kB/s in the first 20 s of the run and then to
   the floor, where a rejoining client cannot finish its world blob inside the reassembly stall deadline. Decision:
   `SharedUplink` keeps the gate for what it was made for (no cut and no hold on a queue few peers see; growth while
   silenced) and reads the *rise* on the floor of the ungated medians (`plain_medians`), so a silenced round is not
   an empty queue and its end is not a rise. `host_queue_ms` is unchanged. Ten seeds per listen row, tag /
   ADR-8733 (2) / this: `listen-uplink/16` (180 s) 9 / 0 / 10 of 10; `good-wifi/16` 10 / 2 / 10; `mixed/16` 0 / 2 /
   10; `congested/16` 1 / 6 / 8; `congested/8` 0 / 10 / 10 and `bad-wifi/8` 6 / 10 / 10, both with the same numbers
   as ADR-8733 (2) run for run. Tests: `rate_control::a_flapping_witness_gate_does_not_ratchet_the_shared_uplink_down`,
   `scale::a_listen_server_holds_sixteen_on_its_uplink_for_three_minutes` (regia_net_soak). The gate plan runs no
   16-client listen row; the scale plan does.
Consequences: on the test machine core (interleaved before/after, three rounds, 60 virtual s, `scale_tick_p99_tiers`) the
server tick p99 goes from 0.61-0.77 / 1.26-1.77 / 3.49-5.22 ms to 0.41-0.47 / 0.68-0.81 / 2.04-2.75 ms at 40 / 64 /
128 clients, server CPU from 1.2-1.3 / 2.6-3.0 / 8.1-9.5 % of a core to 0.9 / 1.5-1.6 / 4.3-5.4 %, and allocations per
tick (p50) from 1,696 / 2,678 / 6,779 to 912 / 1,442 / 3,550 (41.8 to 22.5 per client per tick at 40). CPU per seat:
0.023 / 0.024 / 0.035 % of a core at 40 / 64 / 128 (before: 0.031 / 0.042 / 0.070); what still grows with the count
at 128 is the sample game's own snapshot (every avatar to every client: 453 kbit/s per seat at 128 against 338 at 40).
No wire, format or public API change (`LinkStats` is untouched; the counter is crate-private). The `tick_p99` tiers and
every bar are unchanged; `docs/perf/net-scale-soak.md` has the tables and `docs/perf/budgets.ron` is untouched. Tests:
`connection::scale_work_tests::{a_poll_examines_only_packets_whose_fate_is_open,
no_record_below_the_scan_start_is_without_a_verdict}` (regia_net),
`scale::the_server_allocates_within_its_budget_per_client_per_tick` (regia_net_soak; budget 30 per client per tick at
40 clients on `mixed`). Spec 120 § 1.1 and § 15.2 take a Built note.

## ADR-8887: The `no_wedged_client` harness hole: gaps closed at the peer's removal, judged per connection, outages excuse only themselves plus the input grace
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v0.7 § 2.2 item A (soak bars, harness hole), plan row N-17, and the net-soak-profiles-v2 report ("For the
lead": `report::wedges` builds `server_no_input` from input gaps that start at the first input that arrives, so a
client whose input never arrives is never wedged). ADR-8424 (net-soak-pins-v2) had already closed the end-of-run case
(a peer none of whose inputs ever arrived, still connected at the end of the run) and named one case it left open.
Reading the measurement at integ-v061a (92cd068dd) found three holes, each a client wedged while connected that the
gating bar did not report:
(1) a server input gap was recorded only when the next input arrived or at the end of the run, so a peer the server
removed while its input was missing (a scripted leave, a lost connection) was never judged, whether it had never been
heard or had stopped being heard;
(2) `wedges` judged a gap only when the client was connected as that peer through all of it, so a gap the server
closed after the client's own end was dropped even when the client had been connected and unheard for seconds;
(3) any outage that overlapped a gap excused all of it (`LinkSpec::outage_overlaps`), on the server's input gaps and
on the client's `no_snapshot` and `input_send_failing` gaps alike: a client that sent nothing, or heard nothing, for
the rest of the run after a 3 s outage read "no wedge".
Decision: (a) The server records every input gap whole (outages included) and closes the open one at the peer's
removal as well as at the next input and the end of the run (`PeerState::open_gap`: from the last input, or from
`INPUT_GRACE_MS` after the join when none arrived, ADR-8424). (b) `report::judged_input_gap` judges the parts of a gap
inside the client's own connected intervals as that peer and outside every outage of its link, each widened by
`INPUT_GRACE_MS` (1 s) after its end, the grace a join gets, for the outages the gap overlaps only (a gap that
starts after an outage has ended is judged whole, as before); every part of at least `WEDGE_MS` (2 s) is a
`server_no_input` wedge. (c) The client-side gaps are judged from the end of the same excuse
(`Client::judged_from`) instead of being excused whole. The bar, its 2 s limit and its gating are unchanged; the
excuse is now exactly what the bar's text says ("with its link up"), plus the 1 s grace. (d) Test knobs
`Knobs::silent_inputs` and `Knobs::silent_snapshots` (a `Silence { client, from_ms, until_ms }`) make one client
send no input, or get no snapshot, for a window while it stays connected: the clients the bar must report.
Consequences: `no_wedged_client` is stricter, never looser: every wedge the old rule found is still found (a gap
contained in one connection with no outage is judged whole, as before), and the three holes are wedges. The
ADR-8424 pin `no_wedged_client_fails_without_input_feedback_and_passes_with_it` asked for one wedge per client "from
its last join"; it now asks for one per connection (congested's and rtt-step's scripted leave rejoin client 5, whose
first connection was the hole). Tests: `crates/regia_net_soak/tests/wedge_hole.rs`. Host-visible API in
regia_net_soak: new pub fields `Knobs::silent_inputs` and `Knobs::silent_snapshots` (struct literals must add them or
end with `..Knobs::default()`), new pub struct `workload::Silence`, new pub fn `report::judged_input_gap`. A first version of this lane also
cut the grace from a gap that started just after an outage had ended; the base nightly run caught it (long-outage and
flappy in listen mode reported a `no_snapshot` gap at the base that the first version did not), so the grace applies
only to an outage the gap overlaps, which keeps every wedge the old rule found. No wire,
format or engine change. Soak numbers at the base and with the fix: the lane report
(`sprint-v07-net-soak-wedged-hole.md`). Book: `agents/net-soak.md` (`no_wedged_client` row, "Using it in a test").
Spec 120 § 15.2: a Built note.

## ADR-8221: Client capture with timing and its replay (spec 120 § 15.5, spec 103 § 14)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 15.5 (plan id N231, row P7) asks that a bad-network failure on a client replay to the same corrections.
At the base the only recorder is spec 103's virtual server connection, which has no socket and no timing, playback time is
synthetic, and a client's own stream and prediction were out of scope (spec 103 § 11). A failing soak run printed its bars and
nothing that could reproduce one client's experience.
Decision: (1) `regia_net::capture` (core, no ECS): `CaptureRecord` (session, receive, flush, accept with the sealed flag,
deny, decrypted connection packet, goodbye, ended, input stamp and bytes, game frame marker with a digest), `ClientCapture` (a
ring of exactly `max_bytes`, 4 KiB..=1 GiB, default 16 MiB, allocated once and written circularly; whole-session export),
`CaptureTap` (shared handle), `CaptureFile` (`.netcapture` v1, atomic save, a reader that checks every length before allocating
and a CRC-32 per record), `ReplayFeed` and `compare_sessions`. (2) `NetClient::set_capture` logs at the seam after decryption
and the token check (the plaintext a replay can feed without the session keys) and `NetClient::replay` reads a captured
session instead of its socket: no handshake (the captured accept connects it at the captured header size, so packets are cut
the same), no sends, no connect timeout; the connected-phase timeout still runs, so a replay reaches its own ends. (3) The net
soak's client keeps a chained FNV-1a digest of its output (frame time, phase, corrections, predictions, inputs, commands, every
message it was handed) and writes a frame marker per frame; `workload::replay_client` rebuilds the client from the scenario
JSON in the file label and runs its frames at the captured times. (4) `run_plan` reruns a failing scenario with a capture on
every client (`capture_ring_bytes`: 96 KiB per virtual second, 8-128 MiB per client) and writes
`client-<i>.netcapture` under `REGIA_NET_SOAK_CAPTURE_DIR` (else `REGIA_NET_SOAK_OUT/captures`), printing
`REGIA_NET_SOAK_REPLAY=<file> cargo test -p regia_net_soak --test capture_replay -- --ignored --exact replay_capture_file`.
(5) Differences from the brief: inputs are compared, not injected (the soak client's inputs are seeded, so an equal input
record proves the stamps); "interpolation output digest" is the soak client's output digest, because the soak's sample game
has no interpolation; replaying an ECS world (spec 73 prediction, spec 74 interpolation) through `NetLink` and an agent method
to start a capture are follow-ups. The bound "memory bounded by its ring" is the ring's capacity, fixed at creation.
Consequences: `NetClient` gains three private fields and four methods (additive); `ClientEnd`, `ClientEvent` and the wire are
unchanged (no wire version bump). A new binary format `.netcapture` v1 (`docs/formats/netcapture.md`) is registered in
check-formats, `regia upgrade-project` (recognized, never rewritten) and the fuzz coverage lists (its reader's truncation and
bit-flip test); `format-hashes.ron` needs `cargo xtask check-formats --update`. A capture holds decrypted traffic (private game
data). Specs updated: spec 103 § 14 (new), spec 120 § 15.5 (Built note), book/agents/net-soak.md, book/user-guide/networking.md.

## ADR-8890: Land client capture and replay on the v0.7 net line; replay an ECS world through `NetLink`; agent capture methods
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8221 (N231) built client capture with timing on a lane that never reached v0.6.0, for raw `NetClient`
clients only, and named two follow-ups: replaying an ECS world (spec 73 prediction, spec 74 interpolation) through
`NetLink`, and an agent method to start a capture on a running client. The v0.7 net line (spec 120) needs both so a
player's "it lagged for me" report becomes a file that replays the same frames.
Decision: (1) Merge lane/sprint-net-client-capture-replay (1664d7e78) onto the v0.6.1 roll-up (integ-v061a 92cd068dd).
The merge keeps the base's newer client (version stamps, path validation, the resume ticket, the clock filter): connect and
replay share one private constructor; a replayed deny reads its version stamp; the flush's `poll_transmit` callback drops a
replay's packets (counted, sealed ones too) and a sealed replay cuts packets at the sealed header size. (2) `NetLink` keeps
one `CaptureTap` (`set_capture`, `capture`): every client endpoint it installs (connect, resume, automatic reconnect) gets
it, so each connection is a new session in the same ring; `stop` keeps it so it can be saved after the session ended; a
server link refuses it (`false`). `capture_frame(digest)` writes the game's frame marker at the link's clock.
(3) `NetLink::replay::<G>(feed, opts)` / `replay_on(socket, feed, opts)` start a client endpoint from
`NetClient::replay` with the client configuration a connect would use (shared `client_config`), behind a
`capture::ReplaySocket` that receives nothing and drops what it is given and reports the captured transport's datagram
size (default `MAX_DATAGRAM_BYTES`), so the replay cuts packets as the capture did. The app's bridge, replication,
prediction and interpolation run as live; `replay_progress` reports `ReplayProgress` (receives off the captured time,
receives past the end, records left). Errors: `LinkError::Capture(CaptureError)` with the capture's code
(`capture_protocol_mismatch`, `capture_empty`). (4) The time harness: `TimedHub::capture_client(i, ring, digest)` attaches a
tap and chains a `FrameDigest` (a `fn(&mut World) -> u64`) after each client update; `timed::replay_client::<G>` builds a
fresh client world with the hub's `setup` and a `configure` closure, starts the link clock at the session's first receive,
runs one update per captured receive and compares with `compare_sessions` and the chained digest. (5) Agent methods
`net.capture_start { ring_bytes? }` and `net.capture_save { path, label?, overwrite?, stop? }` act on the app's `NetLink`
(F0002 with `data.reason`: `capture_no_client`, `capture_not_started`, `capture_config_invalid`, `capture_exists`,
`capture_io`, `capture_empty`, `path_outside_project`); paths follow the request-path output-root rule.
Consequences: additive API, except `LinkError` gains the variant `Capture` (an exhaustive match on `LinkError` needs an
arm). No wire change (wire stays at its version; nothing rides wire 6). The `.netcapture` v1 format is unchanged and is a
format-batch-2 row for the 11-28 freeze (check-formats hash row owed). A replay is of one client; the server is not
replayed, and what the client sent is counted, not compared. Specs updated: spec 120 § 15.5 (Built note),
book/agents/net-capture.md (new), book/agents/net-soak.md, book/user-guide/networking.md, book/COVERAGE.md, book/SUMMARY.md.

## ADR-8513: Lockstep match replay `.lsreplay` v1, the bit-exact audit, the replay library and the replay agent methods
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: plan row NL-02 (DO27 absorb plan, A-9): a lockstep match must be re-runnable offline and checked bit for bit,
and the files must not pile up. DO27 keeps a match log of fulls, applied inputs, peer commands and an abort trailer with a
bit-exact playback audit and a replay folder kept to the newest 20 (read as requirements at regia-absorb-4; its library
module adapted). Regia had the desync bundle (ADR-8455: the window around one divergence) and the replication demo
recorder (a different thing, kept separate), but no whole-match lockstep recording.
Decision: `regia_net::lockstep::replay`. The `.lsreplay` v1 file: magic `RGLSRPLY`, version `u32`, a length-prefixed
header (game id, protocol version, protocol id, content hash, engine version, tick rate, seed, Full and hash intervals,
seats), then records `kind u8 | len u32 | payload`: Full 0x01 (flags, tick, world hash, the game's state bytes), Inputs
0x02 (the agreed frame as each seat's sent bytes, the delay, membership), Hashes 0x03 (world and per-subsystem hashes at a
checkpoint), PeerCmds 0x05, Abort 0x07 (tick, code, reason). Every record has a length (DO27's has none) so a reader can
walk the frames without decoding a payload and refuse a length before allocating. `LsReplayWriter` is opt-in
(`LsReplaySettings::record`), driven by the host or a seat (`record_start`, `record_frame`, `record_state`,
`record_peer_cmds`, `finish`); a Full every `full_every` ticks (the tier's 2 Hz or 1 Hz), hashes every
`hash_every_ticks` (default the lockstep checkpoint interval, 30), a byte cap per `ReplayTier` (256 / 64 MiB, DO27's)
that sheds Fulls first and then stops at a whole tick, and an abort record always written. `LsReplayReader` checks every
length against the bytes left and fixed caps (file 256 MiB + 4 KiB, header 64 KiB, Full 32 MiB, other records 4 MiB,
1,024 seats, 60,000-byte inputs, 64 subsystems, 256 commands, names 64 bytes, texts 1,024 bytes) and refuses a newer
version by name before its header. `audit` / `audit_with` re-run the match through the game's `DesyncReplay` hook (the
desync bundle's, ADR-8455) from the first Full, compare every Hashes record bit for bit, compare the replayed state with
each later Full and then load it, and name the first diverging tick, the subsystems that differ there and the last
agreed tick. `ReplayLibrary`: list newest first with damaged files apart, `rotate` to the newest N (default 20) never
deleting an aborted or damaged file, `import` with a SHA-256 duplicate check (`replay_duplicate`), `export` with a
`regia-lsreplay-meta/1` JSON sidecar. CLI `regia net replay-audit <file> [--json]` (exit 0 bit-exact, 1 otherwise);
agent methods `net.replays {dir?}` and `net.replay_audit {path}`; `NetAgentState::{set_replay_hooks, replay_hooks,
set_replay_dir, replay_dir}`. Error codes `replay_not_found`, `replay_io`, `replay_not_lsreplay`, `replay_version_newer`,
`replay_truncated`, `replay_too_large`, `replay_unknown_record`, `replay_invalid`, `replay_game_mismatch`,
`replay_no_hook`, `replay_hook_failed`, `replay_duplicate`. The soak kit's host records on request
(`LockstepScenario::replay`, `LockstepRecord::replay`) and `LockSim` gains a state codec and a `DesyncReplay` hook
(`LockReplay`). The byte codec is a small private one inside the module: the detsim state codec (det-core-06,
`DetState`) and the input-log replay runner (det-core-07) are not on this lane's base; when they land, a game's Full
bytes can be `DetState` frames without a format change (the Full payload is the game's bytes), and the private codec can
be swapped. SHA-256 is the project's own (a copy of `regia_pt::sha256`, no new dependency); the sidecar JSON is written
by hand (`regia_net` has no JSON dependency).
Consequences: any recorded lockstep match is checked offline bit for bit and the exact tick a flipped input or a
non-deterministic step first shows is named (with `hash_every_ticks: 1`; otherwise the first checkpoint after it). New
frozen format `lsreplay` v1 (check-formats, upgrade-project as unmigrated, fuzz target `net.lsreplay`, corpus fixture).
Additive API; `LockstepScenario` and `LockstepRecord` (dev-only soak kit) gain a field each. Not built: the lockstep host
and seat do not own a writer (the game drives it beside its step, as the soak kit does), a seat that takes a state
transfer does not write a fresh Full by itself (it should call `record_start_at` on the adopted state), and the audit
does not apply peer commands (they are recorded for reading). Specs updated: 12 (format table row);
`docs/formats/lsreplay.md`, `book/agents/net-lsreplay.md`.

## ADR-8892: Land the lockstep replay audit; NetExternalStats and `net.external_stats`
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The lockstep replay audit (`.lsreplay` v1, ADR-8513) was built on lane/sprint-lockstep-replay-audit and never
merged; the v0.7 plan (§ 2.2) lands it with format batch 2. External replication (ADR-8186) left an open known issue
(KI-NT-012): it has `ExternalReplication::stats()` but no resource or agent method, so an agent could only see it when
the game wrote its own reply.
Decision: (1) Merge ad93513f8 onto integ-v061a (92cd068dd). The base added `LockstepFrame::match_end` (agreed-tick
match end); the `.lsreplay` frame record does not carry it, and the replay hooks (`LockReplay`, the sample game) set it
`false`: a game's step never reads it and the file's end is the match's end, so the format stays as built (no v2 before
the batch freezes). The `lsreplay` row in spec 12 names v0.7.0 format batch 2. (2) `regia_net::NetExternalStats`
(`external_replication::NetExternalStats`, an ECS resource with `ecs`, a plain value without): per label the newest
`ExternalStats`, the tick it was taken at and a publish count, in `ExternalStatsEntry`; `publish(label, tick, stats)`,
`ExternalReplication::publish_stats(label, tick, &mut NetExternalStats)`, `get`, `entries`, `remove`, `len`,
`is_empty`; at most `MAX_LABELS` = 16 labels (a new label past that is refused, an existing one always refreshes, as
the hub reports). The game publishes at its own rate: the engine still never finds the replication. (3) Agent method
`net.external_stats {replication?}` (read-only) returns `{replications: [...]}` sorted by label: each entry is
`ExternalStats` exactly as serde writes it, plus `label`, `tick`, `publishes` and `totals` (sums over the clients of
every counter, `tier_sent` per tier, and the client count). Codes `external_bad_params`, `external_unknown`.
(4) `cargo xtask det-scan` on the landed replay: the library's four file-date uses (`UNIX_EPOCH`, listing, rotation and
import order by file mtime, never sim state) carry `det-scan: allow(wall_clock)` waivers with that reason, and det-scan
now leaves out the test-only children of a non-`mod.rs` file (`replay.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` is
`replay/tests.rs`; it only knew the `mod.rs` layout), with a unit test. (5) A held lockstep input
(`SeatInput::Held`, new on the base) is recorded as the value the match stepped with, as the desync bundle does.
Consequences: additive API (a new resource, a new method on `ExternalReplication`, a new struct); no wire, format or
settings change. Agents read external replication with the same call in every game that publishes. Tested: the
`regia_net` lib test publishes after a seeded bad-wifi run and compares the entry with `stats()`; the `regia_agent` lib
test runs a seeded lossy run and compares every number of the method's answer with `stats()` and the totals with the
sums. Specs updated: 120 § 7.6 and § 8.6 (Built notes), 12 (lsreplay row); `book/agents/net-external-replication.md`.

## ADR-8182: Connection quality grade, two-way loss, one-way jitter and operator stats rows (spec 120 § 13)
Date: 2026-11-17   Status: proposed
Context: Audit row Q1 (partial): a game could poll RTT, RTTVAR and send-side loss, but had no reliable connection
indicator and could not tell the player why the game felt bad. The client never learned its upstream loss or how many of
its inputs arrived late (the server knew), there was no grade and no event on a change, `jitter_ms` was RTTVAR rather
than a one-way jitter, and datagrams the socket absorbed (a full send buffer) counted as sent. Spec 120 § 13.1 names
`PeerQuality` and `LinkGrade`, § 13.2 the operator rows, § 13.3 `net.quality`.
Decision: (1) `regia_net::quality`: one tracker per link on `NetServer` (per peer) and `NetClient`, sampled every 250 ms
from the connection's cumulative counters into 10 s windows: RTT p50/p95 of the raw samples (the connection now counts
every raw RTT observation), `loss_out` from this end's acknowledgments, `loss_recv` from received packet-number progress,
`loss_in` as the peer reported it, the late and missing input fractions (server totals; the client's from
`LinkFeedback`), the p5 margin. Loss fractions need 32 resolved packets and input fractions 30 ticks before they count.
(2) Grades are spec 120 § 13.1's thresholds on RTT p95, the worst of the three losses and missing inputs. Hysteresis is a
Schmitt trigger per boundary: a worse grade starts when a signal passes its limit and shows after 500 ms in which the
signals stayed past 75 % of it (it shows the strict grade then, at least one step worse); a better one after 2 s with
every signal under 75 % of the better grade's limits. The windows are 10 s values, so they move slowly and a short hold
is enough; the band keeps a signal on its limit from flickering. A link with nothing received since the last sample
moves no grade (the outage's first `interrupt_ms` would otherwise degrade it before `Interrupted`); `Interrupted` shows at once (it is debounced by `interrupt_ms`), once per outage, and the restore brings back the
grade from before the outage; the loss and RTT windows restart 1 s after a restore, so packets sent into the outage do
not grade the link for 10 s after it. `ClientEvent::QualityChanged { from, to }` and `ServerEvent::QualityChanged
{ peer, from, to }` on each change. (3) Spec 120 § 13.1 defines `loss_in` as "loss the peer measured on what we sent", so
`loss_out` and `loss_in` both describe what this end sent; neither says what it receives, which the downstream-loss
acceptance needs. `PeerQuality` therefore adds `loss_recv` (what this end received, measured here) and `rttvar_ms` (the
brief's "next to RTTVAR"); on the server `loss_in` is 0 (clients send no loss report on wire 4). (4) The server's
`LinkFeedback::upstream_loss` is now its tracker's 10 s `loss_recv` (was an 8-record packet-number meter, about 2 s), so
the client's `loss_in` is the server's measurement by construction; the record format is unchanged. (5) One-way jitter
is the RFC 3550 § 6.4.1 interarrival jitter of sender stamps: the server appends `sent_ms u32` (its clock, wrapping) to
every tick sync and the client sends `LANE_CLOCK` (5) `| sent_ms u32` every 250 ms on the essential unreliable class. This
is a framing change inside wire 4, which net-input-feedback (ADR-8077) opened on the v0.5.x line and which has not
shipped; spec 120 § 12.1 lets a lane reuse its line's open bump, so `REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION` stays 4 and the wire-3
refusal test of ADR-8077 covers old peers. A malformed clock record scores one malformed point like a bad game
message. (6) `DatagramSocket::dropped_sends()` (default 0; `UdpTransport` counts `WouldBlock` and a second stale
reset) and `EndpointTotals::socket_dropped`: absorbed datagrams no longer count in `datagrams_out`. (7)
`regia_net::stats::StatsReporter` writes `regia_net::stats` rows: per peer every 10 s, the server every 60 s (tick step
and loop p50/p95/p99, `VmRSS` on Linux/Android, peers by grade, summed rates); on in `server_host` (dedicated), off by
default, addresses redacted unless `show_addresses`. (8) Agent: `net.quality {endpoint?, peer?}`; `net.peers` rows gain
`grade` and `quality`; `net.status` a client's `quality` and `totals.socket_dropped`.
Consequences: The brief also named jitter and the correction rate as grade inputs; spec 120's thresholds do not, and the
spec wins: jitter is reported (RTT p95 already carries what jitter does to the round trip) and the correction rate lives
on the prediction path, which has no `NetClient` yet. `queue_delay_ms` and `send_allowance_bps` read 0 until
net-v2-rate-controller; `RateLimited` waits for it too. Server-row CPU share and desync/resync counts wait for the
lockstep lanes. Costs: 5 bytes up every 250 ms, 4 more bytes per tick sync, a sort of at most 1,024 RTT samples per link
