   it. The schema fingerprint moves (the `rules-ron` row of `format-hashes.ron` needs `check-formats --update`).
7. Already on this base (ADR-8748): `SessionPatch` sets waves, race, zone, elimination and victory;
   `the_genre_sections_resolve_through_extends` covers it. No change.
Consequences: a struct literal of `MatchSession`, `OptionDef`, `RotationView` or `MatchEventFields` users is affected
as listed in the release fragment (`MatchSession` and `OptionDef` gain fields; `RotationView` gains `rules_hash`). A
v0.7 session snapshot does not load on v0.6 (unknown `version`), and from now on an older build refuses a newer
session by name instead of misreading it. A departed player's pawn no longer scores, dies or assists on the score
sheet; games that seat bots through the flow get the same rule for bots that leave. Rule-set options can drive the
match without game code, and a dedicated host can refuse a client with different rule sets at the handshake once
the game opts in (an owner/lead call on when the default turns on: it needs the client side first). Specs
updated: docs/formats/rules-ron.md, docs/specs/102-logic-graph.md (kind list); book pages match-rules, logic-graph,
net-session-players, game-modes.

## ADR-8879: rules-ron payload-free tagged kinds refuse unknown fields (amends ADR-8799)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8799 made every tagged value in a `.rules.ron` file refuse an unknown field through strict mirrors with
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. The verification lane (sprint-rules-ruleset-format-fixes-verification, finding 1)
showed that the attribute does not reach an internally tagged unit variant: serde's internally tagged unit-variant
visitor skips the rest of the map without reading the container attribute. `(kind: "end", ticks: 30)`,
`(kind: "draw", extra: 1)`, `(kind: "sudden_death", ...)`, respawn `instant` / `never`, zone `domination` and victory
`team_elimination` / `surrender` loaded and dropped the field, against `docs/formats/rules-ron.md`.
Decision: every payload-free variant of an internally tagged `.rules.ron` reader is an empty struct variant (`End {}`),
which deserializes through the struct visitor and so honors `deny_unknown_fields`. The mirrors `TimeUpFile`,
`RespawnPolicyFile` and `ZoneModeFile` (`ruleset/strict.rs`) change in place. `VictoryConditionDef` keeps its unit
variants in Rust (no host-visible change) and reads through a new private mirror `VictoryConditionFile` with
`#[serde(from)]`; its `Serialize` is unchanged. The adjacently tagged `TeamSwitchFile` already refused (the derive
reads the outer two-key map with the container attribute) and is unchanged. The shared snapshot types (`TimeUp`,
`RespawnPolicy`, `ZoneMode`, `VictoryCondition`) stay lenient unit variants for snapshots and agent `settings`.
Consequences: the wire text is the same (`(kind: "end")` is one RON map for a unit and for an empty internally tagged
struct variant), so shipped rule sets and the corpus file read unchanged. The `regia_core` schema probe reports an
empty struct variant as `unit` (tag-only map accepted, field index 0 refused as past the end), so the `rules-ron`
fingerprint string and hash do not move; `rules_ron_fingerprint_covers_tagged_enum_payloads` still pins
`3:unit`, `4:unit` for `VictoryConditionDef`. A v1 file with an extra field beside a payload-free kind, which loaded
before, is now `ruleset_parse`; v1 is unreleased (v0.7 window), so no version bump (ADR-8619 rule). Scan of the other
v0.7 strict formats at their lane heads (gait v1, playlist, match results, terrain/world index work): none has an
internally tagged enum with `deny_unknown_fields` and a unit variant. The one other case in the tree,
`regia_editor` `conversation_panel::edit::NewStep::End`, is an agent-method parameter, not a file format; listed for
the lead, not changed here. Rule for new readers: an internally tagged enum that must refuse unknown fields writes its
payload-free variants as `Name {}`.
Specs updated: docs/formats/rules-ron.md (unknown-field paragraph).

## ADR-10082: The v0.7 tunnels re-pin pass, the edited-ground descent of the merged W-11 lanes, and the Stage B switch note
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v07 § 2.2 row E: one re-pin pass on the v0.7 line once the W-11 speed lanes (ADR-8815, ADR-8816,
ADR-8817, ADR-8818) and Stage B correctness (ADR-8898, renumbered from a duplicate ADR-8810 by integ-v07a) have
landed, then the Stage B switch note for DO27. Each of those lanes branched from v0.6.0 and pinned its own cook; this
line is the first where they meet. Lane v07-tunnels-repin-switch-note merged the five branches (ancestry carries
tunnels-perf-low-tiers 01777ede1 and native-acceptance-suite 1d0f9f34a).
Decision:
- **Edited-ground descent (merge of ADR-8815 and ADR-8818).** Lane 001 kept the height-pyramid descent on an edited
  state by trusting a node's cooked range only at a level-0 tile no edit touches; lane 004 gave an edited state its own
  ranges (`GroundEdits::edited_range`, kept when `pyramid_bounds()`) and walked every cell otherwise. Merged in
  `WorldGeom::node_range` (called by `ground_node`): the node's range is the cooked one on an unedited state, the edited state's own at any node
  when it holds them, the cooked one at an untouched tile otherwise, and none (no height tests) on a touched tile of a
  state without ranges. Both range culls and lane 001's height slab use that range. The plain-cell walk stays gated on
  the untouched-tile test, because it reads counts without edits. `GroundLattice::edited_range` (lane 004's accessor,
  now unused) is removed. `touched_tiles_keep_a_range_that_holds_the_edited_ground` pins the rule (a touched tile
  and every coarser node keep a range, and it holds the edited ground). Answers are pinned equal to the full walk by
  `edited_ground_equals_the_full_walk`,
  `edited_map_answers_as_the_reference_walk` and the crater suites.
- **Pins.** Moved: the v2 `content_hash` pins of `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` (003cbe4b… / a96bc485…), because
  ADR-8816's v2 hash meets ADR-8898's cook here for the first time; the cooked value did not move (the v1-layout pins,
  ADR-8898's d594e549… / 1fdd5b7e…, pass). Not moved, and checked on this line: `stage_a_bits` (with and without
  `stage_b`: Stage A, DO27's compat contract, is unchanged), the two-peer golden `tunnel_drive_two_peer.detgold`
  (run hash c08ed591acfdb277 on x86_64-linux), `native_table` (`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 8), the section byte pins,
  the mover walk pins and every native acceptance bar. W-31's D10 reds (`rubble_pile_is_a_sim_floor`, the two-peer
  golden, `native_sweep_bars_switchbacks_and_cinder`, `stage_a_bits`) are green on this line.
- **Named, not changed: `native_resident_geometry_fits_the_sim_budget`.** Switchbacks resides at 34,368,306 B against
  the 35,000,000 B bar of spec 121 § 11 (met), but the cook's estimate (`pitch::sim_ground_bytes`: counts, overrides,
  cuts, triangles, tile levels) reads 33,910,936 B, 1.35 % low against the test's 1 % rule. The gap is the run-time
  query tables the estimate leaves out: query index with ADR-8815's segment tables and ADR-8817's column directory
  392,038 B, height pyramid 43,944 B, ground axis table 20,480 B. Each lane fitted alone; together they pass 1 %
  (lane 003 predicted it). The test is not touched. The fix is a choice for the lead or the owner: (a) the estimate
  counts the query tables (the honest estimate; it moves the cook's `ground_over_budget` check and
  `terrain.bake_report`'s figure), (b) give memory back (a coarser `FINE_M` in `query_column.rs`, slower `support`),
  or (c) a written ruling on the 1 % rule. Recommended: (a), as its own lane.
- **Switch note.** `book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md`: ADR-8538's statement, what DO27 re-cooks (`.meshlayers`
  v2 for every map, a source re-cook for maps with a filled skylight mouth, nav cells v3 and the terrain index v3 when
  format batch 2 lands them), the sim-version bump DO27 makes in v0.7.x (not in the v0.7.0 tag, owner 2026-11-19), the
  W-11 bars measured per device, the D4 bar pending the owner's ruling, and the plan's fallback (Stage A stays the
  default if a bar is still missed at the 11-30 checkpoint). No bar is re-set here.
Consequences: DO27 has one page that says what its Stage B bump takes. The resident-memory rule is red on this line
until (a), (b) or (c) lands. Specs not changed; book page added and linked from `book/SUMMARY.md`.

## ADR-8884: W-11 review fixes: the pyramid's ground tiles walk the single walk's cells, and the fine column directory caps its filings
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Two W-11 reviews filed bugs against the speed lanes. (1) w11-crater-edits-review: with ADR-8818 an edited state
takes the height pyramid in `segment` / `line_of_sight` / `rock_between`, and its answers left
`segment_without_pyramid` (the walk of every cell, the oracle the speed comments pin it to): a dropped ground hit on a
2 mm plateau crater and a one-ulp `t` on an ordinary map (proof tests `degenerate_plateau_segment_matches_the_full_walk`,
`edited_ground_segment_t_matches_the_full_walk`). The same proofs stay red on the merge of all four W-11 speed lanes
(lane 001's descent, ADR-8815, which already walks edited ground through the pyramid), and the plateau test prints
the same disagreement on a fresh state. The cause is not the ranges: every level-0 tile of the descent started a cell
walk of its own, from the segment's clipped entry into the tile, located and clamped into the tile. On a segment along
a lattice line, through a vertex or a tile corner, or vertical on a cell border, that start is a cell the single walk
over the whole lattice never visits (both tiles beside a border line accept the segment), or misses one it does visit,
so the two walks test different triangles and the closest hit differs. (2) w11-native-support-column-review: a legal
`QueryIndex::build` (16 384 floors each covering a 512 x 512 directory, `index_cell_m` 8192) sums the fine directory's
filings in a `u32` and panics on the add (`query_column.rs:220`), or with overflow checks off sizes an empty list and
indexes it; 16 383 such floors ask for about 8 GB.
Decision: (1) `query_segment::GroundPath`: the single walk's start cell, step signs and clip are computed once per
segment, as `ground_cells` computes them over the whole lattice. The walk is the merge of the two sorted lists of border
crossings (`x` first on a tie, `walk_cells`' rule), so the cell it is in when it enters a tile, or when it reaches a
`t`, is found by counting crossings (an estimate from the pitch, corrected on the exact `(border - from) / d` values);
`GroundPath::entry` returns the first cell of the single walk inside a tile that it leaves at the span's start minus
the slack or later, and the `t` it enters it at, or `None` when the walk never gets there (it misses the tile, stops at
the segment's end first, or leaves the lattice first). Both level-0 walks (`ground_cells_from` on edited, cut or
coarse tiles, `ground_cells_plain` on plain tiles) start there and stop past the span's end plus the slack, so a tile
walks exactly the single walk's cells inside it, in its order. The ADR-8818 ranges stay: a node's height range is the
cooked one where it bounds the ground (lane 001's rule), else the edited state's own widened range, else none (the node
is entered on its crossing alone). `GroundEdits::pyramid_bounds` and `GroundLattice::edited_range` are gone (the merge
of lanes 001 and 004 made both unused). (2) `ColumnIndex::build` counts the filings in `u64` before sizing anything and
disables the directory past `MAX_FILED` (16 000 000, the column grid's own reference cap), as it already does past
`MAX_CELL` and the block cap; queries then read the column grid. Shipped maps file far fewer (Switchbacks' whole query
index is 230 802 bytes), so their directories, and every answer on them, are unchanged.
Consequences: `segment`, `line_of_sight` and `rock_between` equal the walk of every cell on fresh and edited ground,
including the review's inputs; `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` stays 8 because the answers on every pinned input are the single
walk's, which they already matched (the two proof tests and the new seam tests are the inputs where they did not); the
native acceptance lines and the two-peer run hash (`74e9d8f805407ffe`) are the same before and after. The path is built
at the first tile the descent reaches (its start cell from the axis table, `GroundLattice::locate`'s search on the same
values), and a tile's entry is two to four short counts. Steam Deck, interleaved with the unfixed merge
(`docs/evidence/w11-review-fixes/`): fresh mixed tick 0.264-0.266 → 0.259-0.262 ms, `segment` 696-701 → 649-651 ns,
`line_of_sight` 556-568 → 536-546 ns; on edited ground `segment` 906-909 → 703-705 ns (the edited ranges now bound the
inner nodes too) and the tick with 30 craters 0.310-0.312 → 0.296-0.297 ms; the 6 m crater (0.092-0.093 ms) and
`support` unchanged. No format, snapshot, state hash or host API change.
Tests: `query_column::tests::directory_disables_instead_of_overflowing_its_u32_lists` (review proof) and
`directory_keeps_its_filing_cap` (61 full-cover floors keep the directory and list in order, 62 and 16 383 disable it);
`crater_edit_adversarial` (review proofs); `query_segment::tests::ground_path_entry_is_the_single_walk_cell` (the entry
against a cell-by-cell walk for every tile and many `t`s on seam segments) and `seam_segments_equal_the_full_walk`
(fresh and edited, with craters on tile corners). Specs: 121 § 6 (the descent note). Supersedes nothing; amends ADR-8815
and ADR-8818 (their level-0 walks and the ranges' gate).

## ADR-8844: Very Low and Medium selectable by name: `ProfileName` (ADR-7977 build A, v0.7)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7977 (design, spec 13 § 3a) made the integrated-GPU floor the existing `QualityTier::VeryLow` and asked
for a build lane so a host can select it by name wherever it names a render preset today. At v0.6.0 (02381fd90) every
such place took `RenderProfilePreset::from_name` only, so "VeryLow" failed everywhere: `render.set_profile`, the
`--render-profile` / `REGIA_RENDER_PROFILE` / `render_profile.txt` readers (`cinematic.rs`), `Regia.toml`
`[platforms.*] render_profile` (`manifest.rs`), the editor's Project Settings check and picker, and (found by this
lane, not in the design) the packaged game's reader of `build_info.json` (`packaged_config.rs`), which would have
logged "invalid render_profile" and ignored a `VeryLow` that `regia package` wrote. DO27's v0.7 switch wants to select
the floor in its Regia.toml and shell by name.
Decision: (1) `regia_render::ProfileName` (`Preset(RenderProfilePreset)` | `Tier(QualityTier)`), in `quality/`,
re-exported at the crate root, with the spec 13 § 3a signatures (`TIERS = [VeryLow, Medium]`, `parse`, `name`,
`preset`, `apply_for_gpu`, `names`) plus `tier()`, `apply_for_gpu_with` (a host's `TerrainVtPolicy`), `From<preset>`
and `Display`. Preset names win; `Low`, `High` and `Ultra` stay unknown (those tiers are rows already, so no row gets a
second name). (2) `cinematic::{choose_profile, ProfileChoice, take_profile_arg, parse_profile_file,
profile_from_scene_dir}` beside the preset readers, same precedence and codes; `choose_preset` and the other preset
readers are unchanged and still refuse tier names. Their unknown-name error is a new variant
`PresetChoiceError::UnknownProfile` (code `render_profile_unknown`, the message lists `ProfileName::names()`), so the
preset readers' message is unchanged. (3) Agent: `render.set_profile` parses a `ProfileName`, gates on its preset
(Very Low gates as Desktop Low: never gated), and applies a tier with the live adapter (`current_adapter`) and the
world's `TerrainVtPolicy`, as auto quality does; `before`/`after` and `render.get_profile` gain `tier`
(`QualityTier::of_settings`, null when customized), `preset` stays `DesktopLow` for Very Low; the result gains
`requested` (canonical name); `render.get_profile` gains `profile_names`; the unknown-name message lists them.
`configuration.packaged_profile` reports the packaged name (`VeryLow`). (4) `Regia.toml` validation,
`Platforms::render_profile` (canonical name into `build_info.json`), the editor's check, picker and setter take
`ProfileName::parse`; errors list `ProfileName::names()`. (5) The packaged game reads a `ProfileName`:
`PackagedConfig::render_profile_name` is new, `render_profile` answers the starting preset (Desktop Low for Very Low),
and the settings applier applies a packaged tier as the tier (GPU levers once the adapter is known, through the
existing `decide_gpu_levers` pass). (6) The showcase reads `--render-profile` with `take_profile_arg` /
`choose_profile`, so the N150 measured row of spec 13 § 3a can start `showcase --demo ... --render-profile VeryLow`.
No preset row, column or golden changes. No format version: `render_profile` in `Regia.toml` and `build_info.json`
is a free string and every old value parses as before.
Owner question Q1 of ADR-7977 (is 720p / 30 fps in 2.5 GiB RAM and 1.5 GiB GPU memory an engine promise?): the plan
default is written here until the owner rules. The tier, the name and the budget row are the engine's (every game
gets them); the performance promise is made only for the measured scene on the measured machine: the forest demo
scene on the Intel N150 min-spec laptop (the "N150 integrated_low row" of spec 13 § 3a). Any other GPU, scene or game
(DO27's maps included) is not promised; DO27 owns the rows for its maps.
Consequences: DO27 can write `render_profile = "VeryLow"` in `[platforms.windows]` and call `render.set_profile
{"preset":"VeryLow"}`. Host-visible API changes are listed under Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-very-low-profile-names.md` (new enum variant `PresetChoiceError::UnknownProfile` breaks
exhaustive matches; `PackagedConfig::render_profile` answers Desktop Low for a packaged Very Low). Spec 13 § 3a's
"(build A)" marks are removed for what landed; book `agents/render-profile.md` documents the names, `tier`,
`profile_names` and the errors. The agent protocol snapshot rows for the two methods were updated by hand; the lead
re-runs `cargo xtask agent-snapshot --update` and `cargo xtask manual`.

## ADR-8873: Multi-level frame budgets from the tunnels showcase scene; the layer stream counts the bytes its meshes hold (plan D8, D9, W-22; v07-tunnels-frame-bars)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v0.7 item E (tunnels showcase, part 2) asks for the D8 frame bars measured on the Regia-owned tunnels
scene (ADR-8825), the D9 counter fix, and the multi-level frame budgets (plan W-22) proposed with measured numbers.
DO27's proposal (phase-4 briefs, Q4): ULTRA, HIGH, LOW and the Deck at most 10 % over the same view outdoors, Deck
layer meshes at most 64 MB; ULTRA_LOW is the owner's floor (the N150 at Very Low, 1280x720, 30 fps, within 2.5 GB RAM
and 1.5 GB GPU memory with tunnels armed; ADR-7977, ADR-8844). D9: `LayerStreamStats::bytes` summed each resident
LOD's cooked record (`CookedChunkLod::bytes`, the postcard payload of the packed chunk mesh), while the stream holds a
`regia_render::CpuMesh` of 96-byte `LabVertex` vertices and `u32` indices per resident LOD, and the renderer uploads
the same 96-byte stride: W-31 measured 107-167 KB counted against 585 KB held on Switchbacks. On the level path
(`drive_layer_stream` with an `AssetServer`) each chunk LOD was also loaded with `AssetServer::load_mesh`, a typed load
that pins its id (ADR-7256): a second decoded copy (`regia_asset::CpuMesh`) of every LOD ever streamed stayed in the
server for the life of the server, evicted LODs included.
Decision: (1) D9 counter. `LayerStreamStats` gains `resident_bytes` and `coarsest_resident_bytes`: the bytes the
resident meshes hold, vertices and indices by capacity (`regia_terrain::layer_mesh_resident_bytes`). They are the
layer geometry's RAM and the size uploaded per drawn chunk, so the layer budgets (ULTRA_LOW 24 MB VRAM / 32 MB RAM,
the Deck's 64 MB) read them. `bytes`, `coarsest_bytes` and `budget_bytes` keep their meaning (cooked record bytes, the
unit the budget compares before a LOD loads) and say so in their docs and the agent page; `terrain.mesh_layers`
reports the two new fields. (2) D9 copy. The stream's mesh is the one CPU copy the draw needs (the entity's
`MeshRenderer` holds the same `Arc`; the stream keeps evicted-from-draw LODs for its hysteresis), so it stays. The
server's pinned copy is waste: `load_layer_chunk_mesh` (now public, the loader `drive_layer_stream` uses) reads the
cooked bytes with `AssetServer::read_cooked` and decodes them for the stream, so nothing is pinned or kept in
`AssetServer::meshes()`. (3) Not changed here, proposed: the budget in resident bytes needs each LOD's vertex count
in the presentation record (a `PRESENTATION_VERSION` bump with its migrator, for format batch 2, freezing 11-28); the
render vertex is 96 bytes for rigid meshes too (joints, weights, color: 48 bytes), a renderer change that would about
halve layer RAM and VRAM. (4) W-22 frame budgets, as perf-budget rows (`docs/perf/budgets.ron`, times as evidence;
the counts stay in tests): `tunnels_{tube,outdoor}_frame_gpu.{deck,n150,desktop}` read the frame job's `perf-frame`
lines (GPU frame p50 from the renderer's timestamps, view pair west). The N150 rows carry the ULTRA_LOW bar
(33.333 ms at Very Low, 1280x720). The Deck and desktop bars are relative (interior frame at most 1.10 x the same view
outdoors, the job's `interior_over_outdoor`): their rows are Unbudgeted evidence, because the registry compares one
number to a fixed limit. The layer-mesh count bars stay in `layer_memory_low_tiers` (now on `resident_bytes`).
Proposed bars (from DO27's Q4, with the measured numbers below): ULTRA (Desktop Ultra), HIGH (Desktop High), LOW
(Desktop Low) and the Deck: tube frame at most 1.10 x outdoor; Deck layer meshes at most 64 MB resident bytes;
ULTRA_LOW: Very Low at 1280x720 within 33.3 ms GPU frame, 2.5 GB process RAM and 1.5 GB GPU memory. The D8 bar as the
brief states it for the Deck (interior at most the outdoor frame, ratio 1.0) is the stricter form; this ADR proposes
DO27's 10 % margin and records both ratios.
Measured (`tests/tunnels_frames.rs`, view pairs of `perf_views.json`, 240 frames, GPU frame p50 from the renderer's
timestamps; JSON reports in `docs/evidence/v07-tunnels-frame-bars/`):

| Device | Profile, size | Pair | Tube ms | Outdoor ms | Ratio | Bar (DO27 1.10 / brief 1.0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steam Deck (plugged in), 3 rounds | Deck, 1280x800 | west | 18.70 / 19.15 / 19.21 | 21.86 / 21.85 / 21.73 | 0.855 / 0.877 / 0.884 | met / met |
| Steam Deck, 3 rounds | Deck, 1280x800 | east | 21.42 / 21.36 / 21.78 | 19.90 / 19.98 / 20.25 | 1.076 / 1.069 / 1.076 | met / **missed** |
| Steam Deck | Very Low, 1280x720 | west | 5.35 | 7.84 | 0.682 | (no bar) |
| RTX 5090 (the build server idx 0) | Desktop Ultra, 1920x1080 | west / east | 3.023 / 2.878 | 5.131 / 4.693 | 0.589 / 0.613 | met |
| RTX 5090 | Desktop High, 1920x1080 | west | 2.733 | 4.915 | 0.556 | met |
| RTX 5090 | Desktop Low, 1920x1080 | west | 0.756 | 1.612 | 0.469 | met |
| RTX 5090 | Deck, 1280x800 | west / east | 0.459 / 0.451 | 1.105 / 0.931 | 0.415 / 0.484 | met |
| RTX 5090 | Very Low, 1280x720 | west / east | 0.261 / 0.273 | 0.865 / 0.721 | 0.302 / 0.379 | met |
| Intel N150 (the min-spec Windows laptop, on AC), round 1 | Very Low, 1280x720 | west | 26.39 | **55.13** | 0.479 | 33.3 ms: tube met, **outdoor missed** |
| Intel N150, round 1 | Very Low, 1280x720 | east | 16.98 | **39.30** | 0.432 | 33.3 ms: tube met, **outdoor missed** |
| Intel N150, round 2 | Very Low, 1280x720 | west / east | 18.84 / 23.65 | **44.90** / **35.22** | 0.420 / 0.672 | tube met, **outdoor missed** |
| Intel N150, scene copy with `scatter: None` | Very Low, 1280x720 | west / east | 16.99 / 24.40 | **35.44** / 32.63 | 0.479 / 0.748 | west **missed**, east met |

The Deck's east pair misses the brief's ratio 1.0 by 7 % in every round and meets DO27's 10 %. Its passes (round 1,
tube vs outdoor): forward 14.03 vs 12.97 ms, post 2.44 vs 2.17, contact shadows 0.94 vs 0.67, prepass 1.08 vs 1.52,
TAAU 1.93 vs 1.88; the hitch report's own window agrees (GPU p50 20.25 vs 18.77 ms, 100 % GPU-bound). The tube's extra
cost is in the forward pass (+1.06 ms; the tube view is lit by the tube's point lights, 48 in the scene; this lane
did not split the pass further). The
terrain selects the same 814 quadtree nodes inside the tube as outdoors (the counter reads the CDLOD selection, not
what the portal cull then draws).
The N150 misses the ULTRA_LOW frame bar outdoors, not in the tube: forward is 43.32 ms of the west outdoor frame
(prepass 4.79, post 1.44, contact shadows 0.49) and 23.23 ms of the east one (prepass 3.64); the tube views are
26.39 ms (forward 20.75) and 16.98 ms (forward 12.03). The hitch report's window agrees (outdoor west GPU p50 59.0 ms,
p99 78.9; east 39.4 / 43.4; 100 % GPU-bound). Its memory is inside the bar: peak process RSS 1.44 GB after the tube
view's app and 1.96 GB after the second app of the same test process (the high-water mark of both), renderer GPU
memory 355 MB. The outdoor views look over the flat plain and its 6,311 (west) / 6,792 (east) rock scatter instances,
and the tube meshes the frustum keeps (they carry no `VisCell` tag, ADR-8825): the miss is the outdoor view's forward
pass at Very Low on this GPU. A copy of the scene without scatter (tunnels still armed) puts the outdoor views at 35.44 /
32.63 ms (forward 29.85 / 27.71): the rock scatter is about 10-20 ms of the miss, and the view without scatter (terrain, sky
and the tube meshes in view) still sits at the bar. The N150 varies between rounds (the same view moved up to 40 %: tube east 16.98 then 23.65
ms; W-31 saw its clock vary too), so its rows are rounds, not a p50 of rounds. ADR-8844's owner default
promises the Very Low bar only for the forest demo scene on this machine, so whether it binds a tunnels map outdoors
is the owner's ruling.
Deck memory: peak process RSS 0.56-0.81 GB, renderer GPU memory 398 MB (Very Low 327 MB). Layer meshes: the cooked
Switchbacks layer streamed along all 455 tube samples peaks at 671,268 resident bytes (190,109 cooked), far under the
Deck's 64 MB and ULTRA_LOW's 24 MB / 32 MB.
Consequences: hosts that build `LayerStreamStats` literally name the two fields (release fragment, Upgrade). A host
reading `AssetServer::meshes()` for streamed chunks finds none. The registry test `the_checked_in_registry_is_valid_and_its_targets_exist`
finds a row's package under `samples/` as well as `crates/`. Owner rulings asked: the 10 % margin vs the brief's 1.0,
and every bar missed in the table.

## ADR-8842: Mesh-layer chunks cross-fade their LOD switches; the level cook's sim ground honors the cooked count mapping
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Two v0.7 leftovers of the mesh-layer stream (plan § 2.2 item E). (1) ADR-8398's `drive_layer_stream` despawned
a chunk's entity and spawned the next LOD's in the same frame, so every LOD switch popped. The renderer already has a
host-driven dithered cross-fade (`regia_render::MeshLodFade`: `c` on the incoming LOD, `-c` on the outgoing one, every
pixel drawn by exactly one of them; the outgoing LOD casts no shadow), which the HLOD cut uses (ADR-2022). (2) ADR-8451's
level cook built its sim ground (`GroundInput`) from the level block's `world_width_m`, `height_scale_m` and
`height_offset_m`, but since ADR-8471 the run-time load builds a count source's terrain from the cooked index's
`CountMapping` instead (`LevelGround::source_mapping`, ignored by the cook). A count source therefore cooked at the wrong
width (one meter a sample) and heights (the block's legacy numbers), and at a placement (centered on the origin) that
differs from the drawn terrain whenever the grid's center is not the origin, which includes ADR-8063's default first
sample (`-n * cell_m / 2`, center `-cell_m / 2`).
Decision:
1. `TerrainLayerStream::fade_frames` (default `DEFAULT_LAYER_FADE_FRAMES` = 8; 0 or 1 = instant, the old behavior).
   When a drawn chunk changes LOD, `drive_layer_stream` spawns the new LOD's entity with `MeshLodFade(c)` and keeps the
   old one with `MeshLodFade(-c)`, `c = k / N` for the `k`-th frame of the fade (the switch frame is `k = 1`), so `N - 1`
   frames are dithered with shares `1/N .. (N-1)/N`; at `k = N` the old entity is despawned and the new one loses its
   `MeshLodFade` (drawn whole). A switch back to the outgoing LOD mid-fade continues from the share it had (the
   ADR-2022 rule); a switch to a third LOD despawns the outgoing entity and fades the current one out from whole. A
   chunk that leaves the stream (out of `visible_radius`) despawns both entities at once, as before; a chunk that
   appears is drawn whole at once. The outgoing entity's `MeshRenderer` holds its mesh by `Arc`, so an evicted LOD
   still draws until its fade ends (the stream's `bytes` does not count it). `TerrainLayerStream::fading()` counts the
   fades in flight; `terrain.mesh_layers` reports `stream.fade_frames` and `stream.fading`.
2. The level cook (`level_job`) builds the sim ground from the run-time map when the cooked index carries a count
   mapping: `LevelGround::mapped_map(block)` is the run-time load's own `mapping_map` (the same `level_terrain_mapping`
   refusals, including a block `world_width_m` that contradicts the mapping), and the ground takes `width_m =
   map.world_width()` (`(n - 1) * cell_m`, one rounding), `offset_m = map.height_offset()` (`-zero_counts *
   meters_per_count`) and `step_m = meters_per_count`. The canonical lattice is centered on the origin (spec 121 § 3;
   `WorldGeomCooked` has no origin), so a mapping whose grid center (`map.grid_origin()`) is not `[0, 0]` is refused with
   the new cook code `meshlayers_ground_offset`, naming the center and the first sample that centers the grid
   (`-(n - 1) * cell_m / 2`), never cooked offset. Without a mapping the ground is the legacy rule, unchanged.
   Heights: the lattice evaluates `offset_m + count * step_m` (frozen, Stage A's formula), the run-time map
   `(count - zero_counts) * meters_per_count`; they are equal in exact arithmetic and equal bit for bit when the
   products are exact (the test fixture's 0.125 m a count); otherwise they can differ by about one `f32` ulp of the
   height (3.8e-6 m at 40 m), far under the lattice's millimeter.
Consequences: `TerrainLayerStream` gains a public field (it has private fields, so no struct literal breaks) and a
method; new `pub const DEFAULT_LAYER_FADE_FRAMES`. `LevelMeshLayersError` gains `GroundOffset` (exhaustive matches
break); `LevelGround::mapped_map` is new. Hosts that relied on one `TerrainLayerChunk` entity per chunk see two during a
fade (set `fade_frames = 0` for the old behavior). A dithered chunk draws through the alpha-test pipeline variant of its
material (the renderer's rule for `MeshLodFade`); whether the frame warm covers that variant is checked by the warm test
the lane report lists. No format, shader, sim, `QUERY_BITS_VERSION`, Stage A or golden change; a count-source level whose
map has mesh layers recooks with a different (correct) ground and `content_hash`. W-16's chunks still cut the canonical
triangles, not W-07's subdivided render mesh (ADR-8576 follow-up, not in this lane). Specs/docs: book/agents/
terrain-mesh-layers.md (stream fields, cook ground with a mapping, `meshlayers_ground_offset`).

## ADR-8874: Shadow views per cell, and the heightfield fills the sun cover (v07-interior-cull-shadows)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 left two sun-shadow gaps underground (plan v0.7 item E, § 2.2). KI-RN-007: indoor
cells did not cull shadow views; a culled cell's draws stayed in every sun cascade as shadow-only
casters (spec 25 § 7.7 "needs design": the cascades see unreached cells through openings). KI-RN-004:
sun sealing (ADR-8414) needs a `SunCover` the host fills; the heightfield did not fill it.
Decision:
1. Shadow views per cell (receiver-side, no cover). A sun shadow matters only on a visible receiver.
   The visible receivers of a frame lie in the boxes of the cells its views reach and, outdoors, in
   the narrowed frusta their walks record into cell 0 (ADR-8413/8843). After the colour, light and
   seal stages, `cull_unreachable_cells` sweeps the world AABB of each rigid sun caster of an
   unreached cell along the sun's travel for every `t >= 0`, grown by `SHADOW_VIEW_MARGIN_M` (1 m:
   filter kernels, normal offset, texel snapping) plus `SHADOW_VIEW_SPREAD · t` (0.02, about 1.1°,
   four times the sun's angular radius: penumbrae). Against an oriented cell box the test is exact
   per axis in the box's frame (`shadow_sweep_touches_box`: each axis gives an interval of `t`);
   against a frustum it is a separating-plane test (`shadow_sweep_touches_planes`: a plane with the
   box's farthest corner more than the margin outside that the sweep never turns toward). Both err
   toward touching. A draw whose sweep touches nothing gets `SUN_SEALED_SHADOW` (or, shadow-only in a
   frame without local lights, leaves the frame). The cull stands down while any view sees the
   outdoors unrestricted (an outdoor or doorway eye, a capped or overflowing walk) or a texture view
   reaches cell 0 (it records no outdoor frusta). Switch: `VisCellShadowViews { cull }` (a separate
   resource, default on, so `VisCellSettings` literals do not break). Counters:
   `VisCellStats::shadow_view_{active,tested,culled_draws,dropped_draws}`.
2. The heightfield cover (`regia_terrain::sun_cover`, opt-in `TerrainSunCover`). In `Render`
   between `extract_frame` (its sun) and the cull, `update_terrain_sun_cover` fills `SunCover` with
   the indoor cells whose every box passes `box_covered` against some terrain: the lowest cover
   over the swept footprint is the minimum of the min-max pyramid's nodes over it (a level with at
   most 16 nodes a side), the footprint grown by `grow_m`, default two cells of the root's
   decimated shadow grid (`coarsest_shadow_cell_m`): a shadow pass draws that grid at the coarsest,
   and its triangles interpolate samples up to a cell away and morph toward the next level. A hole
   (`Terrain::holes`, the open mouths' lattice cut) over the grown sweep, or a sweep that leaves the
   map, is a gap. Recomputed only when the sun, the cells, a terrain or the setting change.
3. Agent: `render.viscells` reports `frame.shadow_view_*`, `shadow_views` and `terrain_sun_cover`;
   `render.set_viscells` takes `shadow_views` and `terrain_sun_cover` booleans (no new error code:
   F0002 for wrong types and for a host `sun_cover` together with `terrain_sun_cover: true`).
Consequences: Casters below or beside the eye's tube leave the cascades with no host work; an outdoor
eye draws exactly as before. The traced sun scene loses the culled casters too (as the seal's do);
it shadows only on-screen pixels. Local-light shadow views, fog lights, procedural sets, scatter,
water, VFX and decals are still not cell-culled in shadow views (KI-RN-007 narrows to those). The
default growth is conservative on big maps (the root's cell is the map width over 16): a host with
known cascade texels passes less. Streamed tile holes are read only through `Terrain::holes`.
Measured (the build server lavapipe, `viscells_shadow_views`): with the eye in a tube the sun casters per
cascade go from [4, 4, 4, 4] (cull off) to [3, 3, 3, 3]; the culled frame is bit-identical to the
frame where the removed caster casts nothing and to the one where it lies 300 m deeper. Against the
frame with the cull off it differs in 517 of 24576 bytes by at most 3: in that scene an extra caster
inside a cascade's footprint perturbs unshadowed texels that little wherever it lies (moving it out of reach
removes the change), a renderer property this cull does not cause; the cause is not isolated. New
`VisCellStats` fields break struct literals (fragment, Upgrade). Updated: `book/agents/viscells.md`,
spec 25 § 7.7, `book/COVERAGE.md`, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-8878: The integrated-GPU budget row `integrated_low` and Very Low's streaming column (ADR-7977 build B)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7977 (spec 13 § 3a) designed the integrated-GPU floor in two builds; build A (ADR-8844) made the Very Low
tier selectable by name. DO27 still had no memory budget row for its floor (2.5 GiB RAM, 1.5 GiB GPU memory), and a
16 GB integrated laptop such as the min-spec N150 is "large" by the low-memory rule (`low_memory::INTEGRATED_LARGE_RAM_MIB`,
15,000 MiB), so at Very Low it streamed textures with Desktop Low's 1 GiB, eager, not the integrated cap.
Decision: build B as spec 13 § 3a states it. (1) `BudgetTier::IntegratedLow` appended (`ALL` = Minimum, Deck,
DesktopHigh, IntegratedLow; name `integrated_low`); `MemoryBudget::for_tier` RAM 2560 MiB, VRAM 1536 MiB with the
arithmetic in its doc; Minimum's doc says "the discrete-GPU minimum". `BudgetTier::names()` (new) lists the names in
`ALL` order. The other exhaustive matches: the frame work ratchet's `tier_resolution` (1280, 720) and `tier_preset`
Desktop Low (Very Low's internal targets are a ninth of Low's at the same output, so Desktop Low at the full 720p is an
upper bound); `ClusterResidency::for_tier` half the Deck's row, 128 MiB / 4 MiB / 128 MiB / 16 MiB (★ until measured;
residency is off at Desktop Low, so it only bounds a host that turns it on); `baked_gi_budget` follows the vram / 8
rule: 192 MiB. `HostMemoryBudget` is per preset, not per tier, so Very Low already gets Desktop Low's row; nothing
changes there. (2) `QualityTier::very_low_columns` also writes the integrated texture cap: a budgeted, enabled
policy's `budget_mib` becomes `min(budget_mib, INTEGRATED_STREAM_BUDGET_MIB)` (384) and `eager` false. The 15,000 MiB
rule and `REGIA_INTEGRATED_LIMITS` are unchanged; a discrete card at Very Low still grows the budget to its VRAM share
every frame; `RenderSettings::preset()` still answers Desktop Low (its whole-profile comparison takes Very Low's
profile, column included). (3) Agent: `render.memory_budget {"tier":"integrated_low"}`; the unknown-tier message
lists `BudgetTier::names()` instead of a hard-coded list. Nothing selects the budget tier automatically; the default
stays `minimum`. (4) The frame work ratchet gains the `integrated_low` VRAM row (`forward_box/DesktopLow/1280x720`),
recorded on lavapipe; no other row is edited. (5) The N150 measured row: a kit outside the repo, run by the lane on
2026-11-20 (S1 and S3 on Vulkan and DX12, all lines pass; `docs/perf-log.md` "N150 integrated_low row"). The binary
was built with the windows-gnu toolchain on the test machine because no build host has cargo-xwin any more (the design
named an MSVC build); the engine code is the same.
Two tests that iterated every tier change with the tier list: `baked_gi::memory::a_layout_a_split_fits_is_within_the_binding`
asserted that a ~233 MiB split layout fits every tier; with a 192 MiB tier it now asserts that each tier fits exactly
when its share holds the parts, no tier is over the binding (the test's point), and the three original tiers still fit.
`regia bake-gi --dry-run`'s test lists the four tier names. Both report an extra `integrated_low` entry by design.
Owner question Q3 of ADR-7977 (a real 8 GB integrated-GPU laptop for the build machines) is not this lane's: listed for the
owner, recommended answer unchanged (no purchase unless DO27's testers report paging on 8 GB machines).
Consequences: a new `BudgetTier` variant breaks exhaustive matches in host code (Upgrade in
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-integrated-low-budget.md`); every per-tier report (`render.memory_budget`, baked GI memory
in `regia bake-gi --dry-run` / `--check-volume` and the level baked GI method) gains an `integrated_low` entry; Very
Low's texture budget is 384 MiB lazy on large-RAM integrated machines (it was 1 GiB eager). Spec 13 § 3a's "(build B)"
marks are removed for what landed; book `agents/instant-load.md`, `agents/load-memory.md` and
`agents/low-memory-gpus.md` document the tier and the column. No format, preset row or golden changes. Provenance:
none (budget arithmetic, no algorithm).

## ADR-8848: Window screenshots reuse their readback, PNG and reply buffers
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8782 (Steam Deck pass, v0.6.0) found each window `seeing.screenshot` adding about 10 MB of RSS, +63 MB
over twenty shots in five steps that then stop: glibc's dynamic mmap threshold keeps the freed frame copy, PNG,
base64 text and serialized reply (built on a fresh connection thread per `regia agent call`) in its arenas. Pinning
the threshold with `mallopt` was ruled out by its A/B (90 -> 61 fps at the 90 cap). Per shot the app side allocated
a mappable GPU buffer, a frame-sized RGBA8 vector (plus one clone per extra request of the same frame), the PNG
(the encoder's whole compressed stream first, then the file), the base64 string, the serialized JSON and
tungstenite's copy of the one reply frame into its write buffer.
Decision: same-size shots after the first allocate nothing image-sized. (1) `regia_render::screenshot` (now a
public module) has `BufferPool`, a mutex-guarded list of at most N byte vectors (largest kept 64 MiB,
`MAX_POOLED_BUFFER_BYTES`; take = smallest fitting, else the largest grown by an eighth more; give with the pool
full frees the smallest), and three statics: `FRAME_BUFFERS` (2, readback pixels), `ENCODE_BUFFERS` (1, PNG
bytes), `REPLY_BUFFERS` (4, base64 text and serialized replies). `screenshot::recycle` gives an image's pixels
back; `release_screenshot_buffers` empties all three, called when the renderer drops its window surfaces (suspend,
exit, a lost surface). (2) Each `WindowSurface` keeps up to two mappable readback buffers (`ReadbackBuffers`; a
capture of another size frees the old ones); they go with the surface. `read_texture_rgba` is the public one-call
form. The last request of a frame takes the capture itself instead of a clone. (3) `regia_agent::image::png_base64`
streams the PNG (`png::StreamWriter`, 64 KiB IDAT chunks: the same deflate stream at the same level, split into
more chunks; pixels are identical) into an `ENCODE_BUFFERS` vector and the base64 into a `REPLY_BUFFERS` vector.
The window screenshot callback and `finish_capture` recycle the image after encoding and move the base64 string into
the reply map (`seeing::png_reply`): `json!` serializes an expression by reference, which cloned the reply text every
shot (the new test found it: one 2,331,328-byte request per shot, the exact base64 length). (4) The WebSocket server
serializes a reply whose top-level strings reach 64 KiB into a `REPLY_BUFFERS` vector (owned by a `Bytes` that
gives it back on drop), sends it as one text message in 64 KiB frames (RFC 6455 § 5.4 continuation frames, so
tungstenite's write buffer stays about 192 KiB instead of a reply-sized copy), and gives the reply's large strings
back after sending. Smaller replies are sent as before.
Consequences: measured by the two new tests (regia_agent `screenshot_buffer_reuse`: real server, a fresh
connection per shot, a 1280 x 800 capture; regia_render `screenshot_readback_reuse` on lavapipe); numbers are in the
lane report. Steady memory after the first shot holds the pools (about 4 MB pixels + PNG + 2 x base64 for a Deck
frame, about the first shot's step today) and one or two readback buffers per window. Host-visible: replies of
64 KiB or more arrive as several WebSocket frames of one message (every WebSocket library reassembles them; the
repo's clients are tungstenite); the module `regia_render::screenshot` is public with the pool API. What is left per
shot is per connection and per encode (tungstenite's 128 KiB read buffer, the deflate state), not per image byte.
The Deck RSS before/after over twenty shots is owed (lane report). A closed secondary window's surface is never
dropped today (the renderer drops surfaces only on suspend, exit and loss), so its readback buffers live until then;
recorded for the lead, not changed here.

## ADR-8833: Fast exit (hide, bounded flush, `_exit`) and a per-user single-instance lock
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Absorb plan row P-07 (v0.7, "ready for DO27 to switch"). DO27's shell carried its own fast quit
(`fast_quit.rs`) and single-instance guard (`single_instance.rs`) because the engine's only exit, the clean
exit (ADR-188), drops the world object by object and then the device with the window still on screen: with
part of the game in swap a quit took seconds to minutes, and the N150 showcase quit hung once in five
(KI-RB-003). Two copies of a game for one user shared save and cache files and one could be left running
unseen. Both are engine-general.
Decision: (1) `regia_platform::ExitMode { Clean (default), Fast }` (resource). `request_fast_exit(world, code,
reason, delay_frames)` arms a hard deadline (`FastExitSettings::hard_deadline`, default 3 s, exit code 5,
`None` in in-process tests), hides every OS window in the request frame through the `platform/<os>.rs` seam
(`hide_window_now`: X11 unmap and Win32 `SW_HIDE` and macOS `orderOut` through winit; Wayland a null buffer
attach and commit through the libwayland-client winit loaded, adapted from the DO27 source), sets
`SurfacesHidden` so the renderer presents nothing more (a Wayland surface given a null buffer must not get
a new buffer), runs the hosts' `ExitHooks::on_fast_hide` hooks, records a `FastExitRequest` and writes
`AppExit` (a host loop that never polls exits cleanly). The runner calls `poll_fast_exit` after each update:
at `flush_frame` it begins a deliberate exit (ADR-276) with the request's code, builds the
`ExitHooks::add_flush` jobs on the frame thread and runs them in parallel threads inside
`FastExitSettings::flush_budget` (default 1.5 s) with an fsync of the files given to `keep_file_on_fast_exit`,
logs and prints one `regia fast exit:` line, flushes stdio (bounded) and ends with `exit_immediately`. While
a fast exit waits for its frame the runner starts no clean exit. In `ExitMode::Fast` every `AppExit` the
runner sees becomes a fast exit (`AppExit::Error(n)` exits `n`). The agent's `quit.request` takes an
optional `mode` (`clean` default, `fast`); `fast` ignores `ClosePolicy` and delays the flush one frame
(`FAST_QUIT_DELAY_FRAMES`) so the reply leaves the socket. (2) `SingleInstanceLock::acquire(app_id, wait)`:
an OS file lock (`std::fs::File::try_lock`: `flock` on Linux and macOS, `LockFileEx` on Windows) on a per-user
path from the seam (`instance_lock_dir`: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` else temp dir with the uid; macOS per-user
`$TMPDIR`; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RegiaEngine\instance`), retried for `wait`, refused with `AlreadyRunning { holder }`
(codes `already_running`, `instance_lock_io`; `EXIT_ALREADY_RUNNING` = 75); Windows raises the holder's window
(`raise_instance_window`). The holder's pid lives in a sidecar `<lock>.pid` that a clean release removes
before unlocking, so a pid found next to a free lock is a dead holder: the lock is taken over and reported
(`took_over_from`). Without file-lock support the pid record decides with `process_alive` (`kill(pid, 0)`;
`OpenProcess` + `GetExitCodeProcess`): a live or unknown pid refuses, a dead one is taken over. Android takes
no lock (one task per app is the OS's rule) and returns an OS-managed guard. `REGIA_ALLOW_MULTI_INSTANCE`
skips the lock. DO27's A/B exit modes (teardown, sync, linger, windowed), its quit report upload, telemetry,
lifeline and shutdown screen, and its startup-origin log line are game-side and not absorbed.
Consequences: New public API in `regia_platform` (see the release fragment v0.1.28-v07-fast-quit-single-instance);
`ExitHooks` gains two private fields (it has no public fields, so no struct literal breaks). `quit.request`
gains an optional parameter and three reply fields in fast mode. The renderer does not register a fast flush
job for the pipeline cache yet (a follow-up; the clean exit still saves it); a fast exit loses only cache
warmth. No format, dependency or permission change. Specs: book/agents/process-guards.md, book/agents/loop.md.
Provenance: docs/provenance.md and docs/ported-sources.toml rows (DO27 regia-absorb-4 c9513623f, adapt).

## ADR-8835: Build-container profiles for Linux packages (C-26)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row C-26 (absorb plan § 2; v0.7 area F) asks for build-in-container profiles for `regia package` so
Linux builds run on the oldest glibc players have: a Steam runtime profile (sniper, glibc 2.31) and Debian 12
(glibc 2.36). ADR-148 chose cargo-zigbuild over the sniper SDK container (same glibc baseline, no container engine
needed), and that stays the default; but zigbuild only relinks against an old glibc's symbol list, while C and C++
dependencies still compile with the build machine's headers and `libstdc++`. A game project's two shell build
scripts (DO27 `shell-regia/tools/steam/steam_build.sh` and `tools/portable/portable_build.sh` at tag regia-absorb-4
c9513623f, mark "requirements", class P1; read as data, nothing copied) record what such builds need: the sniper SDK
with clang as the C compiler (its GCC 10 cannot build some AVX2 intrinsics; a newer GCC's `libstdc++` emits GLIBCXX
symbols the runtime lacks), a Debian 12 image, sources mounted read-only, a cargo home and target directory per
container, and a glibc symbol-version gate on the result (run through `objdump`). The first lane on this row stopped
BLOCKED on unreachable hosts and wrote no code.
Decision: (1) `regia package --platform linux --container steam-sniper|debian12` (`regia_cli::commands::package_container`)
builds the binary inside a container. Base images are pinned by digest, never a moving tag:
`registry.gitlab.steamos.cloud/steamrt/sniper/sdk@sha256:ee829e44…` (tag 3.0.20261110.268881) and
`docker.io/library/debian@sha256:268fb24c…` (tag bookworm-20261104), digests read from the public registries on
2026-11-19. The first run builds `localhost/regia-build-<profile>:<rustc>-<digest12>` from a generated Containerfile
(minimal rustup install of the host's `rustc` version; the Debian profile adds the CI's Linux build packages);
`--container-image` runs a prepared image instead, accepted only when pinned by digest or a local image with a
version tag (`container_image_unpinned`). (2) The tool is found at run time: `REGIA_CONTAINER_TOOL`, else podman,
else docker; none is `container_tool_missing` (never a panic). (3) The cargo workspace and `--container-mount`
directories are mounted read-only at their host paths (so `--remap-path-prefix` and messages agree, and path
dependencies resolve), cargo runs with `--locked` (`container_lockfile_missing` without a lock file), and the target
directory and cargo home are `<target>/container/<profile>/{target,cargo-home}`. docker runs as the workspace owner's
uid:gid; rootless podman needs nothing. The sniper profile sets `CC=clang`, `CXX=clang++`. (4) The floor is the
profile's glibc; `--glibc` must equal it and `--steam` refuses `debian12` (`container_glibc_conflict`); a non-Linux
platform is `container_platform_unsupported`, a non-Linux host `container_host_unsupported`. (5) The glibc gate is
the existing staged-binary check, which now reads the newest `GLIBC_x.y` from the ELF `SHT_GNU_verneed` table and
`DT_NEEDED` from the dynamic section (`commands::elf_versions`, `regia_framework`'s object reader) instead of running
`objdump`, and names the library the newest version comes from. (6) `agent.package` takes `container`
(`package_bad_container` otherwise); `regia package --json` reports the container codes as `error.code`.
Consequences: Packaging a Linux game no longer needs binutils. Container builds are opt-in; zigbuild stays the
default (ADR-148 amended, not superseded). The images are x86_64; no emulation. The real container build is tested
only where an image is already present (`REGIA_CONTAINER_TEST_IMAGE`; farm hosts never pull), so the generated
toolchain images' end-to-end run is owed on a machine with network access. Host-visible: three new `PackageArgs`
fields, `LinuxBinaryReport::max_glibc_from`, the objdump text parsers test-only. Specs updated: `21` § 4 (Linux).
Book: `user-guide/packaging.md` (Build containers), `agents/cook-package.md` (Build containers). No new dependency,
no format change.

## ADR-8845: Overlay asset roots in the live cooker and at runtime
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8155 fills missing glTF buffers and images from `[cook.overlay_roots]` in the batch cook only. Its known
issues were that the live cooker (`LiveCooker`, `cook_sources`) did not fill, so a live cook of a glTF whose payload
lives in an overlay root failed where `regia cook` succeeded, and that the runtime never searched overlay roots, so a
source the game reads directly in a dev tree (a data table, a curve table, ...) was found only when a batch cook had
copied it into `assets/`. DO27 ships content in layered roots (v0.7 plan § 2.2 item F, C-08). The lane brief's
acceptance line "an asset in both resolves to the overlay" contradicts the batch cook's accepted order (ADR-8155: a
file already in the project wins; the earliest overlay root fills a hole). The brief also requires "the same root
order as the batch cook".
Decision: (1) The configuration reader (`OverlayRoots`, `OVERLAY_ROOTS_ENV`) moves to the runtime crate as
`regia_asset::overlay_roots`; `regia_asset_pipeline::overlay_roots` re-exports both, so callers do not change.
(2) `regia_asset::SourceRoots` resolves a path relative to `assets/` in the batch cook's order: anything at
`assets/<rel>` (file, directory or symlink) wins; then the earliest existing overlay root where the path, checked by
`regia_core::project_path::check_relative`, is a file whose resolved target stays inside that root. `None` otherwise;
`path_for` then gives `assets/<rel>` so "not found" errors name the project path as before. The project branch keeps
the old `assets.join(rel)` behavior unchanged. (3) `AssetServer` reads the roots when it opens (a bad table is a
warning there and only `assets/` is searched: the cook already fails on it) and exposes `source_roots()` and
`source_path(rel)`. The data table, curve table, chooser, table source, UI animation pack and loose color LUT runtime
readers use `source_path`. The `dev-assets` source watcher also watches the overlay roots; a data table served from an overlay root
reloads on its file's change only while that file is the one the resolver picks. (4) `cook_sources` fills the holes of
its `.gltf` targets with `fill_gltf_documents` (the batch fill's lookup and refusals, without the walk) before it
cooks; a bad table fails that call with an `Io` error naming `Regia.toml`, as the batch cook fails. It does not write
`overlay_fill.json`. (5) `LiveCooker` watches the existing overlay roots. A change under one runs the batch walk's fill
once, then maps the change to `assets/<same path>` so the glTFs that read it re-cook; the overlay path is still
forwarded as a directly-read source. (6) `cook.overlay_roots` gains an optional `path` and a `resolved` result key
(`{ path, found, source, root_index, file }` or `null`) and the error code `overlay_path_invalid`. On the order
conflict the lane follows ADR-8155 (project, then earliest overlay) and reads "an asset in both" as "in two overlay
roots" (the earlier one wins); a project file overriding an overlay file would make a direct read disagree with the
cooked bytes of the same path. Owner or lead ruling wanted if "overlay over project" was meant; it would be a change
to ADR-8155's fill as well.
Consequences: A live cook writes the same cooked blobs as a batch cook for a glTF whose payload is in an overlay root
(test `live_overlay`). Directly-read sources resolve from overlay roots in dev trees. A filled payload is a hard link
or a copy that the fill never refreshes: an editor that saves an overlay file by rename leaves the project's earlier
copy in place (the batch rule, unchanged); in-place writes reach the hard link. Runtime readers outside the six named
still join `assets/` themselves (baked GI volumes, levels, loading screens). `collect_data_table_changes` gains
an `Option<Res<AssetServer>>` parameter. No content format changed; no new dependency. Spec 12 is unchanged (the
overlay roots are a cook setting documented in `book/agents/cook-overlay-roots.md`).

## ADR-8557: release verify, diff, and upload plan
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row C-16 (owner-approved DO27-absorb, 2026-11-16). A packed release directory needs
a check against its manifests, a diff of two releases, and an ordered upload plan. The behavior
was rewritten in Rust from the requirements at pin `c9513623f` (`regia-absorb-4`). Python was not
copied. C-15 already writes the chunks and `release-chunks` manifests. This row reads them. It
does not replace `regia engine verify` or `regia engine chunk verify`.
Decision: add `regia release verify`, `regia release diff` and `regia release upload-plan`, plus
agent methods `release.verify` and `release.diff`. Shallow verify compares sizes and SHA-256.
Deep verify also decompresses every chunk and checks members, recorded member hashes, and
`content_key`. Diff reports a path that moved between chunks once, and the bytes to download per
platform. The upload command prints an ordered plan (chunks, then payload, then manifests) and
does not contact a host. A later row adds the upload backend. The archive cap stays
`DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` (1.9 GiB). JSON documents are schema 1.
Consequences: hosts that match top-level `regia` commands exhaustively must accept `release`.
`ReleaseCommand` is a new enum. `release.verify` and `release.diff` are new protocol methods
(permission Read, not mutating). A verify report with problems is still a successful agent
result whose `ok` field is false; a missing directory is `release_dir` and an unreadable diff
input is `release_input`. No new third-party crate. No format version bump. `regia upgrade-project`
does not gain a row. The lead runs `cargo xtask manual`. Display sizes are not lockstep math.

## ADR-8687: release manifest signatures and filesystem upload
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: Plan row C-17 (owner-approved DO27-absorb, 2026-11-16). A packed release directory
needs a detached signature on its manifests and an upload backend that follows the C-16 plan.
The behavior was rewritten in Rust from the requirements at pin `c9513623f` (`regia-absorb-4`,
`tools/ops/release_sign.sh`). The shell script was not copied. The brief drops git tags, SSH
signing, timestamp calendars, network calendars and a hosted CLI. Those are a later lane.
Decision: `regia release sign <dir> --key <path> --date YYYY-MM-DD` writes `<manifest>.sig`
beside each manifest. The signed bytes are a release-specific domain, the manifest file name,
the SHA-256 of the manifest, and the date. The key file is the one `regia assets keygen`
writes. A key inside the project is `content_key_in_project` and is not read. `regia release
verify` checks a signature that is present, and requires one with `--require-signature`.
`UploadBackend` has `list`, `put` and `publish`. `FsBackend` and `FakeBackend` are the only
backends. `regia release upload --backend fs:<dir>` follows the C-16 order and writes
`PUBLISHED`. There is no network. The agent method is `release.sign_status` (Read, not
mutating). Ed25519 uses the existing workspace crate `ring`. The key id uses the existing
workspace crate `blake3`. No new third-party crate. No format version bump.
Consequences: `ReleaseCommand` gains `Sign` and `Upload`. `VerifyArgs` gains
`require_signature` and `trust_key`. `VerifyOptions` gains `require_signature` and
`trusted_keys`. Hosts that match `release` subcommands or agent methods exhaustively must
accept the new names. `release.sign_status` returns `release_dir` for a missing directory and
a successful result with `ok: false` when a signature does not verify. `.sig` files are
payload in the C-16 plan, so they upload before manifests. The lead runs `cargo xtask manual`
and `cargo xtask adr-index`. Display and signature checks are not lockstep math.

## ADR-8846: release upload through a hosting CLI; `release-signature` v1 registered (format batch 2)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v0.7 area F and row C-09. ADR-8687 shipped `regia release upload --backend fs:<dir>` and left the
hosted upload for a later lane: a release host is reached through its own uploader program. The `.sig` sidecar
(`RELEASE_SIGNATURE_FORMAT` 1) had no format-registry row, so a field change would not fail `check-formats`.
Decision: (1) `--backend cli:<config.toml>` runs the configured program once per planned file as a child process
(`std::process::Command`, no shell), arguments from templates in a TOML config with the version key
`upload_cli = 1`: `program`, `put` (must pass `{file}`), optional `list` (`SIZE NAME` lines; same-size files are
skipped), optional `publish`, `secret_env`, `vars`, `timeout_s` (default 1800, 1 to 86400). Placeholders `{file}`,
`{name}`, `{dir}` and `vars` keys; unknown keys and placeholders are refused (`upload_cli_config`); `--var
key=value` overrides a defined key. Credentials reach the child only through the environment variables
`secret_env` names (`upload_cli_env` when unset). A config whose program, arguments or vars contain a credential
value is refused before anything runs (`upload_cli_secret`). Every credential value of 4 bytes or more is replaced
with `<redacted:NAME>` in every command line, output tail (2 KiB per stream kept), JSON field and error. A `put`
that exits non-zero is retried up to `--retries` attempts; a time-out (`upload_cli_timeout`) is not retried; a
failed `put` never publishes. `--dry-run` prints the command lines and whether each credential variable is set,
and starts nothing; the agent method `release.upload_dry_run` (Read) answers the same plan. `UploadBackend` gains a provided method `put_file` (default: read and `put`) so a backend can
hand a path to a program. (2) The sidecar is registered as `release-signature` v1 in format batch 2: schema
fingerprint `format,algorithm,key_id,public_key,date,manifest_sha256,signature`, `SignatureDocument` now refuses
unknown fields (unreleased, so no bump), `canonical_signature_json` and `peek_signature_version`, an
`upgrade-project` row (`.json.sig`, unmigrated; a `.json.sig` that does not read as this format is skipped), the
corpus fixture `release-signature/v1.json` (the writer's output for the throwaway seed `[7; 32]`, checked byte for
byte by a test), the fuzz target `release.signature`, the spec 12 rows and the `format-hashes.ron` row. (3) Plan
row C-09: `plan_tree_compressed` and `regia engine chunk plan --compressed [--scratch DIR]` count the chunks and
compressed bytes `cut` writes with the same codec, by cutting into a scratch directory that is removed afterwards;
`PlannedGroup` gains `compressed_bytes`. The closure `entry` param already exists on `editor.content_chunks_set_rule`.
Consequences: `ReleaseUploadArgs` gains `var` (struct literals break). `UploadBackend` gains a provided method
(implementors are unaffected). `regia_release_chunks` exports `CliBackend`, `CliCall`, `UploadCliConfig`,
`BackendSpec`, `parse_backend`, `parse_listing`, `redact`, `resolve_secrets`, `MIN_SECRET_LEN`,
`UPLOAD_CLI_FORMAT` and the signature-format items. `parse_fs_backend` no longer says a hosting CLI is a later lane.
The `upload_cli` config is a tool config read only by this command and is not registered as a content format; if
the lead wants it frozen too, it needs its own row. A real hosting program was not run (no account or credential
in any lane); tests drive a fake CLI that is the test binary itself. Specs updated: spec 12 § 4a rows,
`docs/formats/release-signature.md`, `book/agents/release-sign.md`.

## ADR-8871: Terrain index v3: the source grid's Z spacing and valid-data mask (format batch 2)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: A raster descriptor (ADR-8542) describes count grids with a different spacing on Z than on X and samples
without data. The cooked terrain index v2 holds one cell size (`CountMapping::cell_m`) and no mask, so the cook refuses
both (`terrain_mapping_unrepresentable`, `terrain_raster_missing_data`), and the import-chain review named this a limit
of index v2 to lift in a later format batch. Format batch 2 (v0.7, owner-approved 2026-11-19, freeze 2026-11-28) listed
"terrain-index v3" twice: once for w11-index-build's fixed-width counts and once for this lane. w11-index-build
(ADR-8816) changed `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` (`<map>.meshlayers`), not `terrain/index`, so there is no earlier
terrain-index step on the line to fold into: this is the one v0.7 step of `terrain-index`. The overview cache
descriptor digest (plan W-19, import-chain review finding 3) is `<stem>.overview.json`, a separate, unregistered cache
file, not part of this format; it is settled in the same ADR (last paragraph of the decision) because the batch row
named it.
Decision: `TERRAIN_INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION` 2 → 3. Two optional entries follow `source_mapping`:
`source_spacing_z_m: Option<f32>` (Z spacing when it differs from X; equal spacing is always `None`) and
`source_valid_mask: Option<TerrainValidMaskIndex>` (cols, rows, missing count, packed LSB-first bits in canonical
south/west row-major order, `1` = has data; all-valid is `None`). `CountMapping` is unchanged, so its canonical bytes and
every cook hash that frames them stay as they were. The loader decodes a v1 or v2 payload with its own shape (both
entries `None`) and validates the v3 entries (`TerrainIndexError::BadSourceGrid`: needs the mapping, finite positive Z
spacing not equal to X with a representable extent; mask of the mapping's grid, exact byte count, zero padding,
`missing` equal to the bits' zeros, neither none nor every sample missing). `regia upgrade-project` migrates v1 and v2
files (same row, decode → re-encode, header kept; idempotent). The cook keeps refusing unequal spacing and missing
samples: the run-time `TerrainMap` has one cell size and no hole policy reads a mask yet, and every consumer builds the
map from `source_mapping` alone. To keep a v3 index that holds either entry from being misread, the level loader refuses
it with `level_terrain_mapping` (`TerrainIndex::source_grid_unsupported`, the same `terrain_mapping_unrepresentable` /
`terrain_raster_missing_data` prefixes as the cook). `TerrainIndex::with_source_grid` builds the three entries from a
`TerrainSource`; `ValidMask::to_packed_bytes` / `from_packed_bytes` are the bit layout. `assets.terrain_tiles` reports
`source_grid { spacing_m, missing_samples } | null`.
W-19: the overview descriptor moves to `overview_descriptor` 2 and gains `descriptor_digest`, the BLAKE3 of the compact
JSON of every other field with object keys sorted. `cached_overview` recomputes it, so an added field or a hand edit
(the mapping, say) is a cache miss and the pair bakes again, instead of reporting a georeference the bake did not make.
The file stays an unregistered cache: a version-1 pair is stale and rebakes; no migrator, no format-hashes row.
Consequences: the shape freezes in v0.7, so the TerrainMap spacing work (format batch 2's TerrainMap row) and a cook hole
policy can start writing and reading these entries later without another terrain-index step. Until then a cook of such a
source is refused exactly as before. Every cooked terrain index is re-cooked or migrated (a v2 index still loads).
`TerrainIndex` gains two public fields (struct literals must add them) and `TerrainIndexError` a variant. Updated: spec 12
§ 4a (format row and the batch 2 table), `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9b, `book/agents/terrain-tiles.md`, the
`assets.terrain_tiles` schema, format-hashes row, corpus `terrain-index/v3.bin` (`v1.bin`, `v2.bin` unchanged), the fuzz
target's fixture (now carries a mapping, a Z spacing and a mask).

## ADR-10079: TerrainMap cell-centered sample layout: a host API and a `LevelTerrain` field (scene 13 → 14)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7724 row g, plan W-24, spec 12 § 4a ("needs DO27", moved to v0.7 format batch 2, owner-approved 11-19).
`TerrainMap` is vertex-centered: sample `i` of `n` sits at `i / (n − 1) · W − W / 2`, the first and last samples on the
edges. A heightfield whose samples are the centers of `n` equal cells across `W` (a cell-registered raster, "pixel is
area", and DO27's cell-spaced simulation content) loads stretched by `n / (n − 1)`, every sample off its cell center
(half a cell at the edges). ADR-8179 (grid origin) and ADR-8369 (world depth) let a host match such a grid at run
time with arithmetic of its own, but nothing names the layout: the level file cannot say it, so a level the engine
loads itself (`load_level_terrain`: the editor, `terrain.load_level_terrain`, `LevelTerrainPlugin`, and `regia cook`'s
mesh-layer sim ground) is always vertex-centered. The brief asked to decide between a host API (no format change) and
a `LevelTerrain` field (scene 13 → 14), preferring whichever keeps DO27's existing maps loading without a re-author.
Decision: both, because they serve different callers and each keeps every existing map as it is.
(1) Host API, `regia_terrain::sampler`: `SampleLayout` (a re-export of `regia_scene::level::TerrainSampleLayout`:
`VertexCentered`, the default, and `CellCentered`), `TerrainMap::with_sample_layout(layout) -> Self`,
`sample_layout()`, `cell_extent()`. Cell-centered reads the map's width and depth as the cells' extent `[W, D]` and
puts sample `i` at `(i + 0.5) · W / n − W / 2` (rows likewise with `D` and their own count). It is built by storing the
span between the outer samples, `W · (n − 1) / n` (f64, one rounding), as the map's `world_width` (and
`D · (m − 1) / m` as `world_depth`): every consumer already reads the map through that span, the grid origin and the
depth (sampler, collider, CDLOD selection and draw uniforms, holes, patches, virtual-texture layout), so all of them
agree with no other change and no shader or uniform layout moves. A vertex-centered map is unchanged bit for bit
(setting the layout a map has is a no-op; switching to cell-centered and back restores the same bits). The drawn and
collided ground ends at the outer samples; the outer half cell lies outside `world_min..world_max` and clamps to the
edge sample, as any query past a map's edge does. `with_world_depth` on a cell-centered map takes the cells' depth.
Cell-centered plus a grid origin of `−0.5 · W / n` is DO27's "sample `n / 2` at the origin" grid and stores exactly
the numbers of the ADR-8179 recipe (a test compares the bits on a 256-sample, 80 m map).
(2) File: `LevelTerrain::sample_layout: TerrainSampleLayout` (serde default `VertexCentered`, always written). Scene
format 13 → 14; `migrate_v13_to_v14` is the number-only `respell_level_settings` (a v13 terrain block gains
`sample_layout: VertexCentered` and loads the same heights; a level with no terrain changes only its version);
`scene_schema_fingerprint` adds the enum's variant names. `load_level_ground` carries the layout
(`LevelGround::sample_layout`, `LevelGround::sample_span_m`), `load_level_terrain` builds the map with it, and the
mesh-layer cook hands its vertex-centered lattice `sample_span_m()`, so the cooked world geometry and the run-time
map put every sample in the same place. A cell-centered block's `world_width_m` is the cells' extent; without one it
takes the cooked index's `size_m` (the samples' span, what every cook writes) times `n / (n − 1)`, else one metre a
cell. A count-mapped terrain (ADR-8471) places its samples by the mapping and refuses `CellCentered` with
`level_terrain_mapping`.
(3) Why not one alone: the field alone gives hosts that build their own `TerrainMap` (DO27's shell does) nothing to
call; the API alone leaves the editor, the cook and `LevelTerrainPlugin` unable to know a level wants it. Both keep
DO27's existing maps loading without a re-author: v13 levels migrate to `VertexCentered` with identical heights, and a
host-built map stays vertex-centered unless the host asks.
(4) Editor and agent (rule 8, no new method): World Settings shows the field as Sample Layout (`FIELD_LABELS`);
`editor.terrain_create` takes `sample_layout` and the New terrain dialog has "Samples at cell centers" (a cell-centered
create writes `world_width_m = size · cell_size` and the layout into the level's block; `heightfield.json` keeps the
samples' span); `terrain.set_level_terrain` accepts the field, `terrain.level_terrain` and `editor.terrain_create`
report it, `terrain.get` reports `map.sample_layout` and `map.cell_extent`. Fuzz target `scene.terrain_layout` (a v14
cell-centered level through the scene and settings readers, validation and a map built with the layout). Corpus:
`scene/v14.ron` (the registry fixture re-encoded at v14) and `scene/v14-cell-centered.level.ron`.
(5) Not in this step: `grid_origin_m` and `world_depth_m`, which ADR-8179 and ADR-8369 asked the batch to add. They
need the mesh-layer cook's `GroundInput` (square, centered on 0) to take an origin and a depth first, else the cooked
geometry and the run-time map would disagree. Each may fold into the unreleased v14 before the v0.7 tag (additive,
`Option`, absent = today's), per ADR-7724 (1).
DO27 (the lead forwards this; DO27 needs no change to keep working):
- Nothing is required. DO27's v13 levels load as before; `regia upgrade-project --write` re-saves them at v14 (the
  version line and one `sample_layout: VertexCentered` line in each terrain block change). Host-built maps are
  untouched.
- To store a cell-registered heightfield as such: in the level's terrain block set `sample_layout: CellCentered` and
  `world_width_m` to the cells' extent (`n × cell size`, not `(n − 1) × spacing`); in host code call
  `TerrainMap::from_heights(n, n, heights, W, ..)?.with_sample_layout(SampleLayout::CellCentered)` instead of the
  ADR-8179 width arithmetic.
- DO27's simulation grid (sample `i` at `(i − n / 2) · W / n`) is cell-centered plus `with_grid_origin([−0.5 · W / n;
  2])` (1280 m at 4096 samples: `[−0.15625, −0.15625]`); that is the same map, bit for bit, as the ADR-8179 recipe DO27
  may already use, so switching recipes moves nothing.
- A level switched to `CellCentered` must be re-cooked (`regia cook`): its mesh-layer geometry (`<map>.meshlayers`),
  and anything baked from terrain positions (scatter, navigation, GI heightfield), moves by up to half a cell.
Consequences: scene files are written at v14; a v13 build refuses them with "scene file format version 14 is newer
than supported version 13; upgrade the engine". Struct literals of `LevelTerrain` and `LevelGround` need the new field
(or `..Default::default()` for `LevelTerrain`); `TerrainCreateSpec` gains `sample_layout`; `TerrainCreateDialog` gains
`cell_centered`. A map rebuilt from another map's `world_width()` (deformation and edit-layer rebuilds) keeps the
sample positions but reports `VertexCentered`. Specs updated: 12 § 4a (the scene row and the W-24 row),
`docs/formats/scene-files.md` (v14), `book/agents/terrain-runtime.md` § Sample layout. The feeder issued ADR-8830
to this lane, which `docs/decisions.md` already had (audio stall watchdog, 2026-11-13); integ-v07b renumbered this one
to ADR-10079.

## ADR-10080: GPU mesh layout v3: skinned and morphing meshes GPU-ready, stored tangents reused at load (format batch 2)
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7919 made `regia cook --ship` store vertex-colored meshes GPU-ready but left skinned and morphing meshes
compact: the `gpu-mesh` v2 payload must end after its indices and has no place for a skin's joint names, its second
influence set or sparse morph deltas. DO27's characters are skinned and many props morph, so a shipped pak still
unpacks them and runs MikkTSpace at load. Hosts that build render meshes with `regia_render::CpuMesh::from_cooked`
also ran MikkTSpace on every GPU-ready entry, because the render-vertex builder always regenerated tangents (plan W-14
"MikkTSpace at load"). The owner approved format batch 2 on 2026-11-19 with this row (`gpu-mesh` 2 → 3).
Decision: (1) `gpu-mesh` v3 = v2 plus an optional trailing block after the indices: magic `FGPX`, a `u32` length,
then postcard `GpuMeshExtras { skin: Option<CookedSkin>, skin_influences: u8, morph_targets: Vec<CookedMorphTarget> }`,
the compact mesh's own packed forms. Up to the indices a v3 payload is a v2 payload with another version word, and a
rigid mesh without morph targets has no block, so the writer's bytes for such a mesh change only in that word. The
reader accepts v1, v2 (both must end after the indices, as before) and v3 (ends after the indices or after exactly one
block); the block is validated against the vertex count (skin streams, joint indices, weight sums, morph index lists
and delta sizes, `skin_influences` 4, or 8 with a second set). This stores the whole packed skin rather than ADR-7919's
sketch of "the vertex slots plus set 1": an eight-influence skin's set 0 cannot be rebuilt from the renormalized
strongest four, and the exact round trip is the acceptance bar; the cost is 8 to 16 bytes per skinned vertex next to
the 96-byte vertex. (2) The vertex `JOINTS`/`WEIGHTS` slots stay zero: `load_cooked_model` draws a skinned part rigid
in its bind pose for both forms, and a skinned draw (`CpuMesh::from_cooked`, the counted upload) builds its strongest
four from the skin, as for the compact form. (3) `gpu_mesh_file_from_cooked` converts every compact mesh;
`GpuMeshView::to_cpu_mesh` returns the skin (`eight_influences` from `skin_influences`) and the morph targets exactly
as `CookedMesh::to_cpu_mesh` does; the pak writer's submesh rewrite carries the block. (4) The render-vertex builder
(`CpuMesh::from_cooked`, `from_cooked_rigid`, the counted upload, `load_cooked_model`'s legacy path) draws the mesh's
stored tangents when they are real: one per vertex, finite unit xyz (within 1e-3), a ±1 sign, and not every one the
`(1, 0, 0, ±1)` stand-in `CookedMesh::to_cpu_mesh` writes for the compact form. Otherwise it runs MikkTSpace as
before. The stored tangents of a GPU-ready entry are the ones that pass made at cook from the same positions, normals,
UVs and LOD-0 indices, so the render vertices are bit-identical either way.
`regia_render::tangent_passes_on_this_thread` counts the passes (per thread, for deterministic tests).
(5) Version policy (ADR-7724): one step, 2 → 3, `gpu_mesh_migration_sources` `[1, 2]`; a cache inside desktop paks, so
no `regia upgrade-project` row (the corpus-upgrade test lists it in `NOT_HANDLED` with that reason): v1 and v2 entries
keep loading and the next cook writes v3. A v0.6 runtime refuses a v3 entry with `GPU-ready mesh layout version 3 is
not supported (this runtime reads 2)`, so a pak cooked by v0.7 needs a v0.7 runtime. Corpus: `gpu-mesh/v2.bin` kept
byte for byte, `v3.bin` (two LODs, two submeshes, an eight-influence skin and a morph target) added.
Consequences: Desktop `--ship` / `--gpu-meshes` paks store skinned and morphing meshes GPU-ready (no `compact_meshes`
warning for them); their loads skip the decode and the tangent pass, also through `CpuMesh::from_cooked`. A host
`CpuMesh` that carries real tangents from another source (an importer's glTF `TANGENT`) is now drawn with them instead
of regenerated ones. Host-visible API: `GpuMeshView` gains the `extras` field; new `GpuMeshExtras`, `GpuMeshParts`,
`GPU_MESH_EXTRAS_MAGIC`, `encode_gpu_mesh_parts`, `encode_gpu_mesh_file_parts`,
`regia_render::tangent_passes_on_this_thread`; `GPU_MESH_VERSION` is 3. Paks cooked before v3 keep their skinned and
