morphing meshes compact until cooked again. Specs: 12 § 4a (the v0.7 batch row), the `gpu_mesh` module docs (layout
table), `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md`; book `user-guide/cooked-packs.md`, `agents/cooked-packs.md`,
`user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md`. Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-fmt-gpu-mesh-v3.md`. No new
dependency, agent method or error code.

## ADR-8121: P-17 custom decal textures use the existing v3 format
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: accepted
Context: P-17's original new-v1 wording conflicts with the existing frozen v2
`decal` format and the v0.5.0 baseline.
Decision: Accepted by the lead on 2026-11-16: retain the `decal` identity and
add custom textures in v3, the single v0.6 step. Supply v1-to-v3 and v2-to-v3
migration, upgrade-project support, format-hash registration, all three corpus
versions, fuzz coverage, and the format page. Do not register a competing v1.
Consequences: This change must merge before the v0.6 format freeze.

## ADR-8203: Resolve custom decal images before placement
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: P-17 needs authored color and coverage on the existing projected and
forward decal paths. Runtime crates cannot depend on the asset pipeline.
Decision: v3 adds an optional `texture` path to a cooked RGBA8 image, relative
to its prefab directory. Hosts may also register a decoded `CookedImage`.
The library validates and resolves images at load time, then publishes an
immutable atlas snapshot. The existing four procedural layers keep their
indices and bytes. Custom images fill the remaining forward-atlas layers,
resampled to its existing 64x64 page size; capacity exhaustion is an error.
Loads stage the whole library and commit only on success. Relative paths may
not escape their directory, including through symlinks. No per-frame file IO.
Consequences: Both rendering paths share layer indices. Missing images refuse
placement rather than silently substituting a built-in. No dependency or
renderer frame-graph change is needed; PNG sources use the existing image cook.
The agent spawn method reports the resolved texture and layer. Presentation
only; no lockstep arithmetic or DO27 simulation change.

## ADR-8038: Damage decal atlas and capsule stair walkability
Date: 2026-11-16   Status: proposed
Context: Phase 6 content tools need a cook-side damage decal atlas and a check that a stair is
walkable at a capsule's size. The behavior was read as requirements (owner 2026-11-16 absorb
exception) and rewritten. The runtime already has a 64×64 projected decal atlas; this atlas is a
different product. A parallel flood-fill would drift from `regia_nav`'s slope, headroom, radius
erosion and max-climb rules.
Decision: `regia_vfx::damage_atlas` returns 1024×1024 RGBA8 (sixteen 256×256 cells). Trig, powers
and the noise floor go through `regia_core::math`, so two calls return the same bytes. No PNG
dependency. `regia_nav::check_stair` builds one stair plus two landings with `NavMeshBuilder` and
`NavQuery::find_path`. Capsule radius, height, max climb, max slope and voxel size are settings
(defaults 0.35 m, 1.6 m, 0.5 m, 45 degrees, 0.2 m by 0.1 m). A path is walkable. Otherwise the
flag is too narrow, too steep, riser above max climb, or not connected. Agent methods
`nav.check_stair` (read; empty params fail before a mesh is built) and `vfx.damage_decal_atlas`
(read; pixels only when `generate` is true). No content-format change.
Consequences: new public types in `regia_nav` and `regia_vfx`, documented in
`book/agents/decal-atlas-walkability.md`. The requirements are recorded in `docs/provenance.md`.
A `docs/ported-sources.toml` `[[source]]` row is not added: `notices --check` rejects a
non-permissive licence, and the D-01 schema has not landed. The check is content and navigation,
not a lockstep checksum.

## ADR-8829: Decal v3 lands in v0.7 format batch 2, with damage-atlas cells and footstep surfaces
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Decal custom textures (ADR-8121/8203, decal 2 -> 3) and the damage atlas and stair check
(ADR-8038) were built for v0.6 but missed the v0.6.0 tag, which shipped decal v2. The v0.7 format
batch 2 (owner 2026-11-19, freeze 2026-11-28) carries the decal step. The lane brief asked for "a
walkable atlas region drives nav/footstep surfaces as the ADR says", but ADR-8038 has no such
clause: it adds a cook-side atlas and a stair check with no link between them or to decals. Decals
are presentation; they are drawn, recycled when a pool is full, and differ per tier, so anything
derived from them must never reach navigation or a lockstep checksum.
Decision: (1) decal v3 is the one `decal` step of v0.7 (v0.6.0 shipped v2), migrators v1/v2 -> v3
unchanged. (2) Folded into the same unreleased v3 step under the ADR-7724 fold rule: an optional
`surface: Option<String>` (1 to 32 bytes of lowercase ascii, digits and `_`, omitted from output
when `None`), so the frozen `decal/v3.ron` stays byte-identical and loads, and
`decal/v3-surface.ron` exercises the new field. The schema hash moves at v3; `check-formats
--update` re-records only the `decal` row. (3) `DecalPool` records each decal's footstep surface
(`set_footstep_surface`, interned, at most 1024 names) on every placement path, and
`footstep_surface_at(point)` returns the surface of the highest-priority, then newest, live decal
whose box contains the point; a host footstep probe passes it as the event surface, and `None`
leaves the receiver's (terrain layer) surface. Agent read `vfx.decal_surface_at`; `vfx.spawn_decal`
adds `surface` to its result. (4) The damage atlas feeds decal v3: `damage_decal_cell_image`
crops one 256x256 cell as a `CookedImage`, `DecalLibrary::add_damage_cell` registers a prefab with
it under `damage-atlas/cell-NN`. (5) Navigation is NOT driven by decals: `regia_nav::check_stair`
stays a cook/content check, and no decal field reaches a navmesh, collider or the simulation.
Consequences: one format hash change (decal v3, still one step since v0.6.0). New public items in
`regia_vfx` (no struct-literal break: `DecalPrefab` already has a private field). DO27 can use the
damage-atlas cells as its blood/damage decal images and tag puddles or blood pools with a surface
for footsteps, without any simulation change. Specs updated: `docs/formats/decal-ron.md`, spec 12
section 4a (v0.7 table), spec 26 section "Custom decal images".

## ADR-10076: v0.7 roll-up 2 (integ-v07b): merge resolutions, ADR renumbers, the W-11 D4 owner ruling, three rules-line reds
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: integ-v07b merges the v0.7 net line (wire 6 server, state-ring reorder, the rpc-p95 up leg, 128 clients,
the wedged-client hole, the five land lanes, the migration journal and hand-off), the det lanes, the rules fixes,
the tunnels follow-ups, mesh-layer stream cross-fade, interior culling, the low-tier lanes, the carried fixes and four
format-row lanes onto integ-v07a (4cf3c2caa). Several lanes branched from v0.6.0 and re-merged lanes that integ-v07a
had already combined, so the same code met three resolutions, and the union merges of `docs/decisions.md` put ADR
bodies under the wrong headings.
Decision: (1) Edited-ground descent (`query_segment.rs`): the re-pin lane's `node_range` (ADR-10082) replaces
integ-v07a's inline range (ADR-8895); it is the same rule (cooked range at an untouched tile or an unedited state, the
state's own ranges where it keeps them) and it carries `touched_tiles_keep_a_range_that_holds_the_edited_ground`.
`GroundEdits::pyramid_bounds` is kept again for it (integ-v07a and w11-review-fixes had removed it as dead code).
(2) The mesh-layer cook's sim ground (`level_mesh_layers.rs`): stream-crossfade's count-mapping (ADR-8842) is kept; the
unmapped fallback takes terrainmap-spacing's `sample_span_m` (ADR-10079). `load_level_ground` refuses a v3 index grid
(ADR-8871) before the sample-layout width rule (ADR-10079). (3) The game-modes guide filter (`ruleset_file.rs`): the
guide-red lane's `id:` rule replaces integ-v07a's `entries:` skip; both playlist guide tests stay. (4) ADR renumbers
(numbers from queue/adr-counter): ADR-8830 (TerrainMap cell-centered) -> ADR-10079, ADR-8831 (GPU mesh v3) ->
ADR-10080, ADR-8860 (scale at 128 clients) -> ADR-10081, ADR-8861 (tunnels re-pin pass) -> ADR-10082; the old
numbers keep their v0.6.0 decisions. Re-merged tunnels text that still said ADR-8810 or ADR-8811 now says ADR-8898 or
ADR-8899 (integ-v07a's renumbers). `docs/decisions.md` was rebuilt from integ-v07a's file plus each merged lane's new
or amended ADR blocks taken from that lane's own file (an amendment is taken only when it does not shorten the block),
so every ADR has one block under its own heading. (5) integ-v07a's rules-line reds: `rules.spawn_preview` gets a
`READ_ALLOWANCES` entry in `security_wave2.rs` (its name says `spawn`; it previews the pick and moves no spawn state),
and `lobby-keys` gets a `NOT_HANDLED` row in `format_corpus_upgrade.rs` (lobby platform data, never a project file;
the upgrade-project sweep says so since ADR-2316). (6) **Owner ruling, W-11 D4 (2026-11-20 08:4x, option C):** the
measured native `support` numbers are accepted for v0.7 (Deck 510-1430 ns, 1.07-2.46 of compat, against the 150 ns
and 0.25 bar of ADR-8817), and so is the build server build-host mixed-tick bar (0.36-0.40 ms against 0.25 ms). The bars
are not changed: they stay the v0.8 ground redesign's target, and the v0.7 release notes list D4 as an owner-ruled
exception.
Consequences: lanes not merged here are listed in the integ-v07b report with the reason (the mesh-layer joins lane's
cooked format v2 collides with W-11 index-build's v2 and needs a v3 step). `cargo xtask adr-index` must find no
duplicate number. Specs untouched by this ADR.

## ADR-10063: The excess allowance fills only from target spent below the rate; a shared-uplink flag earns none; a burst packet needs the allowance whole (amends ADR-8859)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: review of lane v07-net-rpc-p95-up-leg (ADR-8859), report sprint-v07-net-rpc-p95-up-leg-review. ADR-8859 says a
sender that fills its target earns no excess allowance. That held only when the buckets had been limited to their depth
first, which production does only under a shared uplink's share (`rate_cap`). A fresh connection's budget bucket starts
at the initial window (`max(max_packets_per_poll, 16)` packets, 76,800 bytes at the defaults), far above its depth
(four packets), and `Pacer::refill_overflow` returned every token earned while the bucket stood above the depth as
unused. A sender that queued 20 kB/s of input bundles on a 16 kB/s target after spending ~41 kB in its first poll
banked the full allowance (4,800 bytes) within two seconds and could then burst a 4 KiB command onto a link it was
already filling: the case ADR-8859's excess bucket exists to prevent (its rejected "debt alone" variant). Review nits:
any positive credit let a whole burst packet out (100 bytes of credit sent a ~1,200-byte packet), and
`Connection::set_shared_uplink(true)` without a rate cap kept banking credit although ADR-8859 says a shared uplink's
peer earns none.
Decision:
1. `Pacer::refill_overflow` returns at most what the interval since the last refill earned beyond what the sender spent
   in it: `min(overflow, max(0, earned - spent))`, where `spent` is the bucket's fall since the last refill (a
   `Pacer::limit` counts as spent, which only lowers it). Below the depth this is the old value (the overflow is already
   bounded by `earned - spent` when the last refill left the bucket at most at its depth); above it (the first burst
   still unspent) a sender earns only what it left unused in that interval, never the startup allowance. Signature and
   `Pacer::refill` unchanged; `Pacer` gains one private field.
2. `Connection::set_shared_uplink(true)` zeroes `message_credit`, and while the flag is set the poll earns none, with
   or without a share in force (the aggregate owns what a peer leaves unused). The buckets are still limited only under
   a `rate_cap` (ADR-8534), as before.
3. A packet of a message's burst leaves only if `message_credit` holds it whole, counted as it is charged (the packet
   header plus the planned body: RFC 2697 § 3, a packet of B bytes needs Te >= B). Acknowledgment records added after
   planning can still take the allowance a few bytes below zero.
Rejected: dropping the allowance on every poll that was not app-limited (the review's second sketch item). Under 1 a
sender that fills its target no longer earns any; dropping banked credit on a held poll would also drop it when only a
background transfer waits, which is the rpc-with-bulk case the allowance exists for (reasoned, not measured).
Consequences: `connection::uplink_cap_tests::a_saturating_sender_from_a_fresh_bucket_earns_no_message_burst` (the
review's proof), `a_shared_uplink_flag_without_a_share_earns_no_message_burst`, `a_few_bytes_of_credit_let_no_burst_packet_out`
and `cc::tests::a_first_burst_above_the_depth_is_no_unused_allowance` pin it. No wire, format or public signature change.
Spec 120 § 4.2 item 7's text (via ADR-8859) is unchanged: this makes the code match it.

## ADR-10061: Pack provenance import stays under assets/ and writes all or nothing (fixes for ADR-8834)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: the review of the C-24 importer (`lane/sprint-v07-provenance-migrator-review` 6472b0826) found four holes in
`regia_asset::provenance_import`. (1) A conflict found during the write loop (`meta_changed`) or a failed write left
earlier sidecars rewritten and answered `applied: true`; `b.obj.meta` linked to `a.obj.meta` with two different rows
made one write clobber the other. (2) `check_rel_path` accepted Windows device names (`NUL`, `mesh/COM1.obj`,
`aux.obj`), segments of only dots and spaces (`.. `, `...`) and trailing dots or spaces (`bar.obj.`), which the
project path rules (ADR-1816, ADR-3206) refuse. (3) A folder link under `assets/` (`assets/out` -> `outside/`) let the
import read and rewrite sidecars outside the project. (4) A record folder skipped a FIFO named `*.toml` (and a link to
a regular record) instead of refusing (or reading) it.
Decision: (1) The write is staged: every new sidecar is written to a fresh temporary file beside its original
(`create_new`), a write error removes them all and answers `provenance_import_write_failed` with nothing changed; then
each original is re-read and the temporary renamed over it; a changed original (`meta_changed`) or a failed rename
restores the sidecars already replaced from the bytes the import read, and the answer is `applied: false`. Before any
write, rows whose `.meta` files are one file (canonical path: a linked `.meta`, or two spellings through a folder
link) are `meta_changed` on the later row, and a `.meta` that is itself a symbolic link is the new conflict kind
`meta_link`: the import neither writes through a link nor replaces it. A `.meta` that is not a regular file (a FIFO)
is `meta_unreadable` without being opened. (2) `check_rel_path` keeps its own rules (`\`, empty and `.` segments
stay refused, which `check_relative` would drop) and adds `regia_core::project_path::check_relative` on top; the code
stays `provenance_import_invalid`. (3) After the join, the source and its `.meta` go through
`regia_core::project_path::check_under_root` against `assets/` before either is read; an escape is
`provenance_import_invalid` and the call returns before any write. A missing `assets/` skips the check (it holds
nothing, every row is `missing_source` as before). (4) The folder scan uses `symlink_metadata`: a FIFO, socket or
device named `*.toml` is `provenance_import_unreadable`; a link counts when its canonical target is a regular file
inside the folder and is `provenance_import_unreadable` otherwise; a folder named `*.toml` is skipped.
Consequences: the "all or nothing" promise of ADR-8834 and the book holds for conflicts found while writing, short of a
crash between two renames or a restore that itself fails (the `meta_changed` detail names any sidecar it could not
put back). A project that links sidecars must give each source its own `.meta` before importing. A concurrent writer
inside the project can still swap a checked folder between the check and the open (the limit `project_path` already
documents). `CONFLICT_KINDS` gains `meta_link`. No format change (the `.meta` stays v2). Tests: `regia_asset`
`tests/provenance_import.rs`: the review's `device_names_and_dotted_parents_are_refused`,
`a_record_folder_refuses_a_fifo_and_reads_a_symlink`, `a_conflict_or_write_error_during_the_write_leaves_nothing_changed`,
`a_symlink_out_of_assets_is_refused_and_writes_nothing`, and `a_linked_meta_is_refused_and_keeps_the_link`,
`two_paths_to_one_sidecar_through_a_folder_link_write_nothing`, `every_way_out_of_assets_is_refused`,
`a_missing_assets_folder_reports_missing_sources`, `a_fifo_meta_is_unreadable_and_does_not_block`,
`record_folder_links_that_leave_or_dangle_are_refused`. Book: `agents/provenance-import.md`. Specs: none changed.

## ADR-10064: Format batch 2 freezes the rules formats: rules-ron v1, playlist-ron v2, match-result v1
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: format batch 2 (owner approval 11-19; freeze Sat 11-28) freezes the three game-rules formats: `.rules.ron`
(`rules-ron`), `.playlist.ron` (`playlist-ron`) and the finished-match JSON (`match-result`). The batch plan listed all
three as new v1 formats. Checked on the merged base (v0.6.0 + v07-rules-match-results-land c9dd2080a +
v07-rules-session-items c79d53807 + rules-unit-variant-strict-fix e1908c18b), with the brief's two questions: does the
schema fingerprint cover every nested enum shape, and does every nested type refuse unknown fields?
- `rules-ron`: yes on both (ADR-8799 strict mirrors and tagged-enum probe, ADR-8879 empty struct variants); every type
  the file reaches is in `rules_ron_schema_fingerprint`. Two gaps from v07-rules-session-items: its corpus file
  `rules-ron/v1-binds.ron` had no `FROZEN.txt` line (`the_corpus_files_are_frozen` red), and its option `bind`
  (ADR-8881) moved the fingerprint without a re-recorded `format-hashes.ron` row (`check-formats` red).
- `playlist-ron`: NOT new. v1 shipped in v0.6.0 (ADR-8345, ADR-8897 fields included; the v0.6.0 table has its row).
  `playlist_ron_schema_fingerprint` listed only `PlaylistFile` and `PlaylistEntry` field names, so the `order` enum
  (`in_order`, `shuffle(seed)`, `weighted(seed)`) was outside the hash, and `PlaylistOrder` (shared with the session
  snapshot and the agent protocol) had no `deny_unknown_fields`: `order: shuffle(seed: 4, cycles: 2)` loaded and
  dropped `cycles`.
- `match-result`: every record struct refuses unknown keys except the timeline row: `LedgerSummary::timeline` holds
  the shared `regia_rules::end_stats::TimelineEvent`, which is lenient (it is also in the session snapshot), so a
  row's extra key was dropped while the same key on a player row was refused.
Decision:
1. `rules-ron` v1 is frozen as it stands: add the `FROZEN.txt` line for `v1-binds.ron` and re-record the `rules-ron`
   row with `cargo xtask check-formats --update` (this lane, this row only). v1 is unreleased (new since v0.6.0), so
   the hash move needs no bump (ADR-8619 rule; the ADR-7724 guard passes a format the last release did not have).
   First version: no migrator, `regia upgrade-project` parses, checks and leaves v1 alone (row exists).
2. `playlist-ron` takes its one v0.7 step, v1 -> v2. The fingerprint gains `PlaylistOrder`'s variant names and
   shapes; completing it moves the hash of a released format, which ADR-7724 (3) allows only with a bump ("the hash
   wins"). v2 has v1's shape: the `.playlist.ron` reader reads `order` through a private `deny_unknown_fields` mirror
   (`PlaylistOrderFile`, exhaustive `From` both ways; the shared `PlaylistOrder` stays lenient for snapshots and the
   agent's `order` parameter, the ADR-8799 pattern). The migrator is number-only: `PlaylistFile::from_ron` reads v1
   and sets the in-memory version to 2 (saving writes v2); `migrate_playlist_ron` (`regia upgrade-project`) rewrites
   the top-level `format_version` number with `regia_core::version::rewrite_ron_version`, every other byte kept, then
   checks the result loads; migration sources `[1]`. Corpus: `playlist-ron/v1.ron` (unchanged) and the new
   `playlist-ron/v2.ron` (weighted order, `no_repeat_last`, a weight, a player gate), plus its crate-local copy in
   `regia_net/tests/fixtures/formats/` (`playlist_fixture_copy` pins both copies); the fuzz target
   `net.playlist_ron` seeds from v2. The v0.6.0 loader refuses v2 with `no migrator from playlist.ron v2` (its
   version peek accepts only 1).
3. `match-result` v1 is frozen with one reader fix: `LedgerSummary::timeline` reads through a private
   `deny_unknown_fields` mirror of `TimelineEvent` (`TimelineEventFile`, exhaustive `From`). The field list is the
   same, so the fingerprint and hash do not move. First version: no migrator (the stub refuses every `from`);
   `regia upgrade-project` probes records by their `format` key and never rewrites them (row exists).
Consequences: a v1 playlist whose `order` holds an unknown field (which v0.6.0 dropped) is now refused with the
field's name; such a file was always a typo. Host code that compared `PlaylistFile::format_version` with `1` after a
load now sees `2` (use `PLAYLIST_RON_FORMAT_VERSION`). A match record with an extra key in a timeline row is
`match_result_malformed`; the engine never wrote one. After this the three formats change only with a version bump,
a migrator, an `upgrade-project` row, a corpus file, a fuzz target and a `format-hashes.ron` row (spec 12 § 4a). The
v0.7 release table (`format-hashes-v0.7.0.ron`) records `rules-ron` 1, `playlist-ron` 2 and `match-result` 1; against
a v0.6.0 baseline the guard sees exactly one step for `playlist-ron`.
Specs updated: docs/specs/12-assets.md (§ 4a rows of the three formats; v0.7 batch table rows), docs/formats/
rules-ron.md, playlist-ron.md, match-result.md (version tables and freeze notes), book/user-guide/game-modes.md.

## ADR-10102: The 2026-11-20 ADR collision scan — twelve lane families renumbered on merge, and the reserved 20000-20199 block
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: the build machines's ADR counter ran behind `docs/decisions.md` until 2026-11-20 05:00: it handed out numbers the
integrated line had already used (the 8860-8901 window and earlier batches back to 8610). The collision-scan lane
(`sprint-adr-collision-scan-z`) diffed `docs/decisions.md` of every `origin/lane/sprint-*` branch updated since
2026-11-19 (226 branches) against `merge-base(02381fd90, branch)` (v0.6.0, with integ-v07a 4cf3c2caab checked as the
merge target) and classified every added `## ADR-NNNN` heading by section identity: heading count at the branch tip,
section title and body hash at the branch, at v0.6.0 and at integ-v07a, and presence at each merge base. Twelve lane
ADR families reuse a number the integrated line already owns (8610, 8640, 8730, 8810, 8811, 8812, 8830, 8831, 8832,
8860, 8861, 8862); every such branch tip already holds both sections, so a blanket replace of the number would
retitle the integrated ADR as well. No two peer lanes were handed the same number; every other multi-branch add was
one ADR propagated along a stack (verification, review and roll-up branches).
Decision: a colliding lane ADR takes, on merge, the number the same ADR already carries on the line that integrated
or renumbered it, when one exists: 8610 -> 8792 (the anim line), 8640 -> 8699, 8730 -> 8897, 8810 -> 8898, 8811 ->
8899, 8832 -> 8900 (integ-v07a, which had already renumbered them), 8830 -> 10079, 8831 -> 10080, 8860 -> 10081,
8861 -> 10082 (integ-v07b), 8862 -> 8888 (integ-v061b/c). A family with no such number (8812, the editor launcher
icons ADR) takes ADR-20000 from a reserved block 20000-20199 that the queue counter will not reach; 20001-20199
stay free for later collisions. The renumber is scoped per branch: the lane's `docs/decisions.md` section is
retitled through its own heading (title-anchored `sed`; the heading invariants — the integrated section keeps its
number, exactly one lane section moves or is dropped — were verified against a sample branch tip of every emitted
script block); branch-authored files that cite the number are blanket-renumbered; files that already cited the
integrated ADR at the branch point are left untouched; generated indexes (`docs/decisions-index.md`,
`docs/manual/*`, `book/reference/*`) are regenerated, never edited. A branch whose tree already contains the target
number drops the stale section instead (one family member today, `sprint-v07-masked-occlusion-low` for 8810/8898,
whose stale body must be diffed into ADR-8898 first). The per-branch `sed` lines live in the lane report;
`cargo xtask adr-index` must report no duplicate numbers after each merge.
Consequences: the twelve collisions clear mechanically without touching any integrated ADR's number or its existing
references. Roll-up ADRs that record their own renumbering stay accurate. The queue counter must skip 20000-20199;
lanes merge cleanly only while the counter stays ahead of `docs/decisions.md`.

## ADR-10088: Wire 6, part 3: every NetLink and NetSession reconnect presents the resumption credential; repeat repairs are staggered
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8902 (part 2) made the server admit a one-round-trip resume, but nothing above `NetClient` presented the
credential, so the net-soak gate plan's two `asym-bufferbloat` `reconnect_within_grace` rows (8 and 32 clients, 3,000 ms
grace) stayed red at 3,104-3,376 ms: the scripted rejoin took the three round trips of the full handshake through the
profile's 1 s downstream queue. ADR-8902 also measured the soak change part 3 owed and left it out, because 3 of 12
`asym-bufferbloat` rows then lost a client to `reassembly_stalled`, two of them a client that never left or resumed. In
each, the client waited 18.6 s for fragment 0 of the server's join-snapshot stream: the server repaired it once per round
trip, in one burst with its neighbors, and every repair was dropped (17 in a row at the gate seed). The cause is the
traffic phase effect of a drop-tail queue (Floyd and Jacobson 1992): the profile's queue is kept full by a constant-rate
cross flow, so whether a full-size datagram fits depends on the instant it arrives; a repair that leaves exactly one
(stable) round trip after the transmission it replaces arrives at the same phase and is lost again, and datagrams that
leave back to back reach the queue at the same instant and are lost together.
Decision: **1. The credential on every `NetLink` reconnect.** The link's resume plan keeps, beside the newest ticket, the
resumption credential of the same accept (`ResumeCredential`, ADR-8858); a new accept replaces both, so a credential never
outlives its ticket, and clones share the credential's flight count, so every attempt of one outage sends a newer
flight (ADR-8858 A3). `NetLink::resume_on`, the automatic reconnect on the endpoint's own socket and on fresh sockets of
the link's transport kind (dedicated, listen and relay links alike: they reconnect through the same plan) present it.
Without a credential (a plain link, a server that keeps no tickets) or after a refusal the connect is the full
handshake that presents the ticket: the three-round-trip fallback spec 120 § 10.3 names. **2. The soak.** The scripted
rejoin presents the credential its leave took, and the `asym-bufferbloat` server keeps tickets for 60 s, as `cgnat`'s
does and as a `NetLink` server does by default; every other profile is unchanged (no tickets). `Profile::resume_grace_ms`
(`None` in every plan) lets a measurement run any profile with tickets kept (`docs/perf/net-resume-wire6.md`).
**3. Repeat repairs** (`regia_net::connection`). A reliable fragment counts the loss verdicts on its transmissions. The
first repair is unchanged: one round trip after the loss, in the same poll as its neighbors. From the second loss in a
row the repair leaves a stagger later than the round trip, in `REPEAT_REPAIR_STAGGER_SLOTS` (8) steps of the round
trip / `REPEAT_REPAIR_STAGGER_DIVISOR` (32), at most 7/32 of a round trip; the slot is the fragment's queue key plus 3
times its loss count, mod 8 (3 is coprime with 8, so eight losses in a row visit every slot, and queue neighbors take
different slots at the same count); no randomness, so a connection's history gives the same schedule. The stagger is a
share of the round trip, so it spreads repairs over several polls where the round trip is long (a standing queue) and
is under one poll on a short path. First repairs, probes, new data and the per-poll resend cap
(`MAX_RESEND_PACKETS_PER_POLL`) are unchanged, and a fragment still leaves at most once per round trip (ADR-7995).
**Tried and taken back out (1):** a second rule, at most one packet of repeat
repairs per poll (so two never leave back to back). It was not needed for the stall (the same 24 `asym-bufferbloat` rows
lose no connection with the stagger alone, and with the cap alone), and it cost a listen host: at 64 clients on the
shared 20 Mbit/s uplink (`regia_net_soak` test `listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh`) the worst
client's staleness p99 went from 6 ticks to 9 (limit 8), with or without the stagger, because the repairs of one burst
were spread over many polls and each took a snapshot's place in its poll's rate; with the stagger alone it is 6.
**Tried and taken back out (2):** further copies of a fragment lost three or more times in a row (one to three more
transmissions within the round, before any verdict). They closed the residual below (74 of 74 rows clean, the worst
fragment acknowledged after 7 losses in a row) and left the listen host at 6 ticks, but they break a bar that stands:
a peer's acknowledgments must never make a fragment repeat more than once per round trip (ADR-7995; tests
`hostile_zero_masks_cannot_resend_a_fragment_more_than_once_per_rtt` and `row6_hostile_zero_masks_bound_the_resends`
went red). **Residual, with its cause.** With the stagger, 71 of 72 `asym-bufferbloat` rows (36 seeds, 8 and 32 clients)
lose no connection; one (32 clients, seed 2213) loses one client to `reassembly_stalled`: one fragment of its join
snapshot was sent 20 times, off the beat, and lost every time. Measured at that bottleneck over the row (the queue's
free room at each arrival): a packet of 1,200 bytes or more is admitted 48 % of the time when it is the first of its
tick, one of 1,000 to 1,199 bytes 68 %, one under 600 bytes 96 %; the free room swings below 2,864 bytes, and a client
whose join snapshot is incomplete gets two snapshot packets every tick (1,055 and 815 bytes on the wire), which fit
where the 1,227-byte repair does not and keep the room at the next tick under a full packet (it was under 1,227 bytes
at 17 of that fragment's 18 later arrivals, and at the eighteenth a snapshot packet left first). So the path drops a
full fragment in 60 to 70 % of its repairs, far above the loss it reports, one repair per round trip (1.04 s behind
that queue) is about 17 tries inside the receiver's stall deadline (18.6 s, § 5.2), and the connection's own
unreliable traffic starves its last full-size repair. A fix has to raise the chance of one try, since the tries per
round trip are bounded: let a repeat repair leave before, and instead of, the unreliable data of its tick and the tick
before (a quiet tick), or repair in smaller pieces (a wire shape, so wire 6 before its freeze). Neither is built here;
see the release fragment's Known issues.
**4. `NetSession`.** A session host's transport keeps tickets for the session's reconnect grace
(`ServerConfig::resume_grace_ms` = `reconnect_grace_s`; 0 keeps none, as before), so a player that times out is dormant
at the transport under its link id while the session holds it in grace. The session client keeps the transport's ticket
and credential of its last accept beside the session's reconnect token and presents them on every connect with
`resume: true` (the automatic reconnect, `resume`, `resume_on`, a game's own `connect` with `resume: true`, direct or by
join code): the transport connect is then a one-round-trip resume under the same link id, and the session's `Hello`
with the reconnect token resumes the player on it. The session core (`SessionServer::link_up`) takes a link id that
still has a peer as a transport takeover in place: the peer is detached and keeps its state while the link waits for
its hello; the hello with the peer's token resumes it exactly as a takeover from a new link does (no `PlayerDropped`),
and any other outcome of that link (another player's hello, a refusal, the handshake timeout, the link going down) is
the loss of the old link with the grace a timeout gets. The driver sends nothing to a dormant transport peer (the
transport would hold a reliable message and deliver it after the resume, ahead of the new welcome) and ends the
transport's hold at once for a player the session does not keep in grace (`NetServer::forget_dormant`), so a transport
hold never outlives the session's. A link the session closes itself while it keeps the player in grace (a suspend's
goodbye, the session's own silence timeout, a reliable overflow on a silent link) is closed with
`NetServer::kick_held`: the far end is told as by a kick and the peer is held dormant as by a timeout, so those
reconnects are one-round-trip resumes too (`SessionServer::grace_holds_link` names such a link). With a session grace
above 0 the transport's per-address holds (ADR-8733) now apply
to session hosts as they do to `NetLink` hosts.
Consequences: measured with the soak's own workload (`regia_net_soak`, virtual time) over `asym-bufferbloat` at 8 and 32
clients on 36 seeds (72 rows): every scripted rejoin is a one-round-trip resume of the held slot (`resumed_one_rtt` =
`held_slot_returns` = rejoins, 0 lapsed), connected 1,040 ms after the link was up (1,056 or 1,280 ms in 15 of 180
rejoins), against 3,104-3,376 ms before; 71 rows lose no connection (the three that lost one with the credential alone
among them) and one loses one (the residual above). The gate plan's per-row before/after table and the per-profile resume times are in the lane report and
`docs/perf/net-resume-wire6.md`. A repair lost twice now waits up to 7/32 of a round trip longer: a cost only on paths
that already lost the same data twice. Host-visible API (release fragment v0.1.28-v07-wire6-soak-bars, Upgrade): two
public constants in `regia_net::connection` (`REPEAT_REPAIR_STAGGER_SLOTS`, `REPEAT_REPAIR_STAGGER_DIVISOR`), one field
of `regia_net_soak::profiles::Profile` (`resume_grace_ms`, `#[serde(default)]`), `NetServer::forget_dormant`,
`NetServer::kick_held`, `NetSession::transport_totals`, `SessionServer::peer_behind`,
`SessionServer::grace_holds_link`. No wire, format, agent-method or CLI change.
Not in this step: lockstep's resume (v07-net-wire6-window-records). Specs updated: spec 120 § 10.3 (Built note);
book/user-guide/networking.md, book/agents/net-soak.md, net-link.md, net-session.md; a provenance row.

## ADR-10093: The soak's outage rows run the resume a game runs: tickets on `flappy` and `long-outage`, the reconnect timeline in the soak client
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: six non-gating bars of the net-soak gate plan were red at v0.6.0 and at the head of every lane since:
`interrupted_once` on `flappy` at 8 and 32 clients and on `long-outage` at 8 and 32, and `resume_same_peer` on
`long-outage` at 8 and 32. The brief asked why `Restored` is never raised and why the resume falls back to a fresh join
(ticket expiry against the outage length, or the dormant path of ADR-8298). Neither. The engine parts exist and work:
a server with `resume_grace_ms` above 0 holds a timed-out player dormant (ADR-8298), and a `NetLink` or `NetSession`
client reconnects by itself with its ticket and reports one `PeerRestored` (ADR-8352). The soak workload used neither.
It drives the bare `NetClient` and `NetServer`. Its server kept no tickets on these profiles
(`Profile::server_resume_grace_ms` was 0 except on `cgnat`), so a timeout was a removal. Its client answered a timeout
with a new `NetClient` and a fresh join, so the server could only admit a new peer, and no layer was there to say
`Restored` (the bare `NetClient` says it only on the connection that was interrupted). So every outage beyond the 20 s
removal timeout (`flappy`'s 22 s on every fourth client; `long-outage`'s 25 s and 45 s) failed both bars by
construction, whatever the engine did. One more failure had a different cause: the gate's `flappy` row scripts client
5's leave at 18.0 s, inside that client's 15.7-18.7 s outage, and the bar asked for a `Restored` on a connection the
client had closed on purpose (the same on clients 13, 21 and 29 at 32).
Decision: (1) The servers of `flappy` and `long-outage` keep resume tickets for 60 s (`OUTAGE_RESUME_GRACE_MS`, the
`NetLink` default `DEFAULT_RESUME_GRACE_MS`), as `cgnat`'s already does. Every other profile's server keeps the
transport default of none, so its packet history does not change. (2) The soak client does what the engine's own game
layers do with the same public parts: after a `timeout` end while it holds the ticket of its last accept it starts
`regia_net::reconnect::Reconnector` with `ReconnectPolicy::default()` (first attempt 1 s after the timeout, doubling to
8 s, a 60 s window, jitter seeded from the ticket), each attempt a fresh `NetClient` on a new port with
`ClientConfig::resume` set and its handshake deadline at the window's end; an attempt that ends with `connect_timeout`,
`full` or `timeout` leaves room for the next, any other refusal ends the timeline; the first accept is recorded as the
outage's `Restored`, as `NetLink::drive_reconnect` reports it; at the window's end the client gives up once and joins
afresh. Without a ticket (every other profile) or after any other end it retries at once as before. It is a third
driver of the one tested schedule, beside `NetLink` and `NetSession`, because the soak's game has its own message and
join types and `NetLink` carries only the replication frame. (3) The soak server treats a dormant peer as a game does:
the avatar stays in the world, nothing is sent to it, none of its ticks are judged, and its resume starts like a join
(the world blob, the input grace). The connection's end is still recorded at the dormancy, by the same policy and at
the same time as the removal was, so `involuntary_disconnects` reads what it read. (4) `interrupted_once` owes no
`Restored` for an outage the client left on purpose inside: the scripted leave is recorded (`ClientRecord::leaves`,
because a goodbye inside an outage reaches nobody and no end record says it), and `OutageCheck::restore_owed` is false
for it. A leave outside the outage excuses nothing. This corrects what the bar measures; its rule, its limits and its
profiles are unchanged, and it still fails on a missing `Restored` of any connection that carries on.
(5) `Knobs::reconnect` and `Knobs::server_resume_grace_ms` switch either half off for a test, so the two bars keep runs
they fail on: no reconnect, no tickets, a 10 s window or a 10 s grace against the 45 s outage.
(6) `interrupted_once` and `resume_same_peer` gate from this commit (`xtask/src/net_soak.rs` `BARS`, `GATING_BARS`), by
ADR-8030's rule: the lane that shows a bar green on every profile it judges flips it. They are green on every gate row
of their profiles (`flappy`, `long-outage`, `good-wifi`, `wifi-to-cell`; 10 rows) and on the same profiles' dedicated
rows at the nightly length (300 s; 8, 32, 64 and 128 clients; 16 rows, every bar green). Listen rows at 300 s fail the
harness bars at the base and at the head (at 8 clients the shared uplink's rate falls to about 40 kbit/s a client
from 60 s on, and a client that joins after that ends with `protocol_error`; numbers in the lane report, not this
lane's subject): on the 16 listen rows `interrupted_once` passes everywhere and `resume_same_peer` fails on
`long-outage/32/listen` only, behind 54 such ends, which no ticket resumes. A soak run in which a player is not told `Restored`, or comes back as another
peer, now fails the verdict; the run of a game that does not resume, which passed the soak until now, fails it on these
two bars alone (`long_outage_without_the_resume_is_removed_and_rejoins_as_a_new_peer`).
Consequences: the six bars pass at the gate seed (numbers in the lane report). The rows' scenario changed on purpose:
`flappy` and `long-outage` now exercise dormancy, the ticket chain and the reconnect timeline at 8 and 32 clients under
their impairments, which no soak row did; their scripted rejoin presents its ticket too (the leave took one), so a
goodbye lost in an outage is a live takeover of the same `PeerId` instead of a second peer beside a ghost. The existing
test that pinned the removal (`long_outage_is_interrupted_once_then_removed_and_rejoins_as_a_new_peer`) keeps its
asserts under the knobs of a game that does not resume, and a new pin states the resume. With a deliberately early
removal timeout the two bars now pass (the players resume) while `involuntary_disconnects`, the gating bar, still
reports all three early removals; without the resume they fail as they did. Not done here: the reconnect attempts
present the 16-byte ticket (the three-round-trip resume); the one-round-trip credential of wire 6 on this path belongs
to part 3 (lane v07-wire6-soak-bars), which also owns the `asym-bufferbloat` server's tickets. Host-visible: none in
the engine crates; in `regia_net_soak`, two `Knobs` fields, three `ClientRecord` fields (serde defaults, so older
records load), `OUTAGE_RESUME_GRACE_MS`, two more entries in `GATING_BARS` (an older `flappy` or `long-outage` result
whose verdict xtask recomputes now reads as failed). Specs updated: spec 120 § 10.3 (Built note); book/agents/net-soak.md.

## ADR-10077: KI-NT batch 2 (transport, security): a plain link holds a candidate's packets until it validates; runtime refusals on the bridge's event stream; `net.rejections`; the rest decided
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.0 left thirteen transport and security known issues (KI-NT-018 to KI-NT-030; KI-NT-028 belongs to lane
v07-net-portmap-df-per-os). The v0.7 bar is "ready for DO27 to switch", security first. Wire 6 is open until 11-28.
Decision, per item:
1. **KI-NT-018, fixed (the part a fix can reach).** On a plain link (loopback, or `CryptoMode::Off`; `Auto` seals every
   other peer) nothing authenticates a packet, so the endpoints no longer apply one from an address the far end has not
   validated (ADR-8299 applied it at once and only refused to move). The packet still has to pass the cheap checks (the
   session token, a packet number newer than any received, the candidate's trial budget, no other peer there, not
   banned); it then makes the address a candidate and is **held**, at most `path::MAX_HELD_PLAIN_PACKETS` (16) packets
   and `path::MAX_HELD_PLAIN_BYTES` (24 KiB) per candidate, and the candidate is probed as before. When a packet from the
   candidate acknowledges a probe, the peer (or, on the client, the server) moves and the held packets are applied in
   arrival order, then that one, from the validated address (their refusals score, as the validated address's do). A
   candidate that never validates takes its packets with it when it is replaced (4 at most) or idle (5 s); a packet over
   the hold's bound is dropped and counted as a refused rebind. An honest NAT move on a plain link therefore loses
   nothing and is delayed by the probe's round trip; an off-path forger who copied the cleartext token can no longer
   inject a message, an acknowledgment or a stall-clock tick from an address it chose. Both `NetServer` and `NetClient`.
   The server's `Source::Unvalidated` delivery path (ADR-8606 residual (a), ADR-8666 (5)) is removed with it:
   `Connection::receive_unvalidated_within` is test-only. Decided, not changed (inherent to a link with no key): (a'') a
   spoofer of the *validated* address can still score or fail a plain peer, and (d) a token-holding forger still makes the
   server do one AEAD open per datagram it gets read on a sealed link, up to the 16,384 read cap (ADR-8666 (3): every cap
   that drops unopened datagrams at the peer's token drops the peer's own). Plain links are for loopback and LAN tests;
   the book says so.
2. **KI-NT-019, decided: no change.** A relay that carries both directions between a client and the server is, to
   either end, the client's NAT: it receives the probe and the client answers it through the relay, so the path
   validates (RFC 9000 § 9.3.3, § 21.1.3.3: an on-path attacker can cause migration). What it gains is the position it
   already had: it can delay or drop traffic, and on a sealed link it reads and forges nothing. Path validation is the
   protection against everyone who is *not* on the path (soak finding F1, `no_hijack`), and that bar holds. No transport
   can tell a full relay from a NAT without an out-of-band secret about the client's address, which no client has.
3. **KI-NT-020, decided: no change in v0.7.** A flood above the 16,384-datagram read cap of one receive waits in the
   socket's kernel queue, and the datagrams of other peers behind it wait for the next receive. Reading further (a bigger
   cap, or reading on and dropping by address) moves the same cost into the tick, one system call per datagram; a
   socket per peer (`connect`ed UDP) or `SO_REUSEPORT` sharding does not help, because the flood is addressed to the
   listening socket and a spoofed source picks its shard. The defense is in front of the server (a host firewall rate
   rule, the provider's filtering, Steam's relay network for Steam games); the engine's part is that a flood costs one
   lookup per datagram and is removed in 2 s (ADR-8181, soak row `flood`). Revisit with a batched receive
   (`recvmmsg`) if a soak row shows a tick over budget under the cap.
4. **KI-NT-021, decided: the bound stands.** A peer that skips packet numbers raises the reassembly stall deadline at most
   to `max(16 x RTO, 8 s)` of its own traffic (ADR-8521): it delays only its own reliable messages, and what it can make the
   server store is bounded per connection and per server, not by the deadline (ADR-7981 items 1-2). Skipping numbers is
   legal (RFC 9000 § 21.4), so a receiver cannot tell it from loss. The resynchronization after 8 packets more than 1,024
   ahead (ADR-8184) is the peer's own sequence: on a sealed link only the peer can send it, and on a plain link item 1 now
   keeps an unvalidated address's packets from reaching the connection.
5. **KI-NT-022, verified on wire 6, decided: by design.** After the client confirmed a resume, its older ticket is spent;
   a later join that presents it (a stale attempt of the same player, or a copy) is refused as a resume (`resume_epoch` on
   the one-round-trip flight; the 16-byte ticket on the full handshake) and becomes a fresh join, which any client without
   a ticket may make; the live peer is untouched. Pinned by `resume_server::a_dormant_peer_resumes_in_one_round_trip_and_its_ticket_is_single_use`
   (wire 6) and `resume_lost_accept::a_confirmed_takeover_spends_the_older_ticket` (both crypto modes). Refusing the join
   instead would gain nothing (the attempt can drop the ticket and join anyway) and would end an honest second
   instance; one seat per account is the game's identity rule, not the transport's.
6. **KI-NT-023, verified fixed by transport v2 (wire 5).** The reliable input lane rides the unordered inputs stream
   (spec 120 § 5.1, ADR-8302), so a lost input fragment holds back neither later inputs nor game messages, and a lost
   fragment is repaired by RFC 9002 loss detection (about a round trip), not an RFC 6298 resend timer. Pinned by the new
   `transport_streams::a_reliable_input_that_loses_a_fragment_is_repaired_in_about_a_round_trip`.
7. **KI-NT-024, fixed.** `ServerBridge::pump_in` returns the replication runtime's refusals (`NetNode::reject`) as
   `ServerEvent::Rejected` (error `WireError::Invalid(detail)`), read since the last pump without taking them from the node,
   ahead of the endpoint's events, so a fatal refusal comes before the `PeerLeft` it causes. ADR-7984 rejected this because
   the runtime does not own the endpoint's queue; the bridge owns both, so it splices them. Bounded at
   `MAX_KEPT_REJECTIONS`. `NetNode::take_rejections` keeps working (a host that reads both sees each refusal twice and
   should keep one).
8. **KI-NT-025, fixed.** New agent method `net.rejections`: per peer, refusals by lowercase code, for each published
   endpoint (the transport's `ServerEvent::Rejected`) and for the server world's runtime, peers that left included
   (`status::RejectionsByPeer`, bounded at `MAX_REJECTION_PEERS` = 256 peers, the stalest row evicted first). Counted by
   `NetServer::rejections_by_peer` and `NetNode::rejections_by_peer`; published in `EndpointReport::rejections`.
   Errors `net_unknown_endpoint`, `net_rejections_bad_peer`. Book page `agents/net-rejections.md`.
9. **KI-NT-026, decided: no change.** Builds older than version stamps are v0.5.x (wire 4 and older); a v0.7 server refuses
   them with `protocol_mismatch` whatever their content, so their missing content hash checks nothing that matters, and the
   1.5 s probe only runs against such a server, to word the refusal (ADR-7985). Wire 6 and every v0.6 build stamp.
10. **KI-NT-027, decided: QUIC stays loopback and LAN for v0.7 and v1.0.** The internet transport is sealed UDP
   (Noise `NX` handshakes and `NNpsk0` resumes, sealed records, path validation, the rate controller, PMTU probing) and Steam networking; every
   gated soak row measures that path. A QUIC WAN path would duplicate the crypto, congestion control and migration
   work under a second set of rules the soak does not cover, and needs certificate trust the engine does not have
   (`quic.rs` mints a self-signed certificate for loopback). Revisit after v1.0 only if a platform requires QUIC.
11. **KI-NT-029, decided: no change.** The kernel caps a socket buffer request (`net.core.rmem_max` on Linux); the bind warns
   and the guide names the sysctl. DSCP is a request the network may ignore. The third part is already answered: since ADR-8407 the live
   game socket's read-back and DSCP mark are in `net.status` (`endpoints[].socket`, `SocketReport`), and
   `net.socket_buffers` stays what its page says, a probe of what a fresh socket with given settings gets.
12. **KI-NT-030, verified fixed** by ce14f7b3e (11-17): the 42 test targets that drive worlds declare
   `required-features = ["ecs"]`, and `cargo test -p regia_net --no-default-features` builds and runs the core tests
   (`feature_matrix` `net-core` row builds them).
Alternatives rejected: dropping a plain candidate's packets instead of holding them (an honest NAT move would lose a round
trip of unreliable input); delivering held packets without the bound (a forger at a candidate address could fill memory
until the candidate is replaced); a new `DenyReason` for a spent ticket (item 5: a wire variant that changes nothing an
attacker can do).
Consequences: Host-visible: new `path::{MAX_HELD_PLAIN_PACKETS, MAX_HELD_PLAIN_BYTES}`, `status::{PeerRejections,
RejectionsByPeer, MAX_REJECTION_PEERS}` (re-exported at the crate root), `NetServer::rejections_by_peer`,
`NetNode::rejections_by_peer`; new field `EndpointReport::rejections` (struct literals add `rejections: Vec::new()`;
serde default); a `ServerBridge` host now gets `ServerEvent::Rejected` for runtime refusals. Behavior: on a plain link a
packet from an unvalidated address is applied only after the address validates. No wire, format or settings change
(wire 6 unchanged). Specs: 120 §§ 10.4, 11.2, 11.3, 11.6 Built notes. Book: `agents/net-rejections.md` (new),
`agents/net-trust.md`, `user-guide/networking.md`. Tests: `path_validation::{a_plain_packet_from_an_unvalidated_address_is_not_applied,
a_plain_server_packet_from_an_unvalidated_address_is_not_applied}`, `path::tests::a_plain_candidate_holds_a_bounded_queue_until_it_is_taken`,
`swallowed_decode_runtime::runtime_refusals_are_rejected_events_of_the_bridge`,
`status::tests::rejections_by_peer_count_per_code_and_stay_bounded`, `regia_agent net::tests::rejections_lists_refusals_per_peer_by_code`,
`transport_streams::a_reliable_input_that_loses_a_fragment_is_repaired_in_about_a_round_trip`;
`malformed_attribution::an_unvalidated_address_cannot_score_a_plain_link_peer` re-pinned (its base assertion that the
forgeries reached the connection was the KI-NT-018 behavior; it now asserts they arrived and none was applied).

## ADR-10052: Wire 6 window records: the unordered RPC frame on stream 7 and lockstep resume on the transport ticket (built); the far-tier record (designed, not built)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 parked three wire-shape items for the next wire step (plan v07-to-v10 § 2.2 item N-23): (1) the
far tier's reduced 5-byte transform record (§ 8.3, KI-NT-007), (2) the resume credential in the `NetLink` / lockstep
handshake payload so a lockstep seat resumes in one round trip like a replication peer (§ 10.3), and (3) the ECS
runtime's `ReliableUnordered` messages on their own unordered stream instead of inside the replication frame on
stream 3 (§ 5.2 open item of ADR-8302). v0.7 opens one wire step (6, ADR-8858 made it); everything wire-shaped must
ride it before the format freeze of 11-28.
Decision (3), built: a `RUMSG` frame (tag 9 after `TAG_STATE_ENTROPY` = 8: tag u8, tick varint, the message list of
`TICK`/`CMSG` frames without sequence numbers). Both sides put every `ReliableUnordered` message of a tick whose
payload is at most `runtime::MAX_RUMSG_PAYLOAD` (one bridge part, 16 KiB, less 512 bytes of framing) in `RUMSG`
frames on the reliable-unordered class; a frame holds at most 32 messages and that payload. The bridge maps the
class to stream 7 (`bridge::BRIDGE_UNORDERED`, the unordered RPC stream of § 5.1) and back. A frame there is always
one part, because an unordered stream hands parts over in any order: a part of several on stream 7 is refused
(`FramePartError::SplitUnordered`; the server kicks with `MalformedPacket`, a client closes with `ProtocolError`, the
oversized-frame rule). A received unordered message waits for its target entity as before (`unresolved_wait_ticks`)
but never for its tick (an ordered one still waits for its tick's frame), so a stalled replication stream does not
hold it. A larger message keeps its tick's ordered frame (exactly once, not unordered): splitting it across an
unordered stream would need per-frame reassembly ids, and a message over 15.5 KiB is a transfer, not an RPC.
The dormant hold (§ 10.3) keeps unordered messages with the rest and sends them as `RUMSG` frames on resume.
Rejected for (3): a new engine stream (stream 7 exists and is unordered at priority 2, the class's place); keeping the
messages in the `TICK` frame and reordering at the receiver (the frame itself waits on stream 3); splitting large
frames with a frame id on stream 7 (a second reassembly with its own caps for a size the class does not need).
Decision (1), designed, not built in this lane (time): the far tier's record is position only, 5 bytes, for an entity
whose profile has `rate_tiers` (both sides know the profile, so other profiles pay no bit): one `far` bit leads such
an entity's update; a far record is `x u15 | z u15 | y u10` = 40 bits, the entity's offset in its current cell
(`POSITION_CELL_BITS` = 20) shifted right by 5 (x, z: 32 steps, 3.2 cm at the default 1 mm step) and by 10 (y:
1.02 m), sent only while the receiver's acknowledged baseline is in the same cell (a cell change sends the normal
record). Both sides store the coarse integers as the new baseline (no drift), rotation and velocity keep the
baseline's, and an owned, forced or spawn record is never far. Owed with it: a codec round-trip test, a fuzz target
seed with far records, `TRANSFORM_RECORD_REVISION` 4 (the protocol hash refuses mixed builds), and a bandwidth row at
40 clients on the crowd scenario (`docs/perf/net-extrapolation-gate.md` style) against today's far tier, which sends
its normal delta at the far rate (7.25 B per moving update on the walking crowd).
Decision (2), built: the credential is the transport's own resume ticket (the 16-byte join-token ticket of ADR-8298
today, the 142-byte resumption ticket of ADR-8858 once v07-wire6-resume-server admits it), which already rides the
sealed handshake payload; the lockstep layer puts no second token on the wire. A lockstep host over `NetServer` with
`resume_grace_ms` above 0 keeps a silent seat's peer dormant like a replication peer. `lockstep::net::SeatPeers` binds
seats to peers and follows the server's events: `PeerDormant` keeps the binding (`peer_of` is `None`, so `send_host`
drops the seat's datagrams and marks a stream payload lagging, the rule for a seat without a connection),
`PeerResumed` resumes the seat in the same pass through `LockstepHost::resume_seat` (the token's rule: a member, or
removed for silence within `resume_window_ms`; authorized by the transport's ticket instead of the u64 token) and
reports `SeatLink::Resumed`, `PeerLeft` unbinds. The seat's first payload therefore leaves right behind the accept:
one round trip after the client's resume flight, where the token flow joins as a new peer and must first send its
token. The u64 `LockstepHost::resume_token` stays for a seat process that restarted (no ticket survives a restart).
Measured in `tests/lockstep_seat_resume.rs` (60 ms each way, seeded conditioner): see the lane report for the two
times. Rejected: a lockstep token field in `JoinToken` (17 struct literals and the `ResumeInit` payload change shape
for a credential the transport already proves); a lockstep-level resume message on stream 4 before the accept (it
would need its own replay rules; ADR-8858 already has them for the ticket).
Not covered: the lockstep soak (`regia_net_soak::lockstep`) has no scripted reconnect, so no soak row shows the
resume time on bad-wifi yet; that row is owed with a reconnect in that driver.
Consequences: wire 6 changes shape for (3) only ((2) adds no wire shape); a wire 5 peer is already refused by ADR-8858's bump. Host-visible API
(release fragment v0.1.28-v07-net-wire6-window-records, Upgrade): `FramePartError::SplitUnordered` (exhaustive
matches), `bridge::BRIDGE_UNORDERED`, `runtime::MAX_RUMSG_PAYLOAD`, `FrameAssembler::receive_unordered`, `lockstep::net::{SeatPeers, SeatLink}`, `LockstepHost::resume_seat`. Fuzz targets
`net.frame_to_client` / `net.frame_to_server` seed `RUMSG` frames, `net.bridge_frame` stream-7 parts (channel byte 2).
(1) must land before the 11-28 freeze or wait for the next wire step. Specs updated: spec 120 § 5.2 (Built
note); book/user-guide/networking.md (reliable streams).

## ADR-10067: v0.7 removes the names deprecated in v0.6: `Channel::Reliable` and `CongestionNotches`
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: spec 120 § 12.3 kept two names for one minor line: `Channel::Reliable` (ADR-8302: the alias of stream 2,
`Stream(StreamId::GAME_RPC)`; received stream-2 messages were reported as `Reliable` whichever form sent them, so one
stream had two `Channel` values and code had to know which one a receive path produced) and
`congestion::CongestionNotches` (ADR-8301: a loss-only budget whose name claimed congestion control; deprecated in its
docs only). v0.7 removes them (plan row N-24, lane v07-net-deprecated-removal). The brief also asks that the notch
oracle (`tests/notch_window_oracle.rs`, an independent model of the window and step rules) keep every assertion.
Decision: (1) The `Channel::Reliable` variant is gone. `Channel` has `Unreliable` and `Stream(StreamId)` only, and
`Channel::of_stream` returns `Stream(stream)` for every stream, stream 2 included. A new associated constant
`Channel::GAME_RPC` (= `Stream(StreamId::GAME_RPC)`) is the one-for-one replacement: it is the same value as the
explicit form, so `==` and `match` on it agree on both ends (a `Channel` derives structural `PartialEq`/`Eq`, so the
constant is a pattern). A constant instead of only the explicit form: about 265 call sites in 58 files (and every game
that used `Reliable`) port by one token, and there is still one value per stream. Every in-repo user is ported; the
one exhaustive match that listed both (`lockstep::net::channel_lane`) loses its now-unreachable arm. Serde: a
`Channel` serializes as `Stream(2)` for stream 2; `Reliable` no longer parses (no engine format stores a `Channel`).
(2) `CongestionNotches` is renamed `LossNotches` (same module, `NotchConfig`, constructor, methods and behavior). The
type is not deleted: its loss-step contract is still useful to a game that trades content for loss (fewer cosmetic
entities) under the allowance, and the brief keeps the oracle as its contract. Its docs now say what it is not
(congestion control) and that sends are sized by the transport's allowance (`NetServer::send_allowance`,
`Connection::send_allowance_bytes_per_second`) with this budget at most a cap below that. The oracle and the unit
tests run unchanged on `LossNotches`. Rejected: deleting the helper (drops a tested contract the brief keeps);
keeping `CongestionNotches` as a `type` alias (spec 120 § 12.3 removes the name in v0.7).
No wire change: stream 2's record form (`0x02`/`0x82`) and the wire version are untouched; the alias only existed in
the API. No format change.
Consequences: breaking API change for hosts (release fragment v0.1.28-v07-net-deprecated-removal, Upgrade):
`Channel::Reliable` -> `Channel::GAME_RPC`, `CongestionNotches` -> `LossNotches`; a host `match` on `Channel` with a
`Reliable` arm and a `Stream(_)` arm puts `Channel::GAME_RPC` first. `cargo xtask api-snapshot --update --breaking`
records both. The net-soak page no longer says the soak sizes snapshots with notches (it uses the allowance since
ADR-8301). Specs updated: spec 120 § 12.3 (Built note); book/user-guide/networking.md (channels, streams, a removal
table, rate control); book/agents/net-soak.md (snapshot sizing).

## ADR-10069: v0.7 hosting and lobby known issues: hidden join refusals, chat and plan replay, the ticket hook on every server, Steam answer matching, launch rollback field, join code withdrawal, mapping off switch, Steam mock MTU and rebinding
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.6.0 notes carry KI-NT-041..052 for hosting, relay, lobby and Steam (plan v0.7-to-v1.0 § 2.2 item A,
batch 4) and plan row N-19 lists design limits. Owner bar: best possible netcode; v0.7 bar: ready for DO27 to switch.
Decision:
1. KI-NT-046 (decided: it leaks). Hub lobby ids are sequential, so `hub_invite_only` / `hub_friends_only` against
   `lobby_not_found` let any session enumerate which private and friends-only lobbies exist. `HubServer::join` now
   answers a refused private or friends-only join with `lobby_not_found`, as for a missing id (every other lobby request
   already answers `not_in_lobby` alike, finding 3 of lobby-hub-join). The hub's refusal counter (`lobby.hub_status`
   `refused`) keeps `hub_invite_only` and `hub_friends_only` for the operator. The ignored review test
   `join_does_not_tell_a_missing_lobby_from_a_closed_one` runs; its draft expected `not_in_lobby` for all three, the
   ADR picks spec 89's `lobby_not_found`, the code a missing lobby already answered (the property, one shared code, is
   what it asserts).
2. KI-NT-045. Each kept chat line (lobby and global) carries a sequence number and the sender's handle then. A line the
   outbox cap drops marks the session's gap (the first dropped sequence per scope); the resync replays the kept lines
   from it on, in order, and clears it; a replay the cap drops again marks it again. A requeue that truncates marks the
   session for removal at `expire` (as before), so it needs no replay. A join plan whose push the cap dropped is kept
   on the join (member's and owner's copy) and the resync sends it once.
3. KI-NT-047. `JoinTicketCheck` is implemented for `Arc<T>`. `SessionServer::set_ticket_check` (and
   `NetSession::set_join_ticket_check`, kept across hosts and applied to a running server) checks the hello's `auth`
   bytes (`ConnectOptions::auth`, already on the wire) after the password and before the authenticator, on every hello
   from a transport link (links from `LOOPBACK_LINK_BASE` up, in-process players, are not checked), resumes included so
   a forged reconnect token cannot skip it. `Refuse` answers `auth_failed` with `ticket_refused`; a late refusal kicks
   with `kicked: ticket_refused`; `end_ticket` runs when the peer is retired (not in grace), when a link with a verdict
   is refused or drops before admission, and for the old ticket when a resume brings other bytes; equal bytes held by
   another peer or link are not ended. `ServerHost::set_join_ticket_check` hands it to the dedicated host's session.
   `NetLink::set_ticket_check` installs it on a link server and `NetLink::connect_with_join` sends a game's join data
   (the resume opener is now a closure holding it). No wire change.
4. KI-NT-048. `SteamAuthSessions` keeps, per Steam id, the begins still waiting for their first
   `ValidateAuthTicketResponse` (at most 8). Steam answers begins in order and the callback names only the Steam id,
   so the oldest waiting begin owns the next answer; an answer owned by a session that ended or was replaced is
   dropped. A cancel of the old ticket after its first answer (a crashed or closed client cancels its ticket) that
   arrives after the restart's begin, while the new session waits for its own first answer, is dropped too:
   `SteamAuthSessions::on_validate_answer` takes `SteamAuthAnswer::{Ok, Cancelled, Refused}` (the live callback maps
   `AuthTicketCancelled`); a ticket just issued is not cancelled before its first answer. Remaining limit: it assumes
   Steam answers every begun session once, in begin order.
5. KI-NT-050. `LobbyBackend::clear_server` (default: delete `regia.server`) is what a rolled-back launch calls. The
   Steam backend deletes the key and writes Steam's no-server values (0.0.0.0, port 0, no Steam id) over
   `SetLobbyGameServer`; Steam has no call that removes the field. Verified with a scripted backend; the real
   backend builds with `steamworks` and needs the owner's two-account session (KI-NT-049).
6. KI-NT-051. `MockDirection::mtu_bytes`: Steam fragments, so a message over the MTU passes the loss models once per
   fragment and is lost when one fragment is; the bottleneck carries each fragment's header. `mobile-4g` gets the
   harness's 1,232 bytes. `MockLink::rebinds_ms` and `rebind_gap_ms` model a NAT rebinding as a reroute gap (Steam
   addresses peers by Steam id; the model value 500 ms, `MOCK_REBIND_GAP_MS`, is not a measurement).
   `MockLink::profile_for_client` adds the harness's per-client extras (flaps shifted by `(i * 137) % 1000` ms,
   `flappy`'s timeout-plus-2 s outage at mid-run on every fourth client, `mobile-4g`'s rebinding at 40 % plus `i * 97`
   ms). A message that fits draws the same random numbers as before.
7. N-19, code withdrawal. A `Register` with a lifetime of 0 (cookie-checked like any register) removes the
   sender's lobby and answers `NotRegistered`, in every framing (registers are sent in the protocol 1 framing; a 0
   used to be clamped to a useless one-second lobby, so no client relied on it). No wire shape changes.
   `RelayRegistrar::revoke_code` sends it until confirmed (a code answer after the cookie-carrying 0 is a relay built
   before this change: the lobby lapses in 1 s); `ServerHost::revoke_join_code` and the console
   `revokecode` use it. Address join codes stay advisory: the host holds no state for them (change the password or
   port), a server-side nonce check would need a join field.
8. N-19 / KI-NT-041, mapping off switch. `--no-port-map` (`CliOverrides::no_port_map`) keeps a host with a remote
   relay from mapping; the host check reports `port_map_disabled`. The `server.toml` key (`[net] port_mapping = false`)
   changes that format and is listed for the v0.7 format batch 2 (v07-fmt-batch2-freeze), with its migrator.
9. KI-NT-044. `PlayerIdentity::load_or_create(path)` keeps a player's key across runs in a `server-key` format file
   (the same three fields, frozen at v1, owner-only, an exposed file refused): a player key is the same X25519 pair, so
   no new format is needed. `HubClientConfig::identity` takes it; the default stays a fresh key per connection.
10. Left, with reasons. KI-NT-041 rest: host-check sessions end 10 s after the introduction; the port-forward check
   cannot tell a forward from an address-only filter with one relay IP (RFC 5780 § 4.4 needs a second address).
   KI-NT-042: no full § 10.7 candidate checks in the relay path, a host-side NAT rebinding still loses relayed clients
   until they rejoin, the `net_game` CLI client resolves a code and connects directly (a relayed join needs a
   `JoinPath` driven beside `NetLink`), `RelayServer::update` is not measured at 4,096 allocations. KI-NT-049 and KI-NT-052 need the owner (two-account Steam, the GOG SDK). N-19 "resumed peer dropped
   while Loading": fixed by ADR-8623 (`session_resume::a_drop_while_loading_after_a_resume_keeps_the_slot`).
Consequences: A private lobby's existence no longer leaks through `join`; a client sees `lobby_not_found` for a
friends-only lobby whose owner has not listed it. Store tickets now gate session games and the dedicated server, so a
DO27-style Steam host can check ownership without dropping to `NetServer`. Upgrade: `LobbyBackend` gained the defaulted
`clear_server`; `MockDirection`, `MockLink`, `MockNetStats` and `CliOverrides` gained public fields (struct literals add
them or use `..Default::default()`); `NetLink`'s resume opener changed (private). Specs updated: 120 § 10.7, § 10.8 and
the ticket-hook section (Built notes), 89 (Built note); book: net-lobby-hub, net-join-helpers, net-host-check,
net-relay, net-dedicated-server, net-lobbies, user-guide/networking.

## ADR-10062: det small follow-ups (plan D-10) and v0.6.0 known issues KI-GP-003..005
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Plan v0.7 § 2.2 item B, row D-10, collects small determinism follow-ups from earlier lane reports, plus three
v0.6.0 known issues: KI-GP-003 (the ECS desync hash's default order depends on entity ids; no agent divergence
injection), KI-GP-004 (the desync mixer cannot see unit fields or skipped option slots and folds hash containers in
iteration order; a partial flag names the tick, not the system), KI-GP-005 (`LockstepSim` and `DetInputSim` have no
blanket impl; `sim.host_snapshot` has no form for a future tick).
Decision:
- **`RegionKey` / `ClusterFlow` (fixed).** `regia_nav::det::flow` used the default 8-cell cluster rectangles and the
  one-byte `NavGrid::labels` while `GridSettings::cluster_cells` is configurable (two-byte `wide_labels` from 16): another
  cluster size gave wrong local fields, and a two-byte grid panicked. `CellRect::cluster` now uses
  `NavGrid::cluster_cells`, every label read goes through the grid's label view at either width, and the public
  `RegionKey` widens to `(u32, u16)` (the label is `NavGrid::region_label`). At the default size the results, the flow
  pin and every existing test are unchanged. Test: `cluster_flow_follows_the_grid_cluster_size` (4, 16 and 32 cells:
  reachability, the bound with the grid's own cluster size, exact arrival cost, region keys, a stamp sync).
- **Float-policy F4 (fixed).** `regia_detsim::golden::record` and `record_injected` call
  `fpu::ensure_default_fp_env()` before the scenario resets, so a thread that inherited flush-to-zero records the
  clean trace instead of a false divergence; `check_golden` adds a sentence to `DetReport::detail` when it had to
  reset the environment. `fpu::set_flush_to_zero_for_tests` is also compiled for the crate's own unit tests
  (`cfg(test)`), still never in a runtime build. No golden moves (every runner already starts on a default thread).
- **Yaw wrap (fixed, ADR-8638's known issue).** `ground_vehicle::{tracked, wheeled}::step` store the yaw wrapped to
  `(-PI, PI]` (the hover step's `wrap_pi`, now `pub(crate)`) after every step; the mid-step nose still uses the
  unwrapped sum of the start yaw and this step's turn, so motion inside a step is unchanged. Unwrapped, a vehicle
  that kept turning lost f32 heading precision without bound (the ulp of a 1e4 rad yaw is 1 ms of a 1 rad/s turn).
  The published bits change once a vehicle has turned past PI: the `ground_vehicle_mix` det golden moves from tick 22
  (4987f794ad0b2650 -> 72fb7c516c003ea2, the same on x86_64-linux and aarch64-macos; re-recorded in its own commit,
  the aarch64-android line dropped until the test Pixel runs it). No other det golden moved. The wheeled radius test now sums the per-tick turn instead of reading
  an unwrapped yaw (same -6 rad bound). `regia_physics::vehicle_track` delegates to the tracked step, so `TrackState::yaw`
  is wrapped too; its ADR-8551 reference comparison wraps the reference's yaw by the same whole-turn loop and keeps `==`.
- **CRLF in `to_ron` (fixed: lint gap).** The four net writers were fixed earlier and `regia_core::ron_pretty()` plus
  the `ron_pretty_lint` test guard direct `PrettyConfig::default/new`, but the lint missed
  `let p: PrettyConfig = Default::default()` (and `<PrettyConfig as Default>::default`), the form the lockstep
  crates use because they cannot depend on `regia_core`. The lint now refuses that form unless the same or the next
  line pins `new_line`; a planted-text test proves it on Linux (the CRLF itself shows only on Windows).
- **ECS desync order (KI-GP-003, fixed by an option).** `EcsDesyncHash::order_by_content` and
  `DesyncHashPlugin::order_by_content`: each component row is folded by its own word (a `Mix` with a fixed tag and the
  outer float rule) and the column folds the sorted row words, then the count, so entity ids do not matter; a failing
  `Serialize` still marks the row partial (new `Mix::note_errors`). The default stays the entity id (pinned words
  unchanged; it also sees two entities swapping their whole values, which content order cannot), and `order_by` stays
  the choice for games with a lockstep id. Agent-protocol divergence injection stays with spec 120's N226/N227.
- **KI-GP-004 (decided, words unchanged).** `Mix`'s words are DO27's (ADR-8078): folding unit fields, skipped option
  slots or sorted hash containers changes the word of every state that has them, which is a hash-version change both
  sides must take on the same build. That belongs to the DO27 switch package (plan v0.7 F, format batch 2), not a
  follow-up lane: the lead or owner schedules it with DO27. Meanwhile det-scan's `hash_iteration` rule and the
  lockstep clippy list keep hash containers out of lockstep state, and the hash docs already state the unit/skip
  limits (ADR-8621). Naming the system of a partial row needs a per-system partial vector in `SystemRing`
  (`sysring` version bump): left for the same batch.
- **KI-GP-005 (fixed: an adapter, since no blanket impl can compile).** `impl<T: DetInputSim<N>> LockstepSim for T`
  does not compile: `N` is not constrained by `LockstepSim`, and `FixedStepSim`'s `Frame`, `write_frame` and `tick`
  cannot be derived from a `DetInputSim` (no frame type, no tick counter). `regia_framework::sim_host::DetInputHost<S,
  F, N>` adapts one: it owns the boundary tick, steps through `replay::advance` (`Inputs = TickInputs<S::Input>`; the
  frame for host tick `t` carries the sim's tick `t - 1`, asserted in debug builds), publishes `F: DetInputFrame<S>`
  (`()` publishes nothing), keeps the last `TickHashes`, delegates `SystemFold` (so `start_lockstep_with_desync`
  works), and its `DetState` body is the boundary tick then the sim's body under `adapter_tag(S::STATE_TAG)` (the last
  tag byte's high bit flipped) and the sim's version, so a bare sim snapshot and an adapter snapshot never load as
  each other. `sim.host_snapshot { tick }` (agent) now takes a snapshot at a tick boundary: at once when the sim is
  there, `sim_host_snapshot_tick_passed` when it is past it (that error used to fall through to `sim_host_stopped`), and
  for a tick ahead `{ tick, pending: true, kept: false }` with the request kept; the next call with the same tick
  collects it. No call blocks waiting for a future tick.
- **Not changed here.** The doubled `[features]` table in `regia_detsim/Cargo.toml` was fixed on the integration line
  (90152c7a5) and cargo refuses such a manifest, so no test is added. The k-th gather early stop landed with
  v07-det-spatial-nearest-p99 (ADR-8875). The DetHover predicted-schedule plugin landed with net-hover-prediction
  (`NetHover`, `DetHoverSteppedExternally`, merged on integ-v07a). Windows tick-profile rows (GetThreadTimes 15.6 ms
  quanta, ADR-8498) need a calibrated cycle clock (`QueryThreadCycleTime` scaled by a TSC-to-QPC ratio measured at
  profiler start) that only a Windows host can prove; left with `--clock wall` as the workaround.
Consequences: `RegionKey`'s label is `u16` (code that built a key from a `u8` label converts with `u16::from`);
ground-vehicle yaw readers get a bounded angle (code that read the yaw as a cumulative turn must sum the per-step
change); ECS games without lockstep ids have an order that ignores entity ids. Release fragment
docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-det-small-followups.md. Book: det-ground-vehicles.md, desync-hash-ecs.md.

## ADR-10070: v0.7 world and gameplay known issues: tunnel chokes, the leaver's character, steep ramp facets, cheap-area search, flag returns, fog cells, Lockstep labels, video audio ring
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: lane v07-ki-world-gameplay (plan v0.7 § 2.2 item H) owns the v0.6.0 known issues KI-WD-015, KI-WD-017,
KI-WD-030, KI-WD-031, KI-ED-019, KI-GP-018, KI-GP-030, KI-GP-033 and KI-AU-028; WD-015, WD-030 and GP-033 face DO27.
(1) KI-WD-030: ADR-8448 left `Crowd::choke_near` without tunnel mouths and junctions because `NavGrid` has no tunnel
layer; `DetAgents::register_choke` was the seam. The layer exists now as `det::layer::TunnelLayer` (portals and
junctions, built by the host per map), still separate from the grid. (2) KI-GP-033: since ADR-2413 a `Gone` peer's
entities go to the server by default, so the character `DefaultRules` (or any rules) spawned for a remote player stays
in the world, server-owned, after the player leaves; `net_session_rules` pinned that ("the player's character stays").
(3) KI-WD-015: the pinned Stage A mesher cuts every four-corner floor piece along the same diagonal; on a bent or
banked ramp one of the two triangles can be steeper than `FACET_SLOPE_LIMIT` (Switchbacks: 1.58 > 1.50, ADR-8447).
DO27's Stage B ruling (ADR-8359) allows the mesher fix only inside the one Stage B sim-version bump, because a changed
cut moves sim bits on every tunnel map; that bump is owner decision 2 of the v0.7 plan (format batch 2).
Decision:
1. **Tunnel chokes (KI-WD-030).** `Crowd::register_tunnel_chokes(&TunnelLayer) -> usize` and
   `DetAgents::register_tunnel_chokes` register each portal's tunnel node (the ramp top at the mouth), ascending, then
   each junction node, ascending, through `register_choke` (its one-metre merge applies; a second call adds none). The
   host calls it once per map after `TunnelLayer::build`. `choke_near` and its `grid` argument are unchanged, so no
   plan, slot or lane bit moves for a host that does not call it. The other parts of the v0.6.0 note (pilot-only
