   crawlways, one-way reservation, dirty-tile re-bake, the layered-bake file, the 16 km limit, ECS linking) stay open:
   each is a navigation feature of its own (a crawlway graph search, a reservation protocol, an incremental bake, a
   frozen format), not a fix, and needs its own lane.
2. **The leaver's character (KI-GP-033).** `regia_net::session::NetDespawnWithOwner` (component, reflected): the
   default hand-off despawns a marked entity whose owner is `Gone`, after a live `NetSuccessor` (which still wins)
   and before the server fallback. The framework's remote join hook inserts it with the `NetOwner` on the character
   it spawns from the rules' `SpawnRequest`. Rules keep a character by removing the marker in `on_player_left` (it then
   goes to the server as before) or by naming a live successor. A takeover bot lifts the marker while it drives the
   dropped player's character (held as a private mark on the character) and restores it when it hands the character
   back; a takeover that outlives its player keeps the character. The hook order is unchanged: the leave hooks
   (rules, persistence capture) still read the character before the hand-off. `net_session_rules`'s
   "the player's character stays, server-owned" assertion was the known issue itself; it now asserts the despawn
   (and its `Despawn` hand-off record), and the kept path is tested in its own test. Local split-screen removal
   (`PlayerManager::remove_player`) is unchanged: it never spawned a networked character.
3. **The steep ramp facets (KI-WD-015): measured, not fixed; owner and DO27 ruling.** A lane test (since removed with
   its code, lane commit history) built the alternative cut: each four-corner floor piece (passage floor, lip, sill,
   mouth cap) split along the diagonal whose steeper triangle is flatter. Measured through the cook's own
   `quantize_mesh` and `floor_slope`, Switchbacks on the canyon ground: pinned cut 2 floor facets over 1.50, worst
   1.582; flattest cut 2 over, worst 1.576 (3526 triangles either way). The diagonal is not the cause: the two facets
   sit at the ramps' bend near (-178, 96) and its mirror (ADR-8447: (-172.5, 90.2), (173.8, 92.6)), where the climb
   lands on the short inner edge of the turn, so both cuts of that piece are steep. Any fix that keeps DO27's
   conditions (centreline heights and width unchanged, ADR-8359) must change how the mesher places the floor's edge
   heights or samples bends, which moves sim bits on every tunnel map: it belongs to the Stage B sim-version bump
   (owner decision 2 of the v0.7 plan), and the ruling that names "the quad-split mesher fix" must be revised, since a
   quad-split change alone measurably does not clear the check. A floor that is level across its width and climbs
   through a tight bend must be steep on the bend's short inner edge, so the ways out are: (a) bank the floor across
   the bend (edge heights follow each edge's own length; the centreline heights and the width stay, the floor is no
   longer level across), (b) climb less through bends (moves the centreline heights, which the ruling excludes), (c) a
   wider bend radius in the layouts (an authoring change), or (d) keep the hashed `waive` list. The owner and DO27
   pick one for the Stage B bump; until then the authored `waive` list stays. No code change for this item; the
   option was removed instead of shipping an API that does not fix the issue.
4. **The cell heuristic and cheap areas (KI-WD-031).** The fine cell search scales its own heuristic when an area is
   cheaper than flat ground, instead of leaving that to the caller: with `c = max(1, (COST_FLAT * min_area_pct + 50) /
   100)` the cheapest straight step costs `c` and the cheapest diagonal `d = 14 * c / 10` (floored), and the heuristic
   becomes `h * d / 14`, below both shares, so it stays admissible. When `d` is 14 (no area under 95 %) nothing is
   scaled and every plan bit is unchanged. The coarse search already clamps region costs to `COST_FLAT`, so its
   heuristic stays admissible and is not touched. "One cost overlay per grid" is kept by design (ADR-8379: a game with
   per-team threat keeps one grid per team or folds the teams into one overlay). `set_overlay` relabelling every
   cluster stays: each relabel bumps the cluster generations that `DetAgents` reads as re-plan triggers, so
   relabelling only the clusters whose overlay cells changed would change which agents re-plan on every overlay
   swap, a lockstep bit change that needs its own versioned lane. The surface-only path-request queue stays open.
5. **Flag returns anywhere and the `WinCondition` adapter (KI-GP-030).** `rules.match_step` takes `return_zones`
   (at most 64 inclusive boxes `{ min, max }`): its drop check returns a flag lying inside any box, wherever it
   landed; a bad box is `F0002` (no new code). `MatchSession::report_win_condition(&dyn WinCondition, &dyn
   MatchView) -> Option<Outcome>` evaluates any win rule and ends the match through `report_condition` with `Draw`
   (winner 0), `LastStanding` (`lives`), `Destroyed` (`structures`) or `Ended`; a match already over is left alone.
6. **Fog cells on the ground, explored ground per team (KI-GP-018).** `FogGrid::update_on_ground(vision, los, ground)`
   applies the elevation rule to cells with the caller's ground height at each cell center (the same radius rule as
   for entities, the hook asked at the same point); without a rule it equals `update`. `FogViewSim::with_cell_ground`
   uses it. `FogViewSim::with_explored_per_team()` (opt-in, one vision rebuild and grid update per player team per
   snapshot) keeps every player team's grid; `set_viewer` swaps grids instead of clearing, and `team_grid(team)` reads
   one. Two parts of the note are by design: ghosts are drawn by the game (ADR-8473 keeps last-seen state, not a
   renderer) and lockstep fog is presentation only (fog must never feed the lockstep simulation, ADR-8523/8524).
7. **Lockstep labels in the editor (KI-ED-019).** `regia_render::gizmos::stroke_text_segments(text, size, anchor)`
   lays text out with the gizmo stroke font as 2D segments (the same layout as `GizmoBuffer::text`); the editor's
   Show > Lockstep overlay draws each det debug text label with it (cap height `DET_DEBUG_TEXT_M` 0.4, the running
   game's value, facing +Z, centered on its point, in its role's color). The other half, contacts and queries showing
   from the tick after the switch turns on, is by design: they are recorded while the broadphase pass and the queries
   run, so a tick that was already stepped has none to show without running its pass again, which a read-only debug
   view must not do (ADR-8562); the grid and occupancy, which are read from the state, show at once.
8. **Video audio without a declared frame period (KI-AU-028).** `pcm_ring_frames` sizes the ring of a clip with no
   `DefaultDuration` for the 4 s cap (still under the 8 MiB byte cap, ADR-7635) instead of a 30 fps guess, so a
   low-rate clip without it no longer overflows: 1.5 MB per 48 kHz stereo player, the ring adds no latency (only queued
   audio does, ADR-7563). `pcm_ring_covers_the_decode_ahead_window` pinned the old guess ("no declared period is 30
   fps"), and so did the undeclared-period row of `pcm_ring_size_is_unchanged_for_real_content` (ADR-7635's proof
   that the byte cap left real content alone); both now assert the 4 s ring, every declared-period row is unchanged. The other two parts are by design (ADR-7563 point 5 and point 2): a live
   `Lockstep` player outside render-out takes audio at the device's pace, because per-step pops would take samples the
   mixer stream also takes or starve the device, while render-out, the consumer that needs exact counts, steps its
   mixdown by the same integer rule; and an accurate resync holds the old picture until the decoder lands, presenting
   the newest due picture after 120 ticks, so a slow decoder cannot freeze the clip.
9. **Left for a render lane (KI-WD-017), with the cause.** The frame warm (`FrameRenderer::prewarm`) builds the
   double-sided and transmissive (glass) pipeline sets only when a mesh in the warm scene carries such a material;
   mesh-layer chunk materials are resolved by the terrain stream (`layer_material`) and their chunks stream in after the
   warm, so a non-opaque or double-sided layer material is never in the warm scene. The fix is a route from the
   resolved layer materials into the warm list (or one warm stand-in draw per distinct layer material) with a lavapipe
   pipeline-count test in the style of `no_pipeline_created_on_update_after_warm`; that is render-core warm code, not
   this lane's area.
Consequences: new public items only (`register_tunnel_chokes` x2, `NetDespawnWithOwner`, `report_win_condition`,
`regia_agent::match_rules::MAX_RETURN_ZONES`, the optional `return_zones` parameter, `FogGrid::update_on_ground`,
`FogViewSim::{with_explored_per_team, with_cell_ground, team_grid}`, `regia_render::gizmos::stroke_text_segments`,
`regia_editor::overlays::DET_DEBUG_TEXT_M`); no struct literal or exhaustive match breaks. Behavior changes: a remote
player's rules-spawned character no longer outlives the player (a game that relied on that removes the marker in
`on_player_left`); a det grid with an area under 95 % plans optimal routes, so its plans can differ from v0.6.x (every
peer runs the same rule); a video clip without `DefaultDuration` gets a 4 s audio ring. No format, golden, agent method
or error code changes. Specs and pages: book/agents/det-grid.md (crowd, areas), book/agents/net-session-players.md
(hand-off), book/agents/match-rules.md (return zones, win conditions), book/agents/fog-of-war.md (cells on the ground,
explored per team), book/agents/editor.md (Lockstep labels), book/agents/video-playback.md and
docs/specs/50-video-playback.md § 2.4 (the ring). Fragment: docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-ki-world-gameplay.md.

## ADR-8537: Mesh-layer joins: picks, the reference export, shadows and canonical collider pieces (plan W-17)
Date: 2026-11-18   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-7974 (spec 26 § 2a.6, § 2a.8) has the cooked mesh layers join the terrain's other consumers: picks, the
path tracer's reference export, the GI bake, shadows and (for hosts that do not lockstep) engine-physics colliders.
Lane W-17 (staged item 15-05, amended A1/A2 by the lead) builds them on the merged W-15 (lattice cut) and W-16 (chunk
stream) head.
Decision:
1. **Pick (built).** A terrain entity with `TerrainMeshLayers` cuts its filled holes as the draw does: the CPU mirror
   `HolesMask::contains_drawn(x, z, lattice)` (an open named hole the lattice holds is cut by its lattice triangles,
   `LatticeHoleCut::cuts_hole`; every other footprint by its shape, as `gpu_words_with_lattice`). The open mouths'
   bands and throats at LOD 0 are terrain surface: `TerrainMeshLayers::raycast_bands` (two-sided ray/triangle), a hit
   reported as `PickSurface::Terrain`, layer 0, the terrain entity. Both `regia_pick` (`world.pick`,
   `raycast_terrain_entity`) and `regia_terrain::pick_terrain` (`terrain.raycast`) do this; the lattice cut is built
   once per terrain per ray (`lattice_hole_cut`). Amendment A2: picks over a mouth use the `TerrainMeshLayers` lattice
   path, not `WorldGeom::segment` (W-11's segment is the sim's query on the canonical set; the pick answers what is
   drawn). Without the component every path is the base's (`contains_drawn(.., None)` is `contains`).
2. **Path tracer reference export (built: band and collar; deferred: LOD 0 of every chunk).** The agent's `current`
   reference trace adds `TerrainMeshLayers::add_reference_pieces` to the frame export: one mesh per open mouth's band
   (LOD 0, plus throat) and one per collar, keys `REFERENCE_PIECE_TAG | mouth << 1 | collar`, the chunks' rock
   material, in the export's local frame. Resident chunk entities are in the export already, at their drawn LOD.
   Deferred (needs design): forcing LOD 0 of every chunk in the export range means reading the chunk LOD files from
   the cooked cache (or the asset server) inside the agent call; which reader and which range (the camera's frustum,
   the trace's bounds) are open.
3. **GI bake export (deferred, needs design).** `.bake.ron` v1 `meshes` entries name a source file resolved against
   the description's root. The chunk LOD 0 meshes live in the cooked cache (`cooked_file_name(chunk_lod_asset_id)`),
   outside the asset root the exporter's paths use, and the band and the collar are not files at all. Either the
   description gains an inline-triangles or cooked-cache source (a shape change, which the brief stops at), or the
   mesh-layer cook writes the band and collar as sub-assets next to the chunk LODs and the exporter learns a
   cooked-cache root. Listed for the lead; no code.
4. **Shadows (already done, verified).** Chunk entities of a casting layer extract as `ShadowCast::All`; a
   `cast_shadows: false` layer's carry `NotShadowCaster` and extract as `ShadowCast::Off`
   (`chunk_entities_cast_unless_told_not_to`).
5. **Colliders (built: the CPU pieces and the tile-following physics pieces; deferred: the cooked flag and the
   untiled body).** Amendment A1: the pieces are the canonical
   triangles (`WorldGeom::triangles`, i32 mm through `mm_to_m`), never the render LODs or the band:
   `TerrainMeshLayers::collider_pieces` gives one `LayerColliderPiece` per layer and presentation chunk (the cook's
   XZ-centroid rule), or one per layer without a presentation section; blocker plugs are left out (the sim's, through
   `GeomState`). They are for hosts that do not lockstep: a lockstep sim uses `regia_world_geom`'s queries (spec 121:
   "an engine physics step that is not bit-identical is not the collision"). Neither crate depends on the other
   (`regia_physics` reaches `regia_terrain` only as a dev-dependency), so the physics half is a component in
   `regia_physics`, `TerrainLayerColliders` (pieces in the heightfield's frame), that the host fills from
   `collider_pieces`. `step_terrain_tiles` (no new system, so the fixed schedule is unchanged) builds a piece as a
   `TriMesh` on the terrain's static body while a built tile overlaps its chunk, in the same step, within
   `max_tiles_per_step`; it removes it when no built tile is under it, when the component changes or goes, and with a
   rebuilt body. A pending piece keeps the step from settling (it counts in `pending_tiles`). Deferred: (a) a terrain
   without `TerrainTileCollision` ignores the component (one trimesh per layer on an untiled body needs the collider
   sync to learn about it); (b) the `collider` flag is in the source document (`MeshLayersDocument`) but not in
   the cooked presentation section, so the run time cannot see it without a `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` change (the
   format is new on the v0.6 line; adding `CookedLayer::collider` there is a presentation version 2 with the recook
   rule), so the level loader does not insert the component; the host opts in.
Consequences: a terrain without `TerrainMeshLayers` picks bit for bit as before (`a_terrain_without_layers_picks_as_before`).
A pick into an open mouth hits the band or the layer, never the cut ground, and ground the lattice keeps is ground even
inside the coverage shape. The agent's `current` reference trace gains the band and collar instances when a terrain has
open mouths. No file format, agent schema or error code changes. Spec 26 § 2a.6 and § 2a.8 gain as-built notes.

## ADR-8872: Mesh-layer joins land on the seam band: drawn chunks at LOD 0 in the reference trace, the cooked `collider` flag (format batch 2), the untiled-body colliders (plan W-09)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The joins of ADR-8537 (lane do27-mesh-layers-joins, W-17) were built on the v0.6 line but not in v0.6.0. Lane
v07-meshlayers-joins-land merges them onto the v0.7 seam band (seam-gpu-passes, ADR-8824, which carries
tunnels-stage-b-correctness, native-acceptance-suite and tunnels-perf-low-tiers) and builds the three deferred items
DO27 needs for its switch: LOD 0 in traces (item 2), the cooked `collider` flag (item 5b) and the untiled-body
collider (item 5a). The GI bake export (item 3) is lane v07-meshlayers-gi-export's. The merge brought two semantic
conflicts: a joins test built `TerrainMeshLayersCooked` without the seam band's `chunk_importer`, and the joins test
cook of Switchbacks met the line's known ramp-facet red (`ramp_facet_slope_over_limit`, slope 1.58 over 1.50, W-11),
which every other test cook on the line waives with `waive_ramp_facets`; the joins cook now does the same. Third, the
seam band's mouth cut puts a ground-level canonical triangle edge on a lattice line the joins pick test samples
(x = 20 m): the pick (`regia_pick::ray_triangle`, edges inside with a `1e-6` barycentric slack, as documented) hits it
and the test's strict Möller-Trumbore oracle missed it by float rounding (11.000 m against 11.099 m). The oracle now
brute-forces `regia_pick::ray_triangle` itself, so it follows the documented edge rule; the assertions are unchanged.
Decision:
1. **Drawn chunks at LOD 0 in the reference trace.** Reader: the stream's own (`load_chunk_mesh`: the asset server
   when the world has one, else the layers' `chunk_dir`), so the trace reads what the stream would. Range: the drawn
   set, every `TerrainLayerChunk` entity whose mesh has instances in the frame export (the resident chunks within the
   stream's visible radius), so the trace and the raster frame hold the same chunks; a chunk outside the radius is in
   neither. `regia_terrain::reference_chunks_lod0` re-points those instances at the chunk's cooked LOD 0 under
   `REFERENCE_CHUNK_TAG | layer << 32 | z << 16 | x` keys; a chunk already at LOD 0 is left as drawn; a LOD 0 that does
   not load leaves the drawn LOD and logs `meshlayers_reference_lod0`. The owner is the stream's (the first terrain
   entity whose `TerrainMeshLayers` has a presentation section). `seeing.reference_trace` scene `current` calls it
   after the band and collar pieces and adds `mesh_layer_chunks: { lod0, swapped, failed }` to its `scene_info` when a
   chunk was seen (the key is absent otherwise, so replies without layers are unchanged).
2. **The cooked `collider` flag (format batch 2 row).** `CookedLayer::collider` (chunk section version 3) carries the
   source layer's `collider`. The chunk section is part of `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked`'s fingerprint, so the file
   version moves 1 -> 2 (one step from v0.6.0's v1, ADR-7724): the header, canonical and presentation sections keep
   their shape. A version-2 chunk section (v0.6.0's) migrates on load with every `collider` false (the true value is
   in the source document, and the cook writes it); version 1 stays `meshlayers_presentation_stale`. Migrator:
   `regia_terrain::upgrade_cooked_mesh_layers` (header number plus the chunk section re-encoded; the canonical and
   presentation bytes are kept, so the lockstep `content_hash` and Stage A do not move), registered for
   `regia upgrade-project` (`migrate_meshlayers_cooked`, replacing the `unmigrated` row) and the fuzz target's loader;
   `cooked_migration_sources` is `[1]`. The cook's up-to-date test also compares the file version and each layer's
   `collider`, so an upgraded file is written again when its document sets the flag.
   `TerrainMeshLayers::cooked_collider_pieces` is `collider_pieces` of the flagged layers (empty without a
   presentation section); `collider_pieces` keeps answering for every layer. `terrain.mesh_layers` rows gain
   `collider`. The level loader still does not insert `regia_physics::TerrainLayerColliders`: `regia_terrain` does
   not depend on `regia_physics`, and the heightfield `Collider` is the host's (often a scene component on another
   entity than the one `spawn_level_terrain` makes), so the host builds the component from `cooked_collider_pieces`.
3. **The untiled body.** A terrain with `TerrainLayerColliders` and no `TerrainTileCollision` gets one `TriMesh` per
   layer (spec 26 § 2a.8 "Without tiling, one trimesh per layer"): the triangles of the pieces with the same
   `TerrainColliderPiece::layer` (new field, the canonical `TriRef::layer`), in piece order, on the terrain's body
   with the heightfield's offset and material, hits reporting the terrain. Built in `step_terrain_tiles` (no new
   system, so the fixed schedule and the determinism traces do not move) before its tile and gate early returns, in
   entity order, all in one step; rebuilt when the component, the collider or the body changes; removed when the
   component, the body or the entity goes, or the terrain becomes tiled. Not counted in `TerrainTileStats`.
Consequences: DO27's switch has the three joins it asked for on the v0.7 line. `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` is a
format batch 2 row (v2): `cargo xtask check-formats` is red on this branch until the freeze lane
(v07-fmt-batch2-freeze) runs `check-formats --update`; the corpus gains `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked/v2.bin` (v1.bin
kept byte for byte). `TerrainColliderPiece` gains `layer` (unreleased: ADR-8537's type is not in v0.6.0).
`CookedLayer` gains `collider` (a struct-literal break for hosts that build presentation sections). Specs: spec 26
§ 2a.6 and § 2a.8 as-built notes; docs/formats/terrain.md § 13.

## ADR-10071: Volume-sourced mesh layers through the host's field (spec 26 § 2a.9, cites ADR-7974)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 26 § 2a.9 lists a `Volume { sdf, iso, cell_m }` layer source: meshed per chunk by `mesh_chunk`, clipped
under the LOD-0 ground, its clip loop at each filled hole zippered like an authored loop (DO27 request TUNNELS_FIX
terrain-mesh-layers-overhangs; KI-WD-016 in the v0.6.0 notes: the cook refused it with `cook_not_built`). Three facts
on the v0.7 line shape the build. (1) There is no volume file format: `sdf` would name one, but the only designed
volume file is the voxel core's `<map>.voxfield` (spec 122, ADR-8116), still a `proposed-formats.ron` row, and § 2a.10
names no other; a new format is out of this lane's scope. (2) `regia_world_geom` (the canonical cook) cannot mesh a
volume: the dual contouring lives in `regia_terrain`, which depends on it. (3) § 2a.9 does not say where a volume
layer's filled-hole footprint comes from: a `Passages` layer's comes from its openings, and a volume has none.
Decision:
1. **The host supplies the field.** `regia_asset_pipeline::terrain_mesh_layers::cook_mesh_layers_with_volumes(req,
   &[VolumeSource])` takes, per `sdf` name, a `&dyn SdfField` (negative inside the solid), the world box to mesh and a
   fingerprint for the input hash. `cook_mesh_layers` is that call with no volumes (byte for byte as before), and a
   `Volume` layer without a `VolumeSource` is still `cook_not_built`. The `.voxfield` reader, when V-02 builds it, is
   one more `VolumeSource` (its body hash the fingerprint); the document format does not change.
2. **Mesh, then clip (regia_terrain `mesh_layer::volume`).** `mesh_volume_layer` meshes the field minus `iso` with
   `mesh_chunk` on one global cell grid (block origins `k * cell_m`), in blocks of the document's `chunk_m` over
   `cell_m` cells, and welds them by position (the module's stitch contract: the union does not depend on the blocks;
   tested with two block sizes). `clip_below_ground` keeps what lies under the LOD-0 lattice ground (the engine's
   diagonal, interpolated in f64): a crossing edge is split linearly in the height difference, from its endpoints in
   a fixed order so both triangles of the edge get the same bits, and the new vertex is placed on the ground; a
   triangle keeps one or two parts in its own winding. The clip runs everywhere, not only outside filled holes, so
   the dome of a cave that breaks the surface is removed inside the mouth too (the brief's "outside filled holes"
   bounds only the acceptance check). The new edges chain into closed clip loops on the ground.
3. **The clip loop is the mouth.** A volume layer's `fills` take its clip loops in `(z, x)` order of each loop's first
   vertex; the loop's XZ polygon (millimetres, a fan from its mean point) is the hole's `MouthFootprint`, so the cook's
   lattice cut, collar and zipper (ADR-8334) join the loop (the layer's open boundary) to the ring as for any layer. A
   fill count that differs from the loop count, an open chain, or a loop that is not star-shaped from its mean point is
   `meshlayers_volume_mouths`. A loop the layer does not fill stays under whole ground. A mesher failure is
   `meshlayers_volume_mesh`; an empty box, a bad cell size or `iso` is `meshlayers_volume_grid`.
4. **Canonical = LOD-0 volume mesh.** `regia_world_geom::cook::cook_with_layers(inputs, &[ProvidedLayer])` cooks a
   `Volume` layer from the caller's millimetre triangles: kinds by normal (`provided_kind`: floor within 45 degrees of
   +y, roof within 45 degrees of -y, wall otherwise; integer arithmetic), no sections, portals, plugs or render
   presentation; the input hash takes the provided `source_bytes` in place of a file. `cook` is `cook_with_layers`
   with none, so every `Passages` cook and its pins (Stage A, `lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned`) are unchanged. The
   chunk cut, LODs, locks and files are the existing steps 2 to 4 (ADR-8398), unchanged.
Not built (deferred): a volume layer that crosses the ground as an overhang above it (the clip removes everything
over the ground; such a layer is a `Gltf` or `Collision` source); concave mouth loops (need an authored footprint or
an ear-clipped one); a `seam_report` sweep on a cooked volume map (the ring is the lattice cut's boundary whatever the
source; `seam_has_no_gap_or_lip_at_any_lod_pair` covers it, and the run-time mouth load from a cooked file is the
seam lane's); the agent surface needs no new method (`terrain.mesh_layers`, `terrain.surface_at` and
`terrain.bake_report` read a volume layer like any other; the new error codes are on the book page).
Consequences: `MeshLayersCookError` gains `Volume` and `VolumeMouths` (exhaustive matches break: Upgrade note);
`regia_terrain::mesh_layer::volume` and `regia_world_geom::cook::{ProvidedLayer, provided_kind, cook_with_layers}`
are new. No format changes (the document already parses `Volume`). Spec 26 § 2a.9 as-built note; book pages
`book/agents/terrain-mesh-layers.md` and `book/user-guide/volume-mesh.md` gain a section each.

## ADR-10072: CPU masked occlusion of the draw list on Desktop Low and the Deck (v07-masked-occlusion-low)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: DO27 asked for units hidden behind ridges, cliff shells and tunnel rock to be culled on Low, the Deck and
the integrated-GPU minimum spec, where frame rate is worst (adoption request masked-occlusion-low-tiers). The plan
made it the v0.7 second cut, released only if the N150 Very Low floor missed 30 fps with tunnels armed:
v07-tunnels-frame-bars (ADR-8873) measured the outdoor views at 35-55 ms on the N150. Those tiers have no GPU
two-phase prepass cull (`two_phase_occlusion` is on in Desktop High and Ultra only), and the CPU culler
`regia_render::masked_occlusion` (v0.5.0) was a library the frame never called. The graph-transient-aliasing lane the
older brief waited on (3307) is not needed: the hook runs on the CPU in `build_draw_list`, before any pass or graph
resource exists, and touches no graph node.
Decision: `frame/masked_cull.rs` owns a `MaskedOcclusionCuller` (256×128, standard depth: the frame's projection is
0 near / 1 far with `LessEqual`) and one call after the draw-list loop. Occluders: visible rigid draws with an opaque
standard material (no blend, mask, glass, hair, graph, override, LOD dither, morph) and CPU vertices whose bounding
sphere's projected radius is at least 8 % of the half-height, largest first, at most 32 meshes and 8192 triangles,
rasterized with the unjittered view-projection (jitter moves occluders and boxes alike); single-sided materials
occlude with front faces only (`Backface::Cull`, counter-clockwise in NDC, the pipelines' default front face).
Culled: visible rigid opaque or alpha-tested draws (not blended, transmissive, hair, glass, overridden or on the
visibility buffer; a vertex graph only with a declared offset), tested with the box around the frustum test's
sphere; hidden ones are marked not visible, so they leave the colour, depth and velocity lists and stay in the
shadow list (as frustum-culled draws do). Main view only: texture views and stereo eyes skip it. Pacing: a frame
with fewer than 32 cullable draws skips the raster (`few_draws`), and after 8 culling frames in a row that hide
nothing the cull backs off to one probe frame in 16 until a frame hides something (`idle`); on the N150 the
showcase tunnel views hid nothing at 9.4 ms (tube, 4 draws tested) and 13.1 ms (outdoor, 1602 tested) of
render-thread raster time a frame before pacing. Skipping is always conservative. A profile column
`RenderProfile::masked_occlusion` (on in Desktop Low and the Deck; the ladder's Very Low inherits Low's; off on
both Mobile tiers, which were not measured, and on High and Ultra, which have the GPU path), handed to
`FrameRenderer::set_masked_occlusion` by the runtime every frame (a bare `FrameRenderer` is off). `preset()` masks
the column (each preset row is compared with the profile's own value), so `render.set_occlusion { masked }` does not
move preset-picked tiers. The culler's per-draw triangle and edge lists are kept between draws. The counts go to
`render.get_occlusion` `masked` (occluders, triangles, tested, culled, raster and test microseconds), not to
`render.frame_work`: that report is the device-independent GPU work with a per-preset ratchet table, and the culled
draws already show there as fewer draws and triangles; CPU microseconds are not device-independent.
Not covered: the terrain heightfield draws on the GPU (a shared pass, not a `FrameMesh`), so ridges do not occlude
on this path. A per-node proxy below the surface (the node's minimum height from the pyramid less the cliff-relief
pad, nodes with holes left out) is conservative on a map without tunnels, but not on a tunnel map: a ray that enters
a mouth travels below the sheet, and where the tunnel cavity dips below a hole-free node's minimum it would cross the
proxy's front face through open air, hiding what the GPU shows through the mouth. A safe terrain occluder needs the
tunnel volumes (or the proxy limited to maps with no holes); proposed as a follow-up, not built here.
Consequences: Desktop Low and Deck frames draw fewer meshes where large opaque meshes hide others (tunnel rock,
cliff shells, buildings); the image is unchanged (lavapipe tests: byte-identical frames, a 16-step camera path, a
back-facing and a blended wall). The CPU cost is on the render thread and reported per frame. `RenderProfile` and
`ExtractedFrame` gain a field (struct literals break: release fragment, Upgrade). Specs: none changed (spec 98's
GPU path is untouched).

## ADR-20000: The editor's app icon and desktop launcher: one SVG, an xtask generator, `regia editor install-launcher`
Date: 2026-11-19   Status: proposed
Context: Owner 11-19: "we need to add an app icon for linux/windows/mac to launch the Regia editor from their
launchers". Games already get icons through `regia package`; the editor had none and no launcher entry on any
desktop. The brand guide (piercingxx-branding BRAND-GUIDE.md § 5, checklist item 6) gives the default app icon: the
underlined-XX logomark on a rounded-square Ink tile. The owner may later pick a per-app Regia mark, so swapping must
be cheap. The editor's Wayland app_id is `regia.editor`, which the owner's Hyprland rule `^(regia\..*)$` matches;
a dock matches a Wayland window to the desktop entry whose file name equals the app_id.
Decision: (1) One source file, `crates/regia_editor/assets/icon/regia-editor.svg`, a verbatim copy of the brand
master `logomark.svg` with a provenance note; `cargo xtask editor-icons` draws from it with the workspace's `resvg`
(ADR-3350; no new crate) the PNGs 16 to 1024, a `.ico` (16 to 256, 32-bit DIBs below 256 and a PNG-compressed 256)
and a `.icns` (PNG payloads `icp4`, `icp5`, `ic07` to `ic14`, `ic10`) with our own writers; `--check` compares. The
macOS images put the tile on 824/1024 of the canvas, centered, because macOS 13 does not mask an `.icns` and every
other app icon leaves that margin; the other platforms draw the tile full bleed (it has its own transparent rounded
corners). The generated files are committed (AGENTS.md rule 2 allows icons). The command also writes a byte-identical
copy of the SVG and the launcher's files to `crates/regia_cli/assets/editor-icon/` (a crate compiles from its own folder,
ADR-1485; a `regia_cli` test compares the two), and `docs/asset-licences.toml` lists both sets under
`LicenseRef-PiercingXX-owner`, the licence of the logomark already in `book/theme/`. (2) The editor sets its window icon
(128 px) on X11 and Windows and the taskbar icon (256 px) on Windows through winit; the X11 class and instance and
the Wayland app_id are `regia.editor` (`regia_editor::app_icon::APP_ID`; the instance was empty). (3) The Linux
desktop entry is named `regia.editor.desktop`, not `regia-editor.desktop` as the lane brief suggested: the brief also
requires the file name to equal the app_id, and renaming the app_id to `regia-editor` would break the owner's window
rule. `Icon=regia-editor` (the hicolor name), `StartupWMClass=regia.editor`, `Exec="<editor>" %F`. (4) `regia-editor.exe`
embeds the `.ico` and version info through `winresource` (already vetted for the game crates, ADR-2645) as a build
dependency of `regia_editor`, `default-features = false`, `compile_for("regia-editor")` so the helper binaries of the
package get none; no resource compiler means a warning and no icon, never a failed build. This amends the docs/03 row
that kept `winresource` out of engine crates: it stays out of every runtime crate. (5) `regia editor
install-launcher [--uninstall]` installs per user, never with elevated rights: the Linux entry and hicolor icons (then
`update-desktop-database` and `gtk-update-icon-cache` when present), a Windows Start Menu `.lnk` made through
PowerShell's `WScript.Shell` (paths passed in environment variables, never as script text) with the `.ico` in
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Regia\Editor`, and a macOS `~/Applications/Regia Editor.app` whose executable is a script that
`exec`s the editor binary (same PID, so the Dock shows the bundle's icon, and a rebuilt editor needs no reinstall).
Bundle id `com.piercingxx.regia.editor` (the maker brand; no company or licensor name), `LSMinimumSystemVersion`
13.0, unsigned. Uninstall removes only a bundle whose `Info.plist` names that id (`launcher_not_ours`). (6) The editor
accepts a bare path argument (what `%F` and a dropped file give): a folder is the project, a file opens the nearest
folder above it with a `Regia.toml`. (7) `regia doctor` reports `editor_launcher_missing` as `info` in the host's
section. No agent protocol method: the command changes the user's desktop, not a project; its CLI `--json` and the
book pages are the agent surface (rule 8, CLI row in book/COVERAGE.md).
Consequences: Swapping the mark is replacing one SVG and running one command. `winresource` enters Cargo.lock.
`EditorArgs` gains a `command` field (struct literals need `command: None`). Wayland shows the icon only through the
installed entry (winit has no Wayland window-icon call). Measured on the Mac (11-19): the running editor is
Launch Services' `Regia Editor` app (bundle id and bundle URL of the `.app`), so the Dock shows the bundle's icon and name. Specs: none changed; docs/03 (winresource, resvg rows) and docs/provenance.md
updated; book pages user-guide/editor-launcher.md and agents/editor-launcher.md added.

## ADR-10107: `no_wedged_client`: a never-heard peer's first input closes its gap from the join grace, not the join
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v07-net-soak-wedged-hole review (`sprint-v07-net-soak-wedged-hole-review.md`, proof
`crates/regia_net_soak/tests/wedge_review.rs`) found that the server's arrival path in `Server::tick` recorded the gap a
peer's first input closes from `last_input_ms`, which `PeerJoined` sets to the join time, while a removal and the
run's end close the same never-heard gap with `PeerState::open_gap`, from `INPUT_GRACE_MS` (1 s) after the join.
ADR-8424 defines the never-heard gap as starting at `joined + INPUT_GRACE_MS` ("the same moment `missed_input` starts
judging it") and ADR-8887 (a) says every server gap is closed that way ("from `INPUT_GRACE_MS` after the join when
none arrived"); the arrival path did not follow either. Effect: the same silence got a different verdict depending on
what ended it. A peer silent for 2.0-3.0 s after its join with its link up was a wedge when its first input ended the
silence and not when its removal or the run's end did; and once ADR-8887 split a gap around an outage, the 1 s join
grace landed inside the judged piece before the outage (the review's case: join 810, outage 3310..3710, first input
4710: 2500 ms judged, 1500 ms of it link-up after the grace, reported as a wedge). The bar's text is "2 s with its link
up"; the first second after a join is the link coming up, the same grace an outage end gets.
Decision: the arrival path closes the open gap with `PeerState::open_gap(now)` before it sets `first_input` and
`last_input_ms`, like `PeerLeft` and `Server::finish`. A later input is unchanged (`open_gap` starts at the last
input). The bar, its 2 s limit, its gating, `INPUT_GRACE_MS` and `report::judged_input_gap` are unchanged.
Consequences: the bar now means what ADR-8424, ADR-8887 and docs/06 say for a never-heard peer however the gap ends:
2 s counted from the end of the join grace. Relative to the reviewed head the bar is stricter nowhere and less strict
exactly where a judged piece of a never-heard gap closed by the first input reached 2 s only by including the first
second after the join (with no outage: a first input 2-3 s after the join); the same silence closed by a leave or the
run's end has not been a wedge since ADR-8424. The alternative, counting every never-heard gap from the join, would
tighten ADR-8424's grace and keep the review's proof red, so it was not taken. A peer silent from its join for at least the grace plus 2 s is still a wedge
(`a_long_silence_after_the_join_then_one_input_is_wedged`). Production netcode is not touched; this is a harness
measurement fix, and no production bug was found. Tests: `crates/regia_net_soak/tests/wedge_first_input.rs` (3, two
red before the fix) and `wedge_review.rs` (6, one red before). Soak runs before/after: the lane report
(`sprint-net-soak-wedged-hole-review-fix.md`). Book `agents/net-soak.md` `no_wedged_client` row and spec 120 § 15.2
Built note updated. No wire, format, API or engine change.

## ADR-10096: `staleness_p99` counts the path's one-way latency: the soak reports staleness beyond it; the accept anchors the client's clock and its first input lead with the handshake's round trip
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Spec 120 § 15.2's `staleness_p99` bar ("<= 4 ticks on every profile except congested (<= 8) and inside
outages") is red on eight gate rows whose round trip is the profile's point: `high-rtt` at 8 and 32 clients (12 ticks),
`rtt-step` (6), `wifi-to-cell` (5) and `rtt-extreme` (47) (plan v07-to-v10 § 2.2, the non-gating soak bars; N-21). The
spec does not say what staleness is measured against. As built (ADR-7899, ADR-8030; `regia_net_soak::workload`
`connected_frame`) a sample is taken every client frame (16 ms) while the client's link is up: the client's estimate of
the server tick (`NetClient::estimated_server_tick`, on a symmetric path the tick the server is on now) minus the tick
of the newest snapshot part the client has read. It is the age of the client's newest state in server ticks, not a
distance to an interpolation target (the sample game has no interpolation timeline). So the path's one-way latency is
inside every sample: the server is on tick `t + 1` when it sends the snapshot of tick `t`, the snapshot crosses the
path, and it stays the newest until the next one arrives. A sender with no delay of its own reads between
`floor(d / tick) + 1` and `floor(d / tick) + 2` ticks on a path of `d` one way, plus jitter and the client's frame.
At the soak's 30 Hz (33.3 ms) the limit of 4 can hold only up to about 60 ms one way; `high-rtt` is 225 or 325 ms
(6 or 9 whole ticks), `rtt-step` 125 ms for a third of the run (3), `wifi-to-cell` 60 ms with 3 % loss after the switch
(1), `rtt-extreme`'s peer 1,500 ms (45). No sender change can turn these rows green as the bar is counted.
Decision: (1) **Measure it.** The soak splits every link-up sample into five parts that add up without a remainder
(`workload::StalenessParts`, in thousandths of a tick): `path` (the one-way latency toward the client in force at the
sample: the server's uplink plus the client's downlink, without jitter or queueing), `transit` (the newest snapshot's
way from the server's send to the client frame that read it, beyond the path: jitter, queueing, anything the sender
held it for, the wait for the client's frame), `hold` (how long it has been the newest: the send interval, lost and
late snapshots), `rounding` (counting in whole ticks, between 0 and 1) and `estimate` (the client's tick estimate minus
the tick the server is really on). The harness knows when the server sent each snapshot, the server's real tick and
every link's latency. Each run reports, per sub-profile, the p99 as the bar counts it, the p99 with the whole ticks of
the path taken off every sample (`beyond_path_p99_ticks`, and the worst single client's), and the mean of each part
(`report::StalenessPath`, `Measures::staleness_paths` in `result.json`; a table in `summary.md` for every sub-profile
over its limit). No bar reads them: `staleness_p99`, its limits and its grouping are unchanged.
(2) **What the engine adds on these rows, and what was removed.** Measured on the gate rows (table below): beyond
the path the four profiles read 2 to 4 ticks at the 99th percentile, inside the limit of 4. The mean of what is added
is about 1.5 ticks: 0.47 for counting in whole ticks, 0.3 to 0.5 for the snapshot interval (one snapshot a tick; the
sample game sends it in two datagrams and either counts as the newest, so a lost datagram rarely shows), 0.2 to 0.5
of transit, and 0.2 to 0.4 of estimate. Transit is the link's jitter plus the wait for the client's 16 ms frame: on
`rtt-extreme`'s peer, a link without jitter, it is 0.21 tick (7 ms, half a frame), so the sender holds nothing back
(the snapshot of a tick leaves in the flush of the iteration that ran the tick). What was the engine's own fault was at
the connect: the estimate (3) and the first input lead (4).
(3) **The accept anchors the client's clock with the handshake's round trip.** The accept carries the server's tick
and no delay, and the connection's first round-trip sample is one round trip away. Until it came back,
`estimated_server_tick` was the whole one-way delay behind the server: on `rtt-extreme`'s peer 45 ticks for the first
3.4 s of its connection (its mean estimate over the gate row was 2.65 ticks behind; it is 0.21 ahead now, like every other client's), on `high-rtt` 7 to 10 ticks for
0.5 to 0.7 s, and the same after every reconnect or resume. The soak's staleness sample under-read by as much in that
stretch, every input of it was stamped for a tick long past (the lead is counted from the estimate), and the first
sample then stepped the clock (a counted resync when the sample came back after the filter's warm-up of 8 syncs, about 2 s, as on `rtt-extreme`; inside the warm-up the step is not counted). The handshake has already crossed
the path two or three times, so the client now times its legs: a leg runs from the first send of a flight to the last
`receive` that did not yet hold its answer. That is a lower bound of the path's round trip however long the client's
frames are: a client whose first frame stalls for seconds with the answer waiting in its socket (ADR-3075) reads no
delay into it. A flight is sent again every `handshake_resend_ms` (250 ms) and the answer does not say which copy it
answers, so a leg is longer than the path only when its first copy or the first answer was lost, by whole resend
intervals; the connect keeps its shortest leg. One tick comes off (the server reads its socket once a tick, so up to a
tick of every leg is its wait), half of the rest is the one-way delay of the accept's clock sample, and
`clock_one_way_ms` keeps using it until the connection has a smoothed round trip of its own. A leg must never read
shorter than the path (the shortest one is kept), so a flight keeps its first send when the challenge or the resume
cookie it answers is replaced: the server may still answer what left before the replacement (it keeps the first key
share it saw). The first version reset the flight there, and under 20 % loss one seed of twelve anchored the clock
12 ticks behind. The filter itself (ADR-8077: the least delayed of 8 syncs, never backward, 5 % slew, forward steps
over 8 ticks) is unchanged.
(4) **The first input lead covers the way to the server** (spec 120 § 9.2's startup rule, which ADR-8077 had left
out). The estimate is the server's tick now, so an input sent now arrives a one-way delay later and the lead has to
cover it. Before the server's first feedback the lead was two ticks and two measured jitters: on any path longer than
that every input was late until the first feedback had come back and raised the lead, a round trip and a one-way
delay after the connect. And because the clock was a one-way delay behind as well, that feedback read a deficit of
the path twice: the lead went to 62 ticks (the input buffer's cap) on a 1,500 ms path that needs 48, and to 22 on a
325 ms path that needs 13, and then came down one tick per five calm seconds (70 s and 45 s of 467 ms and 300 ms more
input delay than the path asks for). The startup lead is now two ticks, two jitters and the path's one-way delay
(`initial_input_lead`, `lead_way_ms`) as the handshake measured it: half its shortest round trip with one tick taken
off, because the server's wait for its next tick is in every round trip and in the lead's two ticks already (counting
it twice started a LAN at three ticks). It is the handshake's value only, never the connection's round trip: that one
grows with every queue the first seconds build while the rate control finds a bottleneck, and a startup lead that
followed it kept `congested` over its 256 kbit/s bottleneck past the fifth second after a connect in 10 of 64 seeds
(crates/regia_net_soak/tests/rate_control.rs; 0 of 64 with the handshake's value, as on the base). After the first
feedback the lead is the feedback's. Measured at 30 Hz, one client, the crate's
conditioner on both directions (crates/regia_net/tests/connect_clock.rs; base / this lane):

| Path one way | Estimate at the accept, ticks behind | Server first has the client's input in time, after the connect | Lead at the connect | Lead after the first feedback | Counted resyncs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,500 ms | 45 / 1 | 4,729 ms / 1,562 ms | 2 / 47 | 62 / 48 | 1 / 0 |
| 1,500 ms, 20 % loss (base seed 1; 12 seeds) | 46 / 1 to 2 | 4,763 ms / 1,521 to 1,566 ms | 2 / 47 | 62 / 48 to 50 | 1 / 0 |
| 325 ms, 0 to 20 ms jitter, 1 % loss (base seed 1; 8 seeds) | 12 / 1 to 3 | 1,062 ms / 354 to 429 ms | 2 / 12 to 13 | 22 / 12 to 14 | 0 / 0 |
| 60 ms, 0 to 10 ms jitter | 3 / 2 | 254 ms / 87 ms | 2 / 4 | 7 / 5 | 0 / 0 |
| 15 ms, 0 to 5 ms jitter | 1 / 1 | 59 ms / 93 ms (no input late either way; the first stamped tick is one later) | 2 / 3 | 3 / 3 | 0 / 0 |
| no delay | 0 / 0 | 87 ms / 87 ms | 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 | 0 / 0 |

At 64 Hz on the 325 ms path the estimate at the accept was 23 ticks behind and is 2, the first in-time input came
1,045 ms after the connect and comes after 357 ms, and the lead after the first feedback was 46 and is 25.
(5) **The bar is not moved; a ruling is asked** (below).
Measured (the gate plan's after-run of this lane on the test machine, 61 runs, release, the gate's seed; every sub-profile over its limit with the link up; means in ticks, they add up to
the mean):

| Run | Clients' profile (clients) | Limit | p99 | Path ticks | p99 beyond the path (worst client) | Mean | Path | Transit | Hold | Rounding | Estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| high-rtt/8/dedicated | high-rtt (8) | 4 | 12 | 6-9 | 3 (3) | 9.84 | 8.23 | 0.48 | 0.31 | 0.47 | +0.36 |
| rtt-step/8/dedicated | rtt-step (8) | 4 | 6 | 0-3 | 3 (3) | 2.96 | 1.66 | 0.28 | 0.28 | 0.47 | +0.27 |
| wifi-to-cell/8/dedicated | wifi-to-cell (8) | 4 | 5 | 0-1 | 4 (4) | 2.83 | 1.25 | 0.30 | 0.49 | 0.47 | +0.32 |
| rtt-extreme/8/dedicated | @rtt-extreme-peer (1) | 4 | 47 | 45 | 2 (2) | 46.20 | 45.00 | 0.21 | 0.31 | 0.48 | +0.21 |
| high-rtt/32/dedicated | high-rtt (32) | 4 | 12 | 6-9 | 3 (3) | 9.83 | 8.23 | 0.47 | 0.31 | 0.47 | +0.35 |
| rtt-step/32/dedicated | rtt-step (32) | 4 | 6 | 0-3 | 3 (3) | 2.97 | 1.66 | 0.28 | 0.28 | 0.47 | +0.28 |
| wifi-to-cell/32/dedicated | wifi-to-cell (32) | 4 | 5 | 0-1 | 4 (4) | 2.84 | 1.25 | 0.30 | 0.48 | 0.47 | +0.34 |
| rtt-extreme/32/dedicated | @rtt-extreme-peer (4) | 4 | 48 | 45 | 3 (3) | 46.21 | 45.00 | 0.21 | 0.31 | 0.48 | +0.21 |
| congested/8/dedicated | congested (8) | 8 | 23 | 0 | 23 (23) | 3.24 | 0.45 | 1.63 | 0.35 | 0.47 | +0.33 |
| asym-bufferbloat/8/dedicated | asym-bufferbloat (8) | 4 | 19 | 0 | 19 (20) | 16.73 | 0.12 | 30.25 | 0.57 | 0.47 | -14.67 |
| congested+bulk/8/dedicated | congested+bulk (8) | 8 | 23 | 0 | 23 (23) | 3.45 | 0.45 | 1.65 | 0.49 | 0.47 | +0.39 |
| asym-bufferbloat/32/dedicated | asym-bufferbloat (32) | 4 | 19 | 0 | 19 (20) | 16.72 | 0.12 | 30.25 | 0.55 | 0.47 | -14.67 |
| mixed/32/dedicated | congested (1) | 8 | 18 | 0 | 18 (18) | 2.69 | 0.45 | 1.19 | 0.34 | 0.48 | +0.23 |
| mixed/40/dedicated | congested (2) | 8 | 22 | 0 | 22 (23) | 3.02 | 0.45 | 1.50 | 0.34 | 0.48 | +0.25 |
| congested/8/listen | congested (8) | 8 | 23 | 0 | 23 (23) | 3.18 | 0.60 | 1.44 | 0.35 | 0.47 | +0.33 |

The eight rows of the four round-trip profiles read 2 to 4 ticks beyond the path: inside the limit. The other seven
rows over their limit are not the path's latency: `congested` (the link's 256 kbit/s queue while the rate control
finds it: the samples over the limit are the first ten seconds of a connection, 3 ticks after that) and
`asym-bufferbloat` (the download's one-second queue: about 30 ticks of transit, and the estimate runs about 15 ticks
behind the server, because half the round trip is not the way down, so the bar under-reads there). They are not
this lane's rows.
Ruling asked of the lead (plan N-21): what `staleness_p99` should be judged on. (a) Recommended: the path-free number.
"Snapshot staleness beyond the path's one-way latency, p99 with the link up, <= 4 ticks (8 for congested clients)",
judged per sub-profile (so seven good-wifi clients do not hide the extreme peer, or the reverse) on
`beyond_path_p99_ticks`; the raw p99 stays in the report. It keeps the bar's meaning (the engine may add at most 4
ticks to what the path costs), is a function of `result.json` already, and reads `high-rtt` 3 (3), `rtt-step` 3 (3), `wifi-to-cell` 4 (4), `rtt-extreme` 2 (2) and 3 (3) on the eight rows.
(b) Keep counting the path and state per-profile limits of the path's whole ticks plus 4 (the same test, written the
other way round). (c) Keep the bar as it is and list the eight rows as red by definition. This lane did none of the
three: the bar, its limit, its grouping and its gating state are untouched (`GATING_BARS`, xtask `BARS`).
Numbers for N-21's other two decisions. Limits in ticks at other rates: what the engine adds is one tick of counting,
one send interval and the client's frame, so in ticks it does not shrink with the tick: the limit of 4 is 133 ms at
30 Hz, 62 ms at 64 Hz and 31 ms at 128 Hz, against a path jitter that stays in milliseconds (`high-rtt`'s 0 to 20 ms
is 2.6 ticks at 128 Hz). Reliable latency on `rtt-extreme`, as measured (no change here): the soak's reliable commands (0.5 to 4 KiB, from the client's send to the server's acknowledgment at the client; gate rows, crates/regia_net_soak/tests/staleness_path.rs prints them): the extreme peer's median is 6.1 s (two round trips of 3 s), its p95 and p99 are at or above 8.2 s (the top of the histogram), the longest 9.2 s at 8 clients and 12.3 s at 32, and 14 of 16 and 57 of 64 commands were acknowledged inside the run; the good-wifi clients of the same rows read 32 ms at the median and 64 ms at p99. `high-rtt` reads 672 ms at the median (one round trip of 450 or 650 ms and a tick each way), 720 ms at p95 and 1.0 to 1.4 s at p99.
Rejected: changing the bar's sample to count from the path in place (moving a bar inside a lane); taking the path off
with the client's own round-trip estimate (the bar would then trust the thing it measures; the harness knows the
latency exactly); timing a handshake leg from the last send of a flight (at most one resend interval, 250 ms: useless
above it) or from the first send to the frame that read the answer (a stalled first frame would read seconds of delay
and put the estimate that far ahead, which the filter corrects at only 5 %); an echoed timestamp in the accept (a wire
field for a number the handshake already has); letting the estimate step backward once the first sample arrives (the
never-backward rule keeps stamped ticks monotonic); pairing the least delayed sync with the minimum round trip of the
last 10 s to take the mean jitter out of the estimate's +0.2 to +0.3 tick bias (after a step up in latency the minimum
is stale for up to 10 s and the estimate would sit the step behind).
Soak effect (gate plan after-run, and eight profiles at 8 and 32 clients over five seeds against the base's client:
`lossy-fat-pipe`, `congested`, `congested+bulk`, `rtt-extreme`, `high-rtt`, `asym-bufferbloat`, `wifi-to-cell`,
`rtt-step`): server ticks without the client's input in time fall from 475-508 to 120-163 per seed and corrected
predictions from about 4,400 to 74-104; on the gate rows `high-rtt` goes from 18 and 66 missed ticks to 0 and from
1.8 % corrections to 0, `rtt-extreme`'s worst client from 1.4-1.6 % missed to 0.2-0.3 %. No gating bar changed in the
gate plan. Open: the not-gating `random_loss_kept` is red on `lossy-fat-pipe/8` in 2 of the 5 seeds with this change
(the snapshot budget fell to 44 and 114 of 140 entities; 126 needed) and in none on the base; the cause is not found
(`lossy-fat-pipe/32` passes on both). `rate_vs_bottleneck` is red on 10 `congested` rows of the sweep with the change
and on 11 without, and the gating `involuntary_disconnects` (`protocol_error` on `asym-bufferbloat`) shows on 1 seed
with it and on 2 without: both are the base's.
Consequences: no wire, format or settings change; `NetClient`'s API is unchanged. `input_lead_ticks()` before the
first feedback reads the path's one-way ticks more than before (unchanged on a LAN). Host-visible API (release fragment
v0.1.28-v07-net-staleness-rtt): `regia_net_soak::workload::ClientRecord` and `regia_net_soak::report::Measures` gained
fields (struct literals need them); `StalenessParts`, `StalenessPath`, `MILLITICKS_PER_MS` are new. `result.json`
keeps version 2 (the new key is additive and reads as empty from an older file). Known limits: a handshake in which
every leg lost its first copy anchors the estimate ahead by half a resend interval per lost copy (125 ms) until the
connection's round trip corrects it at the filter's 5 %; a resume has one leg, so on a lossy path that is the chance
of losing one exchange. The anchor and the first lead are held inside the server's input buffer like every clock sample (64 ticks: 2.1 s at
30 Hz, 1.0 s at 64 Hz, 0.5 s at 128 Hz), so `rtt-extreme`'s 1,500 ms one way is outside it at 64 and 128 Hz: N-21's
bars at 64/128 either leave that peer out or the buffer is sized in time first. The startup margin of two ticks is
15.6 ms at 128 Hz, less than a 16 ms client frame: at 128 Hz the first inputs of a 325 ms path are still late for
0.5 s, until the first feedback adds 3 ticks to the lead (45 to 48). The estimate's steady bias of +0.2 to +0.3 tick (half the smoothed round trip includes the
mean jitter and the ack's wait for a frame; the least delayed sync does not) is left as it is. `staleness_p99` stays
red on the eight rows until the ruling. One existing assertion changed: crates/regia_net/tests/input_feedback.rs
`asym_bufferbloat_inputs_arrive_in_time` asserted that the server reported late inputs (`late_events >= 1`); with the
startup lead no input is late there (0 of 1,110 ticks missed, lead 18 from the first frame), so the line now reads
"reported, or none was late", and the case only the server can see lives on in the new
`an_uplink_that_gets_slower_is_reported_by_the_server` (the uplink goes from 15 to 215 ms after the connect: one
report, 5 of 1,110 ticks missed) and `a_download_that_starts_after_the_connect_is_followed_by_the_lead`. Specs updated:
spec 120 § 9.1, § 9.2 and § 15.2 (Built notes);
book/agents/net-soak.md, book/agents/net-input.md, book/user-guide/networking.md; docs/06-testing-and-ci.md; two
provenance rows.

## ADR-10104: The game pause key, the built-in Paused screen, and the host-authoritative pause later
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked (2026-11-20) for a real-time pause button on the keyboard that freezes everything,
physics included, that each game can turn on, with a default "Paused" screen a game can replace. The engine had
the parts (`Time::paused` freezes gameplay time and the fixed loop, spec 10 § 3.2; the agent's `play.pause`; the
focus-loss pause; input contexts and rebinding; UI layers, focus and the accessibility tree) but no player-facing
pause, no key, and no screen.
Decision: `regia_framework::game_pause` (feature `client`), added by `regia::DefaultPlugins`:
1. **Off by default.** A game turns it on with `[game] pause = true` in `Regia.toml`, or `GamePausePlugin { config:
   Some(GamePauseConfig::enabled()), .. }`. The `[game]` keys (`pause`, `pause_key`, `pause_gamepad`,
   `pause_screen`) are optional and additive, so older manifests read unchanged: `Regia.toml` is the project
   manifest, not a § 4a frozen content format, and the `[runtime]` table set the same no-version rule (ADR-7070).
   No v0.7 format-batch-2 registration is needed. `regia package` copies the table into `build_info.json`'s `game`
   object, which a packaged game reads (as `[boot]`, ADR-7893). Format page `docs/formats/regia-toml-game.md`; the
   `fuzz_targets` doc map points at a deterministic mutation test of the table.
2. **The key is an input action.** `TogglePause` in the consuming `Pause` context (priority 1000), Pause/Break by
   default, a gamepad button only when `pause_gamepad` names one. Added at `Startup` unless the project binds the
   action itself (a project binding wins); also added to `InputDefaults` (reset to defaults) and the player's saved
   overrides for the `Pause` context are merged again, because `InputPlugin` merged them before the action existed.
   The press is read in `Update` from the frame-level edge (`just_pressed_this_frame`), as `skip_video` is.
3. **A pause** sets `Time::paused` (no fixed step: physics, animation, AI and every gameplay system stand still),
   reduces every player's context stack to `Pause` plus `GamePauseConfig::keep_contexts` (gameplay actions then
   evaluate as idle: no new masking API in `regia_input`), sets `CursorRelease` (free, visible cursor; nothing on
   touch devices), shows the screen and sends `GamePaused`. Resume restores the stacks (keeping contexts pushed
   during the pause), clears `CursorRelease` only if the pause set it, and clears `Time::paused` only if it was not
   already set when the pause began (the agent's `play.pause` and the focus-loss pause keep their freeze, the rule
   ADR-7070 uses for focus loss). Run conditions `game_paused` / `game_running`.
4. **The screen.** `PauseScreen::Default` (a dimmed backdrop, "Paused", "Press <key> to resume" from the input glyph
   lookup for the last-used device, Resume and Quit to menu; a `Dialog` on a UI-only input layer, focus on Resume,
   gamepad d-pad/South mapped to UI navigation, en/de/fr/es strings with game overrides by key, neutral styling),
   `None`, `Asset(<.ui.ron path>)` (falls back to the default with `pause_screen_missing` when not loaded) and
   `Custom(builder)`. Buttons carry the UI commands `pause.resume` / `pause.quit_to_menu`; both end the pause and
   send `PauseScreenEvent`, and the game handles `QuitToMenu`.
5. **Networked sessions refuse the pause** (`PauseRefusal::NetworkedSession`, code `networked_session`, a
   `PauseRefused` message): a peer cannot freeze the other players' worlds. Detected from `regia_net`'s `NetMode`
   (feature `net`) or a `NetworkedSession(true)` resource for other transports.
6. **Later step, not built here: the host-authoritative pause.** The server (dedicated or listen host) owns the
   pause: a client's `TogglePause` becomes a pause request on the reliable channel; the server applies its policy
   (host only, any player, a vote, or a per-player pause budget as in competitive games), freezes its simulation
   tick, and replicates a `paused_at_tick` state so every client freezes prediction and interpolation at the same
   tick and shows the screen with who paused; resume carries a short synchronized countdown so clients restart
   prediction together. A dedicated server with no players never pauses. This needs a session message, a replicated
   resource and prediction hooks in `regia_net`, so it waits for the netcode lanes; until then the refusal stands.
7. **Agent protocol:** `game.pause`, `game.resume`, `game.pause_state` (book `agents/game-pause.md`); refusals are
   F0002 with `data.reason` `game_pause_not_installed`, `game_pause_off`, `networked_session`; F0018 while a
   render-out runs. `play.pause` stays the raw time freeze for tests.
Consequences: a game gets a pause with one manifest line; a game with its own pause menu keeps it (`screen = none`
or its own `.ui.ron`). Systems that read raw devices instead of actions still see input while paused and should
gate on `game_running`. Game audio, media players and coroutine waits follow `Time::paused` through ADR-10105 (the
sibling lane that makes the time pause freeze the whole world); this pause sets it. The samples `third_person` and `arena` turn it on. Updated: spec 14 Part B, book
`user-guide/pausing.md`, `agents/game-pause.md`, `docs/formats/regia-toml-game.md`.

## ADR-10105: The gameplay pause freezes the whole game world
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked (11-20) for a real-time pause that "will literally freeze everything even physics", opt-in
per game, with a replaceable default "Paused" screen. `Time::paused` already zeroed the gameplay delta and the fixed
loop's input (specs/10 § 3.2), so everything that reads `Time` stopped. An audit of every runtime system that
advances with time (the table in specs/10 § 3.2a) found what kept moving under a pause: (1) every playing sound (the
mixer runs on the device clock; `audio_sync` fed the mixer bookkeeping the gameplay delta, so ducking and snapshot
blends froze while the voices played on, and a pause screen's snapshot never blended); (2) a video player in
`ClockMode::Audio` (follows the mixer) or `Lockstep` (one step per frame); (3) a `ThreadedSimHost` with real-time pacing
(steps on its own thread's clock; only an OS suspend held it, ADR-8526); (4) coroutine frame waits
(`Co::wait_frames` / `next_frame` counted `Time::frame_count`, which counts paused frames); (5) the VFX entry streak
(its own frame counter, one per `Update`); (6) the renderer's temporal state: the jitter and noise phase, TAA/TSR
history, GI accumulation and exposure adaptation advance every rendered frame, so a still world's pixels still
change under a pause. The sibling lane game-pause-key-and-screen adds the key, the project setting and the screen.
Decision: `Time::paused` is the one switch; each system that kept moving now follows it:
- Audio (`Audio::set_game_paused`, called by `audio_sync` every frame): every voice on a bus that is not exempt holds
  in place (pause with the 10 ms declick fade, `VoiceEntry::held`), voices that start on a frozen bus during the pause
  are held at once, a rebuild replay or a revive re-applies the hold, a held voice's age and virtual cursor do not
  advance, and unpausing resumes exactly the voices the pause held (a voice the host paused stays paused). Exempt by
  default: `Ui` and `Music` with their child buses (`DEFAULT_PAUSE_EXEMPT_BUSES`; a pause screen sounds and the
  soundtrack plays on, as players expect; `Audio::set_pause_exempt_buses` changes it). Voice chat is never held. While
  paused the mixer bookkeeping (ducking, snapshot blends, stream watch, voice chat, music) runs on `RealTime` (the spec
  already said audio reads `RealTime`); propagation fades and patch layers take a zero step.
- Media: `PlayerCore::set_game_held`, set by `tick_players` from `Time::paused`, stops every clock mode
  (`External` too: its host clock is frozen by the pause anyway) and holds the player's audio feed; the release re-anchors the clock, so the position
  continues from the held one (no jump by the paused time).
- Sim host: `hold_sim_host_on_pause` (`PreUpdate`, `SimBridgePlugin`) holds the host while paused and releases only a
  hold it took (`PauseHold`), like the suspend hold.
- Coroutines: frame waits count unpaused frames (`Co::game_frame`); `Co::frame` stays `Time::frame_count`.
- VFX entry streak: a playing streak holds its frame and replays its ribbons while paused.
- Render: `SceneHold::set_follow_pause(true)` makes the paused-scene hold (ADR-7890) follow `Time::paused`
  (`scene_hold::follow_pause`, `PostUpdate`): the first paused frame renders and keeps the scene, every later paused
  frame composites only the UI over the kept image, so the world pixels are identical for the whole pause and the
  renderer's temporal state does not move; the first frame after the pause is the frame a never-paused run renders at
  the same renderer frame index (ADR-7890 test d). Off by default: an app that sets `Time::paused` for inspection
  (the agent's `play.pause`, an editor) or a game with a live photo-mode camera keeps live frames; the game-pause
  plugin (sibling lane) is expected to turn it on with the pause feature. Freezing the jitter phase without the hold
  was rejected: a converged TAA history fed one fixed jitter drifts to the aliased single-sample image, and every
  other temporal accumulator (SSAO, SSGI, DDGI) drifts the same way.
Not changed, with the reason (real time on purpose): UI (focus, gestures, scrolling, transitions, the soft cursor),
the spectator camera (flies while a replay is paused), `ShakeClock::Unscaled` camera shake, the baked-GI stream fade,
the net replay transport and voice-chat transport, loading/feedback/perf overlays, the audio output gate and stall
watchdog, quality and thermal governors, save timestamps and debounce. `ScriptCtx::time().frame_count` keeps counting
paused frames (documented as `Time::frame_count`). Already frozen by `Time` (verified by the audit and, for the
first four, by tests): physics (no fixed step; the interpolation blend is the banked overstep, unchanged), joints,
character controllers, vehicles, cloth, ragdolls, animation (clips, graphs, IK, morphs, motion matching), VFX scene and
particles, decals, fire lights and debris, weather and the material clock (wind, foliage sway, scrolling materials:
`material_clock(elapsed, delta)` of the paused clock gives `now == prev`), water, AI, navigation, rules, fluid, timers.
Known limits: a `MusicSystem` track keeps playing when a game removes `Music` from the exempt list (its stems run on
the music clock; use a snapshot to mute Music under the pause screen); a threaded sim host's presentation snaps to the
newest frame on the first paused frame (a held host publishes a still pair: at most one tick's blend).
Consequences: `VoiceEntry` gains the pub field `held` (struct literals break); `SceneHold` gains fields (no public
literal: it has private fields). No content format changes. Specs updated: 10-core § 3.2a, 16-audio § 2 (game
pause), 14-scene-and-framework (coroutines). Agent: `render.scene_hold` reports `follow_pause` and `paused`,
`render.set_scene_hold` takes `follow_pause`; `play.freeze_state` is new (book/agents/game-pause-freeze.md).

## ADR-10131: Property-track warnings are remembered per world (v07-anim-owed-evidence)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: `regia_animation`'s `property::tests::perf_g_bad_paths_warn_once` failed under parallel test threads and
passed alone (integ-v06r-det, contact-curves, retarget-ik-goals, integ-anim-v07a reports). The property animator
used `eval::first_warning`, a process-wide "already warned" set of formatted keys with a 1024-key cap that the IK,
chain-IK, body-aim and warp nodes share. Two defects follow: (1) once anything in the process has used up the cap,
no property track warns again (the parallel lib tests fill it, which is the flake); (2) the key holds the entity id,
and entity ids repeat between worlds, so the first entity of a second world (a reloaded level, a second app in one
process) never warned about the same bad path. Each warning check also formatted a key string every fixed step.
Decision: the property animator keeps its own `PropertyWarnings` resource per world: `(entity, kind) -> paths`
(`kind` = no dot, unregistered component, missing component, unsupported leaf, bad field path; an unsupported leaf
is keyed by path only, as before), capped at 1024 entries per world. A repeat lookup allocates nothing. The other
users of `first_warning` are unchanged (their keys hold rig and joint names, not only entity ids). The flaky test is
not weakened or serialized: its assertion is unchanged and it also checks its own world's count; a new test
(`property_warnings_belong_to_their_world`) fails on the base (the second world's warning count is 0) and a unit test
pins the per-world cap.
Consequences: Property-track warnings come once per entity and path in each world, whatever else the process logged.
No public API, format, agent method or dependency change. Specs updated: none.

## ADR-10129: Locomotion framework rows: typed `body_path` reads, coverage apps write outside the source tree
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Three v0.7 locomotion items (plan v0.7-to-v1.0 § 2.2 D). (1) The `check-features` rows `framework-bare` and
`framework-visual-log` were red from 5ac8991ad: `install_tier.rs` imported `crate::settings` (behind `client`),
`sim_bridge_presentation.rs` imported `Transform` and `photo_mode.rs` imported `Path` without that cfg. (2) The
locomotion-agent review's finding 8: `locomotion.rs` read parameters with `.get(k).and_then(Value::as_*)`. Of the three
sites at c38e14767, `ground.kind` was already rewritten by the review fixes; `body_path.points` and `body_path.speed`
remained in the required `.ok_or_else` form, which the ADR-2622 ratchet does not count. They refused with
`gait_input` but did not name the field. (3) A `regia_agent` test left `crates/regia_agent/asset_ids.assetids.ron` in
the source tree. The coverage harness `coverage_calls::app` (used by `every_dispatched_method_is_called` and
`seeded_fuzz_answers_inside_the_contract`) had no `AgentSettings.project_dir`, so `req_path::project_root` fell back to
the working directory, which `cargo test` sets to the crate directory. The fuzz sends every method its contract
example, and `assets.ids_export`'s example is `{ "out": "asset_ids.assetids.ron" }`. The fuzz's random project-relative
paths had the same root.
Decision: (1) Nothing to change on this base. integ-v06s-freeze-b (211bdb918, `install_tier`) and integ-v06s-freeze-d
(30a962735, photo mode and `sim_bridge_presentation`) added the cfgs. Both rows were rebuilt here to confirm.
(2) `body_path.points` and `body_path.speed` read through `crate::params::opt_array` / `opt_f64`. A missing, `null` or
wrong-typed value keeps the code the page lists, `gait_input`, and adds `data.param` (`body_path.points`,
`body_path.speed`) and `data.expected`, like the typed readers. `tests/typed_params_ratchet.rs` gains a `STRICT` list
(`locomotion.rs`): files in it may not hold the chain at all, not even in the `.ok_or` form. (3) `coverage_calls::app`
inserts `AgentSettings { project_dir }` with one `regia_test_utils::unique_temp_dir` per test process.
`coverage_apps_write_outside_the_source_tree` asserts that the root is outside the workspace and that the
`ids_export` example writes there.
Consequences: `anim.gait_simulate` refusals of a bad `body_path` field carry two more `data` keys. The code and message
are unchanged (`book/agents/locomotion-quality.md` error table). No format, dependency, schema or permission change.
A new file joins the strict ratchet by adding one `STRICT` row. Other test harnesses that dispatch in a bare world
still fall back to the working directory. The lane checked the regia_agent tests it ran for new files in the tree
(report `sprint-v07-anim-framework-rows`). A suite-wide untracked-file guard belongs in the gate (the gate tree has no
`.git`), not in a crate test.

## ADR-10183: Format batch 2 freeze: the v0.6.0 baseline, the corpus-upgrade test from v0.5.0 and v0.6.0, the row audit
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: Format batch 2 (v0.6.0 → v0.7, owner-approved 2026-11-19, ADR-7724 one-step rule) needs one freeze run.
That run records every batch row with one `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and shows that a v0.5.0 project and a
v0.6.0 project upgrade (plan v0.7 exit bar 6). At integ-v07c 71773be0c the audit found four problems. (a)
`check-formats` still measured the one-step rule against `docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.5.0.ron`, although v0.6.0
was tagged (02381fd90). The formats v0.6 added (`logic`, `playlist-ron`, `terrain-index`,
`terrain-mesh-layers-cooked`) are new against that table, so a second step on any of them would pass unseen. The book
(`book/changing-a-content-format.md`, "One step per release") says the baseline moves at each minor tag. (b) Two
registered formats, `netcapture` (ADR-8890) and `release-signature` (ADR-8846), had no `format-hashes.ron` row. (c)
`hub-toml/v1.toml` was in the corpus but not in `FROZEN.txt`. (d) `netcapture` had no spec 12 § 4a row, and
`lsreplay`, `lobby-keys` 1 → 2, `hub-toml`, `scene` 13 → 14 and wire 6 had no batch-2 row.
Decision: (1) `docs/formats/format-hashes-v0.6.0.ron` is `git show v0.6.0:docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` byte for
byte (240 rows) under a header comment. `RELEASE_BASELINE` points at it, and so do the `--since-tag` help, the book
and spec 12. Test: `the_release_baseline_is_the_v060_table` (xtask). It also shows that a two-step move of a
v0.6-added format now fails. (2) The freeze run is one `cargo xtask check-formats --update` at this lane's head. It
records `netcapture` v1 and `release-signature` v1 and re-records the rest of the line unchanged. The row list is in
the commit message. (3) `hub-toml/v1.toml 379 15b282021c29edc5` is added to `FROZEN.txt`: one inserted line, no other
line touched. (4) `crates/regia_cli/tests/format_corpus_upgrade.rs` gains `a_v050_project_upgrades_to_the_current_formats`
and `a_v060_project_upgrades_to_the_current_formats`. For every format whose version moved since that release's
frozen table, the corpus fixtures of the version the release wrote go into one project. A missing fixture is a
failure unless `format-corpus-exceptions.ron` excuses it. The dry run must plan each file as `migrate` from exactly
that version, except the formats `NOT_HANDLED` names. `--write` must reach `current`, and a second `--write` must
change no byte. The fixture placement is shared with the existing all-old-fixtures test (`place`). (5) Spec 12 § 4a
gains the missing rows, and `docs/guide/upgrade-v07.md` is the upgrade guide. It covers what each project rewrites
and re-cooks, `regia upgrade-project --write`, and what DO27 must cook again. (6) The xtask test
`v060_note_truth::upgrade_draft_lists_every_format_change_since_v050` read the live registry, so every v0.7 bump
turned the v0.6.0 note red (13 errors at the base). It now reads the frozen v0.6.0 table, which is the note's scope,
as `v050_note_truth` did after its tag. The live check moves to `v070_guide_truth`: every format that moved since
v0.6.0 has a row in the upgrade guide stating its step, and every new format is named there. The checked bar is the
same; only the document it is checked against moved. (7) Found while running the checks: the format corpus could
not patch `release-signature`'s version (`"format": 1`), so its future-version refusal was not checked.
`JSON_VERSION_KEY` gains `("release-signature", "format")`. The corpus-upgrade test placed the old `scene/v13.ron` and
`playlist-ron/v1.ron` under bare `.ron` names, which `upgrade-project` does not read. Its SUFFIX table gains `scene` →
`level.ron` and `playlist-ron` → `playlist.ron`. The integ-v07c line also failed clippy `type_complexity` in
`regia_detsim::fog`, which is now fixed with a `GroundHeight` alias.
Consequences: from this commit, a frozen format changes for v0.7 only through a lead-approved re-run of the freeze.
Late rows wait for batch 3 (v0.8). Rows not on the line at the freeze: the Stage B sim-version step
(`MATH_BITS_VERSION` 1, v07-det-atan2-canon), `server-toml` 4 → 5 (only with the `--relay` off switch) and `bake` 3 →
4 (only if v07-meshlayers-gi-export's ADR picks a shape change). Branches not merged at the base that touch formats:
v07-meshlayers-gi-export, fmt-logic-uianim-review-fix, v07-wire6-far-tier-record. The v0.7 release commit writes
`format-hashes-v0.7.0.ron` the same way. No dependency, agent method, error code or schema change.

## ADR-10050: Wire 6 acknowledgment frames carry their newest packet's arrival; an app-limited sender's delay cut needs its own packets' one-way delay to confirm it (amends spec 120 § 4.1 item 2 and § 4.2 items 1-2, ADR-8692, ADR-8859)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-8692 measured the up-leg cause of `rpc_p95_with_bulk`: on congested+bulk a client's round-trip delay
detector cuts an app-limited target on an idle 1 Mbit/s uplink (73 cuts on seed 1), and left two candidates: (a) a
one-way delay from receive timestamps, which changes the wire, and (b) a confirmed minimum (the 5th percentile of the
round minima). Lane v07-net-delay-detector, base v07-net-rpc-p95-up-leg 79679c4a1 with v07-wire6-resume-ticket
00c9fe2ba merged (wire 6 opens there; one wire step for v0.7). Everything below was measured on the build server with one diag
binary per code state and one environment switch per variant (a scratch overlay, never committed: per-role cut counters,
the switches), so every "base" row is the same binary with the rule off and the same bytes on the wire. Rows: the
`rpc_p95_with_bulk` bar on congested+bulk/4, 60 s; ADR-8534's rows congested/4 20 s, listen-uplink/64 20 s,
bufferbloat+bulk/4 30 s, lossy-fat-pipe/4 20 s; 25 profiles at 8 clients, 60 s.
(1) The mechanism is wider than ADR-8692 (a)-(b). With an arrival stamp in every acknowledgment frame (the first
build of this lane) a client's one-way delay samples on seed 1 resolve to 2 ms, and whole rounds read 26-36 ms over the
minimum in both the round trip and the one-way delay while the client sent 150-500 bytes in a 96 ms round. A delay
sample is one acknowledgment frame's newest packet, and it carries the phase of the receiver's socket reads: the 30 Hz
