record of the same version can arrive before or after a far one, and the server only learns what arrived from
acknowledgments that lag: whichever tie-break the client uses, there is a window in which the server codes a
transform delta against a value the client does not hold. (c) Size: with its framing a 40-bit record is 67 to 75 bits
(id, length, kind and tick distances are 26 to 34 of them), while the exact delta of a walker on a straight line, whose
position residual is predicted from the baseline's velocity (ADR-8522), is 52 to 68 bits. A fixed 5-byte record alone
makes the walking crowd's far tier larger, not smaller.
Decision: (1) The far record is its own state record kind, 3 (the kinds are a 2-bit field and 3 was free): `far :=
base_ago | far position | entries`. No other record pays a bit and the client needs no profile. (2) The far position
is `1 | x u15 | z u15 | y u10` (the designed 40 bits) or `0 | residual x3` (x, z, y), the residual classes of the
delta record applied to the coarse integers against the baseline's coarse position; the server writes the shorter. A
coarse integer is the offset inside the cell rounded to the nearest `2^5` steps (x, z) or `2^10` steps (y), so the
shown position is within half a coarse step of the server's (1.6 cm and 0.512 m at the 1 mm step, half of what the
designed truncation gives) and a position on the coarse grid (the origin, a floor at height 0) is exact; an offset in
the last half coarse step of a cell, which would round out of it, takes the exact record. The cell is the baseline's:
the server sends the form only while the baseline it names is on the same grid, in the same mode and in the same cell
on every axis. (3) The coarse position is a function of the server's position alone, never of the baseline, and both
sides compute a baseline's coarse position the same way from either form of it, so every far record of a version
decodes to one position and the residual form is exact under any loss, repetition or reordering. (4) A version held
in its far form (the client's `ClientVersion::far`, the server's `ConnEntity::base_far` once only far records of the
baseline are acknowledged) is a baseline for component deltas and for further far records and never for a transform
delta: the exact record that follows it is absolute (a delta against it is a decode error on the client, which asks
for the full state). On the client an exact record of a version replaces its far form in whichever order the two
arrive, and on the server an acknowledged exact record of the baseline's version clears `base_far`, so "the client
holds the exact form" is only ever concluded from an acknowledgment that proves it. (5) Rotation and scale of a far
version are display state: the copy keeps what it shows. The velocity is dropped, so an interpolated proxy infers it
from the far positions (spec 120 § 9.7) instead of extrapolating a stale one. (6) Selection: a far-tier update (not
owned, not forced, no teleport or resend, no parent change, no extrapolation gate on the entity, acknowledged state
channel) takes the far form when it is at least one byte shorter than the exact record (any shorter once the copy is
held in its far form: leaving it costs an absolute record, so a walker whose predicted delta is as short as the far
record stays exact). With a far baseline a record is due only when the coarse position or a component changed; a copy held in its far form stays an update
candidate, and the first record after it leaves the far tier (or is forced) restores the exact transform even when the
entity did not change. (7) `ServerReplication::set_far_records(false)` keeps exact records in the far tier (a game
whose far copies need rotation or sub-metre height; the before column of the bandwidth table).
`TRANSFORM_RECORD_REVISION` is 4: the protocol hash refuses a mixed pair at the handshake (`protocol_mismatch`,
`regia_net::replication::transform_record (different)`); the wire version stays 6.
Rejected: the lead bit (above); a far baseline for transform deltas with a tie-break on the client (no tie-break
closes the acknowledgment lag); a sub-form of kind 3 for an exact delta against a far version (rotation and velocity
would still travel absolute, 16 bytes against 22 for the absolute record, once per tier exit); truncation as designed
(twice the error, and a floor at height 0 would show half a metre low or high); keeping the baseline's velocity (a
far copy would extrapolate along a heading it left); the far form on the reliable tick stream (no acknowledged
baseline to take the cell from) and for gated entities (the gate models what the client extrapolates from exact
records; a gated entity already sends about a twentieth of the bytes).
Not covered: `external_replication` (spec 120 § 8.6) carries game-encoded records, so its far tier's record is the
game's (`tier_of` tells it the tier). A far copy's baseline expires with the 64-version ring like any other (spec 120
§ 8.1 known limit): an entity that changes every tick and loses two far records in a row gets a full state.
A copy held in its far form is visited by the per-connection walk every send tick (it is "behind" until its exact
state is acknowledged). (ADR-10199 corrects what this paragraph said next, that the tier interval holds such a copy
before any encoding: it does not, and ADR-10199 bounds the cost.)
Consequences: spec 120 § 8.3 (Built note), § 12.1 (the wire 6 row names the far record); the state record layout in
`replication/state_channel.rs` and `replication/transform_record.rs`; `docs/perf/net-far-record.md` (the bandwidth
table, 40 clients). Host-visible API (release fragment v0.1.28-v07-wire6-far-tier-record, Upgrade):
`StateCounters::far_records` (struct literals), `ServerReplication::{far_records, set_far_records}`,
`replication::{FAR_RECORD_BITS, FAR_XZ_SHIFT, FAR_Y_SHIFT}`. Agent: `net.state_channel` `far_records`,
`peers[].far_records`, `transform_record.{far_record_bits, far_xz_shift, far_y_shift}`. Behavior change: a project
with `rate_tiers` shows far copies at coarse positions with their last near or mid rotation. Fuzz:
`net.state_frame` seeds two far records (both forms).

## ADR-10199: A far copy settles: a version that has stood for two seconds goes exact (amends ADR-10124 (6))
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10124 (6) keeps a copy held in its far form an update candidate until it leaves the far tier, because
the exact state is owed then and no change of the entity announces a tier change. Its text said the tier interval
holds such a copy before any encoding. It does not: the tier hold compares the ticks since the copy's last *sent*
record with the tier's interval, and a far turn with no news sends nothing, so from one far interval after its last
record on the copy passes the hold on every send tick. A far crowd that walked and then stood was therefore walked
(`copies_visited`), read by the priority pass (`priority_slots`), ranked and encoded for every connection on every
send tick, for as long as it stayed far: 64 copies and 64 slots a send tick for a 64-walker crowd and one viewer,
where the same crowd on exact records costs 0 and 0 (test
`a_far_crowd_at_rest_settles_exact_and_leaves_the_walk`). At the scale of the 128 x 20k relevance bars (spec 120
§ 8.4) that would be the whole far population of a world at rest, on every connection, every send tick: the cost
an acknowledged connection's watch list exists to avoid (the bench itself moves every entity every tenth tick, so
it does not show it). It also left a standing far object with a rotation and a height it never had on the
server, for as long as nobody came near.
Decision: a version that has stood for `FAR_SETTLE_SECONDS` (2 s; `round(2 * tick_hz)` ticks between the version's
tick and the send tick, at least 1) never takes the far form. A copy held in its far form whose entity came to rest
so gets the exact record (absolute, as after any far baseline) at its first send tick past the settle time, still in
the far tier; the acknowledgment clears `base_far` by ADR-10124 (4)'s rule (an exact record of the baseline's
version), the copy is even with the server and leaves the walk. A lost settle record is offered again when its
packet resolves, like any update. Nothing changes on the wire or on the client: the settle record is the record a
tier exit sends, sooner. The protocol hash is unchanged by this ADR (revision 4 stays ADR-10124's).
Why 2 s: it must be longer than the far interval (0.5 s by default), or a walker's last far record and its settle
record would be one record and the far form would never be held; and long enough that an entity pausing between
moves does not pay an absolute record (about 22 bytes per far viewer) per pause. It is short against how long far
objects stand. The cost before the settle is bounded: at most 2 s of send ticks per stop and connection.
Rejected: keeping the copy off the walk and re-adding it when its tier changes (the packer reads a copy's tier from
the relevance pipeline's per-slot distance, so this needs a hook where the pipeline re-evaluates a held copy and a
per-connection list for the walk: a change to the N214 hot path, not examined further in this lane, and a far object
at rest would still show a rotation and a height it never had; it stays an option if a record per stop ever
matters); settling at the first far turn after
the last change (0.5 s: every pause of a stop-and-go walker would cost an absolute record); a profile field for the
time (no game has asked; `set_far_records(false)` is the switch for a game that wants exact far copies).
Not covered (known limit): a far copy whose transform keeps changing inside one coarse step (an entity turning on
the spot, a sway below 3.2 cm) makes a new version every tick, so it never settles; it is encoded on every send tick
and sends nothing, where an exact far copy is held by the tier interval between its records. Letting a far turn with
no news use up the tier interval needs a per-copy stamp (the slot's `last_sent` also drives `max_interval_ticks`,
which must keep counting sent records); it is left for the lane that next touches the packer, with this test's
counters as its bar.
Consequences: spec 120 § 8.3 (Built note: the settle rule); `replication::FAR_SETTLE_SECONDS` (new public constant);
agent `net.state_channel` `far_settle_seconds`; book `agents/net-far-record.md` and `agents/net-state-channel.md`;
`docs/perf/net-far-record.md` (the walk at rest); release fragment v0.1.28-v07-wire6-far-tier-record. Tests:
`a_far_crowd_at_rest_settles_exact_and_leaves_the_walk` (new);
`far_and_exact_records_mix_soundly_under_loss_reorder_and_duplication` gains a crowd that settles far on the bad
link, and `far_and_exact_records_mix_soundly_over_a_seed_sweep` (new) runs the mix over 64 seeds with a link and
flap lengths of their own, every other one settling far (3,000 seeds ran clean on this head: 1,688,992 far records,
no record error, every copy exact at the end); `a_far_crowd_travels_as_far_records_and_comes_back_exact`
now walks its viewer up 90 ticks after the stop instead of 210 (before the settle time, so it still tests the tier
exit of copies held in their far form; its quiet window before that is 30 ticks instead of 120, with the same bar of
0 records). Behavior change against ADR-10124 alone: a far copy at rest shows the exact transform after about 2 s
instead of when the viewer next comes near.

## ADR-10200: integ-v07-net: the first flight on by default (R1 (d)), `random_loss_kept` reads outside a first flight, `config/net.ron` v4, the asym-bufferbloat physics bound (R2), and the net lanes' merge reds
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed (item (1), the default, is revised by ADR-10231: the first flight is off by default in v0.7; every "on by default" below reads "when switched on")
Context: lane integ-v07-net lands the v0.7 net lanes together on integ-v07c (71773be0c): v07-net-delay-detector
(b06deec36, ADR-10097), v07-net-staleness-rtt-random-loss (b499cce8e, ADR-10157), v07-net-staleness-queueing
(7d742b4eb, ADR-10145, ADR-10156), v07-net-reassembly-stalled (a0deebb4c, ADR-10125), v07-wire6-far-tier-record
(7793e13b2, ADR-10124, ADR-10199); v07-net-staleness-rtt (62abce21f) was already on the base. The lead ruled on
ADR-10145's two open questions: R1, option (d) (ADR-10156's first flight on by default, in `RateConfig::default()`);
R2, asym-bufferbloat's `staleness_p99` is bounded by another flow's queue, accepted as a physics bound. The lead also
accepted `rate_vs_bottleneck`'s seed-sensitive second on the gate seed (congested/8 100.8 % at the base, congested+bulk/8
104.1 % after ADR-10145; neutral to better over 40 seeds, ADR-10145's table). ADR-10145 and ADR-10156 are accepted.
Decision:
(1) R1 (d). `RateConfig::default().first_flight` is `true`, and so is every derived default (`RateConfig::client()`,
`RateSettings::default()`, `LinkConfig::default()`, every session's link). The transport's own tests of the initial
window (the 64-packet first burst and the acknowledgment trains, windows and rates it makes: the 34 tests
ADR-10156 counted, 18 in the library and 16 in eight integration targets) build their links on a named fixture with
the first flight off (`blind_link()`, `cc::tests::blind`); their assertions are unchanged. The soak's knob
`Knobs::first_flight` is an `Option<bool>` (`None` keeps the engine's default); the staleness tests compare the blind
start and the first flight by name.
(2) `random_loss_kept` reads a rejoin's first round as follows: the smallest snapshot budget after 5 s is taken
outside the peer's first flight (`NetServer::in_first_flight`, true until a feedback round has acknowledged one of
the sender's packets). During a first flight the allowance is the essential floor's rate by design (80 of 140
entities on lossy-fat-pipe), not what random loss left of the path; the bar asks the second. The flight's own minimum
is kept apart (`ServerRecord::min_flight_entity_budget`) and pinned by
`staleness_stages::a_first_flight_dips_the_snapshot_budget_to_the_floor_and_no_further` (the dip is the floor's and
no deeper). Judging from after each connect's first round, as ADR-10156 suggested, is this rule; `rate_vs_bottleneck`
keeps its 5 s settle.
(3) `config/net.ron` format 4 (format batch 2): `session.rate_control.first_flight` (`RateSettings::first_flight`,
default `true`), passed to both ends by `RateSettings::{server, client}`. A v1 to v3 file has no key and loads with
the default; `migrate_net_settings` and `regia upgrade-project` stamp version 4 by a version step
(`net_settings_migration_sources` [1, 2, 3]); version 5 and newer are refused. `docs/formats/net-ron.md` has the
version 4 section; the corpus fixture `net-settings/v4.ron`, its FROZEN line, the format-hashes row and the spec 12 § 4a
batch row are this lane's (lane v07-fmt-batch2-freeze owns the batch table: the row is listed for it).
(4) R2: asym-bufferbloat/8 and /32 keep `staleness_p99` red (non-gating) as the bound ADR-10145 measured: 29.9 ticks of
another flow's queue on the downlink, `sender_hold` 0.00. No bar moves.
(5) The brief's reds, causes and fixes. (a) `listen_uplink_start_starves_nobody_and_keeps_the_uplink_over_seeds`: on
the merged head with the first flight off, seeds 36, 90 and 177 have no wedge (36 was red on the pure merge of
delay-detector onto integ-v07b; a later merge on the line, not this lane, cured it); with the first flight on, seed 90
had `client 61 no_snapshot for 2000 ms from 2866 ms`. Cause, as the brief located it: `cc::UPLINK_STARVED_MS`, a flat
second of unanswered sending before a peer counts as starved (`server.rs` `share_uplink`), so a crowded uplink took its
first target a second after the host's drop-tail queue began to starve its last-served peers. Fix:
`Connection::starved_after_ms`, eight of the path's minimum round trips plus the acknowledgment delay
(`UPLINK_STARVED_RTTS`), within 250 ms (`UPLINK_STARVED_MIN_MS`) to 1 s; 1 s before a round trip is known. After: no
wedge on 36, 90, 177 either way; seed 3's worst client staleness p99 6 with the first flight (9 before the fix).
(b) `frame_rate_io::the_same_client_at_30_and_300_fps_sends_the_same_per_second` (300 fps 33.1 datagrams/s against
30.0): red on the integ-v07c base already (the test machine run on 71773be0c, before this lane's merges: the same 33.1); not
delay-detector's (its branch has no clock stamp and passes). The client's clock stamp (peer-quality, ADR-8889, on integ-v07b) was queued as essential
data every 250 ms in whatever flush came due, and in a flush between ticks (nine in ten at 300 fps) it left in a
datagram of its own: 31 extra datagrams in 10 s, with no ack-only packet, resend or probe among them (diagnostic
counts). Fix (`client.rs` flush): a due stamp is queued only in a poll that sends a datagram anyway
(`Connection::sends_anyway`: an acknowledgment is due, or essential or unreliable data waits), and on its own after one
more sample interval (`CLOCK_RIDE_WAIT_MS`). (c) `quality_signals`: the three reds are peer-quality's, red on its own
base before delay-detector (its report: "red on this base for seed reasons, owner ruling"; all three red on the
integ-v07c base too, the test machine run on 71773be0c); on this head two of the three pass (`flappy_shows_interrupted_once_per_outage`,
`good_wifi_grade_stays_good_for_ten_minutes`) and `bad_wifi_reports_fair_or_poor_within_three_seconds` stays red at
seed 1 (client first fair/poor at 4,250 ms, bar 3,000): its path loses no packet in its first seconds, and spec 120
§ 13.1 grades loss and round trips, not jitter. Grading jitter is a spec change; not made (ruling owed).
(6) Merge reds fixed (compile): integ-v07c's flapping-gate test builds `UplinkPeer` with delay-detector's `loss` and
`starved`; delay-detector's `one_way_delay`, queueing's and reassembly-stalled's connection tests send on
`Channel::GAME_RPC` (ADR-10067 removed `Channel::Reliable` on integ-v07c); far-tier-record's `ClientVersion::far` and
delay-detector's `RoundSample` one-way fields in other lanes' lib-test literals.
(7) What the first flight costs on this head, measured (A/B: the same seeded runs with `Knobs::first_flight`
`Some(false)` and the default): with it off, the merged head passes every soak test below; with it on they fail.
(i) `rate_control::lossy_fat_pipe_keeps_the_snapshot_budget_at_the_seeds_that_lost_it` and
`staleness_stages::a_first_flight_dips_the_snapshot_budget_to_the_floor_and_no_further` (`random_loss_kept`, gate plan
lossy-fat-pipe/8 and /32, non-gating): budgets of 63 to 100 of 140 entities after 5 s outside the flight. Trace (seed
56, client 5): the join's first flight ends with ADR-10156's "the path fell behind" verdict on a 100 Mbit/s path, the
startup begins at about 31 kB/s with the pacer holding, and a loss cut on the early loss memory (16.8 %) takes it to
28.9 kB/s, where it holds for seconds. The verdict counts as due what the sender sent less what one minimum round trip
and 25 ms cannot have acknowledged; the minimum round trip excludes the receiver's acknowledgment delay (the soak's
client acknowledges at its 16 ms frames), so on a fast path the acknowledgments still owed read as a path behind.
Not fixed here: the fix needs the receiver's acknowledgment delay in `RoundSample` and its own measurement
(follow-up). A guard is in: the round that ends a first flight is not ADR-10157's "filled round before" (its packets
left at the floor's rate); it did not cure (i). A second mechanism, fixed: `cc::tests::a_tick_quantized_game_under_its_target_is_never_cut_for_random_loss`
(ADR-10157) cut 6 of 32 seeds with the default on, because the app-limited bound (1.5 times the recent delivery plus
1,250 B/s) read the rounds whose packets the flight had held to the floor's rate as what the game uses: a 52 kB/s game's
unconfirmed start rate fell to 65 kB/s, where the game read as saturating and random loss cut it. The bound now reads
the delivery after the flight (`RateController::flight_limited_until_ms`: the round that ends the flight and the next,
whose packets also left under it); the test passes on 32 of 32 seeds. The soak's (i) is pacer-limited, not app-limited,
and keeps its numbers.
(ii) `rate_control::congested_recovery_keeps_headroom_over_more_seeds`: seed 50, 2 of 14 seconds at 105 % of the
256 kbit/s link (ADR-10156 known limit (iv)). (iii) `staleness_stages::a_first_flight_keeps_congested_under_its_staleness_limit_at_the_default_start_rate`:
the staleness bar passes; the test's own price check fails on congested (a first flight's join 656/880 ms against the
32 KiB/s start's 656/672). (iv) `capture_replay` (2): a capture replays with a one-tick input divergence early in the
session; not traced, and not attributed to the flip or a merge (`workload::replay_client` replays with
`Knobs::default()`). `input_feedback::asym_bufferbloat_inputs_arrive_in_time` is red on this head, not attributed either.
The pinned transport tests of ADR-10156's list pass on `blind_link()`.
Consequences: a connection's first 0.1 s on a good link carries the essential floor's rate instead of the 64-packet
window (ADR-10156's price table); a thin link's join no longer fills its buffer. Host-visible: `RateConfig::default()`
and `RateSettings::default()` change value; `RateSettings` gains a public field (a struct literal without `..` no
longer compiles); `NetServer::in_first_flight` is new; `regia_net_soak::workload::Knobs::first_flight` is an
`Option<bool>` and `ServerRecord::min_flight_entity_budget` is new. `config/net.ron` is format 4.

## ADR-10189: Half fragments on an unmeasured or long path: a lost fragment is repaired in half a packet
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10125 found why a join snapshot behind a full byte-limited queue (the soak's `asym-bufferbloat`) ended
with `reassembly_stalled`, and moved the repair to the first place of its poll. It left one thing open: that queue
admits a full-size packet about six times in ten at best, a fragment can only be repaired whole, and a full fragment
is a full packet, so the fragment a stream waits for could still lose try after try (3 of 400 measured rows had a join
snapshot that took more than 15 s of the 18.6 s stall deadline, and 1 of 9,000 never arrived). ADR-10125 named a wire
shape as the way out (a record carrying part of a published fragment). It is not needed: the size of a fragment is the
sender's choice at the moment it cuts the message, the wire carries any size (a fragment record is a stream, a
fragment id, two flags and a length), and the receiver stores fragments by id whatever their length. The offline model
of that queue (ADR-10125; the same arithmetic as `regia_net_soak::impair::DirState`, 30 seeds) puts a packet of one
half fragment, first in its poll, at 89 to 95 % admission with the state waiting and 92 % with the state in the packet
behind it, against 56 to 59 % for a full fragment.
Decision: sender only, no wire change. **1. The cut.** A reliable message of more than one fragment, queued while the
path is not measured yet or while its round trip spreads repairs (`Connection::cuts_small_fragments`: no round-trip
sample, or `repair_packets_per_poll` under 8, that is a round trip of 8 ticks or more), is cut into half fragments:
`(fragment room - 5) / 2` bytes (`SMALL_FRAGMENT_DIVISOR`), so that two of them with their record headers fill the
room of one full fragment. A measured short path cuts full fragments, as before. A message that fits one fragment is
never cut (it may share a packet with the tick's records, which half fragments do not), and nothing is cut small
where a half would be 256 bytes or less (it would take a redundant copy at every transmission, ADR-8400). **2. Ids to spare.** Half
fragments use twice the fragment ids. The cut is small only while the stream then holds at most a quarter of
`max_reliable_in_flight` in queued fragments (`SMALL_FRAGMENT_QUEUE_DIVISOR`: 256 of the default 1,024, about 150 kB);
a longer backlog (a bulk transfer) keeps full fragments. The admission checks of `Connection::send` (`TooLarge`,
`Backpressure`) still count full fragments, so every single message that was accepted before is accepted now; a
stream can run out of ids at most an eighth of `max_reliable_in_flight` earlier than before. **3. A half fragment
takes a full fragment's place in a poll.** It shares a packet with other half fragments only: the tick's records end a
packet in front of it exactly where they would in front of a full fragment (with a probed path MTU above the base a
full fragment fits behind them, and so does a half), two halves ride where one full fragment rode,
and the first flight of a message is the same packets as before, each five bytes longer (the second record header).
Its repair leads its poll under ADR-10125's rules; with rate control on the lead is paid for with its pair (two
halves) outside a spread and alone inside one, so `listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh` reads 6
ticks of worst staleness, as before. **4. In a spread poll the repair leaves alone.** Where repairs leave one packet
per poll (a round trip of 20 ticks or more), that packet is one half fragment and nothing else, about half a packet
on the wire; the tick's records ride the next packet of the same poll. Redundant copies and ordinary unreliable data
are not added to it. **5. Nothing waits for a half fragment's repair.** ADR-10125's rule 4 (ordinary unreliable data
waits for spread repairs) now applies to repairs of full fragments only: half a packet finds room with the state in
the packet behind it, and with twice as many repairs the wait would cost twice the state (measured both ways, below).
The exemption holds only while the pacing allowance carries the repair's packet and the one behind it. Where it does
not (a share of an uplink smaller than the tick's state), the repair cannot lead, the state takes the allowance
whenever there is any, and without the wait the repair never leaves: there rule 4 applies to half fragments too
(test `half_fragment_repairs_get_their_turn_on_a_tight_allowance`; on the build without this, no repair left in 15 s).
**6. A fix to ADR-10125's lead.** A repair no longer leads a poll whose recovery budget (ADR-7950) lets no reliable
packet leave: the credit and essential records it displaced had no packet to ride and expired. Both found by an
independent review of this change. ADR-10125's other rules, ADR-10088's stagger, the once-per-round-trip bound of ADR-7995 and the
receiver's stall deadline (ADR-8521) are unchanged. Rejected: the part record (a wire shape, receiver storage for
partial fragments and per-part acknowledgment state, for the same admission); cutting every message small on every
path (a measured short path loses nothing to full fragments, and twice the ids for nothing); cutting messages that
fit one fragment (a one-fragment message may share a packet with the tick's records and a half fragment may not:
cutting it would take that away).
Consequences: measured with the soak's workload over `asym-bufferbloat`, 8 and 32 clients, 200 seeds (400 rows, 9,000
joins and rejoins, virtual time; `regia_net_soak` test `reassembly_stall`, `join_snapshot_sweep`): rows that lose a
connection 4 at the base, 0 with ADR-10125, 0 now; join snapshots that never arrived 133 of 9,004, then 1 of 9,000,
now 0 of 9,000; join snapshot time (median / 90th / 99th percentile / slowest) 9,264 / 13,728 / 17,568 / 27,664 ms at
the base, 3,888 / 6,384 / 9,728 / 15,664 ms with ADR-10125, 2,960 / 3,936 / 5,040 / 7,328 ms now; rows whose slowest
join snapshot took more than 15 s of the 18.6 s stall deadline: 252, then 3, now 0 (1 row over 7 s). The slowest join
snapshot of 9,000 now ends well inside half the stall deadline. With the state waiting for half fragments too (rule
5 left out; measured first) the same sweep read 3,216 / 4,272 / 5,472 / 9,152 ms and the gate plan's two
`asym-bufferbloat` rows read 25 to 27 ticks of `staleness_p99` instead of 20 (a non-gating bar, red before): twice
the repairs, twice the waiting, for a slower join. The gate plan has no red gating bar on two seeds (61 runs each,
`net-soak: 61 runs, PASS (0 failed bars are known blockers, 0 are new)`), and against ADR-10125's tables no verdict
and no gating bar moves; the same 21 non-gating bars fail at each seed. `asym-bufferbloat`'s `staleness_p99` reads 20
ticks on both rows and both seeds, as with ADR-10125. Columns that move, all inside their limits or on bars that
were red: the one-client `staleness_p99` of `mixed/32` reads 19 ticks at both seeds (18 and 20 before) and of
`mixed/40` 22 instead of 21 at the second seed (limit 8); the slowest rejoin of `downstream-loss/8` reads 736 ms
instead of 464 at the first seed and of `downstream-loss/32` 464 instead of 768 (grace 3,000 ms); missed input moves
by 0.01 % on four rows (limit 3 %) and the corrections of `high-rtt/8` read 1.9 % instead of 1.7 at the second seed; `congested/8/listen` delivers 68 and 83 kbit/s down at the mean instead of 63 and
66. `listen_uplink_at_64_clients_drops_nobody_and_stays_fresh` reads 6 ticks of worst staleness, as before. `cargo
test -p regia_net` and `-p regia_net_soak` are green; one existing unit test,
`one_fragment_reliable_send_keeps_the_body_allocation`, pinned the full cut on a fresh connection: it keeps every
assertion and now states its path (measured, short), and `the_half_cut_keeps_the_body_allocation` asserts the same
for the half cut. Not closed: (a) a message of one fragment between half
and a full packet is still repaired whole (cutting it has the cost named under Rejected); (b) the first flight still
leaves as one burst before any round trip is measured and is lost whole behind that queue, one round trip on every
join there (lane v07-net-staleness-queueing builds a paced first flight, ADR-10156); (c) bulk-stream repairs keep
their place behind state, and a bulk backlog past a quarter of the ids keeps full fragments; (d) a spread poll repairs
one half fragment where it repaired one full fragment, so on a long path whose loss does not depend on size (random
loss on a satellite link) the repair rate in bytes is half of ADR-10125's, one packet of 600 bytes per tick; a second
half-size repair packet per poll would give it back (the model admits two halves in a tick at 77 to 84 % each) and is
not built or measured; (e) `limit_packet_bytes` re-queues never-sent half fragments as ordinary fragments. Host-visible API (release
fragment v0.1.28-v07-net-reassembly-stalled, Upgrade): `Connection::cuts_small_fragments`, two public constants in
`regia_net::connection` (`SMALL_FRAGMENT_DIVISOR`, `SMALL_FRAGMENT_QUEUE_DIVISOR`), all additive. Behavior: a reliable
message of more than one fragment queued before the first round-trip sample, or on a round trip of 8 ticks or more,
is sent as twice as many fragments of half the size (counters that count fragments or resends read twice as high for
it; packets and bytes are the same but for five bytes a packet); a stream reaches `Backpressure` up to an eighth of
`max_reliable_in_flight` earlier when such messages are queued. No wire, content-format, agent-method or CLI change.
Specs updated: spec 120 § 5.3 (Built note); book/user-guide/networking.md; a provenance row.

## ADR-10231: integ-v07-net, third session: the first flight stays off by default in v0.7 (revised ruling), the reds the on-by-default had hidden, the input lead lowers on a measured margin, the half-fragment cut follows the path's own length, and the bad-wifi grade bar's two readings
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: lane integ-v07-net (ADR-10200) had applied the lead's ruling R1 (d): ADR-10156's first flight on by default.
Its own A/B then showed soak and unit tests that pass with the first flight off and fail with it on, and the lead
revised the ruling (2026-11-20 21:4x): for v0.7 the first flight stays off by default, built and opt-in; a v0.8 lane
fixes those reds and turns it on. The lead also asked for the last `quality_signals` red to be ruled from the spec text
if the spec is clear, and for the `input_feedback` red to be bisected and fixed. With the default back off, the
suites showed three reds that the on-by-default had hidden or that the lane's own fixes had made; this ADR records
each cause.
Decision:
(1) The revised ruling. `RateConfig::default().first_flight` is `false`, and so is every derived default
(`RateConfig::client()`, `RateSettings::default()`, `LinkConfig::default()`). The first flight stays built:
`RateConfig::first_flight`, and the `config/net.ron` key `session.rate_control.first_flight` of format 4 (format
batch 2), default `false`. A v1 to v3 file has no key and loads with the first flight off, as it ran before;
`migrate_net_settings` stamps version 4 by a version step. The pinned assertions are back at the flight-off
defaults (`cc::tests::the_first_flight_is_held_to_the_floor_and_starts_from_what_it_delivered`,
`connection::uplink_cap_tests::a_first_flight_sends_eight_packets_and_then_the_floor_until_the_path_answers`,
`integration_migrations::net_settings_v4_adds_the_first_flight_key_off_by_default`,
`staleness_stages::a_first_flight_dips_the_snapshot_budget_to_the_floor_and_no_further`, which asserts ADR-10156's
dip again and no longer that `random_loss_kept` passes with the first flight on). The 34 transport tests of
ADR-10156's count keep the named fixtures ADR-10200 gave them (`blind_link()`, `cc::tests::blind`,
`staleness_stages::blind_start`): the fixtures name the default now, the assertions never changed, and the release
that turns the first flight on does not have to touch them again. ADR-10200's fixes for the first flight stay and
stay covered with it on (`the_round_after_a_first_flight_is_no_evidence_against_the_path`,
`a_tick_quantized_game_after_a_first_flight_is_never_cut_for_random_loss`, new: ADR-10157's game on 32 seeds after a
first flight). ADR-10200 (2) stands for a run that opts in: `random_loss_kept` reads the budget outside a peer's first
flight and the soak keeps the flight's own minimum apart; no plan flies one. The A/B and what the v0.8 lane owes
are in ADR-10156 ("Revised ruling"). The frozen corpus fixture `net-settings/v4.ron` keeps `first_flight: true`
(frozen while the default was on; a frozen file is never re-blessed, and it now holds the key at its non-default
value); the format's shape hash does not change with a default.
(2) `input_feedback::asym_bufferbloat_inputs_arrive_in_time` ("the lead rose after the start-up spell: [18, 17, 18,
18]"). Bisect: green on integ-v07c (71773be0c) and at each of the five merge commits with the first flight off;
red from this lane's clock-stamp fix (ADR-10200 (5) (b), 2d912e4e2); with `client.rs` of merge 5 swapped in the head
passes with leads [18, 18, 18, 18]. The stamp fix is right (a client sends the same datagrams per second at any frame
rate) and changes which datagrams this test's client sends, so its seeded path draws other jitter and loss. What the
other draw showed is the lead controller's own: `LeadController::on_feedback` (`feedback.rs`) counted a record as
calm when the *corrected* p5 margin was two ticks, and the correction adds how much further ahead the client stamps
now than it did for the p5 input. The stamp offset follows the client's tick estimate, which wanders with the queue
on the way down (asym-bufferbloat: every tick sync a second late), so five seconds of a spare tick that was only
expected lowered the lead to 17, and the next measured margin raised it to 18 again. Fix: a lowering rests on a
margin the server measured. The calm window reads the smaller of the measured and the corrected p5; a deficit still
reads the corrected one (a late spell is answered once, ADR-8077), and a negative correction still counts, so a lead
that was raised too far comes down one tick per calm window as before. Spec 120 § 9.2: "Calm is every record for 5 s
showing a corrected p5 of at least 2 ticks" now reads "a measured and a corrected p5". Tests:
`feedback::tests::an_expected_spare_tick_does_not_lower_the_lead_and_a_measured_one_does` (new); `input_feedback` 8
of 8 and `connect_clock` 7 of 7 pass.
(3) `one_way_delay::a_queue_on_the_way_out_still_cuts` (delay-detector's guard: a reliable upload at eight times a
256 kbit/s uplink; "after 10 s the sender's packets still wait 1258 ms at its own bottleneck", bar 400). Bisect:
green through merge 3, red from merge 4 (reassembly-stalled) with the first flight off; the on-by-default had hidden
it. With the half-fragment cut off, or the repair spread off, it passes. Trace, once a second: the blind initial
window puts 81 kB into the 32 kB/s link in the first second (2.2 s of queue), the controller cuts to 8.4 kB/s and the
queue drains by the fifth second, in both variants. Then they part. Without the small cut the round trip estimate
follows the drain (1,033, 634, 288 ms), the startup's second overshoot comes at 6 s (62 kB in a second, 1.1 s of
queue) and the path is settled by 9 s. With it, the round trip reads 1,637 ms and the minimum 96 ms from the fourth
to the ninth second with the queue empty (no round-trip sample is taken in those five seconds), the target stays at
14.9 kB/s, and the same overshoot comes at 10 s and larger (target 29.7, then 118.9 kB/s; 1.26 s of queue), inside
the test's window. `Connection::cuts_small_fragments` (ADR-10189) read "a long path" off the round trip now, and a
round trip is also long behind a queue the sender built itself on a short path. Fix: the small cut follows the
path's own length, the shortest round trip of the last `MIN_RTT_WINDOW_MS` (10 s), never over the round trip now
(`Connection::path_round_trip_ms`); an unmeasured path still cuts small, and the spread of repairs still follows the
round trip now. A queue of other traffic that stands from the connect (asym-bufferbloat, the case ADR-10189 was
built for) is in the shortest round trip too; a queue the sender built is the rate controller's to drain. Not
closed: why no round-trip sample is taken for five seconds while half fragments leave behind the sender's own
queue (the trace is in the lane's report), and the startup's second overshoot itself, which both variants show.
Test: `repair_lead_tests::a_queue_of_the_sender_s_own_does_not_cut_its_messages_small` (new).
(4) `connection::repair_lead_tests::a_leading_repair_never_costs_the_tick_its_records` (reassembly-stalled's) was red
on the merged line with the first flight off: red at merge 5 with only the compile fixes (`17 led`, kept 0), and
green on the reassembly lane's own base. Its engine claims held on every run: each poll a repair leads still carries
the tick's two records, and the message arrives once. What failed was the test's premise, "a poll with a small
allowance kept its order": the small allowance was the loss cut a thin sender took for its lost repairs, and
ADR-10157 (merge 2) no longer cuts a thin sender for random loss (the likely merge; not bisected to a line, the test
does not exist before merge 4), so every poll's allowance carried the lead. ADR-10200 moved the test's sender onto
`blind_link()` while its peer kept the default first flight, and it passed for the peer's first flight, not for the
premise. The fixture now states the allowance the test's own text names, "a shared uplink's fair share": after the
warm-up `Connection::set_rate_cap(Some(48_000.0))`, about 800 bytes a tick, under the packet a full fragment fills.
No assertion changed. With it: 3 polls lead, 12 keep their order, the message arrives once. The window is narrow
and is recorded so nobody reads the number as a property of the engine: an uplink share of 36 or 42 kB/s fails the
test's own checks (too few repair polls; the message misses the test's last 600 ms), 56 kB/s and more keep no poll
(the tick sends a few hundred bytes, so the bucket fills and every poll pays for the lead), and a project rate
(`rate.max_bytes_per_second`) of 20, 32 or 48 KiB/s gives kept 0, 0 and 1 with no delivery at 48.
(5) `capture_replay::{a_bad_wifi_capture_replays_to_the_same_corrections_and_digest,
a_failing_run_writes_captures_that_replay}` are red on integ-v07c (71773be0c) itself with the same divergence
(`input tick 16` captured, `15` replayed), so they are neither the first flight's nor this lane's merges'. Cause:
ADR-10096 anchors the client's clock and startup lead with the handshake's shortest round trip
(`client.rs` `on_accept`: `handshake_one_way_ms` from `handshake_rtt_ms`), and a replay runs no handshake
(`replay_receive` feeds the captured `Accept` to `on_accept`; the capture had no record of a challenge or of when a
flight left), so the replayed client anchored with a one-way delay of 0 and stamped its first inputs a tick lower.
Fix: the capture holds the anchor. `CaptureRecord::Handshake { rtt_ms }` (record kind 11, eight bytes) is written in
front of the accept it led to, a replay takes the round trip from it before it handles that accept, and the
comparison of a replay leaves the record out, as it does the accept (the replay was fed both). The kind is additive
in `netcapture` version 1, which has not shipped (v0.7 is its first release; ADR-7724 folds a later change into the
unreleased version): a capture written before it has no such record and replays as it did, the frozen corpus file
`netcapture/v1.bin` is unchanged, and the format's shape hash moves once (`cargo xtask check-formats --update`).
Tests: the two `capture_replay` tests; `capture::tests::the_handshake_round_trip_is_a_record_the_replay_is_fed` (new).
(6) `quality_signals::bad_wifi_reports_fair_or_poor_within_three_seconds`: the spec text does not settle it, so both
readings are recorded. Spec 120 § 13.1 defines the grade by round-trip p95, loss and missing inputs, and says
"Jitter is reported but not graded"; its v0.7 Built note (ADR-8889) says "A loss fraction counts from 67 resolved
packets" and keeps the 500 ms hold; and row N110's acceptance says "bad-wifi fair/poor within 3 s". On wire 5 each
end resolves about 33 packets a second on this profile, so a loss fraction first counts about 2.0 s after the
connect, and a grade can show 2.5 s after it at the earliest, and only if two packets of the first 67 were lost in
one direction. Measured on this head (20 s, ms after the connect, client / server): seed 1 4,250 / 4,242; 2 2,750 /
3,233; 3 2,500 / 3,225; 4 3,250 / 3,234; 5 4,750 / 2,720; 6 3,250 / 2,724; 7 2,750 / 2,992; 8 6,500 / 2,965. Only
seed 7 meets 3 s on both ends; the test stops at seed 1. It is not one unlucky seed, and it is not that the path
loses nothing early (seed 1's first loss resolves at 3.25 s; other seeds lose earlier and still miss): the 67-packet
count and the acceptance row do not fit together at this packet rate. Reading A (the acceptance row governs): the
grade needs a signal that tells bad-wifi from good-wifi inside 3 s, which at these rates is jitter or RTTVAR (4 to 6
ms against 0.5 to 1); that changes § 13.1 ("not graded") and needs a limit that good-wifi never crosses in ten
minutes. Reading B (§ 13.1 and the 67-packet count govern): a link is `Good` until its loss fraction counts and
passes a limit, and the acceptance is restated for wire 5 as "within 3 s of the loss window counting" (about 5 s
after the connect at 30 Hz), or the count goes back toward 32 with a rule that one loss is not a rate (a second
loss before 67 packets counts), which brings back some of the early `Fair` spells on good-wifi that ADR-8889 removed.
Not ruled, and nothing changed: the test, its seeds and its bar are as they were.
(7) The reassembly lane finished after this lane's merge 4 took its session-2 head (a0deebb4c, whose code names
ADR-10189 without its text). Its finished head 28160f7e5 (Status DONE: ADR-10189, the review fixes, two tests, docs)
is merged on top, so the line carries the ADR its code cites.
Consequences: host-visible against ADR-10200's head: `RateConfig::default()`, `RateSettings::default()` and the
`config/net.ron` key default are `false` again (the values before ADR-10200); nothing else of ADR-10200's API moves.
The input lead comes down later on a link whose tick estimate moved forward (it waits for a measured spare tick);
on a steady link it behaves as before. A reliable upload behind its own queue on a short path is cut into full
fragments. `CaptureRecord` has a new variant (`Handshake`): an exhaustive match needs the arm. Spec 120 § 9.2 and
§ 5.3 (Built notes), `docs/formats/net-ron.md` (the key's default), `docs/formats/netcapture.md` (kind 11), spec 12
§ 4a (the batch rows), `book/agents/net-soak.md`.

## ADR-10215: A record without a velocity clears a proxy's replicated `NetVelocity` (fixes review R1 of ADR-10124)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10124 drops the velocity from a far record (the client infers it from the positions, spec 120 § 9.7),
and the snapshot side does that: the decoded far version and the buffered far snapshot have `velocity: None`. The
component side did not follow. `write_transform` (direct copies) and `net_interpolate`'s pose write (interpolated
proxies) only inserted `NetVelocity` when the record or the sampled pose had one and never removed it, so a far-tier
copy kept the velocity of the last exact record it got, for as long as it stayed far. Review
`v07-wire6-far-tier-record-review-oai` R1: one turning far-tier walker (seed `0x10124`), 400 ticks, then stopped for
120 ticks: the copy still had `NetVelocity(1.3125, 0, 0.15625)`; gameplay and animation reading it saw a walker
moving that stood, or moving the wrong way after a turn. The same hole was there before the far tier for a proxy
whose server entity dropped its `NetVelocity`, or whose mode went from `Movement` to `PositionOnly`, but nothing
exercised it.
Decision: a received record (spawn, update, far update, either channel) or a sampled pose without a velocity
removes the copy's `NetVelocity` when replication owns it: on a proxy, that is a copy with neither
`NetOwnedLocally` nor `NetPredicted`. A copy this client owns or predicts keeps whatever its game or prediction
wrote (unchanged: a record with a velocity still writes it on any copy, as before). The rule is one crate-private
predicate, `replication::is_replication_owned_velocity`, used by both writes; `net_interpolate`'s query already
leaves owned and predicted copies out. An interpolated pair with one velocity-less side (an exact snapshot blended
into a far one, or back) has no velocity either, as `sample` already said; the inferred extrapolation velocity of a
velocity-less proxy stays unwritten (it is a guess). The first exact record after the copy leaves the far tier (or
settles, ADR-10199) writes the current velocity again. No wire, codec, snapshot or protocol-hash change.
Consequences: a far-tier copy has no `NetVelocity` while it is shown from far records, as the v0.1.28 far-record
fragment already promised; code that read `NetVelocity` on a far copy as "still moving" sees `None` (read the
position history, or `NetSnapshotBuffer`, for an inferred one). Docs: `NetVelocity` rustdoc; book
`agents/net-far-record.md` (Velocity row); spec 120 § 8.3 Built note. Tests: the review's two proofs
(`review_far_record_clears_the_previously_replicated_velocity`,
`review_interpolated_far_record_clears_the_previously_replicated_velocity`) now pass;
`a_far_copy_never_shows_a_stale_velocity_and_gets_the_current_one_back` and
`an_interpolated_far_copy_never_shows_a_stale_velocity_and_gets_the_current_one_back` (new, `far_tier_record`)
check over 600 far-tier ticks of a turning walker that the copy's velocity is absent or one the server had within
the records' reach, then current again after the viewer walks up; the unit test
`replication::tests::a_velocity_less_record_clears_only_a_proxys_velocity` pins the ownership rule (proxy cleared;
owned and predicted kept; a `PositionOnly` record clears; a velocity writes again).

## ADR-10161: Shadow views count the edge slack; the sun cover bounds the drawn coarse shadow mesh
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The review of ADR-8874 (`sprint-v07-interior-cull-shadows-review`) found two holes. (1)
`cull_shadow_views` tested the recorded outdoor frusta only when a view's narrow walk reached cell 0,
but the outdoor walk widens the frustum by the terrain's two-pixel edge slack (`OUTDOOR_EDGE_SLACK_PX`,
ADR-8413) and can record a mouth the narrow walk missed; terrain, grass, impostors and water draw
there, so a caster whose sun shadow lands only in that band was sealed or dropped (test
`a_mouth_in_the_edge_slack_keeps_the_caster_that_shadows_only_that_band`). A render-to-texture view had
the same hole: it records no frusta and stood the cull down only when its narrow walk reached cell 0.
(2) `terrain_min_cover` trusted the min-max pyramid over the footprint grown by two root shadow cells,
but a root (and next-level) shadow vertex reads the box-filtered height pyramid at its morphed
position, which averages samples up to about three root cells away (`NodeReach::reach`); on the
128 m test map a sample 25 m off the footprint pulled the drawn root mesh 9.3 cm under the trusted
minimum (`the_root_shadow_mesh_over_the_sweep_stays_above_the_grown_pyramid`).
Decision: (1) Every recorded outdoor frustum of every window view is a receiver, whatever the narrow
union says. The cull stands down when any window view has no restricted list (eye outdoors, a capped
walk, an overflowing list), or when a texture view reaches cell 0 through its narrow walk, its
slack-widened walk (`outdoor_portals` into a reused scratch list, only while the shadow-view cull is
on), or a depth-capped walk. (2) `terrain_min_cover` returns the lower of the pyramid minimum over the
rectangle grown by `grow` and, for every shadow level whose full-morph reach is longer than `grow`, a
lower bound of the mesh that level draws over the rectangle: the lowest bilinear read of the levels
each candidate vertex blends (`vertex_mip` at morph 0 and 1), over the box its morph moves it across,
with the pyramid's own texel filter evaluated on demand (`parent_taps`). Candidate vertices are those
of every triangle that can overlap the rectangle (grid points within one shadow cell plus one step of
it; the morph moves a vertex at most one step toward +X/+Z). A drawn point is a convex mix of its
triangle's vertices and a vertex height a convex mix of its bilinear reads, so the bound holds for
every morph factor. A level where cliff relief can act (its fine grid and normal taps are not
modelled), that reads a level above 6, or that has more than 4096 candidate vertices falls back to the
pyramid over the rectangle grown by its reach (lower, never wrong). The default growth stays two root
cells: with the drawn-mesh bound any growth is safe, and the default keeps the finer levels on the
cheap pyramid read.
Consequences: No visible shadow caster is culled in the slack band, by a texture view, or past a
depth cap; the in-tube counter bar of ADR-8874 is unchanged ([4, 4, 4, 4] to [3, 3, 3, 3]). A texture
view costs one more portal walk per frame while the shadow-view cull is on. The cover seals fewer cells
next to a filtered dip just outside the growth (it was wrong to seal them). Not covered: cliff relief
(`TerrainRelief::cliff_relief`, default 1) displaces steep-face vertices by up to `CLIFF_RELIEF_MAX_M`
(8 m at strength 2) along the face normal in the shadow passes too; the cover does not see that setting
(it lives on the shared draw), so a tunnel whose swept cover holds a face steeper than 0.7 rad can be
sealed under a recess the relief carves. Proposed follow-up: pass the relief strength into
`TerrainSunCover` and pad the minimum by its displacement over steep nodes. No format, migrator or
agent change. Updated: `book/agents/viscells.md`, spec 25 § 7.7, `docs/provenance.md`.

## ADR-10132: Looped `.uianim.ron` frame events sit on the plan's pass boundaries; the format-batch ADR becomes ADR-8900
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v07-fmt-logic-uianim review (sprint-v07-fmt-logic-uianim-review, proof tests at 985fbdd27) found two
bugs. (1) `UiAnimDef::compile_events` put pass `n` at `(n as f32 * duration + local) / speed`. That is not monotone in
f32 (a 0.1 s loop x 8: the pass-6 end at 0.70000005 comes before the pass-7 start at 0.7), and an event authored at the
pass end can land past `TweenPlan::duration`, the left-to-right sum of the step lengths (a 0.3 s loop x 7: 2.1000001 >
2.1). Playback (`UiTween::with_events` sorts; a finished tween flushes the cursor) still fired every event, but
`ui.play_anim` `sample` walked the unsorted list with `take_while` and had no end flush, so it dropped events playback
sends. (2) Two decisions were numbered ADR-8832, so `cargo xtask adr-index` failed.
Decision: (1) `compile_events` reads the pass boundaries from the plan itself: `compile` and `compile_events` share
one step builder (`compile_passes`, per track and pass), each boundary is the largest per-track running f32 sum of the
step lengths through that pass (the same additions, in the same order, as `TweenPlan::duration`), and an event goes at
`start + local / speed` clamped into `[start, end]` of its pass, or exactly `end` when it is authored at the pass end
(the start of a backward pass). Times therefore never decrease, an end event and the next pass's start event share
the boundary time (each fires once, end first), and the last boundary equals the plan's duration bit for bit.
`ui.play_anim` `sample` moves the same cursor playback moves (`UiTween::take_crossed_events` with elapsed clamped to
the plan's duration and every event once the time reaches it), so it lists exactly the events `advance_tweens` has
sent by that time. Single-pass placement is unchanged except that an event at the end is the plan's duration itself.
The `.uianim.ron` file format, its version (2) and its meaning (each event once per pass at its authored time) do not
change; no `format-hashes.ron` row or spec 12 § 4a row moves. (2) The format-batch decision (`.logic.ron` and
`.uianim.ron` 1 -> 2) becomes ADR-8900, from the reserved block 20000-20199 (ADR-10102; ADR-20000 is the only number
used there). The glyph-atlas decision keeps ADR-8832. Every format-batch citation moved, except the first comment line
of three frozen fixture files (`format-corpus/logic/v2.ron`, `format-corpus/uianim/v2.ron` and the fuzz copy
`fuzz_targets/fixtures/logic-vars.example.ron`): their bytes are pinned by `FROZEN.txt`, which is never edited, so
their "ADR-8832" means ADR-8900.
Consequences: `sample` and playback agree at every time, including at and past the end. `compile_events` now errors on
an unknown track property when the animation has events (it builds the plan steps); `to_tween` and `ui.play_anim`
already compiled the plan first. Proof tests: the review's two `anim_timeline` tests, a sweep over 6 pass lengths x
both loop modes x 6 speeds x reverse x every loop count to `MAX_LOOPS`, and an agent test that steps a real
`advance_tweens` and compares `sample` at every update. Specs: none (the format page describes the per-pass rule, which
holds).
Integration note (integ-v07-freeze, ADR-10265): the integration line had already renumbered the format-batch decision
from ADR-8832 to ADR-8900 (integ-v07a), so this lane's ADR-20132 is folded onto ADR-8900 and every citation reads ADR-8900.

## ADR-10147: Lockstep probe ring holds the replayed history; a thinned feedback window keeps a released seat released
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v07-net-ki-lockstep review (two proof tests on `lane/sprint-v07-net-ki-lockstep-review`, 351410423) found two bugs in ADR-8855. (1) The per-tick hash ring the desync probe reads (`LockstepHost` and `LockstepSeat`, `HASH_RING_TICKS`) only ever appended, and no replay path wrote it: `record_replayed` replaced the subsystem rows only, `revote`/`resynced` sent a vote only, and the server's observer, after `load_observer_state`, reported only its checkpoint hash. The probe takes the first copy of a tick (`find`), so after a replay or a state transfer the ring still held the hashes the simulation had stepped before it. When that voter is the next probe's reference, every other voter's first diverged tick moves to the first stale tick: in the review's run a delayed observer load (replay 121..=199) made seat 1's drift at 190 read as 181. ADR-8855 called the stale observer hashes "diagnosis only"; the run showed they move another seat's diagnosis. (2) `judge_hold_release` cleared `hold_released` whenever the feedback window had fewer than 30 arrivals, so a loss burst on a released seat armed the two-window hold again while its median was still about 21 ticks past an 8-tick window: the other seat waited out the grace until a fresh half second of arrivals existed (336 of 350 ms in the review's run).
Decision: (1) The probe ring keeps one hash per tick, ascending (`put_ring_hash` in `lockstep/host.rs`, shared by host and seat): a tick reported again replaces its hash in place; a tick older than the newest goes in tick order (a full ring drops its oldest tick and never stores one older than all it keeps); the live path is still one `push_back`. Every replay path writes it: `record_replayed` (host and seat) puts the world hash in the ring as well as the rows; new `LockstepHost::report_replayed_hash` and `LockstepSeat::report_replayed_hash` do it for a game that reports plain hashes (no vote); `revote` (host and seat) and `resynced` (seat) put the voted hash at the checkpoint. The observer thread, after a load, reports its hash after every replayed frame with the checkpoint's (`ObserverReport::Loaded` carries them); the server writes them all into the host's ring and the observer's `recent` hashes before it calls `revote`, because the revote can close a checkpoint and start a probe. Replace-in-place rather than the subsystem ring's rewind-from-tick: a replay that stops early (a missing frame) would leave holes, and the probe's `map_while` stops at the first missing tick. A pending probe is not affected: the host reads its own rows when the verdict starts the probe, and a seat answers `Order::Probe` when it arrives, before the `Resync` order the same verdict queued after it. The soak kit's replay paths (`regia_net_soak` lockstep runs, vectors) report their replayed hashes the same way. (2) A released seat is held for again only when the feedback window has at least `HOLD_RELEASE_SAMPLES` arrivals and their median margin is two ticks inside the window; a thinner window keeps the previous decision. The release side already needed the full count.
Consequences: Fault-free runs are unchanged: the live path appends as before, and the hold decision changes only for a released seat with a thinned window (no fault-free run has one); the lockstep determinism golden (`lockstep_golden`) pins simulation hashes, which neither change touches. After a replay, a voter's probe rows are the history its simulation has now, so the next probe names each diverged voter's own first tick. A forging seat's self-check replay now writes its honest hashes over its forged live ones (its forged revote stays at the checkpoint), so a probe of it can name a later tick than its first forged one; the forger is still the only voter named (`a_seat_that_forges_hashes_is_resynced_then_removed_and_the_others_never_stop` passes unchanged). A released seat stays released through a loss burst for up to half a second after its link comes back fast (until 30 fresh arrivals show the median back inside); its inputs are merged late meanwhile. Host-visible API: two new methods (no break). Specs: none changed (spec 120 § 7.6 already says the probe compares per-tick hashes since the last agreed checkpoint).

## ADR-10184: The DO27 switch package for v0.7: one book page, links not copies, and the v0.7.x promise
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.7 exit bar 7 (plan v0.7-to-v1.0 § 2.2) is "ready for DO27 to switch": a list of what DO27 switches
to, the Stage B switch note, and the format batch 2 upgrade guide. The owner set on 11-19 that DO27's own pin runs and
its sim-version bump are v0.7.x work with a 48 h fix turnaround, because DO27 is paused until the v0.7 tag. The
pieces already exist in three places: the adoption guide (`book/user-guide/adopting-features.md`, v0.5 rows), the
Stage B switch note (`book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md`, ADR-10082) and the format lanes' release notes;
the batch's upgrade guide (`docs/guide/upgrade-v07.md`) is written by the freeze lane at the 11-28 freeze.
Decision: One book page, `book/user-guide/do27-switch-v07.md`, next to the other DO27 pages in the user guide. It
holds (a) the absorb list (absorb plan § 6 and the absorb-gaps rows: DO27 component, Regia API, format read, parity
test, state on the line), (b) a link to the switch note, (c) DO27's part of format batch 2 with links to each format
lane's release notes and the upgrade guide's path, and (d) the v0.7.x promise. It links and never copies: the switch
note and the upgrade guide stay the single source of their text. Every Regia name on the page is checked against the
code of the line it was written on; a name that does not exist is a bug in the list. A row whose lane has not landed
says "not on this line" with the lane's name, never a date. The 48 h promise covers engine bugs that block DO27's pin
runs or its bump; a missed bar goes to the owner with the measured number, not into a fix.
Consequences: DO27 has one entry page for the switch. The page must be re-checked when the absorb lanes land on the
v0.7 line (the "state" column moves) and when the freeze lane merges (the upgrade guide's path becomes a link). No
spec, format, API or dependency change.
## ADR-10130: Locomotion follow-ups L-05: idle landing bend limit, idle turn hold, graph foot turns, posture params
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.7 plan item L-05 collects locomotion follow-ups from the animation reports. (1) `anim.gait_simulate`
on seeded rubble with steering reported `max_foot_jump` above `swing_bound` (0.298 against 0.265, hexapod, seed 11).
A sweep over five seeds, three steer values and three rubble heights found nine runs over the bound (worst 0.3308
against 0.2979, seed 42, steer 0.2, amplitude 0.15), all at the step where the body first drops below `idle_speed`:
a foot whose swing ended in that step (arc progress 0.997) jumped from its walking landing to neutral. The idle settle
of ADR-8539 shrinks a landing heading by the share of the remaining swing a step covers, so a swing that goes idle at
progress `u` moves its landing by `heading * step_length / 2 * du / (1 - u)`; near touchdown that is the whole
`step_length / 2` (0.3 m) in one step. The rubble only decided which foot was in that state. (2) `params` of
`anim.gait_simulate` could not set `GaitParams::posture`. (3) Graph foot-placement output
(`FootPlacementOutput::GraphParams`) wrote the targets but no foot tilt or toe bend, which a `TwoBoneIK` node cannot
express (KI of ADR-8388 and ADR-8505). (4) KI-AN-005: a driven body whose yaw changes on only some steps (a 20 Hz
heading under a 60 Hz presentation) switched between the idle turn thresholds and the tighter settle threshold every
few steps: 99 lift-offs against 54 for the same turn at 0.3 rad/s over 10 s. (5) The gait-driven-body report listed
"driven bodies below `idle_speed` replant every step"; that was the state before ADR-8539.
Decision: (1) The idle bend of a landing moves it at most `2 * step_length` per `settle_period` of time, the re-aim
the published swing bound allows per step (its shortest swing is at most `settle_period`). Earlier in the swing the
proportional bend of ADR-8539 is smaller than that limit and unchanged (a stop that enters idle before about three
quarters of a swing still lands exactly at neutral); a swing that goes idle later lands short of neutral and the
normal settle step (`settle_distance`) takes it the rest of the way. The swing bound formula is not changed. (2) `params.posture` is an
object of the `.gait.ron` posture fields (`swing_weight`, `height_tau`, `height_slew` with `null` for no limit,
`attitude_weight`, `max_pitch`, `max_roll`, `attitude_tau`) written over `GaitPosture::UPRIGHT`; a non-object, an
unknown field or a non-number is `gait_settings`, and ranges are checked by `GaitParams::validate` as before.
(3) Graph output turns each foot joint by the plan's tilt (pre-multiplied onto the solved foot's object rotation, as
`apply_foot_plant` does after its own solve) and bends each toe joint by the plan's toe rotation, on the evaluated
pose in the pose-output slot of `apply_animation` (after the ragdoll blend, before gaze). Joint positions do not move,
so the graph's targets stay valid. Flat feet with no toe bend skip the step and the pose copy. (4) `GaitState` keeps
the idle turn thresholds for `settle_period` seconds after the last step whose yaw changed (private field
`turn_hold`, `#[reflect(ignore)]` so reflected and saved data do not change). A turn updated every step is unchanged while it turns; after it stops the feet settle `settle_period`
later than before. (5) No code change: a test proves a driven body creeping at half `idle_speed` for 1200 steps never
replants and never snaps a planted foot. Part one of KI-AN-005 (a foot whose neutral is refused and whose nearest
valid foothold is within `settle_distance` stays and counts as settled) is kept as the rule: stepping would step in
place; the book states it precisely. KI-AN-006 (gait math is presentation only) is a design statement and stays.
Consequences: Fail-before / pass-after tests: `regia_animation --test gait_followups` (rubble sweep, idle drift,
intermittent yaw), `--test foot_placement` (`graph_params_turns_the_foot_by_the_tilt`,
`graph_params_on_level_ground_leaves_the_foot_on_the_shin`), `regia_agent --test locomotion_followups` (rubble seed 11
and sweep through the dispatcher, posture params). Behavior changes are presentation only (feet never feed a checksum;
nothing enters `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`): idle landings late in a swing, the first `settle_period` after a turn
in place, and graph-output feet on slopes and stairs (rigs with graph output on uneven ground render differently: the
third-person fox; goldens are listed for the lead). `presentation_trace_pin` (a presentation trace, never a
simulation pin; shared by `tripod_preset_matches_the_six_leg_stepper_bit_for_bit` and
`attitude_weight_zero_matches_the_upright_trace`) ends with 90 idle ticks after a turn and is re-pinned
(0x04fbcfb25b1c4232 -> 0xa3337df3c2f49638): both the bend limit and the turn hold act in that window. Owner ruling
needed: `settle::stop_settles_to_neutral_within_two_periods` asserts that a dead stop settles within two
`settle_period`s (37 steps at 60 Hz); with the bend limit, stops whose swing in progress is past about three quarters
need a third swing: 39, 38, 37 steps at stops 90, 91, 92 and again at 108, 109, 110 (others 8 to 36), worst one-step
foot move 0.048 m. Landing such a swing at neutral inside two periods needs the jump of (1) (up to `step_length / 2`).
The test is left unchanged (red at stops 90, 91, 108 and 109); the choice between the two properties is the owner's.
A third option, stretching the late swing until its bend completes, keeps both but changes the idle schedule and is
not built here. No format, dependency or public API change: `GaitState` gains an
unreflected private field (it has private fields, so no literal breaks). Books: `procedural-gait.md` (turn hold, refused neutral),
`locomotion-quality.md` (`params.posture`), `foot-planting.md` (graph foot turns), `gameplay.md` (comment).

## ADR-10162: A late idle landing stretches its swing instead of landing short
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10130 limits the idle bend of a swinging foot's landing to `2 * step_length` per `settle_period`, which
removed a one-step foot jump of up to `step_length / 2` (0.3308 m measured on rubble) when a body went idle near
touchdown. A dead stop that catches a swing past about three quarters of its arc then lands that foot short of
neutral and needs a third idle swing: 37-39 steps at 60 Hz against the two-`settle_period` bound of
`tripod_gait settle::stop_settles_to_neutral_within_two_periods` (37), which went red. Lead ruling (option c of
ADR-10130): keep both properties, never raise the test's limit, never bring back the jump.
Decision: the idle beat clock slows while a landing still needs more bend than the limit allows over a full clock
step. `idle_clock_rate` takes, for each swinging foot that lands at its heading (tripod or hanging mode), the
proportional bend of ADR-8539 over a full idle clock step, `shift * slope * progress / (1 - u)` (`shift` the
landing's distance from neutral, `slope` arc progress per beat phase, `u` the stored arc progress), and scales the
clock step by `limit / bend` when it is larger. With the clock slowed the bend of each step equals the limit, the
remaining heading and the remaining arc shrink together, so the rate holds for the rest of the swing and the landing
reaches neutral exactly at touchdown. A walking landing (`step_length / 2` from neutral) needs at most a quarter of
a `settle_period` of swing, so a dead stop settles within `max(1 - u, 1/4) + 1` `settle_period`s (tripod). Swings
that went idle earlier than about three quarters never slow the clock (the proportional bend is below the limit),
and idle settle and turn swings have no heading, so the schedule of every other case is bit-identical (the clock
rate is exactly 1). The bend limit of ADR-10130 stays as the backstop (a landing it leaves short is finished by a
settle step).
Consequences: `stop_settles_to_neutral_within_two_periods` passes unchanged; the item-1 rubble tests of ADR-10130
pass unchanged. New tests in `regia_animation --test gait_followups`: dead stops at every tick over three walking
cycles settle within two periods with a bounded one-step foot move (flat), and never jump on rubble. Presentation
only (feet never feed a checksum; nothing enters `docs/ci/lockstep-closure.toml`). `presentation_trace_pin` (a
presentation trace, never a simulation pin; shared by `tripod_preset_matches_the_six_leg_stepper_bit_for_bit` and
`attitude_weight_zero_matches_the_upright_trace`) brakes its integrating walker to idle with a swing late in its
arc, so the stretch acts there and the pin moves (0xa3337df3c2f49638 -> 0x8e1c5c05224234f3, the same value in all
three tests). Measured on the build server: slowest dead stop over stops 60-170 settles in 36 steps (limit 37), worst
one-step foot move 0.0607 m on flat ground and 0.0809 m on rubble (the ADR-10130 jump was 0.3308 m). No format, API,
reflection or dependency change. Book `procedural-gait.md` (stopping) updated.

## ADR-10265: v0.7 freeze, gate candidate 1: late-lane merges, the format-batch ADR number, and the peer-quality reading
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: The v0.7 freeze (lane integ-v07-freeze, base v07-fmt-batch2-freeze 15e2293fd) merges the lanes that reported
after integ-v07c and makes the first v0.7 gate candidate. Three things needed a decision: (1) lane
fmt-logic-uianim-review-fix renumbered the format-batch decision (`.logic.ron` and `.uianim.ron` 1 -> 2) from the
colliding ADR-8832 to ADR-20132, while the integration line had already renumbered the same decision to ADR-8900
(integ-v07a); (2) the integ-v07-net report left `regia_net` `quality_signals::bad_wifi_reports_fair_or_poor_within_three_seconds`
red with two readings of spec 120 and asked the freeze to pick the one the spec text supports; (3) the merges touched
format rows again after the batch-2 freeze run (integ-v07-net: `net-settings` 3 -> 4, the `netcapture` kind 11 fold).
Decision: (1) ADR-8900 stays the format-batch number (it is the one on the line and in every document the line has
cited since integ-v07a). The lane's code and tests merged unchanged; its citations read ADR-8900; ADR-10132 keeps its
own number and gains an integration note. ADR-20132 is not used. (2) The spec text supports reading B: § 13.1 says
"Jitter is reported but not graded", and the v0.7 Built note (ADR-8889) moved the loss count to 67 resolved packets
on purpose (good-wifi showed `Fair` for 2.5 s with 32). The "within 3 s" figure in the v0.5.x Built note was measured
on wire 4 at 32 packets. Reading B needs N110's acceptance bar restated for wire 5 (about 33 packets a second per
end, so a loss fraction first counts about 2 s after the connect). Moving a bar is an owner ruling (AGENTS.md rule
4), so the freeze changes neither the test nor the spec: the test stays red and is listed for the owner with the
measured numbers of the integ-v07-net report (first `Fair`/`Poor` 2,500 to 6,500 ms on the client, 2,720 to 4,242 ms
on the server over eight seeds). (3) One `cargo xtask check-formats --update` after the last format merge, its rows
named in the commit; `format-hashes-v0.7.0.ron` is written by the release commit, not here. (4) The net-soak gate
row is turned on (`xtask::net_soak::GATE_ROW_ENABLED = true`) by the procedure its module docs, the book page and
docs/06 set: both blockers (`v051-net-input-mtu`, `v051-net-input-rejection`) are merged, and `cargo xtask net-soak
--plan gate --release` on the freeze tree read `61 runs, PASS (0 failed bars are known blockers, 0 are new)`, with
`rate_vs_bottleneck` x1 and `staleness_p99` x15 red but not gating (owned by later lanes). The build machines gate script's own
step is the lead's. (5) Base reds that are mechanical are fixed on the candidate, each with its fail-before line in the
commit: the third-party notices table, two agent-coverage rows, a stale COVERAGE format row, 24 provenance row shapes
and 9 source classes (requirements-only DO27 reads take `regia-design` and adapted DO27 code takes `do27-owner-code;
approval: ADR-8012`, as the log's other rows do), an unsafe inventory row and a `SAFETY` contract, the typed-parameter
ratchet in `net.replay_audit`, and `default-run = "regia"` for `regia_cli` (its second binary made `cargo run -p
regia_cli` ambiguous). Reds that need a design choice are listed for lanes in the freeze report.
Consequences: `cargo xtask adr-index` regenerates `docs/decisions-index.md` after the merges. The freeze report
(`<scratch>`) carries the merge table, the exit-bar table and the checks.
Release fragment `docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v07-freeze.md`.

## ADR-10264: Switch-package review fixes: prescribe `regia cook --clean` for the skylight re-cook, and record that `MATH_BITS_VERSION` 1 already is the `atan2` canonicalization
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: The review of the v0.7 switch package (lane do27-switch-doc-fix) found two defects with committed failing
proofs (branch v07-switch-review, cc628c353). (1) `upgrade-project --write` migrates a v1 `<map>.meshlayers` to v2
preserving the geometry and the input hash (`regia_terrain::upgrade_cooked_mesh_layers`), and
`terrain_mesh_layers::up_to_date` then accepts the migrated file (header at the current version, same input hash,
same chunk importer and grid, chunk LOD files present), so the ordinary `regia cook` the page prescribed returns
`cooked=false` and the widened skylight cuts (ADR-8898, K8) are never applied; `regia_world_geom::cook::input_hash`
has no cook-revision component, so a pre-K8 and a post-K8 cook of unchanged sources hash identically. The positive
control in the review's test (delete the cooked cache dir, cook again) rebuilds the correct cuts. (2) The F-01 row
called the `atan2` canonicalization future work ("would move it before the tag") while `MATH_BITS_VERSION` 1 already
is that canonicalization (ADR-8876, landed): `math::atan2` differs by one ulp from DO27's documented old wrapper
(libm `atan2f` with canonical inputs and output) on finite inputs where libm is not correctly rounded (e.g.
`atan2(8.681013, -8809090.0)`: `0x40490fd6` -> `0x40490fd7`), so an adopter following the row could miss an
already-required sim-pin change.
Decision: Documentation only, as the lane brief requires. `book/user-guide/do27-switch-v07.md` (section (c) row and
closing steps) and the switch note's re-cook row (`book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md`, "What DO27 re-cooks")
now prescribe `regia cook --clean` as the first cook after `regia upgrade-project --write` for maps with filled
skylight mouths, naming the mechanism (the migration keeps the input hash and the chunk LOD files survive; `--clean`
deletes the cooked cache, `CookArgs::clean`, which is what forces the rebuild). The F-01 row and the switch note's
version paragraph state that version 1 is the landed canonicalization, what moves (one-ulp rounding differences
versus DO27's old wrapper; signed-zero and NaN policy versus bare libm) and what DO27 re-records (its checksums,
replays and goldens that call `math::atan2`; `MATH_BITS_VERSION 1` in the handshake; `atan2_libm` for old-bit
parity), citing the lane's release notes. The review's tests are merged as the proof: the math-status test passes
with this fix; the skylight-cut test still fails and proves a code defect (an up-to-date acceptance that survives a
semantics-changing cook across a migration), which this lane reports and does not fix.
Consequences: DO27's first post-upgrade cook rebuilds the whole cooked cache (slower, correct). The code defect is
open for the lead: candidate fixes are a cook-revision component in `input_hash` or a migrator that invalidates the
chunk section; until one lands, `regia cook --clean` after `upgrade-project --write` is the documented procedure. No
spec, format, API or dependency change; two book pages, this record and one release fragment change.

## ADR-10266: Freeze `.gait.ron` v1 in format batch 2
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: `gait` v1 (gap G7, buildout-anim-gait-format e2fc65919; `deny_unknown_fields` on `GaitPatternSpec` from
anim-locomotion-review-fixes) was on the line as a new format of the v0.7 window. The owner approved it for v0.7
format batch 2 (11-19, freeze Sat 11-28; procedure ADR-7724). After the freeze, a shape change needs a v2 step, a
migrator and a test against the old-bytes corpus, so the corpus must hold every shape v1 can take. The corpus had one
file, `gait/v1.ron`: a six-leg `Tripod` with no pattern switching, no `Explicit` pattern, no posture and every leg
overriding its hip offset. Eight of the nine `GaitPatternSpec` variants, the posture block and one side of most
optional fields had no frozen bytes, so a future migrator could break them and no corpus test would notice.
Decision: v1 is frozen as it is: no field, variant or code changes, so `GAIT_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 1, the
fingerprint (and the `format-hashes.ron` row, hash `928384ee…`) does not move, and the migrator registry stays empty.
The freeze adds evidence only. (1) Three corpus files beside the unchanged `gait/v1.ron` (the ADR-7724 rule for a
second file of one version): `v1-hexapod-switching.ron` (`Wave`, `Ripple`, `Explicit`, `Tripod` with switch speeds
and hysteresis, a posture with a height slew limit, legs that mix hip offset and reach overrides with none),
`v1-quadruped.ron` (`QuadrupedWalk`, `Pace`, `Trot`, `Bound`, a posture without a slew limit, no reach limit, ground
band or body joint) and `v1-biped.ron` (`BipedWalk` with only the required fields), listed in `gait/index.ron` and
`FROZEN.txt`. (2) `regia_animation --test gait_v1_freeze`: every variant and both sides of every optional field are in
some corpus file (an exhaustive `match` with no wildcard, so a new variant does not compile until a corpus file covers
it), two, four and six legs are present, every nested block (root, `speeds`, `settle`, `turn`, `foothold`, `posture`, a
leg, `Explicit`) refuses an unknown field with `gait_parse` naming it, every corpus file is refused at versions 0, 2
