and `u32::MAX` by both the loader and `migrate_gait_ron` (`gait_version`), and the v1 migration is the identity
(twice equals once). (3) `regia_cli --test format_corpus_upgrade`
`upgrade_project_leaves_gait_v1_files_and_skips_a_newer_one`: every gait corpus file placed as `.gait.ron` is listed
as `gait` v1 `current`, a v2 file as `newer`, and `--write` run twice changes no byte and writes no backup.
The fingerprint (`gait_schema_fingerprint`) already lists every nested struct and the `GaitPatternSpec` variant names
and payload shapes (`8:{offsets,duty}`); it hashes names, not field types, as every format's fingerprint does, so a
type change is caught by the corpus files failing to load, which is why every shape needs a file.
Consequences: a gait v2 starts from a corpus that reaches every v1 shape. The `anim.gait` fuzz target, the
`check-formats` and `upgrade-project` rows and the `anim.gait_validate` agent method are unchanged. Spec 12 § 4a
(both `gait` rows), `docs/formats/gait-ron.md` and `book/agents/procedural-gait.md` say v1 is frozen. No API,
reflection, schema, golden or dependency change. For the batch freeze lane (v07-fmt-batch2-freeze): the `gait` row
needs no `check-formats --update` (version and hash unchanged).

## ADR-8798: Headless agent writers and reads use the one project root
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The write-path confinement review (lane sprint-agent-write-path-confinement-review, proof tests in
`crates/regia_agent/tests/write_path_confinement.rs`) found that with `AgentSettings::project_dir` set and no
`AssetServer` (a headless host), four default-allowed methods wrote a project-relative path under the process
working directory instead of the project: `ai.bt_edit`, `ai.statetree_edit`, `anim.montage_slot_edit` (and
`anim.montage_edit`, same root) and `audio.loopgen_render` (`out_dir`; `audio.render_check` and
`seeing.dump_resource` share that helper). `level.export_bake` used the asset server, else `current_dir()`, and
the project reads of `logic.*`, `statetree.*` (and state-tree includes), `vfx` system assets, `fuzz.run`
fixtures and the loopgen `path` read from `.`. Each had its own `project_root` with a `PathBuf::from(".")` or
`current_dir()` fallback that skipped `AgentSettings`, against ADR-7871 (the working directory is the project
root only when neither root is set). Two checks also let a path through: `state_tree::resolve_file` passed when
the parent could not be canonicalized, and `bake_export::agent_target` walked with `Path::exists` (false for a
dangling symlink) and passed when either side failed to canonicalize; `ai_bt::confine` passed when the root
did not canonicalize.
Decision: Every one of those sites resolves through `req_path::project_root` (asset server, then
`AgentSettings::project_dir`, then the working directory only when neither is set); the local copies are gone,
so there is never a second root. The write checks use `regia_core::project_path`: `state_tree::resolve_file`
calls `resolve_write`, `ai_bt::confine` and `bake_export::agent_target` call `check_under_root` (the deepest
existing ancestor, a dangling symlink counted as existing, must resolve under the canonical root; a root that
cannot be resolved is refused). `loopgen_render`'s `out_dir` and the read helpers call `req_path::allowed_path`
and `req_path::project_file`. Error codes are unchanged (`bad_path`, `export_path_invalid`,
`path_outside_project`, not-found).
Consequences: The review's six proofs pass, plus two new ones (reads, and the state-tree and slot-table symlink
cases) and unit tests in `bake_export` and `state_tree`. Host-visible: a headless host that sets `project_dir`
now gets these files under it (a relative `loopgen_render` `out_dir` reply names the project path, not `./...`);
a project-relative `ai.statetree_edit` path with `\\` separators lands in sub-folders on Unix as it already did
for `ai.bt_edit` (ADR-5597); an `ai.bt_edit`/`ai.statetree_edit` write under a project root that does not exist
is refused (`bad_path`) instead of attempted. `book/agents/safety.md` (Request paths) names the rule. No format,
dependency, permission-class or error-code change. Methods that refuse without an asset server (`lightmaps`,
`profiler`, `terrain`, `terrain_source`, `terrain_heights`) are unchanged.

## ADR-8888: Notices name every bundled third-party asset; the editor theme's fonts merge over the host's (amends ADR-8589)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: A host of the engine crates reported two problems after building on v0.6.0. (A) `regia_editor` compiles in three
SIL OFL 1.1 fonts (JetBrains Mono, Space Mono, Geist; ADR-8585), but the font paragraph of `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (and
its CLI copy, which `regia package` ships) did not name them, and gave no copyright line or licence text for them or for
the runtime UI's Inter and Noto subsets, which are `include_bytes!` into every binary: "the licence texts ship next to
the font files" is true only in the repository. `docs/asset-licences.toml` recorded each file's licence, but nothing tied
a shipping third-party file to an entry in the notices, so the gap could not fail a check. (B) Since ADR-8589 the
theme's first `theme::apply` installs the editor's font table built from egui's defaults, even when the theme sets no
fonts, so a host that had installed its own fonts first lost them (its `light` family vanished, and egui panics when a
widget asks for a family the live table lacks).
Decision: (A) `docs/asset-licences.toml` gets `[[notice]]` rows (name, licence, files, and either `licence_file`, the
licence text beside the files, or `ported`, a `docs/ported-sources.toml` project). `cargo xtask notices` writes them as a
"Bundled fonts and assets" section: each entry with the `Copyright` lines read from its licence file's header (never
typed by hand), its files, and the full SIL OFL 1.1 text once (`xtask/src/notices/ofl-1.1.txt`, the text of the licence
files beside the fonts). `notices --check` (and the write) fails when a tracked file whose asset row is `third_party`
and `ships = true` is covered by no `[[notice]]`, when a row's glob matches nothing, its licence file is missing, has no
`Copyright` line or (for OFL-1.1) lacks the OFL text, or it names an unknown ported source. Rows cover the editor's three
fonts, the manual's two woff2 subsets, Inter (including the product viewer sample's copy), the seven Noto subsets and the
SMAA lookup tables (via the Bevy SMAA ported-source entry). The demo's notices
(`docs/demo/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES-demo.md`, `cargo xtask demo-notices`) carry the same section, trimmed to the files
inside the demo's crates (the runtime UI's fonts and the SMAA tables; not the editor's or the manual's), and
`demo-notices` fails on the same problems. (B) Merge, not opt-out: the
theme builds its table with `theme::font_definitions_over(base, fonts)`, which keeps every face and family of `base`,
appends the ADR-8589 fallbacks, puts each theme face first in the family it sets (the family's own chain stays behind
it), replaces only the two families the theme defines itself (`display`, `prose`), and first drops faces a previous theme
installed (keys starting `theme:`). The base is the table the host gave `theme::set_host_fonts` (new; it installs that
table at once when no theme is applied yet, or reinstalls the merged table when one is); otherwise, once a pass has run,
the table the context draws with; otherwise egui's default table (the v0.6.0 result). The live table cannot be read
before egui's first pass (egui panics, and the shipping profile aborts on panic), and a `set_fonts` issued in the same
pass is not visible yet, so a host that installs fonts at start-up calls `set_host_fonts` instead of
`egui::Context::set_fonts`. An opt-out flag was the other option; it would leave such a host without the editor's glyph
fallbacks and the brand faces, and still lose its fonts by default, so the merge is the smaller behavior change: hosts
that install no fonts get exactly the v0.6.0 table (`font_definitions(fonts)` is the merge over egui's defaults).
Consequences: (Numbering: this lane wrote it as ADR-8862, a number v0.6.0 already uses for `stream_not_cooked`; integ-v061b renumbered it to ADR-8888 on merge, in every reference.) `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `crates/regia_cli/assets/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` gain the section (the
generator changed, so the resolve seal was refreshed by `cargo xtask notices`). A new shipping third-party asset now
needs a `[[notice]]` row as well as its `[[asset]]` row. `xtask::notices::render_crates` takes the resolved notices
(`&[ResolvedNotice]`) before the seal inputs. New editor API: `theme::set_host_fonts`, `theme::font_definitions_over`.
Tests: xtask `a_bundled_font_without_a_notice_fails_the_check` (fixture font), `notice_rows_must_be_complete`,
`bundled_assets_render_with_the_ofl_text_once`, `the_repository_notices_name_every_bundled_font`,
`demo_notices_list_only_the_fonts_its_crates_compile_in`; editor
`theme_fonts_merge_over_the_host_table` and, in `tests/theme.rs`, `host_fonts_registered_before_the_theme_survive_it`
and `fonts_a_host_set_in_an_earlier_pass_survive_the_theme`. No format, dependency or agent-protocol change.

## ADR-8883: v0.6.1 net fixes: a held slot is spent at confirmation, the host queue needs a majority of blocks, non-payload records run the stall clock, a verified-then-refused Hello counts
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: three reviews of the v0.6.1 net fixes left four red proofs (net-soak-followups-review 55aacc65d,
net-review-fixes-verification 2b3fab2ac, security-gaps-fixes-verification 3d831ae77):
- A. A goodbye hold (ADR-8733 (1)) was spent inside `admit` as soon as any join presented its ticket, before that client
  confirmed, and from any address block. A lost accept then left the client with a spent ticket: its retry was a fresh
  join that a full block refused `full`. A join from another block spent the hold of a player still away.
- B. `cc::host_queue_ms` (ADR-8733 (2)) read four delivering witnesses as the host's uplink and returned the upper
  median: four of eight peers on slow downlinks (one machine can be four connections, `max_peers_per_ip` 8) set the
  host signal and cut the shared rate of the four peers that saw no queue (spec 120 § 1.1).
- An authenticated `Join`, `Accept` or `Deny` touched liveness but never entered `Connection::receive`, so a drip of
  them held a reassembly gap past the § 5.2 ceiling (`Join` is not scored, so the malformed leak never removed it).
- A hub Hello whose player proof verified and whose session was then refused (bad or taken handle, key in use, session
  cap) was not counted toward `PROOF_FAILURE_LIMIT` (ADR-8734): one link kept the hub doing four X25519 per Hello.
The v0.6 wire stays as it is. The ADR-8733 (3) amendment (the v0.7 one-round-trip resume) is written elsewhere and is
not part of this ADR.
Decision:
- A. A held-slot return from the hold's own block *claims* the hold (`AddressHolds::claim`): a claimed hold is neither
  counted (`held_in_block`) nor found again, the new peer stands for the slot. The presented ticket goes on the new
  peer's unconfirmed chain (`UnconfirmedTokens::after_resume`), so a retry with it after a lost accept is that peer
  (a takeover, or a resume once it timed out into dormancy, whose `Dormant` row already keeps the chain). The hold is
  spent, and `held_slot_returns` counted, at the peer's first authenticated payload, beside the ADR-8535
  `retry_tickets.confirm`. A claimant that leaves any way but dormancy, or whose dormancy ends, spends its claim
  uncounted (the slot it stood for is free again). A ticket from another block is a fresh join for that block and
  leaves the hold alone (and counts in `resumes_refused`).
- B. `host_queue_ms` returns 0 unless at least `UPLINK_SHARED_QUEUE_PEERS` delivering witnesses *and* a strict majority
  of the samples see a queue over 25 ms; the median is still index `len / 2`. With a strict majority both medians lie
  among the witnesses' samples, so the review's lower median would only move F5's calibrated reading (ADR-8733) and the
  existing `the_host_queue_needs_enough_delivering_peers` values; the gate is what closes the hole. New
  `host_queue_ms_by_block` / `SharedUplink::update_by_block` fold the peers of one address block (`AddrBlock`) into one
  sample first (delivery summed, queue the largest among the block's delivering peers); the server's `share_uplink`
  uses them. Peers behind a configured relay address (and any without an address) are each their own block, named
  inside the reserved 100::/8, so relayed play keeps its witnesses. Both layers are needed: blocks alone still let four
  distinct slow players of eight set the signal, the majority alone still lets one machine be five of eight.
- The server counts an authenticated non-payload record (`Join`, `Accept`, `Deny`) from an attributed source toward a
  stalled reassembly before handling it: `Connection::note_authenticated_record` stores the arrival, counts the gap at
  most one RTO, withholds the loss stretch (as ADR-8764's unparseable path) and fails the link with
  `reassembly_stalled` past the deadline; the server then drops the peer the way `deliver` does (`Rejected` event,
  `ProtocolError`). `session.touch` stays first (§ 10.3). An honest client sends none of these while a fragment of its
  own waits (it resends `Join` only before it has an accept), so nothing honest changes; a late duplicate `Join`
  during a stall only withholds that stall's loss stretch. The unknown-kind record (scored, untouched) is unchanged.
- The hub counts a refused keyed Hello (proof present) toward `PROOF_FAILURE_LIMIT` on the shared refusal arm, through
  one helper with the verify-fail path (no double count: that path returns before). The limit stays 4, a success still
  clears the count, so three refused handles and a good fourth still connect. Keyless Hellos (no proof, no key work)
  are not counted, as before.
Consequences: no wire, format or agent-method change. Public additions: `cc::host_queue_ms_by_block`,
`SharedUplink::update_by_block`. `host_queue_ms` reads 0 for an even split it used to read high. `held_slot_returns`
now counts at confirmation, not admission. Specs updated: `docs/specs/120-net-next-generation.md` § 4.2 (host signal),
§ 5.2 (non-payload records), § 10.3 (claimed holds); book pages net-link, net-trust, net-lobby-hub. Tests:
`address_hold_replay` (the review's three plus `a_held_slot_return_that_times_out_is_resumed_by_its_ticket`),
`address_hold::a_claimed_hold_is_not_counted_or_found_again`, `cc::half_the_peers_on_slow_downlinks_do_not_cut_the_shared_uplink`,
`cc::one_machines_connections_are_one_witness_of_the_host_queue`,
`server::an_authenticated_join_drip_cannot_hold_a_reassembly_gap_past_the_ceiling`,
`hub::host::a_verified_proof_with_a_refused_hello_is_still_checked_without_bound`.

## ADR-10066: Atomic-write temps are created fresh, never written through a link; notices bullet each font's own copyright record
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: two v0.6.1 candidate reviews. (1) The ADR-8798 project-root fix checked the destination of every agent
write, but the writers filled their temp sibling with `std::fs::write`, which follows a symbolic link. A project that
already holds a link at the predictable temp name (`ai/guard.bt.ron.new`, `.hero.slots.ron.<pid>.tmp`,
`.yard.bake.ron.<pid>.tmp`; a cloned repository is enough) received the bytes at the link's target outside the
project, and the call reported success (proofs `planted_temp_symlinks_are_not_write_targets`,
`bake_export::tests::replace_file_does_not_follow_a_planted_temp_symlink`). `audio.loopgen_render` had closed the same
hole in ADR-3206. (2) The notices copied the copyright header of each font's sidecar licence file, and several
sidecars named other years or wording than the font files that ship (Geist 2026 against the font's 2024, Inter 2020
against 2016, Noto Color Emoji 2021 against 2022, Noto Sans Hebrew 2022 against 2024, the editor Space Mono file had
four notices on one line, Noto Sans KR/SC use `(c)`). OFL 1.1 requires the font's copyright notice with each copy
(proof `bundled_font_copyrights_match_the_font_name_table`). The same review found ADR-8862 used twice; integ-v061b had
already renumbered the fonts decision to ADR-8888 in every reference, so this lane changes no number (renumbering a
second time would only move the v0.6.1 note's citations).
Decision: (1) One helper, `regia_agent::req_path::write_new_temp`, creates every atomic-write temp of the agent
crate: it unlinks whatever is at the temp name (a link itself, never its target; a directory there is an error) and
opens the temp with `create_new`, which refuses an entry planted again in between. Used by `ai_bt`, `state_tree`,
`anim_montage_edit` (`write_atomic`, `commit_all`, and the rollback restore, which now writes a fresh temp, puts the
original permissions on it and renames it over the file instead of writing through the path), `bake_export`
`replace_file` (so `write_atomic` and `level.export_bake`), and the same pattern in `fluid` (`.fluidcache`),
`curve_tables`, `tables`, `plugins` (`Regia.toml`), `trace` screenshots and the perf-gate baseline. The destination
checks (`resolve_write`, `check_under_root`) are unchanged; a link at the destination that resolves inside the project
is replaced by the rename, as before. The montage `inside` check now also refuses a dangling symlink at the file
itself (`bad_path`), as `book/agents/safety.md` already said of every ADR-8798 writer (review nit). (2) `cargo xtask notices` reads each covered `.ttf`/`.otf` file's own copyright
record (name ID 0 of the OpenType `name` table, the Windows Unicode record preferred) and bullets it first, then the
licence file's other copyright lines; `notices --check` (and `demo-notices`) fail when a font's record is not a
copyright line of the notice's licence file, so the sidecar that ships beside the font stays true. A licence-file
header line starting with `(c)` or `©` now counts as a copyright line. The eight sidecars were corrected to their
fonts' records; WOFF2 files (book fonts, Brotli) are not read and keep their licence file's lines.
Consequences: no wire, format, agent-method, error-code or CLI change. A stale regular file at a temp name is
replaced instead of overwritten in place (same result). Notices bullets change wording for Geist, Inter, Noto Color
Emoji, Noto Sans Hebrew, KR, SC and Space Mono; the notices files and the CLI mirror are regenerated. Book pages
`book/agents/safety.md` (temp files) and `book/user-guide/sbom.md` (copyright source) updated. Tests:
`req_path::tests::write_new_temp_never_writes_through_a_planted_link`,
`anim_montage_edit::tests::commit_all_and_write_atomic_never_write_through_a_planted_temp_link`,
`anim_montage_edit::tests::slot_edit_refuses_a_dangling_symlink_at_the_table`,
`notices::tests::a_font_copyright_record_missing_from_its_licence_file_fails_the_check`, and the review's proofs above.

## ADR-10225: Regia Engine is MPL-2.0; templates MIT-0/CC0; docs CC-BY-4.0; a CLA; a default engine credit
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed (the owner's decision of 2026-11-20 ~21:0x, final; ships in v0.6.1); supersedes ADR-006 and ADR-007 (in part: its royalty terms)
Context: The owner decided ("set in stone", 2026-11-20) to replace the proprietary royalty licence (`LICENSE.md`
v1.x, ADR-006, ADR-007's 3 % royalty) with an open-source licence, and to ship the change in v0.6.1 ("that license
change needs to happen now with v0.6.1"). The same licence will apply to the sister projects (outside this
repository). The public repository will be a fresh snapshot, never this history. The licensor's legal name is not
decided.
Decision:
1. **Engine code: Mozilla Public License 2.0.** `LICENSE` holds the verbatim MPL-2.0 text (copied from a registry
   crate that ships it, compared byte for byte with a second registry copy); `LICENSE.md` is gone. The workspace
   declares `license = "MPL-2.0"` (no `license-file`); every engine crate inherits it. `deny.toml` now checks the
   workspace's own crates too (`[licenses.private] ignore = false`), so a crate without an allowed licence fails.
2. **Why MPL.** It is file-level copyleft (MPL § 1.10, § 3.3): a game's own files, a studio's tools and a private
   console-platform module written as separate files stay closed under any terms, even linked into one executable
   (a "Larger Work"). A change to one of Regia's own files stays under the MPL and its source must be made available
   when shipped (§ 3.1, § 3.2), so improvements in forks can be merged back. With the CLA (item 5) the licensor
   can relicense future versions or sell editions (a supported or console edition) without asking each contributor.
   The MPL is compatible with the permissive dependency set (03 § 4); Regia's files are not marked "Incompatible
   With Secondary Licenses".
3. **What the MPL asks of a game developer.** Nothing for their own files. Shipping an executable that contains
   Regia means telling recipients where Regia's source is (MPL § 3.2(a)); the executable may be under the game's own
   terms (§ 3.2(b)). `regia package` writes this for them: `REGIA-ENGINE-NOTICE.txt` (the MPL notice, the engine
   version and the source-location line; the URL is `[package] engine_source_url` in `Regia.toml`, else the
   engine's setting, today the placeholder `<release host>`; a shipping package warns while the placeholder is in
   use) and `REGIA-ENGINE-LICENSE.txt` (the MPL text), in every Linux, Windows, Android and server package.
4. **Credit default.** `regia package` appends "Made with Regia Engine" to the package's `CREDITS.txt` by default.
   It is not a licence condition: `--no-engine-credit` or `[package] engine_credit = false` removes it.
5. **Contributions: a CLA.** Contributors keep their copyright and grant the licensor a licence that includes the
   right to relicense; signed once through a GitHub CLA bot (`CLA.md` individual and entity forms,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md`). The licensor is written `<licensor legal name>` until the owner sets it, and
   `.github/workflows/cla.yml` stays disabled (manual trigger only, a guard step that fails) until then.
6. **Templates, samples and starter content:** code **MIT-0**, assets **CC0-1.0** (texts beside
   `crates/regia_templates/templates/` and `samples/`; sample crates declare `license = "MIT-0"`). The earlier
   `LicenseRef-Regia-Starter` pack licence is withdrawn. **Docs and the book: CC-BY-4.0** (`book/LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0.txt`).
7. **SPDX lines.** Every first-party `.rs` and `.wgsl` file under `crates/`, `xtask/`, `extensions/`, `fuzz/`,
   `examples/` starts with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0`; under `samples/` and the templates `MIT-0`; a file
   listed under `files_to` in `docs/ported-sources.toml` carries its upstream id and keeps its attribution header.
   `vendor/` and test inputs under `tests/**/fixtures/` are out of scope. `cargo xtask spdx --check` (preflight, CI,
   the conventions gate list) enforces it; `--write` fixes it. The template `windows_build.rs` gained the line, so
   its pinned hash moved (the old one joins `EARLIER_WINDOWS_BUILD_SCRIPTS`; `regia upgrade-project` updates
   untouched copies).
8. **Trademarks.** The licence grants no trademark rights (MPL § 2.3). `TRADEMARKS.md`: "Made with Regia Engine"
   credits and redistribution of unmodified releases may use the name and logo; a modified distribution shipped
   as a product must use another name; no use may suggest endorsement.
9. **No acceptance step, no royalty.** Nothing in the product asks anyone to accept a licence, reports revenue or
   names licensees. The old licensor name is removed from the current tree (history keeps it until the planned
   purge); no business name is written anywhere.
Consequences: Updated: `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLA.md`, `TRADEMARKS.md`, `.github/workflows/cla.yml`,
`docs/07-licensing.md`, `docs/03-workspace-and-dependencies.md` § licences, `docs/00-vision.md`, specs 19, 21, 57, 61,
94, the book (new `user-guide/licensing.md`; install, packaging, test bundles, demo legal, distribution pages), the
editor About box (MPL-2.0 and a link), `regia package` (notice, licence text, credit), `cargo xtask dist` and the demo
package (ship `licenses/LICENSE`), the notices/SBOM headers, `deny.toml`. Open for the owner: the licensor's legal name
(CLA, trademark owner, copyright lines) and the public release host (`<release host>`). Counsel reviews the CLA and
trademark texts before the public release.

## ADR-10230: The v0.6.1 AI readme: the onboarding overlay without `regia setup`, skills outside `.claude/`
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: The owner asked for an AI readme for the public Regia-Engine repository (github.com/Regia-Engine/Regia-Engine)
in v0.6.1. The v0.8 onboarding work (ADR-10128, ADR-10135, spec 125) wrote the user `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`README.md`, four Claude Code skills, an MCP template and the `llms-txt` / `onboarding-lint` xtasks, but they drive the
v0.8 `regia setup` and `regia licence` commands, which v0.6.1 does not have, and the lint reads spec 125, which is
v0.8-only. v0.6.1 is also the first MPL-2.0 release: there is no licence to accept. Writing the skills under
`dist/public-root/.claude/skills/` also makes every assistant session opened on this repository load the user-facing
setup skills as its own.
Decision: (1) The v0.6.1 overlay keeps the three working modes, the labeled questions and consents, and the rules (no
acceptance on the user's behalf, no administrator command, downloads named with their size first, nothing leaves the
machine), but its bootstrap is the hand install of `book/start/install.md` run by the assistant: prerequisites (the
user's administrator commands), `rustup-init` checked against its `.sha256`, a git clone or the release archive,
`rustup toolchain install`, `cargo build --release -p regia_cli -p regia_editor`, `regia doctor --json`, `regia new`,
`regia run`, `regia editor`, and for modes 2 and 3 a project `.mcp.json` entry for `regia mcp --project DIR`. Six
questions (`machine`, `install_from`, `targets`, `mode`, `client`, `template`, `project`; no `licence`); consent steps
`rust_toolchain`, `engine_source`, `build_tools`, `shell_path`, `android_tools`, `cross_tools`, `warm_build`, `connect`.
(2) `cargo xtask onboarding-lint` reads `xtask/onboarding/contract.md`, a short contract numbered like spec 125's
sections, in place of the spec; the pending-commands list is empty, so naming a command v0.6.1 lacks fails. (3) The
skills' sources move to `dist/public-skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; the export writes them to `.claude/skills/<name>/` in the
snapshot, and the lint fails on a `.claude/` folder in the overlay (`skill_in_overlay`) and resolves skill links from
the published folder. (4) `.gitignore` re-includes `dist/public-skills/` and the snapshot's root `dist/mcp/`.
Consequences: the AI readme matches what v0.6.1 ships and the lint keeps it honest against the CLI. When the v0.8 line
merges, spec 125 and its Appendix A replace the contract (point `onboarding_lint::SPEC` back at the spec, restore the
pending list), and the v0.8 skills must move to `dist/public-skills/` too. Specs updated: none (spec 125 stays v0.8).
The export (ADR-10229) must map `dist/public-root/*` to the root and `dist/public-skills/*` to `.claude/skills/*`, check
the marker `<!-- regia:user-agents-md -->`, and leave out `dist/public-root/`, `dist/public-skills/` and
`xtask/onboarding/forbidden-terms.txt`.

## ADR-10229: The public repository is a checked single-commit export (`cargo xtask public-export`)
Date: 2026-11-20   Status: proposed
Context: v0.6.1 is published to a new public repository as a fresh single-commit snapshot of the gated tree, never
this repository's history (owner 2026-11-20). The private tree carries material that must not ship: the builder
manual and assistant state, farm bookkeeping and scripts, lab evidence logs, runbooks and plans that name build hosts
and paths, lane release fragments, and the deny list. Spec 125 § 11 asks for a manifest, an overlay of user-facing
root files and a `--check` that fails on forbidden terms; spec 125 is not merged yet, so this ADR records the first
cut.
Decision: `cargo xtask public-export --rev REV --out DIR` reads the revision's tracked files from git (`ls-tree` and
`cat-file --batch`, never the working tree), drops the `exclude` globs of the reviewed manifest
`xtask/public-export.toml`, applies its `scrub` rewrites (whole text files; Rust and WGSL only inside `//` comment
lines, so code and test data never change), removes workflow jobs that run on self-hosted runners (a workflow left
with no job is dropped), and copies the overlays in order, a later one replacing an earlier one's file: this lane's
minimal `xtask/public-export/root/` (a user-facing `AGENTS.md` with the marker line `<!-- regia:user-agents-md -->`,
`CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`), then the AI readme lane's `dist/public-root/` (ADR-10230) and its skills
`dist/public-skills/` into `.claude/skills/` where that lane has landed. `--check DIR` fails on any manifest
`rule` hit (private IPs, host names, home and build paths, email addresses outside the reserved example domains, the
private repository slugs, agent account names, farm and model talk in the book and root docs, other engines' names
outside the cleanroom policy, secret patterns), any `hashed` term (names that must never be printed: the old
licensor name, stored as BLAKE3 digests of their lowercase words and reported by label only; `--hash-term` prints an
entry), files over 50 MB, missing licence files, a root `AGENTS.md` without the marker, a broken link in the root
entry files, and an `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` target the export dropped. Every hit prints as `file:line [rule]
detail`. The manifest names private hosts, so it is excluded from the export itself. Spec 125 § 11's
`dist/public-export.toml` path and `llms.txt` regeneration follow when spec 125 lands; the manifest moves then.
Consequences: a release is exported and checked by one command before the lead pushes it; leaks are fixed in the
manifest (exclude or scrub) unless they are real leaks in shipped text. Tests that read excluded internal files
(lab evidence, lane fragments, runbooks) cannot pass in the export; the export's CI is the hosted-runner jobs.

## ADR-10254: v0.6.1 release: the licensor, the public source URL and the CLA bot switch
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10225 (MPL-2.0) left two placeholders for the owner: the licensor's legal name (`<licensor legal
name>`, in CLA.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, TRADEMARKS.md, the MIT-0 copyright lines and docs/07) and the public release host
(`<release host>`, the default source location in every package notice and bundle README). Its CLA workflow stayed
off by failing while CLA.md held the name placeholder, so filling the name would have armed the bot. The owner decided
both on 2026-11-20 and wants the bot off until the company's registration is confirmed. The export lane's manifest
(ADR-10229) expected the public repository at `Regia-Engine/regia`; the owner named it `Regia-Engine/Regia-Engine`.
Decision:
1. Licensor: **Sphenisca Regia LLC** in CLA.md (both forms), CONTRIBUTING.md, TRADEMARKS.md, the template and sample
   `LICENSE-MIT-0.txt` copyright lines, docs/07, the book Licensing page and the starter-content review. The demo EULA
   draft (written for the earlier proprietary licence) and the ADR-006 open-question row are marked superseded by
   MPL-2.0, not filled.
2. Public source URL: **https://github.com/Regia-Engine/Regia-Engine** is `regia_cli`
   `package_legal::ENGINE_SOURCE_URL` and `xtask` `dist::ENGINE_SOURCE_URL` (package notices, test bundle READMEs, demo
   CREDITS.txt). `SOURCE_PLACEHOLDER` (`<release host>`) stays as the "not set" value: a project whose `Regia.toml`
   still names it gets the shipping-package warning, and its test stays. Tests that asserted the placeholder in the
   default notice now assert the real URL (an intended output change).
3. CLA bot: `.github/workflows/cla.yml` runs its job only when the repository variable `CLA_ENABLED` is exactly
   `true` (job-level `if:`); the placeholder grep is gone and the triggers are declared. The owner sets the variable
   after the LLC is registered and counsel has read CLA.md (docs/07 § 4 "CLA bot switch"). A test
   (`workflow_yaml::the_cla_bot_runs_only_behind_its_switch`) keeps every job of the file behind the switch.
4. Public export manifest: the `public_url` rule flags links to `Regia-Engine/regia`, `regia-dev` and
   `regia-engine-dev`; `private_repo` also covers `regia-engine-dev` and the working repository's old personal path.
Consequences: package notices name a real location, so a default shipping package no longer warns. Turning the bot on
is one repository setting plus the signatures branch and token. Specs updated: 21 (engine licence notice), docs/07,
book Licensing; release notes v0.6.1.

## ADR-10281: v0.6.1 gate fixes: spliced shader snippets drop the SPDX line; the hot fixture journal knows its file
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.6.1 gate (lavapipe stage) failed on two binaries, both side effects of the SPDX first lines
(ADR-10225). (1) `regia_render::cloud_shadow_wgsl()` and `surface_weather_wgsl()` dropped the first line of their
library module to remove `#define_import_path`; with the SPDX line first they dropped that instead and kept the import
line, so `terrain.wgsl`, which holds both texts verbatim, no longer contained them
(`terrain_cloud_lookup_matches_the_engine`, `terrain_surface_weather_matches_the_engine`). (2) After the
`regia_editor` hot reload tests, `samples/hot_fixture/src/lib.rs` had no SPDX line
(`spdx::tests::the_repository_has_every_spdx_line`). The hot host never touches line 1: the ADR-8787 guard's journal
lives in `target/hot-reload-m3/`, which outlives the source tree. A gate tree rebuilt from `git archive` over a warm
target that still held a journal from a run killed under the pre-SPDX fixture "restored" that stale text over the new
committed fixture, and the guard's `Drop` wrote it back at the end.
Decision:
1. `shader_lib::library_snippet_body` drops one leading `// SPDX-License-Identifier:` line and then the import line;
   both accessors use it. Composed shaders and `terrain.wgsl` are unchanged; a unit test pins the contract.
2. The journal (`hot-fixture-lib.rs.journal`, format 1) records the fixture file's identity (device, inode, birth time on
   Unix; birth time elsewhere). In-place writes (the host's edits, the guard's restore) keep it; a checkout or an
   archive extraction replaces the file and changes it. A journal whose identity differs is stale: it is moved to
   `hot-fixture-lib.rs.stale` and the current source is the original. A legacy `hot-fixture-lib.rs.pristine` journal
   (no identity) is restored only over a source that is visibly edited (a scripted line missing or added), otherwise
   set aside the same way. The repository SPDX check keeps covering the fixture.
Consequences: a warm target can no longer roll the fixture back to an older tree's text; a killed run in the same tree
is still restored. Two new scratch-file tests cover the stale and legacy journals. No public API or format change.

## ADR-10307: v0.7 freeze fix round b: the v0.6.1 release on the v0.7 line (ADR-8883 on the v0.7 shared uplink and held-slot path)
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: tag v0.6.1 (MPL-2.0 switch ADR-10225, AI readme files ADR-10230, public export ADR-10229, gate fix ADR-10281,
and lane v061-net-fixes-c, ADR-8883) merged onto the v0.7 freeze candidate. ADR-8883 was written against v0.6's
`SharedUplink` and held-slot code, and the v0.7 line had changed both: the shared uplink reads a probe, a loss and a
starved-peer signal and keeps an ungated median floor (ADR-10097, ADR-10081 (5)); the held slot also has the one-round-trip
resume path (wire 6, ADR-8858/ADR-8902), and records carry no `Source` (ADR-8717). ADR-10050's text noted that
net-fixes-c was not on the v0.7 line yet.
Decision:
1. Host queue witnesses: the strict-majority rule of ADR-8883 is part of `host_queue`'s witness flag (at least
   `UPLINK_SHARED_QUEUE_PEERS` delivering peers see a queue *and* they are more than half the peers). The median it
   returns stays ungated, so v0.7's ungated floor still reads every round. `SharedUplink::update_by_block` and
   `host_queue_ms_by_block` fold one sample per address block first (ADR-8883), and the floor reads those samples too.
   `NetServer::share_uplink` passes the blocks (relayed peers each their own block) and keeps v0.7's wire-share ratio.
   The loss (`host_loss`) and starved-peer signals of ADR-10097 still count peers, not blocks: one machine with several
   connections can still add up to those counts (an open item for the net lane, not changed here).
2. Held slots: the take at join (and its `held_slot_returns` count) is replaced by ADR-8883's claim at join and spend at
   the first authenticated payload, on the full handshake and on the resume path's `HeldSlot` join alike; v0.7's
   resume link match is unchanged. The ADR-8883 stall-clock rule (an authenticated `Join`, `Accept` or `Deny` record runs
   a waiting reassembly's stall clock) applies to every such record in `on_peer_record`: plain links only bring
   payloads there.
3. Lobby hub: v0.7's draining and limits gates run first; ADR-8883's rule that a verified proof whose Hello is refused
   still counts toward `PROOF_FAILURE_LIMIT` applies to the refusals of `connect_player` (as in v0.6.1). A refusal by the
   v0.7 limits gate after a verified proof is not counted (open item for the net lane).
4. `regia_nav_det` (a v0.7-only crate) takes `license.workspace` (the workspace's `license-file` is gone, ADR-10225).
Consequences: `regia_net` keeps both lines' tests (the v0.6.1 ADR-8883 unit tests run on the v0.7 uplink with the
peers' loss and starved fields at zero). The base reds this round fixed are listed in the fragment
`docs/releases/v0.1.28-integ-v07-freeze-b.md`. Specs: none changed (spec 120's ADR-8883 notes arrive with the tag).

## ADR-10327: v0.7 resumed freeze: preserve the small-median uplink hold and compile the arena tutorial
Date: 2026-11-21   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.6.1 merge's unconditional strict-majority witness gate in ADR-10307 conflicts with the existing
ADR-10097 hold tests. `a_hold_keeps_the_uplinks_measured_rate` has no held target, and
`a_few_peers_keep_the_cautious_hold_and_never_probe` reads `None` instead of `Some(300000.0)`.
The book checker also compiles the capture-the-flag tutorial without its `arena` dependency.
Decision:
1. Refine ADR-10307's composition: retain the minimum four delivering witnesses. Require a strict majority when
   the median exceeds `QUEUE_DELAY_THRESHOLD_MS`; retain the small-median signal at or below that threshold
   for ADR-10097's cautious hold. Count address blocks before applying the same rule. The ungated median floor,
   loss signal and starved-peer signal are unchanged. Keep every existing assertion of both branches.
2. Add the existing `samples/arena` crate to the generated book-snippet manifest, so the tutorial is checked
   against its real API instead of ignored.
3. Reject the inherited, uncommitted parity-gap allowances. Missing gait load/save agent routes remain red
   until implemented; golden and exit-bar failures remain for the lead and owner.
Consequences: spec 120's shared-uplink gate description records the small-median refinement. This changes no
wire format, dependency version or agent schema. Full net-soak and platform checks are required before release;
the lane report records actual results rather than treating an interrupted runner's shell status as success.

Verification refinement: `gait_rig::reset_survives_a_refused_frame` used a non-finite probe hit to cause a refused
step, but ADR-8721's `GroundProbes::probe` deliberately filters such a hit to a miss before the gait sees it.
The isolated run reports `None` instead of `Step` while the recovered foot offset is already 0.0000 m.
Use a non-finite `GaitVelocity` for the refused frame instead: it reaches `at_rest_driven`'s input refusal after
the restart flag is read. Retain the warmup, required `Step` and sub-millimeter replant assertions, and also
assert that the refused step preserves the entire prior `GaitState`. A negative control that consumes restart
before attempting the step must still fail the repaired regression. No production gait or probe behavior changes.

## ADR-10346: v0.7 freeze round c: mesh-layer cook invalidation and verification
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10264's regression proves that migrating a legacy mesh-layer package and cooking
normally can retain pre-skylight cuts: the format migrator preserves the input hash, and the
input hash has no semantic cook revision. A layout upgrade does not certify that geometry was
recomputed. The freeze also owes deterministic drift attribution, demo notices, N110 measurements,
side-lane integration and complete verification.
Decision: version the existing input-hash domain for the skylight cook semantics, independently
of the frozen file layout. The terrain package migrator invalidates the header's input hash
when upgrading an old file, keeping all canonical geometry and presentation data. Already
upgraded caches with the old input-hash domain also miss the current cook key. The first
ordinary cook rebuilds from source; subsequent unchanged cooks skip and write nothing.
Preserve every acceptance bar. N110 measurements go to the owner. Re-record a deterministic
pin only under the lead's explicit authorization after the test machine merge attribution.
Consequences: no serialized shape, format version, dependency or agent method changes.
The cache identity changes; canonical content hashes change only when source is actually
recooked into different geometry. The `--clean` workaround is no longer needed for this
migration once verified. Detailed before/after evidence is retained in the lane report.

## ADR-10355: ground_vehicle_mix determinism golden attribution after the v0.7 freeze merges
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: the v0.7 freeze inherited `det_golden::engine_scenarios` failing only on
`ground_vehicle_mix` (measured b36d8caad780952e against the committed golden
e88b942047d56a86, first diverging tick 22; tick hash 834cab319b3b211f versus
9a1fe53c04f04125). A first-parent bisection over the freeze merges (good 929175099c,
bad 4f5b913878) on the test machine attributes the move to merge 05c3bfeedb, the merge of
lane v07-det-small-followups (29e1c543c6), whose commit 5d27b9e442 (ADR-10062) made
ground vehicles publish wrapped yaw - an intended simulation change whose own tests
assert yaw stays in (-PI, PI]. That lane did not re-record this golden. The scenario
has no ECS or FixedUpdate schedule, and both bisection sides replay deterministically,
so this is neither the known new-FixedUpdate-system pin movement nor a determinism bug.
Decision: the integration lane does not bless the golden. The measured value, the
attributed merge, the intended change and the deterministic replay evidence are
recorded for the lead, who re-records `crates/regia_detsim/goldens/ground_vehicle_mix.detgold`
(hash.x86_64-linux b36d8caad780952e) only after the cross-target legs agree on that
hash (`cargo xtask det-golden run --legs host,qemu` on a host with qemu-aarch64; the
the test machine has no qemu-user), citing merge 05c3bfeedb, commit 5d27b9e442 and ADR-10062.
Consequences: `engine_scenarios` stays red at the freeze head until the lead's
re-record; every other det scenario passes. No bar, tolerance or golden file is changed
by this lane.

## ADR-10375: Delegated hub sessions, relay-only reach, and an ECS-free join surface (spec 89 NL-07..NL-11)
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: BZ-28 (pinned to v0.6.1, request R23, relayed 2026-11-22) wants players to browse one community hub
and never see an IP, with a listen session or a dedicated server the player owns, and with the relay as a
fallback or as the only path when the host hides its address. The v0.7 freeze already has the hub (NL-04,
ADR-8559), join brokering (NL-05, ADR-8607) and the packaged hub process (NL-06, ADR-8648). Spec 10's
"v0.6 NL-07" is peer logging (ADR-8149), so the lobby rows continue at NL-07 inside spec 89 and do not
reuse that id. `PlayerKey` and `ServerKey` are X25519 (`crypto`). `server_host` is behind the `ecs`
feature because the module imports `regia_app` and `regia_ecs`, which also hides `relay_split`,
`JoinTicket`, `JoinPath`, `JoinSocket` and `RelayRegistrar` even where those files do not use the ECS.
`RelayRegistrar` additionally names `LinkSocket`, an alias in the ecs-only `link` module. `HubReach` is
ecs-only because it calls `JoinPath`. A measured reading of the freeze (spec 89 § 16.1) shows: `server_host`
never opens a hub lobby; `broker_reach` still plans a punch when the only offer is a relay, and `approve`
copies both sides' candidates; members receive `ServerSet` with the session address; `regia-lobby-hub`
does not run `RelayServer`.
Decision: (1) **Binding.** An owner binds a server by a Noise `X` message to the hub's `ServerKey`
(prologue `regia.lobby_hub.server_binding v1`, payload `version || server_key || expiry_ms || serial`),
verified by the hub with the same `snow` path as `verify_player_proof`, including the RFC 7748 low-order
check. No Ed25519 key is added. RFC 8032 is not the construction. Empty proof list = ownerless public
server, which may create its own public lobby (request 1.7, absent today). Up to 8 owners per server.
Revocation is a hub-side set of `(player_key, server_key, serial)`, persisted in `revocations.ron`, and it
refuses that owner's next `CreateDelegated` in the same call. Existing lobbies stay up. (2) **Delegated
lobby.** The bound server, not the owner, sends `ReachOffer` and `Approve`, using capacity, `bans.ron`,
the password gate and `JoinTicketCheck`. The owner keeps kick, close, settings and explicit transfer to
another bound owner. Owner disconnect starts a grace (`grace_ms`, default 600_000, cap 86_400_000, `0` =
indefinite) and does not emit `OwnerChanged` and does not assign the server as owner. Listen lobbies keep
the ADR-8633 hand-off. This amends ADR-8559 and ADR-8633 for delegated lobbies only. (3) **Relay-only.**
A flag on the server, the lobby or one offer. Empty candidates are not the flag: today's `broker_reach`
still returns `Punch`. When the flag is set the path is `Relay` or `NoReach`, both plans carry no
candidates, and the member's ticket is rewritten to an unspecified address so the ticket bytes leak
nothing. `JoinPath::relay_first` and a registrar that does not introduce that member enforce it on the
relay socket. Checked on wire bytes. (4) **Addresses.** Version-2 rooms and directory cards carry no
`SocketAddr`. `ServerSet` becomes `SessionConfirmed { confirmed: bool }`. `regia.server` and any lobby or
member value that parses as an address is `hub_address_in_data`. The only address channel is one member's
plan and that session's plan, and only when relay-only is clear. AskReach adds 4/10 s per key, 16/10 s per
address, 2 in-flight per key, 64 in-flight on the hub, on top of `AdmitGate`'s 30/s and 20/s. A banned
player key (owner, server or hub file) is refused before any candidate is copied. (5) **Admin** stays on
`server_host`'s `admin.token`. The hub does not carry it. Named out in spec 89 § 16.6. (6) **ECS-free.**
Move `relay_split`, `JoinPath`, `JoinSocket`, `JoinTicket` and a generic `RelayRegistrar<S: DatagramSocket>`
into `regia_net::join_exec` (always compiled). `HubReach` follows. `server_host` re-exports the old paths
and stays `ecs`. (7) **Process.** Extend `regia-lobby-hub`; do not add a binary. `hub.toml` format 2 adds
relay port 7812, the AskReach numbers, a ban file and a log dir. v1 migrates with `relay.enabled = false`.
Key rotation is a second process and a client pin list (new, then old), because one Noise handshake holds
one static key. Overlap is an operator window, not a wire field. (8) **Wire.** `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` 2.
Every new count and string is capped before allocation (spec 89 § 16.2). The hub socket drops `RGN1` and
`RGNR`. (9) **This lane is the spec.** No runtime code. Build lanes and the acceptance rows are in the
lane report. `docs/formats/hub-toml.md` is not edited here; the build lane bumps it with the migrator.
Consequences: games can pin a hub and a dedicated `ServerKey` without learning the owner's address, and can
run the join on a socket they own without linking the ECS. Host-visible breaks, landed by the build lanes,
are listed in `docs/releases/v0.1.28-v08-spec-net-delegated-sessions.md` (wire 2, `ServerSet` removed,
`ReachOffer.relay_only`, `hub.toml` v2, new `HubError` codes, `HubReach` available without `ecs`). No new
crate dependency. No golden. Listen-lobby owner hand-off is unchanged. Remote admin is unchanged.

## ADR-10378: Hub wire generation 2 stays compatible with a v0.7.0 client
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: BZ-28 request R23 ships in v0.7.1 as an additive patch on the v0.7 line (spec 89 § 16.2,
NL-07..NL-11, ADR-10375). ADR-10375 (8) and acceptance row 10 say a version-1 peer and a version-2
hub refuse each other at the handshake with `protocol_mismatch`. The lead's patch-compatibility
ruling overrides that: a v0.7.0 client must keep working against a v0.7.1 hub, and a v0.7.1 client
must keep working against a v0.7.0 hub. This lane is encode and decode only. Binding checks, grace
behavior, relay-only planning and the AskReach rate limits are later lanes. `hub.toml` v2 and its
migrator are NL-11.
Decision: (1) `HUB_WIRE_VERSION` is the codec generation and is 2. `HubWire::PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays
`HUB_WIRE_VERSION_V1` (1), so `protocol_id` does not change and the handshake still completes.
`HubWire::GAME_VERSION` is `"2"`, which the version probe reports and which is not part of
`protocol_id`. A client treats game version `"2"` as codec generation 2 and every other text,
including empty and `"2.0"`, as generation 1. (2) A missing tail is the version-1 message. `Offer`,
`AskReach` and the plan's synthetic offer append one byte `1` only when `relay_only` is true. A
trailing `0` stays an error. Directory and room tails, when any extra is non-default, start with
marker `0xA2`. `ServerSet` and `RoomState.server` stay, so a v0.7.0 member still receives the
session address. `SessionConfirmed` is added beside them and carries no address. (3) A version-2-only
request (`RegisterServer`, `RevokeBinding`, `CreateDelegated`, `SetReachMode`, `SetBans`,
`CloseLobby`) from a peer that has not announced generation 2 is `HubError::NeedsWireV2`
(`hub_needs_wire_v2`). The hub replies `Refused` and does not disconnect. `AnnounceWire` with any
byte other than 2 is the same refusal and does not raise the dialect. A v0.7.1 client that has
recorded a v0.7.0 hub (game version other than `"2"`) returns `hub_needs_wire_v2` locally and sends
nothing. (4) The new calls decode and the host arms are exhaustive. Their behavior returns
`HubError::NotReady` (`hub_not_ready`) until the next lane. `plans_for` is the exception: it returns
today's mapped, punch or relay plans and ignores `relay_only`. (5) Caps are checked before any
`Vec::with_capacity` from an untrusted count: 8 owner proofs, each proof a fixed 145-byte array,
game version 32 bytes, 256 server bans, 64 lobby bans. A grace `u32` outside `0` or
`1..=86_400_000` is `WireError::Invalid("hub grace")`. Spec 89 § 16.2 says `RegisterServer` clamps
a larger grace to 24 h. This codec rejects it. The behavior lane clamps only a value the codec
already accepted. `GraceStarted.deadline_ms` is an absolute timestamp and is not range-checked.
(6) The 49-byte binding payload encodes and decodes. `verify_binding` and `verify_server_presence`
return `hub_not_ready` and do not run Noise.
Consequences: v0.7.0 listen lobbies and today's brokering still work against a v0.7.1 hub, and the
reverse. Exhaustive matches on `HubRequest`, `HubEvent` and `HubError` gain arms. Struct literals of
`ReachOffer`, `HubLobbyCard`, `RoomState` and `DirectoryPage` that name every field gain
`relay_only`, the lobby extras, and `servers`. `HubLobbyCard`'s new fields are `#[serde(default)]`.
No `hub.toml` change. No new agent method. `hub_needs_wire_v2` and `hub_not_ready` show up in
`lobby.hub_status`'s `refused` map. The api snapshot for `regia_net` records the break. No new
dependency. No golden. `plans_for` keeps eight arguments, the signature the later lanes call.
`#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on that function records the freeze. Clippy's limit is 7.

## ADR-10384: Delegated hub sessions run on the v0.7.1 hub
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: BZ-28 request R23, spec 89 § 16.3 and § 16.7 (NL-07), on top of ADR-10375 and the wire
codec of ADR-10378. A v0.7.0 client must keep working against a v0.7.1 hub. This lane runs binding
verify, server presence, ownerless create, grace, the server's offer and approve, and revocation.
Relay-only planning (NL-08), AskReach windows (NL-09), the ECS-free move (NL-10) and `hub.toml`
format 2 (NL-11) stay later lanes. `wire.rs` is not edited.
Decision: (1) Binding and presence are Noise pattern `X` (`Noise_X_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s`) in
`regia_net::crypto::binding`. Prologues are `regia.lobby_hub.server_binding v1` and
`regia.lobby_hub.server_presence v1`. The binding payload is the fixed 49 bytes. The low-order
check is the all-zero X25519 output, copied from `verify_player_proof`, and it runs after the
constant-time payload compare (ADR-8734). Crypto failure is `hub_binding_invalid`. Expiry `0` does
not expire. Any other expiry must be at most 366 days ahead (`31_622_400_000` ms) or the proof is
`hub_binding_invalid`. A past expiry is `hub_binding_expired`. More than 8 owner proofs is
`hub_binding_invalid`. (2) `CreateDelegated` needs a proven player, an online server and a live
binding. The lobby kind is dedicated, the stored address is empty, and `regia.server` in that spec
data is `hub_address_in_data`. Listen create still stores the session address and still emits
`ServerSet`. An ownerless register (no proofs) may `create` a public lobby; the displayed owner is
the server handle. A later register that adds owners while an ownerless lobby exists is
`hub_binding_invalid` and changes nothing. (3) The server session is the only caller of
`offer_reach` and `approve` for a delegated lobby. The owner's offer or confirm is
`hub_not_session` or `hub_address_in_data`. The member plan's ticket is the server's `ReachOffer`
ticket, so the joiner's handshake pins that `ServerKey`. The owner's candidates are not copied.
`relay_only` stays ignored (`plans_for` is unchanged). A published ban or `load >= capacity` makes
`approve(true)` send `ReachDenied` and return `Ok(None)`. The password gate, `bans.ron` and
`JoinTicketCheck` stay the game server's job before `Approve`. (4) When the owning player leaves,
a delegated lobby enters grace and does not emit `OwnerChanged`. `grace_ms` of `0` is indefinite
and is not remapped to 600_000. The client API's `None` is 600_000. The same player key reconnects
into the lobby without `OwnerChanged`. Listen hand-off is unchanged. Close, server offline, or a
nonzero grace deadline closes the lobby. The hub does not stop the game process and does not make
the server the owner. (5) `RevokeBinding` inserts `(player key, server key, serial)` before it
returns. The next create is `hub_binding_revoked`. Existing lobbies stay. The cap is 4096
(`hub_revoke_full`). The set is also `revocations.ron` format 1, written by a temp file plus
rename. A missing file is empty. A corrupt file is an error and does not panic. This is not a
frozen content format. (6) A wire-1 directory page drops dedicated lobbies and server cards. A
wire-1 join of a dedicated lobby is `hub_needs_wire_v2` and does not disconnect. `set_reach_mode`
and `set_bans` still return `hub_not_ready`.
Consequences: exhaustive matches on `HubError` gain the § 16.9 variants. `verify_binding` takes
`now_ms`. `HubReport` gains `servers` (`#[serde(default)]`). New public types include
`HubServerCard`, `HubNotice`, `LocalBinding` and `ServerRegister`. `HubServer` and
`HubLobbyBackend` gain register, revoke, create, close and binding methods. `#[doc(hidden)]`
`forge_low_order_binding` and `forge_low_order_presence` are test helpers. No new dependency. No
golden. No `hub.toml` change. `ServerSet` stays for listen lobbies. `lobby.hub_servers` and
`lobby.hub_bindings` are report and client data, not new agent methods. The api snapshot for
`regia_net` records the break.

## ADR-10376: ECS-free hub join on a caller-owned socket
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: BZ-28 runs its own simulation and depends on `regia_net` without the ECS
(ADR-8032, ADR-8501). The hub (`lobby::hub`), join brokering (NL-05, ADR-8607), NAT
checks and the relay already compile that way. The pieces it still had to turn `ecs` on
for were the dedicated-server host's relay helpers (`relay_split`, `RelayRegistrar`,
`JoinTicket`, `JoinPath`, `JoinSocket`) and `HubReach`, which owned the member's game
socket. A game that already owns that socket could not run a member's `JoinPlan` without
linking `regia_ecs`, `regia_app`, `regia_scene`, `regia_asset` and `regia_platform`.
The spec lane v08-spec-net-delegated-sessions is writing NL-06..NL-10 in
`docs/specs/89-lobbies.md`; this lane does not edit that file. The notes below are the
design for the ECS-free path only (request R23 item 4). Delegated sessions, relay-only
hosting, address-scraping limits and the deployable hub binary are other lanes.
Decision:
1. Keep one `server_host` implementation. `join`, `relay_path`, `ExitCode`, `HostError`,
   `HostState`, `HostClock`, `MonotonicClock` and `TestClock` compile with or without
   `ecs`. The ECS runtime (`ServerHost`, `HostGame`, config, crash, health, link admin,
   link game, lockstep game, platform, shared port, signals) moves into a private
   `ecs_host` module that the parent re-exports only with `ecs`. The ECS host calls the
   same helpers; their behavior does not change.
2. Declare `server_host` twice in the crate root, once `#[cfg(feature = "ecs")]` and once
   `#[cfg(not(feature = "ecs"))]`, and re-export `HubReach`, `ReachSocket` and
   `ReachState` the same way. The API snapshot keeps every existing `ecs` signature and
   records the ecs-free signatures as additions. One declaration would drop
   `#[cfg(feature = "ecs")]` from those lines. `mod reach` is no longer cfg-gated; the
   reach code did not use the ECS.
3. `RelayRegistrar::new` keeps the parameter type name `LinkSocket`, so the ecs snapshot
   line does not change. With `ecs` that name is still `crate::link::LinkSocket`. Without
   `ecs`, `server_host::join::LinkSocket` is the same `Box<dyn DatagramSocket + Send>`,
   public so the signature does not name a private type. `link` stays ecs-only.
4. `JoinPlanDriver` runs a member's `JoinPlan` on queues the caller owns. The game binds
   `local`, pushes each received datagram (`push_datagram`), calls `advance(now_ms)` with
   its own clock, and sends what `poll_send` returns. `take_endpoint` returns the same
   socket `HubReach::take_socket` would, on those queues, plus the plan's `ServerKey`.
   After that, push and poll keep feeding both the endpoint and a relay control half that
   is still running. Each direction holds at most `PLAN_QUEUE` (4096) datagrams. A longer
   datagram than `MAX_DATAGRAM_BYTES` is refused whole. A full send queue returns
   `WouldBlock` and counts a drop. Empty datagrams are delivered. The driver adds no wire
   format, no `JoinPlan` field and no error code: `hub_key_mismatch`, `hub_reach_invalid`
   and the existing `JoinError` codes.
5. No new agent method. Without `ecs`, read `NetServer::status` and `peer_rows`. The hub's
   existing methods are unchanged.
Consequences: `cargo test -p regia_net_soak --no-default-features --test ecs_free_join`
runs a `JoinPlan` on `SimNat` and `TestClock` for the mapped, punch and relay paths and
checks the sealed handshake pinned the owner's `ServerKey`. That package depends on
`regia_net` with `default-features = false` and turns `regia_net/ecs` on only through its
own `ecs` feature. A const assert fails the build when `ecs` is off and
`regia_net::ECS_FEATURE` is still set. `cargo test -p regia_net --no-default-features`
does not prove this: that crate's dev-dependencies unify `ecs` (and `voice`) back on.
`cargo tree -p regia_net --no-default-features -e normal,build` must not link
`regia_ecs`, `regia_app`, `regia_scene`, `regia_asset`, `regia_platform`, `regia_audio`
or `bevy_ecs`. ECS callers of `HubReach` and the host helpers keep their tests unchanged.
Snapshot additions are not breaking; no public struct field or enum variant was added.
The forbidden-crate list in `xtask` `NET_CORE_FORBIDDEN` is unchanged.

## ADR-10395: Delegated hub resync and server-link replacement
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: Security review of NL-07 (spec 89 § 16.3, ADR-10384) found three breaks. The review's
tests stay as written. This lane does not pick a new design (no ADR-10393). A parallel lane edits
`lobby/hub/server.rs` for ask limits; these edits stay in `resync`, `owned` and `register_inner`.
Decision: (1) A resync, including the one `take_events` appends after an outbox overflow, sends
pending `ReachAsk` events and a dropped approver plan to the session that approves. That is the
listen owner, or the dedicated server session even when its `lobby` is `None`. The owning player
of a delegated lobby is not that session, so the member's candidates are not replayed to them.
(2) A second link that takes a server key moves the server seat only. On a delegated lobby it
does not write the new member in as `room.owner` and does not rewrite player member ids. The old
link keeps its lobby. When the host disconnects that link, the owning player's drop enters Grace
with no `OwnerChanged`. `grace_ms` 0 holds the lobby, and the same player key reconnects as owner.
The new server session is not the owner: an owner-only call from it is `not_owner`. An ownerless
lobby still moves with the server seat. (3) A listen lobby is not a server seat. Replacing a
server link does not clear that lobby on the old session, so the host's disconnect runs listen
hand-off: a solo lobby is deleted, and a lobby with a guest goes to that guest with `OwnerChanged`.
Consequences: no new public type, field, enum variant, error code or dependency. No `hub.toml`
change. No golden. `not_owner` is now returned where a delegated server session that is not a
lobby member previously received `not_in_lobby` from an owner-only method. The three
`review_` tests in `lobby_hub_delegated` pass. Listen hand-off and the ordinary two-session
delegated path are unchanged.

## ADR-10391: Relay-only hub plans hide both addresses
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: BZ-28 request R23 (NL-08, spec 89 § 16.4) ships in v0.7.1 as an additive patch.
`ReachOffer.relay_only` is already on the wire (ADR-10378) and was ignored.
`broker_reach` returned `Mapped` whenever a mapped candidate existed, and `Punch`
when a relay or any candidate existed. `plans_for` copied each side's candidates
onto the other's plan. `JoinPath::relay_first` skipped the introduction only after
the path was already `Relay`, and an empty candidate list still planned a punch.
The other side's address bytes still traveled. v0.7.0 clients must keep working
against a v0.7.1 hub. This lane does not edit `server.rs` or `wire.rs`.
Decision:
1. `plans_for` hides the exchange when its `relay_only` argument is set, or when
   either offer's `relay_only` is set. The only success path is `ReachKind::Relay`,
   and only when the owner's offer has a relay and a join code. Otherwise
   `BrokerError::NoReach`. Neither plan carries a candidate or a mapped address.
   The member's ticket is rewritten with `JoinTicket::from_game_socket` (unspecified
   address, port 0, the same server key). The relay address and the join code stay.
   The owner's ticket stays empty. A listen lobby with every flag clear keeps today's
   order: mapped, then punch, then relay.
2. `broker_reach` honors `owner.relay_only` without a signature change. A mapped
   candidate does not win. The member's flag and the lobby argument are applied in
   `plans_for`, because `broker_reach` does not take them.
3. `JoinPath::relay_first` is the member path (`HubReach` already calls it for
   `ReachKind::Relay`). It gathers and sends no local candidates, sends no
   `PunchIntro`, and does not start or answer connectivity checks.
4. `RelayRegistrar::relay_only` is called before the first `update`. It rewrites
   the token the same way, sends `Register` with no candidates, ignores an
   introduction, and does not answer or send connectivity checks. It still renews
   the join code and confirms allocations. `from_game_socket` alone is not
   relay-only: that ticket is the normal punch-capable host path.
   `server_host` does not call `relay_only` yet.
5. `set_reach_mode` and `set_bans` still return `hub_not_ready`. `approve` still
   passes the lobby flag as `false`, so a room's stored `relay_only` does not apply
   until that call passes the flag. An offer that sets the field does apply.
   No new agent method. No new public field or enum variant. `#[non_exhaustive]`
   is not added here: the delegated public types live in files this lane does not
   own, and adding it is a snapshot break.
Consequences: `cargo test -p regia_net --test lobby_hub_relay_only` captures
`HubEvent::Plan` bytes and the `Register`, `PunchIntro` and check datagrams.
A flag-clear run must show the host octets in `Register` and the member octets in
`PunchIntro`. `Allocate`, `HostInfo` and `ClientJoined` may still name the address
the relay observed. `cargo test -p regia_net --test lobby_hub_join` keeps the
mapped, punch and relay paths for a listen lobby with the flag clear. No new
dependency. No golden. No `hub.toml` change.

## ADR-10396: Relay-only hide review — replies and the lobby flag still name the other side
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: Review of NL-08 at `cc34070dc3` (ADR-10391) against the owner-facing promise
that no address of the other side appears in any byte either party receives on the
relay-only path. The plan-byte and `Register` / `PunchIntro` / check coverage in
`lobby_hub_relay_only` holds. A completed relay join, a stored server or lobby flag,
and `ReachAsk` do not.
Decision: Verdict is FIX FIRST. This review adds failing tests and does not change
the planner, the relay, or `approve`.
1. `HostInfo` and `Allocated` deliver the host address to the member. `Allocate`
   repeats that address. `ClientJoined` delivers the member address to the host.
   `relay_only_replies_must_not_name_either_side` fails on all four.
2. `approve_inner` still passes the lobby flag as `false`. A server presence with
   `relay_only` is stored on the room, and the plan is still `Mapped`.
   `server_flag_hides_both_plan_directions` fails at `assert_rewritten`.
3. `set_reach_mode` still returns `hub_not_ready`, so a listen lobby cannot set or
   clear the lobby flag. `listen_lobby_flag_hides_the_exchange` fails on `NotReady`.
   Clearing `ReachOffer.relay_only` does restore mapped, then punch, then relay.
4. `ask_inner` still sends the member's candidates in `ReachAsk` when either offer
   sets `relay_only`. `relay_only_ask_must_not_name_the_member` fails for both pairs.
5. `ecs_host::start_relay` never calls `RelayRegistrar::relay_only`. No new test:
   the call site is private, and a reconstruction would stay red after the one-line
   fix. `relay_only_register_omits_the_host` already shows that `from_game_socket`
   without `relay_only` puts the host octets in `Register`.
Consequences: `cargo test -p regia_net --test lobby_hub_relay_only` is red on those
four tests and green on the other eight, including the offer-flag clear and
`ReachDone`. Bounded decoding is unchanged (`wire.rs` hostile-count, cap, and
relay-only tail tests). No new public item, no snapshot edit, no dependency.

## ADR-10399: Relay-only replies and the stored flag hide both addresses
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10396 (review of ADR-10391) is FIX FIRST. On the relay-only path the
owner's promise is that no address of the other side appears in any byte either
party receives, in both directions, for a host-set flag and a member-set flag.
Plan bytes, `Register`, `PunchIntro` and connectivity checks already hold when
`RelayRegistrar::relay_only` and `JoinPath::relay_first` are used. The completed
join, the stored lobby flag and `ReachAsk` do not. `ecs_host::start_relay` never
calls `relay_only`.
Decision:
1. A `Register` may carry `RELAY_HIDE_ADDR_EXT` (`0xA1`) after its cookie.
   `RelayRegistrar::relay_only` sends that byte and no candidates. The relay
   stores the flag on the lobby (a renewal that omits it clears the flag) and
   publishes `0.0.0.0:0` in `HostInfo`. `Allocate` with an unspecified address
   resolves the lobby by comparing every lobby's bind key and accepting a hidden
   match. `Allocated` and `ClientJoined`, including a `Refresh` reply, name
   neither side. Forwarding still uses the real UDP endpoints. A hidden lobby
   sends no punch introduction. A register without the byte is unchanged.
2. `approve` passes the room's stored `relay_only` into `plans_for`. The
   signature of `plans_for` is unchanged.
3. `set_reach_mode` stores the flag. The listen owner, a delegated lobby's
   owning player or its bound server, or an ownerless lobby's server session
   may set or clear it. Members are sent the room. `set_bans` stays
   `hub_not_ready`.
4. `ReachAsk` omits the asker's candidates when the lobby flag, the asker's
   offer flag or the owner's offer flag is set. The stored ask keeps the
   candidates, so a later clear still has them.
5. `--relay-only` on the dedicated host calls `RelayRegistrar::relay_only` and
   does not start the router mapping or the host check. There is no `server.toml`
   key. The default remains a punch-capable host.
Consequences: `encode_register_hidden`, `RELAY_HIDE_ADDR_EXT`,
`CliOverrides.relay_only` and `HubServer::set_reach_mode` are public additions.
No new type, so no new `#[non_exhaustive]`. No new agent method. No new
dependency. No golden. The lead runs `cargo xtask api-snapshot --check`.

## ADR-10392: AskReach windows, bans before candidates, and a confirmed-session flag
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: NL-09 (spec 89 § 16.5, request R23) on the v0.7.1 hub. `AskReach` had no
10-second window and no in-flight cap. A ban was not checked before a candidate list
could be copied into an event. `confirm_session` stored a `LobbyServer` and pushed
`HubEvent::ServerSet` with that address to every member. Directory cards and presence
rows already hid `regia.server`; member data, room snapshots and `lobby()` did not.
The delegated lane changed the public hub protocol types `HubRequest`, `HubEvent`,
`HubError`, `HubReport`, `ReachOffer`, `RoomState`, `DirectoryPage` and
`HubLobbyCard`. The lead accepts that break for v0.7.1 only if each of those types
is `#[non_exhaustive]` and the release note names the one-line downstream fix.
`AdmitGate` (30 per second per address, 20 per second per identity) stays in front
of the core. This lane does not change `broker_reach`, `wire.rs` message layout, or
`join::set_bans` (that free function still returns `hub_not_ready`).
Decision:
1. `HubServer::ask_reach` checks, before any candidate is cloned into an event or a
   join map: missing lobby (`lobby_not_found`, before bans), hub-operator ban, lobby
   ban, server ban (`hub_banned`), dedicated `load >= capacity` when `capacity > 0`
   (`hub_server_full`, including members), then for a non-member visibility
   (`lobby_not_found` unless Public), closed (`hub_lobby_closed`) before full
   (`hub_lobby_full`), then `not_in_lobby`. A member of a listen lobby that later
   closed or filled may still ask. Then the listen owner (`not_owner`), a dedicated
   server with no session (`hub_server_offline`), and no offer (`hub_no_reach`).
   `check_offer` runs before the stamp. In-flight caps, then the 10-second windows.
   The address window is checked first. A refusal stamps neither window. A missing
   address skips the address window. A keyless session skips the key window and is
   still counted against the per-identity in-flight cap on its own member id.
   Replacing an `Asked` or `Planned` join credits one slot and still stamps the
   window when the ask is admitted. Caps, clamped by `HubSettings::sanitized` into
   `1..=` the wire cap and never raised: 4 asks per key per 10 s, 16 per address
   per 10 s, 2 in flight per key, 64 in flight on the hub.
2. Bans are player-key sets. The hub operator set is at most 4,096
   (`HubServer::set_operator_bans`). A lobby set is at most `MAX_LOBBY_BANS` (64),
   owner only, via `HubServer::set_bans` and the host's `SetBans`. A server set is
   the existing `RegisterServer` list (`MAX_SERVER_BANS`). Over cap is
   `hub_reach_invalid` and the previous set stays. Address bans stay on the
   dedicated host's `bans.ron`. `hub.toml` does not grow a `[bans]` table.
3. `set_data` and `set_member_data` refuse a value that parses as a `SocketAddr`,
   or `udp:` plus one, or `steam:` plus ASCII digits, with `hub_address_in_data`.
   The check is after ownership or membership, so a non-owner still gets
   `not_owner`. Any `Some` on `regia.server` is the same refusal. `set_data` of
   `None` on that key withdraws the confirmed flag. `confirm_session` stores only
   that flag. The `Option<LobbyServer>` argument is ignored as bytes. The same flag
   is a no-op. A dedicated confirm is `hub_address_in_data`. Members are told
   `HubEvent::SessionConfirmed` only. `RoomState.server` stays on the wire for a
   version-1 decoder and is always `None`. A wire-1 peer is sent `ServerSet` of
   `None` instead of `SessionConfirmed`. Wire 2 receives the flag. Neither carries
   an address. Directory, query, presence, room, `lobby()` and member data drop
   `regia.server` and any address-shaped value.
4. The eight public protocol types above are `#[non_exhaustive]`. No other public
   type gains that attribute. `HubSettings` and `HubLimits` gain the four AskReach
   fields. Under `[limits]` in `hub.toml` the keys `ask_per_identity_per_10s`,
   `ask_per_address_per_10s`, `ask_inflight_per_identity` and `ask_inflight_hub`
   are optional. Format version stays 1. A value above the wire cap is stored and
   clamped by `settings().sanitized()`. Zero is refused. No new agent method:
   `lobby.hub_status` `refused` already counts `HubError::code()`.
Consequences: `cargo test -p regia_net --test lobby_hub_ask_guard` covers rows 4,
5, 11 and 12 (one key, many keys on one address, bans before candidates, full /
closed / invisible asks, and an `RGN1` plus an `RGNR` datagram dropped on the hub
socket). A struct pattern over one of the eight types adds `..`. An exhaustive
match adds `_ =>`. Another crate builds a `ReachOffer` with
`ReachOffer::default()` and then field assignment. `HubSettings` and `HubLimits`
literals add `..HubSettings::default()` or `..HubLimits::default()`. The lead runs
`cargo xtask api-snapshot --check` (and `--update` if `non_exhaustive` must be
recorded), `cargo xtask check-formats --update` for the optional hub.toml keys,
and `cargo xtask manual`. `join::set_bans` and `set_reach_mode` still return
`hub_not_ready`.

## ADR-10400: Address spellings and a ban that lands during an ask
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: ADR-10392 (spec 89 § 16.5) promised that a listing, a query, a presence
event or a lobby-data read contains no address, and that a banned key gets no
candidates. The predicate behind that promise accepted a Rust `SocketAddr`, a
case-sensitive `udp:` plus one, and a case-sensitive `steam:` plus digits.
Bracketed IPv4, a `udp://` URL, an uppercase prefix, an IPv6 named zone and
`Steam:` plus digits were stored by `set_data`, `set_member_data` and create,
and they showed on `lobby()` and on directory cards. `approve_inner` rechecked a
dedicated server-seat ban and `load >= capacity`, and did not recheck the
operator set or the lobby set, so a ban that landed while the ask was open still
copied the owner's candidates into a `Plan`. `clean_handle` accepted a handle
that is a socket address, and that handle was published on the presence row, the
directory card, the room member name and the invite.
Decision:
1. `value_carries_address` is a whole-value spelling. It is true for a
   `SocketAddr`, for a bracketed IPv4 or IPv6 with a port (a zone is split off
   before the address is parsed, so a named interface zone counts), for `udp:`
   or `udp://` in any ASCII case plus one of those, and for `steam:` in any
   ASCII case plus ASCII digits. A bare address with no port, a hostname and a
   port alone are not that spelling. `set_data`, `set_member_data` and create
   refuse it with `hub_address_in_data`. The forms `SocketAddr` already accepts
   stay refused.
2. `approve_inner` treats an operator ban and a lobby ban like the dedicated
   server-seat ban. The member is sent `ReachDenied`, the call returns
   `Ok(None)`, and no `Plan` is built. A keyless session still matches none of
   the three ban lists. Ask-time bans stay `hub_banned` and still copy no
   candidate.
3. A handle that the spelling accepts is not stored. The session opens under a
   stand-in of at most eight bytes, no longer than the spelling, with no `.`
   or `:`. The same spelling always maps to the same stand-in, so a reconnect
   and an invite of that spelling find the session. Presence, directory cards,
   room member names, invites and chat from-handles carry the stand-in.
Consequences: No new public type, field, variant or error code. No
`#[non_exhaustive]` change. A host that put one of these spellings in lobby
data now gets `hub_address_in_data`. A host that used a socket address as a
handle sees the stand-in on the directory. The lead runs
`cargo xtask api-snapshot --check`, `cargo xtask check-formats --update` and
`cargo xtask manual`. This lane edits no format and no generated book page.

## ADR-10397: The lobby hub process also runs the relay
Date: 2026-11-22   Status: proposed
Context: NL-11 (spec 89 § 16.8, request R23) on the v0.7.1 hub. `regia-lobby-hub`
constructs a `HubProcess` and never a `RelayServer`, so a packaged hub cannot
hand out a relay allocation. v0.7.0 clients must keep working against a v0.7.1
hub. `hub.toml` is format 1. ADR-10392 said the format version stays 1 and that
`hub.toml` does not grow a `[bans]` table. This decision supersedes those two
sentences for the relay, the ban file and the log directory only. The optional
AskReach keys and the `AdmitGate` limits stay as ADR-10392 left them. The
systemd unit is not rewritten: its `ExecStart` is the binary plus `--config`
and `--key-file`, and the relay port comes from `hub.toml`.
Decision:
1. `hub.toml` `format_version` is 2. A version-1 file still loads. A missing
   `format_version` is 1. With no `relay.enabled` key, version 1 leaves the
   relay off and version 2 turns it on. An explicit value wins.
   `migrate_hub_toml` rewrites the top-level version line and appends `[relay]`
   with `enabled = false`, plus `[bans]` and `[log]`, only when those tables
   are absent. It does not insert the AskReach keys (a second `[limits]` would
   duplicate the table). A file that is already version 2 is returned
